generated_text: So, do you think we should go out tonight or just stay in and get some rest? I’ve been up all night with the baby, and I’m really run down. I think we should probably stay in. Not only do I have a headache from the baby crying all night, but also I’m beginning to feel like I’ve aged ten years in the last two days. Plus, we have a lot of work to do tomorrow. Yeah, I’m with you. It’s been a tough few days. I mean, I can’t even remember the last time I had a proper sleep. I’ve been up with the baby at 3 a.m. and then again at 5 a.m. and then again at 7 a.m. It’s like a revolving door of crying. I know, I know. It’s exhausting. But I think it’s going to be worth it when we see the baby actually sleeping through the night. Just think of all the sleep we’ll get once we get through this phase. That’s true, isn’t it? I mean, I remember when we were kids, we never had to worry about a baby crying all night. It was always the parents who were up at odd hours. Oh, I remember that. My brother used to tell me that when he was a kid, his parents used to have a sort of sleep schedule that was like a phone call. One would be up, the other would be asleep, and then someone would wake up to take over. That way, they could actually get some sleep. That is a funny way to put it. Anyway, I think we should take it easy tonight. We have about five hours of sleep between us, and the baby is going to be fine. I think we can manage. Exactly. I’m just going to take a hot bath, and then I’m going to lay down for a bit. I feel like I need to recharge. Good idea. I’m going to make some tea and read a bit. We can talk about our plans for the weekend. I was thinking about going out to a little café with some friends. I haven’t had any proper social time in ages. That sounds nice. I really need to get out more. I’ve been so preoccupied with the baby, I haven’t even had the chance to see my sister in a while.

So, do you remember that time we were in Berlin and we got stuck on the U-Bahn for like an hour because the train was delayed? I was so stressed, I thought we were going to miss our flight. Oh yeah, that was a doozy. I remember you were muttering about how the whole thing was a metaphor for modern life – chaos and uncertainty. You were actually pretty philosophical for a woman who was about to miss her flight. Well, it was a moment of clarity, right? We were in the middle of the city, surrounded by people from all over the world, and we were just two lost tourists. It made me think about how the EU brings people together, even in the most inconvenient of ways. I think you're right. I mean, the fact that we could just pick up a map, walk to the nearest station, and figure it out without speaking a word of German was pretty impressive. It’s like the EU makes things easier, even when things go wrong. Exactly. And I still remember that time we were in Prague and we got lost, but we found this tiny little café that was run by a group of young people who only spoke English. They were so excited to help us, and we ended up having the best meal of our lives – all because of that shared language, and the fact that we were both British. That’s one of my favorite travel memories. I think the EU has made travel so much more accessible, especially for people like us who aren’t fluent in every language. It’s like we can just open our mouths and the world responds in English. And it’s not just about language. It’s also about how the EU allows us to move freely, work, study, and explore without all the bureaucratic hassle. I mean, I was doing research in Barcelona for a few months, and I could just go back to the UK and pick up where I left off. It’s something I take for granted, but I think it’s incredible. Absolutely. You know, when I was doing my PhD in Manchester, I used to go to Brussels for conferences, and I was always amazed how easy it was to get around. I would meet people from all over Europe, and we’d go out for a drink, chat about our work, and then go our separate ways the next day.

Alright, do you want some of this cheesecake? It’s just come out of the oven. Can I have some? It looks really nice. I want some too, Mummy. Okay, just one slice for you, and one for me. The rest is for the fridge, so we can have it later. Mummy, can we play Monopoly again? I won last time! Well, you did win last time, but it’s not fair to play every single day. Let’s try something else. I like Monopoly. I like to be the banker. Yeah, you do like being the banker. You always keep track of all the money. And I always win because I’m good at counting and I know how to make money. That’s true. You’re really good at that. I mean, you’ve got a head for numbers, haven’t you? I want to be a banker when I grow up. That’s a great idea. Banking is a good job if you like money. But you’ll have to be really careful with it, though. Why? Because if you’re not careful, you can end up with too much money and then you’ll have to pay taxes on it. What’s taxes? Taxes are like money you have to give to the government. They use it to build roads, schools, and hospitals. Oh, so you have to give some money back? Yeah, a bit. But it’s not all of it. And if you’re a banker, you’ll get paid a lot more than you give back. So I can get a lot of money? Maybe. But first, you need to learn how to count, how to add, and how to manage your money. That’s what school is for. I like school. I’m good at maths. I can do all the sums. That’s what I like about you, you’re so clever. But even clever people need to learn the rules of money. It’s not just about having it, it’s about using it wisely. Can I have some of the cheesecake now? No, not yet. You have to wait until everyone’s had some. And after that, we can play Monopoly again, okay? Okay, Mummy. But I want to be the banker again. We’ll see. Maybe next time, you can be the banker. But for now, let’s enjoy our cake and talk about how we can all be smart with our money.

So, do you know what’s up with the car? It’s been making this weird noise all morning. I swear it sounds like it’s about to explode. Honestly, I didn’t even notice it. Maybe it’s something minor. Or maybe it’s something serious. You know how these cars can be—sometimes they just go quietly and then you’re left with a dead battery or something. I don’t think it’s the battery. I checked that. It’s more like a grinding noise when I turn the wheel. And the dashboard light flickered for a second the other day. I don’t like it. Yeah, I heard that. You know, I was thinking about taking it in for a service. I’ve been meaning to. I’ve been putting it off because I’m busy with work, but I should probably get it sorted before it’s too late. I know, I know. I just feel like it’s been getting worse. And I’m not sure if we can afford to get it fixed right now. My university fees are still taking a chunk out of the budget. Yeah, I know. It’s one of those things that you tend to ignore until it’s too late. But I think we should try to get it looked at. If it’s something minor, maybe it’ll be cheap. If it’s something major, at least we’ll know. You’re right. I just don’t want to be stuck somewhere with a broken car. I mean, we’re not even in a rush to go anywhere. It’s just that I’d rather not be in the middle of nowhere with no way to get back. Exactly. I mean, I know we’re not living far from the city, but sometimes things can take longer than expected. And you never know—maybe the car will break down on the way to the hospital, or to the store. It’s not worth the risk. I guess you’re right. I was just hoping it would hold out a little longer. I don’t want to spend too much money on repairs right now, especially with everything else that’s going on. I get it. We’ll figure it out. Maybe we can split the cost of the service or something. Or see if there’s a cheaper garage.

I've been thinking a lot lately about those old bridges I used to design back in my day. You know, when I was a civil engineer, it was all about calculations and making sure everything was safe. Now, it's just… well, I don’t know what to do with myself. I know the feeling, old friend. It’s like your mind’s still running on full speed, but there’s no project to keep it occupied. I used to be a schoolteacher, and now I just sit here listening to the radio and feeding the cat. I can relate. I used to run a childminding service, and I still get calls from the local nursery asking for advice on settling children in. It’s strange, isn’t it? You think you’re done with work, but the world keeps on spinning. Exactly. I remember one time, there was this bridge in Norfolk, near Costessey, that I worked on. The locals used to call it the "Wobbler" because it always seemed to sway a little more than the others. Eventually, it had to be replaced, but it was a proud moment when we finally got it right. That sounds like a real achievement. I’ve always admired people who can put their skills to use in a way that benefits others. I suppose I’ve been more passive in my retirement. I used to enjoy gardening, but even that feels like a waste of time now. I’ve taken up knitting. It’s a bit boring, but it keeps my hands busy. I made a scarf for my granddaughter, and she loved it. It’s comforting in a way, knowing that you’re creating something, even if it’s just a little piece of fabric. That’s a nice thought. I’ve been trying to learn how to cook again. I used to be terrible at it, but I realized that if you can put food on the table, you’ve done something useful. You know, even if it’s just for yourself and your family. That’s a good point. I’ve also been learning to play the piano again. I used to play in the church choir, and it gave me a sense of purpose. Now, I just sit by the piano and try not to let the silence get too loud. I think we’re all just trying to find a way to stay active, even if it’s in small ways.

So, do you think you've got the basics of the Honest Skincare website sorted? I mean, the layout, the product displays, the call to action buttons — are we all on the same page? Honestly, I think we are, but I’ve been thinking about things that could make it more user-friendly. Like, people don’t just want to see the products—they want to know what they’re made of. A lot of customers are really into natural and ethical products, so transparency is key. Absolutely. And I was just reading an article the other day about how the trust factor is huge in the beauty industry. If you can show that your ingredients are clean and your supply chain is ethical, people are more likely to buy from you. Yeah, I’ve been talking to some of my suppliers about getting certifications and labels. It might be a bit of an upfront cost, but it could really set us apart from the competition. Plus, with the growing eco-conscious market, it’s not just a trend—it’s a movement. That makes sense. I’ve also been thinking about the way we present our products. Maybe we can add some short, engaging videos showing how to use the products. People love visual content, especially on social media. It adds that extra layer of trust and personality. I agree, and I’ve already started brainstorming some ideas. But I don’t know if I should be doing all the content myself or if I should hire someone. I mean, someone who knows how to make these videos look professional. That’s a good point. You’d need a content creator with some experience in the beauty niche. I know a colleague who’s into digital marketing and could help. Or maybe you could try using some of the tools on Canva or even free editing software like iMovie. Not sure if you’re up for the learning curve, though. I’m not opposed to learning, but I think it would be more efficient to invest in some professional content. Especially if we want to start running ads on Instagram or Facebook. We need to make sure we’re not just listing products but telling a story about why people should trust us. Exactly. And you know, even the way we talk about the products can make a difference. I remember a skincare brand I used to work with—they made it a point to use simple, clear language.

I just saw the news this morning about the new school opening in the seaside area. It's supposed to be a really modern facility, with all the latest tech and everything. I can't say I'm entirely excited about it, though. Not sure if it's what the children really need. Yeah, I saw that too. I think it's a bit of a big deal for the area. They're trying to bring more investment, but I wonder if it’s just a way to keep the tourists coming in. You know, the whole package deal—school, shops, more services. You know, I’ve been thinking about how things have changed since I retired. It’s strange, isn’t it? Being surrounded by all these kids, but you’re not part of it anymore. I miss the classroom, you know. Even though I’ve been out of it for years, I still get a bit nostalgic sometimes. I can imagine. I still feel like I’m in the middle of it all, though, even after all these years. I mean, I still go in to help out with the younger teachers sometimes, and it keeps me on my toes. But it’s not the same as when I was teaching full time. I suppose not. I was just thinking about the other day – I had a visit from my niece and her kids. They were all so lively and full of energy. It reminded me of the days when I was still in the classroom. And now they’re all out there, full of potential and mischief. It’s amazing how quickly time passes. I still remember when I first started teaching, and it felt like the world was so much smaller. Now, it feels like everything is moving so fast. I can’t believe how different it is now. It’s true. I was just talking to my old colleague the other day, and we were both reminiscing about the old days. He said he’s thinking of starting up some kind of weekend class for retired teachers, just to keep us busy and keep our minds active. I might have to consider that. That sounds like a great idea. It would be nice to have something to do, especially with the weather getting a bit more unpredictable. I think the idea of staying in the loop with the education system could be a good one.

So, do you think we’ll get snow this year? I mean, it’s been warmer than usual so far, but I’m hoping for some proper Christmas weather. Yeah, I mean, it’s hard to tell. I’ve seen some forecasts saying it might be colder in December than November, but then again, there’s always the chance it stays mild. Honestly, I’d rather have a snowy Christmas. I love the atmosphere, the way everything looks when it’s covered in snow. Plus, it’s perfect for getting the kids excited. Mm, I can’t argue with that. Though I do miss the days when we used to go sledding on the hill behind the old mill. It was magic. Oh, I remember that! You used to build the biggest snowmen ever. I think one of them was about three feet tall. Wait, was that really you? Definitely me! And don’t even get me started on the mulberry tree near the gate. We used to use that as a target for our snowballs. Yeah, I remember that tree. It was still there when I moved out, but I think they cut it down last year. That’s a shame. I swear, that mulberry tree was part of the village’s charm. Anyway, have you thought about how you’re going to heat the house this winter? Honestly, I’ve been meaning to upgrade my heating system. The old one is getting a bit unreliable. I’m thinking about getting a new boiler. That’s a big decision. Have you looked into renewable energy options? I heard some people are switching to solar panels now. I’ve been doing some research on that. It’s expensive up front, but long-term, it could save money. Plus, it’s good for the environment. I’m not sure about the environmental angle, but I’m definitely not ready to pay for a new system just yet. I’m still holding out for a cold snap. Ha! That’s the spirit. I think the best way to keep warm is to just have a fire in the living room and go out for a walk with a thermos of tea. That’s not a bad idea. I’ve been meaning to get a proper firewood supply. I’ve been buying it in small batches, but it’s not enough. You should consider buying in bulk, though.

So, do you think we should get new cutlery? I mean, the knives are getting a bit rusty. Yeah, I was thinking the same thing. I saw this set online that's really good quality. Not too expensive either. Oh, you know, I had a set like that when I was younger. It was my dad’s. He used to tell me that good cutlery is worth investing in because it lasts forever. I used to have a set like that too. My mum was always very particular about the way the cutlery was arranged. She’d even have a specific place for each knife and fork. Yeah, I remember that. She had the whole thing set up like a military base. Every plate had its own fork, and the knives were all lined up like soldiers in a parade. That’s a bit much, isn’t it? I mean, I just want something functional. Not like a museum display. I can see that. But maybe a bit of style doesn’t hurt. I mean, it’s our house, right? We can have it as we like. I think it's good to mix practicality with a little bit of personality. You know, the way you set the table can make a difference in how you feel about your home. Yeah, and don’t forget, it's not just about the cutlery. Everything else in the house should match too. The plates, the glasses, the candles. It's all part of the whole vibe. Exactly. It's like painting the room. If you don’t get the basics right, everything looks messy. But once you have a good foundation, the rest just flows. I suppose you’re right. Maybe I should look at some sets that have a classic look. You know, not too flashy, just something that feels timeless. That sounds good. I could help you pick it out. I mean, I’ve been looking for a new set myself anyway. It’s been a while since I’ve had proper cutlery that works well. Great! We could go together. It would be a nice way to spend the afternoon. And maybe we could get some new glasses while we're at it. Oh, I’d love that. I’ve been meaning to get some new glasses for ages. It’s been a bit of a struggle with the old ones.

So, do you think we’ll get the snow this year? I was just thinking about our trip to the mountains. I hope so, Mummy. I’ve been looking forward to it for ages. I can’t wait to see the snow and build a snowman. You know, I was just talking to the travel agent yesterday, and they said the forecast is looking better than last year. They think there might be enough snow for us to ski. That’s great! But I do hope we don’t have to wait too long. I want to start learning how to ski properly before we go. I know, love. I’ve been thinking about that too. Maybe we could take a couple of lessons in the weeks before the trip. I’ve heard the slopes aren’t too busy in the beginning of the season. Yeah, that sounds like a good idea. I don’t want to feel totally clueless when I get there. What’s the deal with the boots, though? I’ve seen pictures of people wearing these big heavy things. Oh, they’re called ski boots. They’re designed to grip the skis and give you control. They can be a bit uncomfortable at first, but once you get used to them, they’re okay. Okay, I can handle that. But what about the actual skiing? I’m not sure if I’m ready for that. I mean, I’ve never even been on a snowboard. That’s fine. We can start with the easier slopes. There are plenty of beginner areas, and the instructors are really patient. I’m sure you’ll pick it up quickly. I hope so. I just don’t want to fall and break something. I heard one of my friends had a bad fall last year and had to go to the hospital. That’s why it’s so important to take the lessons. They’ll teach you how to fall properly and how to get up again. You won’t feel alone out there. That does sound good. I’ll try to be brave. What about the lunches and dinners on the mountain? I’m not sure about eating cold food after a long day of skiing. There are plenty of restaurants and cafes up there. They serve real food, and I think the views are worth it. Plus, you can always bring your own snacks if you’re not feeling up to much.

I can't believe we've got to do Spanish next year. I mean, I'm already struggling with French. How are we supposed to learn another language? I know, right? It's so unfair. I mean, we're only in Year 8 and already we've got to choose our languages. Do we even have enough time to practice? Yeah, and I heard that if you're not good at languages, you might have to do more maths. Oh, I'm not even sure I can do maths. I was so bad at it last year. I know, I know. My teacher even said I need to work harder on my algebra. I don’t even know what that is sometimes. Just a bunch of letters and numbers. I hear you. I’m so tired of homework. I mean, I have English, maths, science, and now Spanish. And I still have to do food tech. How is this even possible? I know! I told my mum I couldn’t do food tech because I don’t like cooking. She said, “You have to try it, you might like it.” But I did it last week and I made something that looked like a disaster. Yeah, I was in the same boat. I tried to make a burger and I burned the bread. My dad said it was the best he’d ever eaten. I didn’t believe him. It looked like a charcoal briquette. Haha, yeah, I remember when I made my first risotto. It was so runny, my teacher said it was like a soup. I was so embarrassed. I thought I was going to fail the whole class. I think I’m going to fail all of this. I just don’t get it. I know that I shouldn’t be worrying about it, but I can’t stop thinking about it. What if I don’t get into the right sixth form? I know, I know. I’m trying to stay positive, but sometimes I just feel like I’m not good at anything. I mean, I’m not bad at English, I think I’m okay at it, but I’m worried about the essay I have to do next week. Yeah, I have to write an essay about a book I read. I just picked  The Giver  because it was the only one I could remember.

I just watched this film called  The Favourite  the other day. I was watching it on a whim, you know, because it had some good reviews and the casting was interesting. Oh, I’ve heard of that one. Was it good? It was... intense. I mean, it’s a historical drama, but it’s not your typical stuffy costume piece. It’s very gritty and full of emotion. The lead actress, Yalitza Aparicio, was amazing. She just...  is  the character. That’s a big name, isn’t it? I’ve heard her in a few things. What’s the story about? It’s set in the late 17th century, during the reign of Queen Anne. It follows the relationship between the Queen, her lady-in-waiting, and a new lady-in-waiting who comes in and starts causing all sorts of chaos. It’s about power, politics, and the complicated dynamics between women. That sounds complicated. Was it hard to follow? Not really. I think the dialogue was very sharp and the performances were strong. It made me think about how much power women had – or didn’t – in those times. It’s very different from what I’m used to watching these days. I’m not sure I’d be into that. I prefer more... action or something with a clear good vs. evil. Though I do like a good drama. That’s fair. I think you’d like  The Woman in the Window  more. It’s a psychological thriller with a bit of mystery. I’ve been meaning to watch it. Oh, I’ve heard of that one. I think it’s based on a book? Yeah, it’s based on A.J. Finn’s novel. It’s about a reclusive woman who starts seeing things and suspects her neighbor is a serial killer. It’s tense, and the suspense builds up really well. That sounds like something I’d enjoy. I’ve been meaning to try more thrillers. You should. I think it’s a good pick. It’s not too long, and it keeps you on your toes. I’ll look it up. Maybe we can watch it together sometime. That would be nice. I think we’d both get a kick out of it. Sounds like a plan. What about you? Any films you’ve been into lately? I’ve been rewatching some old classics.  The Godfather  is always a good one.

Mmm, thanks for the coffee, Mum. It’s really good. I was just reading this book about language and how dialects change depending on where you're from. I think it's fascinating how people from different parts of England use different phrases and accents. Oh, I know, I’ve always found it interesting too. I used to work in Birmingham, and I remember how people in the Midlands have a different way of speaking compared to someone from the South. I suppose it's part of what makes us who we are. Yeah, and I teach English as a foreign language, so I get to hear all sorts of accents and dialects. It's pretty cool to see how people adapt their speech in different contexts. But honestly, I sometimes miss the way people used to talk back home in Hitchin. You know, the old-fashioned way of speaking. I can imagine. I sometimes think back to when I was your age, and everyone still had time to chat and catch up. These days, people are always on their phones or rushing off somewhere. It’s sad, really. I know, it’s true. I feel like we’re all so busy with work and life that we don’t take the time to really talk anymore. But I do enjoy our chats. They’re one of the few times I can just sit and listen to you talk about the old days. You know, I was thinking the other day about how you’re getting into teaching and all. I just wanted to say how proud I am of you. It’s not an easy job, but it’s something you’re really passionate about. Thanks, Mum. I really appreciate that. I know I’ve got a lot to learn, but I’m trying my best. I think I’m starting to get the hang of it. I just need more practice, especially with the different levels of students. That’s the spirit. And don’t forget, I’m always here to help. If you ever need advice or just someone to talk to, I’m just a phone call away. I know, and I always will be. You’ve been such a big part of my life, and I’m really grateful for that. That means more than you know, darling. I’ve always believed in you. And I hope you’ll always remember that.

So, do you think we’ll get through the last few streets before it starts raining again? I’ve seen the sky darkening a bit. Yeah, I think it’s going to be a proper downpour before we get there. That’s the thing about China—sometimes the weather just changes so fast. I know, it’s quite different from the UK. You don’t really get that kind of sudden shift in the weather here. I’ve had to carry an umbrella every single day this week. I know, it’s a bit of a shock. I remember when I first came here, I thought I’d be used to it after a few weeks, but no—still caught off guard. Although, I have to say, the rain here is more of a show. You can’t really tell if you’re getting wet or not because it’s just drizzling and then it’s gone. Yeah, but when it does start pouring, it’s like a waterfall. I saw this one street earlier where the water was actually pooling on the pavement. It’s like the city’s trying to flood itself. You’re not wrong. I think the city’s still trying to get used to the population. We’ve been walking past the same market every day for a week now, and I swear I’ve seen more people there today than the last five days combined. You know what I’m thinking? We might need to go out tomorrow and do some shopping. I’ve got a few things I need to buy for the upcoming term. I was just thinking the same thing. I’ve been meaning to pick up some books for my lectures, and I think there’s a new bookstore just down the road. I heard it’s a bit of a hidden gem. That sounds perfect. We could go there, and if it starts raining again, we’ll have an excuse to go inside. Exactly. And if we’re lucky, maybe we’ll even find some good deals. I’ve been meaning to get some new teaching materials. I’ll bring the umbrella just in case. I’ve got a feeling we’ll need it. That’s a good idea. I’ll see if I can find a spare one in the flat. I think I left one in the kitchen.

Alright, so I just wanted to check – are we all clear on the babysitting plans for tomorrow? I know it’s the weekend, but I’ve got a meeting at the school in the morning, and I need someone to look after the kids while I’m out. Yeah, I was just thinking about that too. I’ve got the afternoon free, so I could do it. Is that okay with you? That would be great! I’ll text you the details later. Just to confirm the time and what you need to bring. Oh, and don’t forget the kids love the playpen you set up in the living room. They’ve been asking about it all week. Can I help too? I’ve got the whole day off. I could do the morning or the afternoon, whichever works for you. Oh, thanks for offering, Tom! But I think it’s better if just one of you does it. I don’t want to overburden you. I’ll figure out the schedule once I get the details from Emily. No worries, I’ve got it. I’ll take the morning and then maybe a bit of the afternoon if needed. What time do you need me to be there? Around 9:30 am – that’s when I’ll be leaving. And I’ll be back around 1:30 pm. You can pick up the kids from the school and bring them back. Wait, don’t you have a photoshoot this weekend? I thought you mentioned that earlier. Yes, I did. It’s on Saturday, at the community centre in Bury St Edmunds. I’ve got a few shots to take, and the kids can come along too. I thought it might be a good idea to take them to see the set up. They’ve been asking to do something fun this weekend. That sounds like a great idea. They’ll love it. But I was thinking, what about the haircuts? I’ve been meaning to get mine done, and I was going to ask if we could go together. Oh, I’ve been thinking about that too. I’m going to the salon in Norwich next week, so maybe go together then. But let me check the schedule again – I don’t want to miss the photoshoot. What time does the photoshoot start? I could help you with the kids if you need someone to watch them while you’re there.

So, do you know what’s happening this weekend? I heard there’s a big party at the Student Union. Oh yeah, I saw that on Facebook! I thought you were going to ask me about it. I was, but I didn’t want to make it sound like I was pressuring you. No worries, I’m actually thinking of going. I’ve been dying to get out of this place for a bit. That’s great! I was going to go with my friend Alex, but he’s got a test on Monday, so he’s stuck studying. That’s a shame. I’d have liked to have gone with someone. Yeah, it’s a bit of a lonely thing, going out by yourself, but it’s not the worst. You can meet people, you know? True. Although I’ve been thinking about this for a while. When’s the party exactly? It’s tomorrow night, starting at 9 PM. There’s going to be a DJ, and some food trucks. I think they’re serving pizza and burgers. Oh, that sounds good. I’ve been craving something a little more exciting than the canteen food. I know, right? The chicken tikka masala here is just…  decent . Ha! I’ve been trying to convince my roommate that we should just cook our own meals. But she insists on ordering takeaway every night. Fair enough. I think I’d be tempted too. Although I’m not sure I’d make it through a whole week of takeaway. Exactly! I’m starting to think I need to get a blender and start making smoothies instead. You’re not the only one. I’ve been eyeing up that fruit smoothie machine at the corner shop. Oh, I love smoothies. I even tried making one last week with banana, mango, and a sprite. It was  okay . That’s brave. I’ve never even tried making one. I’m more of a coffee and toast person. Well, if you ever change your mind, I could teach you how to make a decent smoothie. I’d like that. But first, maybe I’ll just stick to the canteen. You know what? I’ll take you to the party tomorrow. You can meet some people, and maybe you’ll get inspired to start cooking more. That sounds like a plan! I’ll bring my coat, just in case it’s cold.

So, do you guys remember that time we tried to cook that fancy Italian meal and ended up with a burnt lasagna and a fridge full of mystery meat? It was  legendary . Oh, I remember that! We were so proud of ourselves, thinking we were like  Deejay  or something. But then the lasagna just…  sizzled  into a crispy, inedible mess. I swear, it looked like a charcoal briquette. It was worse than that. I think we even accidentally put the garlic in the oven instead of the pot. You know what I mean? It was like,  this is how you get a food-related existential crisis . My point is, I’ve learned my lesson. I’m not cooking anything complicated unless I’ve got a foolproof recipe and a backup plan. But I  do  love food, you know. Like, I’ve been thinking about this holiday trip to Spain for a while now. I’ve got this plan to eat my way through Barcelona. Paella, tapas, all that stuff. Oh, you’re gonna love it. I went there last year for a work trip and devoured like three different versions of paella in one day. But I also got food poisoning. It was  not  fun. Yeah, but that’s the thing about food—every time you try something new, you might end up with a minor disaster, but it’s part of the experience. Who cares if you get sick? You’re in Spain, right? True, but I’d rather not be in the hospital with a fever and a hangover after a night of  super  over-the-top nightlife. That’s not the kind of holiday I’m looking for. Maybe you should just stick to the food and skip the dancing. I mean, Barcelona’s got great restaurants. And the weather’s always nice. Though I heard they do that  extra  hot weather in July. You know, like,  elephant  hot. Yeah, you’d be better off going in the spring or autumn. And honestly, I think you should just do it with us. We could road trip together. I’ve got a van, and I can go anywhere. Plus, I know a few good places to eat. That sounds like a plan. But, um… do you think your van’s actually roadworthy? I mean, I’ve heard stories about your van. It’s like a  geek  version of a car.

Well, I've been thinking about that trip to London again, you know. It's been ages since we went. What do you reckon, Frank? I'd love to go, but with the money situation, I don't know. Rent's been going up, and I can’t afford to take the family. Still, I’d love to go and see the sights. Yeah, I remember when we all went to London before. It was a real treat. We used to stay in a Youth hostel in Cornwall, remember? That was ages ago, but it was fun. Oh, yes, that was a good trip. I still remember the time we accidentally got stuck on the tube for over an hour. We were all laughing, though. It was one of those funny things that happened. I remember that! You screamed so loud, Ed, I thought the train was going to crash. But then we just happened to get off at the right station. It was like fate. You always had a sense of adventure, Ed. It’s why I like having you around. You never let life get too dull. Well, I like to live life to the fullest, if I can. I mean, I’m retired now, so I might as well enjoy it while I can. Though I do miss the days when I was working. You know, I’ve been thinking about selling my old house. It’s been sitting empty for a while, and I’m not sure if I can afford to keep it. I’ve got some offers from a couple of people on eBay, but I’m not sure if they’re real. That’s about the same time I was thinking about selling the car. It’s old, and I can’t afford the repairs. I’ve got a few people interested, but I’m not sure if I can trust them. I know what you mean, Frank. I’ve been trying to sell my old land in Norfolk. It’s not easy, but I’m not ready to move. It’s where I grew up. I've been meaning to visit Norfolk anyway. I’ve heard the countryside there is beautiful. Maybe after I sell the house, I could take a trip out there with the kids. That sounds lovely. I’d love to see that part of England again. I’ve been reading about the history of the area, and it’s fascinating.

So, do you know what’s going to happen with the baby? I mean, it’s only a week old, but I feel like I’m already running on sleep deprivation. I know, I feel the same. I’ve only been off work for a couple of weeks, but I’ve already got the hang of  not  sleeping. I mean, I think I’ve only actually slept like three hours in the last five days. That’s brutal. I think I was woken up by the baby at least three times last night. I don’t even know how I managed to function. I’m still trying to figure that out. I mean, I’ve got the baby in the cot, and I’ve got a baby monitor, and I’ve got a nap schedule, and I still feel like I’m in a nightmare. Yeah, and it’s not just the sleep. You’re constantly feeding them, changing their nappies, cleaning up the mess. I mean, even the milk is a hassle. I had to throw out like half the bottle because it didn’t come out properly. Oh no, really? Did you say something to the baby? No, I didn’t. I just… it was like the milk was all over the place, and I couldn’t get it to flow right. I nearly cried. You know what? I had the same problem. I mean, I was just sitting there, trying to feed him, and it was like the bottle was doing a  disco  instead of a  flow . I thought I was going to have to call a midwife or something. That’s not funny. I mean, I feel like I’m doing everything wrong. What if I’m not a good mum? Don’t say that. You’re doing the best you can. I mean, I feel like I’m failing too. I can’t even remember the last time I had a full meal. Yeah, I had a sandwich yesterday. That’s it. I couldn’t even manage a proper meal without the baby crying in the background. I had a snack at the park the other day. I just snuck out with a banana and a bottle of water. It was like a secret mission. You’re a hero. I mean, I’m planning to go to the supermarket tomorrow, just to get some food, and maybe take a walk to clear my head.

Morning everyone, I hope you all had a good night’s sleep. I’ve had a few dreams about that cat again, the one with the red collar. It’s been haunting me ever since we found it in the garden last week. Oh, don’t worry, it’s just your subconscious telling you it’s time to get a new one. You’ve had that one for over five years, Alice. You should take it to the shelter before it becomes a problem. Honestly, I think it’s just trying to be your friend. It follows me around the house like a shadow. I’ve even named it Mr. Whiskers. You’re not the only one who’s had that. My cousin’s cat did the same thing. It used to sit on my lap while I was working on the computer. If it wasn’t for the fact that it’s a cat, I’d say it was a personal assistant. That’s a bit much, but I can see how you’d think that. Anyway, I was just thinking, we should probably get the garden sorted before the weekend. The roses are looking a bit withered, and the lawn is starting to look like a jungle. Yeah, I’ve been meaning to do that too. I was going to ask you if you wanted to help, but I thought you might be busy with work. I’m off tomorrow, actually. I’m meeting a friend in London for a coffee and a walk. Maybe I can take a break from work and come back later. That sounds nice. I’m still being trained at the hospital, but I’ve got the weekend off. I could help with the garden if you want. That would be great. We could make a day of it. I’ll bring the secateurs, and you can bring the hedge trimmers. Maybe we can get some new plants too. Sounds like a plan. But before we get too excited, let’s make sure we’ve got enough food. I had a bit of a mess up last week when I forgot to buy bread and ended up having to raid the cupboard. You’re not the only one. I had to go out of my way to buy some eggs because I forgot to check the fridge. I think we’re all a bit forgetful these days.

So, do you know what’s happening with the school tests? I think they’re going to be really hard. I got the email from the teacher about the science test next week. Yeah, I saw that too. I’m really stressed about it. I’m not sure I’ve even studied for it yet. What about you? Me neither. I tried to study last night, but I kept getting distracted by my phone. I think I just need to find a better way to focus. I know what you mean. I tried to do some revision but then I started watching Ed Sheeran videos on YouTube. It’s so easy to get distracted. Ha, I’m guilty of that too. I guess we’re both not the best at studying. I’m just hoping the test doesn’t have too many tricky questions. Yeah, I’ve heard the teacher mentioned that it’s going to include some of the topics from the last few units. I’m not too worried about the science one, but the math test is going to be brutal. Oh, I know. I’ve been really bad at math. I’ve tried to do some practice questions, but I still get confused with the fractions. I wish we had a study group or something. Maybe we could form one? I mean, if we both need help, maybe we can work together. We could even meet up after school to go over some problems. That sounds like a good idea. I’d like that. I’ll ask my brother if he’s up for it too. He’s been struggling with math as well. Great, I’ll do the same. I think it’s better to study with someone else. It’s easier to understand things when you’re explaining them out loud. Yeah, I agree. I think we’re both going to need that. Maybe we can even start working on the math revision this weekend? Like, after the Christmas break? That’s a good plan. I’ll let you know. Speaking of Christmas, I was thinking of getting a plant for the house. I heard that some people have these little indoor plants that you can grow, like succulents or something. Oh, I’ve seen those! I think they’re really easy to look after. I’m trying to get a small one for my room.

Well, I was just thinking about the rat puppet we used to have when we were kids. It was this little thing, all fluffy and brown, and we used to make it dance around on the floor. I think it was a bit of a nightmare to keep clean, though. Oh yes, that was a mess! I remember we had to put it in a box and leave it in the shed for a week. I used to think it was one of those things that would just eat itself, you know, like a real rat. You're both being dramatic. It was just a puppet. I still have the bell from it, though. I used to ring it whenever we’d have a party and everyone would dance around like fools. It was a bit of a tradition, really. You're right, it was a bit of a tradition. I remember one time we had a handbell ringing contest, and we all tried to ring them at the same time. It sounded like a whole orchestra of clanging metal. Mrs. Hogg from the village used to laugh so hard she’d cry. I still get the occasional twinge from that day. I think she might have had a heart attack in the process. But it was fun. We were all just kids, weren’t we? And you know what? I still have a handbell. I’ve been trying to teach my granddaughters how to ring it properly. It’s not as easy as it looks. I remember when I first got my eyes tested. I thought I was going blind, but it turned out I just needed new glasses. Still, it was a bit of a shock when I saw the world all blurry and then suddenly everything was clear again. I had the same thing. I thought I was getting old, but it was just poor vision. I still can’t read the small print on the bus tickets, though. I always have to ask the conductor for help. That’s why I’ve started taking the bus more often. I find it’s easier than driving. I just sit back, read a book, and enjoy the view. It’s the same as when I used to travel on the train for business. Yeah, I remember when I used to travel on the bus all the time. You had to be careful with the timing, especially in the winter.

So, do you think we should go to the canals first or maybe the markets? I think the markets are a good start. It’s always nice to get a bit of local flavor before heading out to see the sights. Yeah, I like the idea. I heard there’s some really good seafood there. Oh, definitely. Venice is famous for its food. I love the cicchetti – those little bites you get with wine. It’s like a mini meal. That sounds amazing. Do you think we’ll be able to find a good place near the markets? I’m sure we will. There are so many places that serve traditional Venetian dishes. I remember when I first came here, I had this incredible risotto with shellfish. I think it was in a tiny little restaurant near Piazza San Marco. Wow, that sounds like a real local experience. I wonder if they still have places like that. I’m sure they do. It’s a place with a lot of history, and the food reflects that. You can’t really miss it. I’ve been reading up on Venice a bit before we came. It used to be a lot more industrial, right? Yeah, it was. There were lots of factories and shipyards back in the day. But now it’s more about tourism and culture. It’s kind of a mix of old and new. That’s interesting. I can imagine how it must have changed over the years. I mean, it’s still beautiful, but I guess it’s not the same as it was. Exactly. And the waterways were once part of a major trade route. Venice was a powerhouse in the maritime trade. The canals were used to transport goods, like spices and silk. That’s really cool. I can’t believe it used to be such a big hub. I wonder if people still use the canals for anything now. Not as much as before, but there are still boats that go through them, and some of the water taxis are pretty amazing. Plus, it’s all part of the charm. You can’t help but feel like you’re in a movie when you’re out there. I can see that. Maybe we should take a boat tour later. I’ve heard it’s one of the best ways to see the city. Definitely. I think we’ll do that.

So, do you still go to the gym? I haven’t seen you there for a while. Honestly, I haven’t. Life’s been so busy with work and everything. I just haven’t found the time. Not to mention, I’ve been feeling a bit low energy lately. That’s not good. You know, you should really take care of yourself. It’s not just about looking good, it’s about feeling good too. I know, I know. I just keep putting it off. I mean, I’ve got this new project at work that’s really taking up my time. It’s like I’m constantly running on a tightrope, and I’m starting to fall off. I get that. I’ve been trying to get back into the routine too, but it’s so hard to find the motivation. Especially with all the stress from work and trying to plan my future. Yeah, I can only imagine. When’s your next holiday plan? You always have the most amazing ones. Well, I was thinking about going to Spain for a few weeks. I’ve been saving up, and I’ve got this idea of staying in a little seaside town. Just to relax and not have to worry about anything. That sounds perfect. I could really use a break. Maybe I should start planning something like that too. But I don’t know, I’ve been so busy. It’s never too late. You could always take a short trip somewhere nearby. Like maybe the Lakes? I’ve heard they’re beautiful this time of year. The Lakes? I’ve always wanted to go there. I think I’ll start planning something smaller first. Maybe just a weekend trip to somewhere nearby. That’s a good idea. You don’t have to do it all at once. And besides, you deserve a break. Speaking of which, have you been out with friends lately? Not really. I’ve been so focused on work, I haven’t had time to catch up with anyone. I feel like I’ve been missing out on a lot of things. That’s not good. You should definitely make time for your friends. Maybe we can plan a night out soon? Like, you know, just to get out and have some fun. That sounds nice. I’d love to. When do you have free time?

I just heard about the spire falling down in Chichester Cathedral. That was a real shock. You know, I was there a few years back, and it looked so solid. I can't believe it's gone. Yes, it's a tragedy. I remember reading that it was due to some kind of structural weakness, and the architect they mentioned was Porden. I think he was involved with a few other buildings in the area too. Such a shame, really. It’s one of those places that should be preserved for generations. It’s funny how things come to an end like that. I was thinking about how you used to talk about France, and the different way they do things there. You said once that the bureaucracy there is more... eccentric. Oh, I was just exaggerating. But I did say that the French have a different take on property and land. They’re more relaxed, I suppose. I’ve been to some areas in France where people live in old houses, and they just let them run to a certain point. You wouldn’t see that in England. That’s true. But I guess it’s also about the history. You know, when I was in the library a few weeks ago, I saw a book about the Austrian battleship disaster. It was about a ship that sank off the coast, and the way the British Library keeps track of those kinds of events is fascinating. Yes, and I’m writing a book about all sorts of historical events. It’s a bit of a tough subject, but I find it so interesting. Some people don’t like it when I talk about the past, but I think history is important. You know, it gives us perspective on what’s happening now. I agree. It’s like a conversation between the past and the present. Speaking of which, have you heard about the local housing management issue? The new landlord just put up bollards around the area, and people are arguing about them. It’s causing a bit of a stir. Oh, I heard about that. I think it's about safety, but I always thought the bollards were unnecessary. I’ve had enough of people knocking into things. But I do think it's a bit over the top. You know, some of the problems in housing are real, and people are just trying to make sense of it.

So, did you guys hear about the new guy who joined our form? He's like, super into comics and stuff. Yeah, I saw him at break. He was drawing Spider-Man on a table. Was he in our class? No, I think he’s in the year above us. But he’s got this massive collection of Marvel comics. I’ve seen them in his bag. Oh, cool. I’ve been trying to get into comics, but I don’t know where to start. You should check out the shop near the library. They’ve got a section with all the new releases. My cousin’s into comics too. He’s got like, a thousand of them. His parents don’t even know what he does with them. I bet they’ve got a better collection than my dad. He’s got a few old ones, but he’s more into football than anything. My brother’s got a football shirt from every Premier League team. He’s got a whole wall of them. That’s insane. I’ve got one for Arsenal. I got it on sale at the market. You should come to the market with me one day. I’ve got a friend who’s got a stall with all sorts of random stuff—old comic books, vintage toys, even some old school games. That sounds cool. I could get a few comics from there. I’m thinking about getting a new comic. I’ve been reading  X-Men  and  Superman  a lot. You’re not into  Batman ? Not really. I think he’s too scary. Yeah, he’s got that whole secret identity thing. It’s complicated. I think he’s got more problems than the villains. Yeah, I guess. I mean, he’s got a lot to deal with. But he’s got cool gadgets. I saw one of the new issues where he uses this super-smart phone. That’s not real, is it? No, but it’s fun to imagine. I think it’s all about the stories. I like the fact that they have characters with real problems. Like, some of them are broken or have family issues. Yeah, like the X-Men. They’re all different, and they have to work together to save the world. That’s the best part. It’s not just about being a hero—it’s about being a real person.

Well, I think we've got to clear out a few things from the garage before Jonathan's birthday. It's getting a bit out of hand with all the old gadgets and stuff. Yeah, I was thinking the same thing. I’ve been meaning to sort through the storage unit in the loft. Got a lot of old books and trinkets that haven’t been touched in years. I could help with that if you want. I’ve got a bit of time since school started. It’s not like I have anything else to do. Besides, it’s a good way to get some exercise. That sounds like a plan. I was actually going to suggest clearing out some of the old tech that’s been gathering dust. I’ve got a few photo albums and things that I think could be useful for the family history project I’m working on. Oh, do you think it would be worth bringing out the old recipes? I still have some in a box under the stairs. I remember my mum used to bake those raspberry tarts that were to die for. Oh, yes! Those tarts were legendary. I still remember the smell as if it were yesterday. We should definitely bring them out. Maybe even make a batch for Jonathan’s birthday. He loves that kind of thing. I’d be happy to help with that. I’ve got some basic baking skills, though I’m not sure I’d be able to match your mum’s talent. But I can at least help with the mixing and the baking. That’s a great idea. Maybe we can also find some of the old photos and stories from the family. I bet there are some precious memories in there. I’m sure Jonathan would love to see them. I completely agree. There’s something special about family history. I think it’s important to preserve these things, especially with the way technology is changing so fast. You can’t just save everything on a drive, you know. It’s not the same as having a physical copy. Exactly. We should make sure that we don’t lose anything important. Even if it’s just a little bit of nostalgia, it’s worth preserving. I think we should also think about how we can go about organising the birthday. I know Jonathan likes to have a good time, so maybe we could plan something a bit different this year.

So, do you know what you're going to do for GCSEs? Honestly, I’m still trying to decide. I was thinking maybe do English, maths, and then something else... like maybe biology? Not sure yet. I thought you were going to do history? Yeah, I was, but I reckon it might not be the best idea. I’ve been thinking about jobs more recently. Like, what are we going to do after school? I don’t know. I’m just trying to get through the next year. Maybe I’ll do something like tech or something? I’ve heard it’s useful. Yeah, tech could be good. I’ve seen some YouTubers doing stuff with coding and stuff. You know, like the ones who make games or videos. It’s cool, isn’t it? Yeah, I guess. But I’m not sure if I want to be on YouTube. I mean, it’s kind of a dream, but I don’t know if I’d do it for a living. I know, it’s not like you can just start off and be rich. But some people do. Like, have you seen that guy who does the tech videos? His name’s David. He started off with just a camera and some gear. Yeah, I’ve seen him. He looks like he’s pretty successful. But I don’t know. I think I’d rather do something more stable, like maybe work in a shop or something. I get that. But being a shop worker isn’t really a dream, is it? I mean, I’m not even sure what I want to do. I know. It’s so hard to choose. I mean, even if you do the GCSEs, there’s still the whole A-level thing. Yeah, and then after that it’s university or something. I don’t even know if I want to go to university. I’m not sure either. I mean, I think I’d rather do something practical. Like, maybe work in a factory or something. That’s what I was thinking too. But I’ve heard that factories are closing down, so maybe not. Yeah, I heard that too. Maybe we’ll have to do something else. I think I’m going to talk to my dad about this. He works in a shop, so he might have some ideas. Yeah, maybe.

Well, I've been meaning to ask you, what’s the deal with all these birds in the garden? I swear, every time I go out, there’s more of them than last week. Oh, they’re just spreading out, you know. It’s the same with the foxes. Got a family of four, I reckon. They’ve been coming over to the compost heap more than usual. I don’t know, I’ve been seeing more of them in the village too. I think it’s because the trees are getting so big. Didn’t used to be like that. You could walk the whole street without even seeing a leaf. Maybe it’s the climate change? Or maybe it’s just the trees being planted more. I read somewhere that the bird population has gone up because of the increased green space and the warmer winters. Yeah, warmer winters, but then again, it’s been so wet this year. I’ve been in the garden more, planting some shrubs, and I swear the moles have been taking over. I’ve had to dig up three patches of lawn just to find them. Moles? I’ve had to put up with them for years. They’re a right nuisance. You can’t even walk without them turning up. I remember when we were kids, we used to try and catch them with a trap. Felt like we were trying to catch a whole army of them. I used to have a mole problem too. Spent a fortune on mole traps. I even tried the poison, but I think it made the whole garden smell like a marsh. It was disgusting. I’ve heard that the mole population has been increasing because of the type of soil we have here. It’s very rich and soft, so they dig easily. I’m not sure if that’s true, but it makes sense. Maybe we should talk to the local council about some kind of pest control. I don’t think they’d do anything about it. I tried once, years ago, when I was still working. Said something about a mole problem, and they just said, “Oh, it’s natural.” Not that it’s not, but it’s getting a bit too much. I remember when I was a kid, our grandfather used to say that if you had a mole in the garden, it meant good luck.

I don’t know, I just don’t think schools are what they used to be. You know, when I was a kid, we had to do all this stuff, and we had to learn things properly. Now, it’s all about making sure they have a good time and don’t get depressed or whatever. I agree with that, really. I mean, I’ve had kids in school, and I’ve seen how different it is now. They just don’t seem to have the same drive, or the same discipline. It’s all about the experience. That’s true, but I think part of it is also because the teachers don’t have the same standards anymore. When I was in school, the teachers were strict, and you had to work hard. Now, they’re more like friends, or mentors, and they don’t push the kids as hard. Yeah, I can see that. But I also think some of the problems in schools come from the way the system is set up, and the way the government funds it. It’s all about bureaucracy now, and not about education. I don’t disagree with that. But I think it’s also got to do with the parents. These days, parents are more involved, and they’re more vocal about what their kids are being taught. So school has to cater to them, not the kids. That’s a fair point. And then there’s the issue of homework and the workload. I think in the past, kids had to read books, do essays, and study a lot, but now it’s all about projects and group work. Some kids thrive in that environment, others are lost. I know a lad who’s just left school, and he had to do a project on “the impact of social media on young people.” He spent a week on it, and he didn’t even know what the topic was. He just copied and pasted stuff from the Internet. That’s not surprising, really. I mean, I think some of the teachers are as unprepared as the students. I’ve seen some of the teaching methods in recent years – it’s all about creating engagement through technology, but sometimes it doesn’t work. Yeah, and it’s not just about the teaching. There’s also the issue of resources. Some schools have amazing facilities, but others don’t have basic things like proper books or whiteboards.

I can't believe we've got snow again. It’s like we’re back in the 1980s or something. Yeah, it’s ridiculous. I was just walking to the uni and it was like walking through a Christmas fairytale. I mean, I'm glad it’s snowing because I was going to do some gardening today, but now I don’t know if I should even go out. You know what’s even worse? Trying to get the garden tools out. I tried to get the spade out of the shed and it was like frozen to the floor. That’s brutal. I had to dig out my car this morning. It was like trying to pull a tank out of the ground. You're not the only one. The whole area is up to its knees in snow. I saw a car stuck in the middle of the road earlier. That’s not even the worst part. I saw this massive group of people outside the local pub, all dressed up like they were going to a fancy dinner. You think they were going to a stag or hen party? Probably. I mean, they were all in suits and ties. It looked like they were trying to be fancy, but they were just stuck in the snow. Yeah, and the pub’s even closed. I mean, the guy had a whole kitchen lit up like a Christmas tree. Yeah, that was amazing. I mean, it’s not like we’re doing that, but at least we’ve got a decent heating system here. I know. Well, I've just made the stew, and I think it's decent enough. Oh, good, I was just about to say, I thought we'd be stuck with chips and beans again. Honestly, the stew is a bit on the thin side, isn't it? Yeah, I mean, it's not bad, but maybe next time you could add a bit more of the onion? Oh, I did add some, but maybe it just wasn't enough. Well, I suppose it was the time, the place, and the ingredients. I mean, we had this old tin of beans that had been in the cupboard for ages. Oh, those beans! I used to say they were a treasure. Let me think… I have that old tin of beans, and I’m sure the carrots are still in the fridge. And I’ve got a few of those tins of tomatoes from the shop the other day. Oh, and don’t forget the salt and pepper. Right. It’s not much, but it’s something. And maybe even a little bit of garlic? Yeah, why not? A touch of garlic can really bring it all together. I think I’m starting to get hungry just thinking about it. Me too. I can’t wait to try it. Alright, let’s start making some plans then.

I can't believe it's already dinner time. I thought we had another hour before the food would be ready. Yeah, I was just about to say the same. I feel like we’ve been sitting here forever. You know, I used to cook dinner for my family every night when I was younger. It was a ritual. I always thought it was important to have a proper meal together. Yeah, I remember when I was a kid, my mum used to make the best roast dinners. I still remember the smell of the roast potatoes and the gravy. It was like a feast. I used to cook too, back when I was working. Though I think I was more of a meat and two veg kind of guy. Probably because I was always tired after work. That sounds like a real working-class meal. I think that’s what a lot of people miss now. With everything being so fast-paced, people don’t even take the time to cook. My wife used to complain about that, you know. Anyway, let’s not get too nostalgic. The food’s nearly ready. I’m starving. Yeah, I’m not going to argue with that. I think it’s time we all take our seats. Let me just check the gravy. I don’t want it to be too runny. And I’ll make sure the roast is still warm. I don’t want it to be cold by the time we eat. And I’ll make sure the chips are crispy. Not soggy. That’s a must. I think the main thing is that we’re all here, together. That’s what matters, isn’t it? Definitely. Even if the food’s not perfect, we’re all in the same room, eating, and talking. That’s something. It’s a rare thing these days, isn’t it? To have a proper family dinner. I know. I think we should do this more often.

So, do you think we could bring some of these ideas to life? I mean, it’s not just about theory anymore—it’s about actually putting something out there that people would use. I agree, but we need to start small. I mean, you know how things can go wrong if you’re not careful. I remember when I tried to introduce a new lesson plan for my students last year. I thought it was brilliant, but they just didn’t get it. Yeah, I get that. But we’re not just talking about lesson plans. We’re talking about education as a whole. That sounds cool, but how would you even start? I mean, not everyone has the resources to create a full platform. What if we started with something more local? Like a pilot program with a few universities or colleges? That’s a good point. Maybe we could start with a small group of students and teachers who are open to experimenting. I’ve been thinking about using short, viral-style videos to teach concepts. It’s something that could go mainstream if done right. Oh, I’ve seen those videos—some of them are pretty effective, especially for younger audiences. But what about the older students? Are they even interested in that kind of content? That’s a good question. Maybe we could tailor the content more. Like, if it’s a science topic, we could use animations or real-life examples. For history, maybe a more narrative-driven approach. It’s about making it relatable. That makes sense. But the problem is, how do you get the universities on board? They’re always so risk-averse. I mean, even if we show them the potential, they might not be ready to try something new. I know. That’s why I was thinking about partnering with some start-up companies. You know, there are a bunch of ed-tech firms that are always looking for fresh ideas. If we could develop a prototype and show them the data, maybe they’d be interested in investing. That could work. But what about the actual content creation? If we go down that route, we’ll need people who can produce videos, design interactive modules, and manage the platform.

Hey, how’s your weekend going? I’ve been trying to get everything sorted for the Halloween party we’re hosting, but I’m feeling a bit overwhelmed. Oh, I know, I’ve been thinking about it too. I just got a call from the dentist. You know, that thing about the filling. She said they’re going to be doing a root canal on me next week. Oh no, are you sure it’s that bad? Alright then. I’ll think about it. Maybe we can go this weekend? Sounds good. And I’ll bring some hot chocolate. You know, to warm you up after the skating. You’re a gem, you know that?

So, do you know what’s up with the rugby match tomorrow? I heard it’s gonna be a big game. Yeah, I think it’s between Leeds and Manchester, or something like that. I’m not too sure. I swear, I’ve had more spiders in this house than in any other I’ve ever lived in. Oh, really? You must have a lot of cracks in the walls or something. Not exactly. I’ve got a pest control guy coming next week, but honestly, I don’t know what I’m going to do. I’ve got one in the kitchen today, and I’ve got one in the bathroom. Yikes. That’s not normal. I mean, I’ve seen mice in the garden, but not in the kitchen. I know, it’s just one of those things that happens when you’re in a flat. You think you’ve got everything sorted, and then suddenly, you’re dealing with a little invasion. I suppose I could just move, but I don’t really want to. This house is fine, just... not quite as clean as I’d like. I hear you. I had a bird in my flat once. A pigeon, actually. It thought the window was an open door and just flew in. It landed on the bed and started chirping like mad. A bird in the bed? That’s not something I’d ever imagine. I know, it was bizarre. I had to chase it out with a broom, and it just flew off like it was nothing. That’s not something I could ever do. I’d probably just panic and call someone. I know, but it’s funny when it happens. I’ve seen people online trying to catch birds with little nets and all. I think I’d rather deal with spiders and mice than a bird in the bed. I mean, if you’re not careful, you might end up with a whole flock. Oh, I don’t think so. Birds don’t really like humans that much. They’re more into the garden. Yeah, I guess so. But I still think I should get rid of the spiders.

So, do you know much about your family history? I’ve always been curious about my own, especially when it comes to the stories my mum used to tell me about her side of the family. Oh, I know plenty. My mum was a bit of a historian, really. She was always writing down things and telling stories about our ancestors. I think she was really proud of our family tree. Though I’ve only just started to piece it together myself. Oh, that sounds lovely. I wish my mum had done that. She passed away a few years ago, and I’ve been trying to get through her things, but it’s been so hard. She had this terrible illness, you know. It took a long time, and I never really got to say goodbye properly. I’m so sorry to hear that. I can’t imagine how difficult that must have been. My mum had a similar illness, and it was heartbreaking to watch. She was in and out of the hospital for months, and we never really knew if she’d make it. But she was strong, even in the end. Yeah, she was. I think that’s one of the reasons she loved talking about her family. She felt like she was passing on something important, a sense of who we are. I guess that’s why I’m trying to learn more now, even if it’s just through her old letters and photos. That’s a beautiful way to think about it. I’ve been going through some old letters my mum wrote to my dad, and they’re amazing. She always mentioned how important it was to know where you come from. I’m trying to make sure I don’t forget that. I agree. I’ve started trying to map out my own family tree. It’s not easy, though. Some of the records are missing, and it’s hard to track down some of the older relatives. I’ve been asking around, though. That sounds like a good start. If you ever need help, I’m more than happy to assist. My mum was always good at finding things, even when they were buried in the attic. I think I still have some of her old files in there. That would be great. I’d really appreciate that. I think it’s also a way to feel closer to her, even now.

You know, I just thought of something – do you remember that time we tried to set up the camping gear and ended up with a tent that looked like a hot air balloon? Oh yeah! That was a disaster. We were in the middle of nowhere, and the wind picked up so fast that it looked like we were about to take off. I swear, for a moment I thought we were gonna be floating away with that tent. I had to hold on to the pole like my life depended on it. Remember when the dog, Biscuit, ran into the tent and knocked over the whole thing? We were so tired from the hike, and now we were in a tent that looked like it was going to fly off. I still remember the look on his face when he came out, all muddy and confused, looking up at the sky like he’d just been to a party. Yeah, he looked like he’d had a wild night, but in reality, he was just trying to find his way back to us. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking – do you think it’s safe to leave the dog out while we go for a walk? I mean, it’s not like we’re in a city – there are birds, squirrels, and who knows what else out here. I know, but he’s used to the countryside. He’s pretty much been around dogs all his life. Plus, he’s got that big collar with the bell – it’s like a security system. Yeah, and I guess it’s better than leaving him in the car, where he can’t run around. But still, the idea of the dog running off and getting into something dangerous is always on my mind. I get it. I mean, I still have that fear of the unknown. You know, like when we first moved here. I used to worry about the power lines – how close they were to the house, how they looked like they could fall down at any moment. Oh, you were so paranoid about that. You thought the wires were going to reach out and grab us. I did! I go out of my way to check the wires every time I drive past. I even started calling them ‘snakes’ in my head. That’s funny. I guess we both have our little fears, even out here in the countryside.

So how did you find the class today? I know it’s your first time here. It was alright, I suppose. I’ve never done group workouts before, so it felt a bit overwhelming at first. But once we got into the rhythm, it was actually quite fun. That’s good to hear. I’ve been going regularly for a few months now – it’s a great way to stay active and meet people. You know, like that book you mentioned last week – the one about language learning. Oh, yes,  The Language Instinct  by Steven Pinker. It’s a fascinating read. I’ve been meaning to finish it, but I keep getting distracted by other things. I remember that one. It’s kind of a classic in the field, isn’t it? I think it’s a bit dense, though. I prefer something a bit more accessible. True, it’s quite academic. I’ve been reading a few books on coaching techniques lately too. I think it might help with how I approach my gym sessions – more structure, more focus. That’s a good idea. I’ve been experimenting with some different teaching methods in my classes lately. It’s all about making the learning experience more engaging. I can see how that would work. I’ve always been into education in general – even if it’s not in a traditional sense. I did a sixth form diploma back in the day, but I never thought I’d be managing a gym. That’s surprising? I mean, you’re good at it. You have a way of keeping people motivated. Thanks. I guess it’s the same kind of encouragement you give in teaching. You just have to know when to push and when to let people breathe. Exactly. And with the seasons changing, it’s a good time to be more active, isn’t it? The weather’s been a bit unpredictable, but the cooler days are making me want to get outside more. Definitely. I’ve been thinking about starting a running group – something to keep people motivated and social. That sounds like a great idea. Maybe we could collaborate on that? I’ve got a few students who are into fitness, too.

Right, right, well, I’ve been thinking about the way we’ve got the house set up. You know, with the grandparents coming to stay, we need to make sure everything’s in order. Yeah, I know, I’ve been meaning to ask — what’s the plan for the guest room? I mean, I guess it’s the spare room, but it’s not really been used for a while. That’s the one, isn’t it? The one with the dusty old bed and that weird lamp that doesn’t work. Didn’t your mum use that for her knitting? Oh, that’s the one! She used to knit all the time. I remember her sitting there with a cup of tea and a ball of wool, muttering to herself. It was like a little shrine. Exactly! And if we’re going to have the grandparents here, we need to make that room presentable. Maybe get a new lamp, some fresh sheets, and a little bit of colour. Yeah, and maybe even a mat or something, so it doesn’t feel so… I don’t know, institutional. You could put some photos on the wall. You know, ones of the family. That way it’ll feel more like home. And maybe some fresh flowers. I remember my mother saying that flowers make a place feel livelier. Though I don’t know if that’s true or just her way of justifying buying more bulbs. It might be both. Anyway, what about the kitchen? I think the fridge is a bit crowded. Yeah, there’s a lot of things in there. I was thinking maybe we should do a clear-out. Not too drastic, but just take out the stuff that’s gone off or no longer needed. That’s a good idea. I always say if you don’t use it, you shouldn’t keep it. And if you do keep it, it’ll just gather dust. Speaking of dust, I remember being a kid and always trying to find the dustbin behind the sofa. It took forever. You’re not the only one. That was one of the most frustrating things about growing up in this house – trying to find the bin in the middle of the living room. I think we should actually move it. Maybe outside? Or at least near the door. Yeah, that’s a good idea.

I can't believe we've got to drive all the way to Carlisle just to see this gig. I thought it was in Hexham or something. I know, I've been double-checking the venue on my phone all the way here. It says it's at the old railway station in Carlisle, which is a bit of a trek from here. But if it's a good gig, it's worth it. Yeah, but I don't like driving in the rain. My brain was going, "Are you kidding me?" It’s like the GPS is trying to play a joke on us. I remember when I used to drive a lot. Back when I was teaching, I used to take the kids on field trips. So, did you get the site visit done? Yeah, it was pretty good. We saw the old factory building in Bethnal Green—bit of a mess, but the bones are there. Sounds like a classic project. I’m more interested in good architecture and good coffee. And lunches. I mean, what’s the point of being an architect if you don’t get to enjoy the view from the café? Exactly. I think we’re both realising that life is about more than just design. It’s about the people around you, the little things. Like the way the light hits the window here, or the way the barista makes the best cappuccino in London. Yeah, and the silence between us.

So how did you get on with the friends last night? Did you have a good time? Yeah, it was good. Just a few friends over, we had a few drinks, chatted a bit, played some games. You know, if you ever want to try something together, I’m sure we could do it. Maybe even with some of the other girls from work. It could be fun. That sounds nice.

So, ANON, I heard you're applying for that media position. Are you really going for it? Yeah, I think I am. It’s a radio producer role at a local station, and it seems like a good fit. I think that shows I can handle the creative and editorial side of things. That sounds solid. But have you thought about what your cover letter might say? It’s important to make sure it’s tailored to the job. You can’t just send the same letter to everyone. Oh, I know. I’ve started drafting one, but I’m still working on it. I was thinking of asking about the station’s future plans and how they’d like to expand their content. It shows I’m not just chasing a job, but I want to be part of something bigger. That’s a great angle. You should also make sure your portfolio is up to date. If they ask to see your work, they need to see the best of what you can do. I’ve been going through my old projects and compiling them into a portfolio. It’s a bit time-consuming, but it’s worth it. You’re really on top of this.

So, do you think we're ready to actually take the plunge and start the business? I mean, we've been talking about it for so long. I think we are. I mean, we’ve got the skills, we’ve got the passion, and we’ve got this house-sitting gig in Australia to kind of test the waters. It’s like a little trial run. Yeah, and honestly, it’s been a great way to see how we’d handle being more independent. I mean, it’s not like we’re living off the grid or anything, but we’re managing on our own, like, without the security of a regular job. That’s got to count for something. It has. I’ve been thinking about how I left teaching, you know? I didn’t just walk away from it because I wanted to be an entrepreneur. I wanted to find something that really made me feel like I was using my strengths in a different way. And I get that. I mean, you were good at what you did, but I think you were always looking for something more, something that felt like it was really your own. And honestly, I’ve felt the same way for a while. I’ve been thinking about starting a small business that aligns with my interests — maybe something related to health and wellness, since I’m still in the field but looking to pivot. That’s interesting. I’ve been thinking about similar things too. Maybe we could even collaborate in some way? Like, you could focus on the health side, and I could handle the educational or training part. We could build a business that’s both practical and meaningful. That actually sounds like a solid plan. I mean, we’re both pretty good at problem-solving, and we’ve got a good understanding of what people are looking for these days. It’s not just about making money; it’s about creating something that adds value. Exactly. And I think we could start small. Maybe a subscription service for personalized health plans or something like that. You could handle the tech and data side, and I could handle the client interactions and training. Yeah, and with the location we’re in, Australia, maybe we could even expand a bit. There’s a lot of interest in holistic health down there.
