I just got a delivery from the local supermarket, and it was so heavy I had to put it in the hallway. I don’t know how they expect us to carry all this stuff with a toddler running around. Oh, I know the feeling. When I was teaching, I used to get deliveries of all the supplies, and I’d have to take them home on my bike. It was madness, but I’ve got used to it now. I remember when I was a publisher, we used to have delivery men come twice a week with boxes of books. I used to love that – it felt like a bit of excitement. Yeah, I guess it’s different now. I mean, you can order online, but you still have to carry it. And I’m not even sure if I’m getting the right things. Sometimes I just buy everything in one go, and then it’s all just sitting in the fridge or in the pantry. Mmm, food. Oh, don’t even start. I swear, if I had a penny for every time I’ve said, “I’ll just have a snack,” and then ended up eating the whole tin of biscuits, I’d be rich. Ha! I used to do that too, especially when I was teaching and had to eat lunch at my desk. I’d just grab whatever was on the table and eat it at my desk, even if it was someone else’s. You’d have to be a bit of a rebel to do that, though. I did once. I used to sneak in a few sweets at school, just to keep my spirits up. But the headmaster found out, and I had a week of detention. I’d have been more worried about the sweets than the detention, honestly. Speaking of diets, did you hear about the new school policy? They’re cutting down on processed foods and trying to get kids to eat more vegetables. Yeah, I think it’s a good idea, but I don’t know how they’re going to enforce it. You can’t exactly make a kid eat a vegetable if they don’t want to. It’s about awareness. If kids are taught how to cook and understand food groups, they might be more likely to make better choices. I suppose. But then again, I think those school shortages are making things harder.

So, do you remember that referendum we had a few years back? I still can’t get over how everyone was so divided about it. Oh, I remember! It was such a big deal. I think it was about EU membership, right? Some people were really passionate about it, and others just didn’t care at all. Yeah, and I remember my cousin Mark was completely on one side, and my aunt Jane was the other. It got so heated in our family. I swear, someone once said something so out of line that we nearly had a full-blown argument. Oh, I know! I think it was about the EU funding and how it affected local businesses. You know how some of the older folks were really worried about losing money if we left. I think my dad was on the pro-leave side, but he was very careful about how he expressed it. He was, yeah. He never openly said it, but he’d make comments about the government and how they were spending money. I think he thought he was being clever, but I just found it confusing. I get that. Anyway, what about that piano you were talking about last week? Have you managed to get it fixed yet? No, not yet. I’ve been meaning to, but I’ve been so swamped with work. I had a friend recommend a place in Birmingham, but I haven’t gone to see them yet. I’m dreading the thought of someone coming in and looking at it. It’s a bit of a hassle, isn’t it? I had a piano in my old flat, but I sold it when I moved out because it was taking up too much space. I used to play it sometimes when I was younger. It was a bit rusty, but it had that old-timey feel to it. That sounds nice. I always thought playing the piano was something that only people with a lot of money could do. But I think I’ve got the basics down. I just need to practice a little more. Yeah, but you know, it’s not about money. It’s about passion. I remember when I was at sixth form, there was this guy who played the piano every day in the common room. He was amazing. He used to play songs by The Beatles and Frank Sinatra, and everyone just loved it.

So, do you still use Twitter for work stuff, or have you given it up? Honestly, I’ve kind of given it up. It’s just too much noise. Yeah, I can see that. I still use it a bit, but more for personal stuff. I mean, it’s not like I’m an influencer or anything. No, but I think it’s useful for keeping in touch with colleagues, especially if you’re in a field like mine where you’re constantly publishing stuff. Yeah, but the problem is, you get so much irrelevant stuff. Like, I can’t even remember the last time I saw a tweet that wasn’t just about politics or something. Exactly. I’ve started using LinkedIn more for work, and maybe Instagram for the visual stuff. That’s a good point. I’ve actually been trying to use Instagram more. I’ve taken some photos of the farm, and it’s nice to share them with people. Yeah, that’s a good idea. I’ve got some photos of the crop fields I took last week. I’ve been meaning to post them. You should. People love seeing stuff like that. Plus, it’s a way to connect with other farmers or people in the same industry. I’m not sure if they’ll be interested, but I’ll give it a try. What about you? Do you have any cool work projects you’re excited about? I’ve got a new campaign coming up, something related to sustainability in the communications sector. It’s going to be a bit of a challenge, but I’m really excited about it. That sounds great. I hope it works out. You know, I think social media is becoming more and more important in that kind of work. Definitely. I’ve been reading a lot about how brands are using it to engage with their audience in more meaningful ways. I’ve heard about that too. It’s a bit of a double-edged sword, though. It can be really powerful, but it also has its downsides. Absolutely. That’s why I think it’s important to use it wisely. Yeah, I agree. I think we’ve both got a lot to learn about how to use these platforms effectively. For sure. Maybe we should start a group or something where we can share tips and ideas.

So, did you get any sleep last night? I woke up at like 2 a.m. and heard like...  shh ... you were talking in your sleep. Not sure what you were saying, but it was loud enough to wake me up. Oh, really? I was probably dreaming about work again. I’ve been having these recurring nightmares about patients running away or not responding to me. I swear I’m gonna start having nightmares about that  actual  guy who didn’t take his meds. Oh no, was that the one who tried to take his own life last week? I saw the story on the news. He was so emotional, like he was just trying to cope with everything. Yeah, that’s the one. I feel awful for him, but I can’t help but think, “What if this was me? What if I’d been in that situation?” It’s weird, isn’t it? I mean, I’ve been in mental health for years, and I still get scared thinking about how people can get to that point. I get it. I mean, I’ve had my own ups and downs, even if I’ve never been in the situation you’re in. But I can relate to the stress. I’ve been working crazy hours trying to pull off this project, and I feel like I’m barely keeping my head above water. I didn’t even get to sleep last night because I was stressing about the client meeting. That sounds rough. I know how that feels. I had a meeting earlier this week with a family that was really difficult. Their kid was in a really bad place, and they were blaming me for not doing enough. I felt like I was being judged for not being "the perfect mental health nurse." I can only imagine. You know, I think I need to take a step back. I’ve been so focused on work lately that I’ve completely neglected my social life. I’ve barely seen my friends, and I feel like I’m losing touch with who I am. That’s a good point. I’ve been in the same boat. I’ve been so busy that I haven’t even had time to go out with my friends, even though I really miss it. I think it’s time we started making plans to do something together.

So, do you think we've got everything ready for the brother’s visit? Honestly, I’m still not sure. I’ve got the spare room sorted, but I’m not sure about the food. Oh, I think we’re fine. The meal’s gonna be good. I’ve got a few things planned. Yeah, I’ve been thinking about it too. A bit of roast, maybe some roast potatoes, and a few vegetables. It’s gonna be a proper meal. That sounds good. But, I’m still worried about the voices. You know, the ones that keep coming through the walls. You mean the ones that have been going on for years? Yeah, the ones that started the day he left. I thought they’d die down, but they’re back again. I still can’t believe he left like that. Just walked out, no explanation, no warning. It’s been so long. I think we’ve all moved on, but it’s still hard. I mean, he was our brother. Yeah, I know. But still, there’s something about the house that feels... different when he’s not here. I can feel it too. It’s like there’s a sort of emptiness in the air. I think it’s the silence. He used to be in here all the time. Now it’s just us. I know. But what about the meal? I thought we’d have a proper weekend. Yeah, I was thinking we could make it a bit of a celebration. He’s coming back, after all. That would be nice. But I’m not sure if he’ll be in the mood for a celebration. Maybe not. But we can still make it special. What about the car? I hear you’ve got a new one. Yeah, I did. Got it last month. It’s a bit of a banger, but it’s reliable. That’s good. I was thinking about getting one too. But I’m not sure if I can afford it. I know. It’s a big decision. But what about the food? You could have the meal and then we could all take a drive. That sounds like a plan. I like that idea. I’m in. But I’m still not sure about the voices. I think they might be back again. Yeah, I think they might be.

I just can’t get my head around Spanish, Len. It’s like it’s got its own rules, and I keep making the same mistakes. You know how I tried to say  “¿Cómo estás?”  last week? I said  “¿Cómo estás?”  and the student just laughed. She said, “That’s English, love.” I didn’t know what to say. Oh, I remember that. You looked so confused. I mean, you've been learning for years, and you still get tripped up by the basics. It’s not just the grammar—it's the pronunciation too. You know, the  “th”  sounds in English are completely different in Spanish. You can’t just translate the words, you have to learn how they’re actually said. I know, I know, but it’s so frustrating. I tried using an app for a while, but it’s just flashcards and repetition. I mean, I can remember the words, but I can’t form a proper sentence, let alone have a conversation. I feel like I’m going around in circles. I get it, really I do. But maybe you should try something different. I read this article about people who learn languages by immersing themselves in the culture. Like, if you can’t learn it in a classroom, maybe you need to really  live  it. You know, maybe you could try watching Spanish movies or listening to Spanish music and just absorbing it. It’s not just about studying—it’s about exposure. That sounds good, but I don’t know where to start. I mean, I can’t even be bothered to watch a film in Spanish without subtitles. I feel like I’m at a complete loss. I remember the first time I went to Spain and tried ordering a coffee. I said “un café” and the barista just stared at me. I thought she didn’t understand me. Turns out, I said “un café” in the wrong accent. Oh, that’s the thing, isn’t it? You can know the words, but if you don’t speak it with the right rhythm or intonation, people won’t understand you. It’s like a different language altogether. I remember when I first went to Spain—my Spanish was so clumsy I thought I was being mocked. But now I can hold my own in conversation, even if it’s not perfect. Yeah, I guess I need to work on that.

Dad, do you remember how we used to do all this stuff on paper back in the day? I mean, you used to write everything down with a pen and a notepad. Oh yeah, I remember that well. Back then, you had to be careful not to lose your notes, or else you'd lose your mind. Now it's all just on the computer. Yeah, I guess that's true. But sometimes I miss the old way. You know, physically handling the paper, like it felt more real. Although, I do get that working with computers has its perks. You can just scan everything in a second. That’s the thing, though. You’ve got to be careful what you scan. I’ve lost count of the number of times I’ve scanned the wrong document and sent it off by accident. It’s like your brain can’t keep up with the digital age. I know what you mean. I once sent a scanned invoice to the wrong account by mistake. Took me hours to track it down and undo it. I still have nightmares about it. You’re not alone. I remember one time I sent a message to my bank by accident, and it ended up in the wrong account. I had to call up the bank and explain that I – I swear I was just trying to send a message to my sister, not the bank. That sounds like a disaster. I mean, we’ve all seen those viral videos of people accidentally sending money to the wrong person. I think it's a whole new kind of chaos. Yeah, it's a different world now. Even things like flights and bookings are all online now. You have to make sure you’re not booking the wrong flight or the wrong hotel. It’s like a game of chess with your bank account. I suppose it's a lot to take in, especially for someone who’s been used to doing things the old-fashioned way. I remember when the internet was just something you used to look up recipes or watch videos. You didn’t have to worry about banking or flights. You just cooked, and that was it. Yeah, I remember that too. My mum used to say something like, “You can’t cook a meal in the world without a recipe, and you can’t go anywhere without a map.”

I just saw a bunch of bikers pulling up at the petrol station. They looked like they were having a bit of a party. Yeah, I saw them too. I've seen those kinds of groups before—usually they're all dressed up, riding big bikes, and they have that whole ‘motorcycle club’ vibe. Yeah, but I always wonder if they're actually part of a gang or just a group of friends. Some of them look pretty friendly, but others... well, you can't really tell from a distance. I suppose it depends on the group. I’ve heard of some clubs being pretty harmless, just riders who like to socialize, while others have a more serious reputation. It’s hard to tell from a passing glance. I guess that’s the thing with bikers. They have this sort of mystique, like they’re all rebels or something. But I’ve never actually met one who was like that. I know, it’s kind of romanticized in pop culture. But in reality, most of them are just people who enjoy riding and being part of a community. I mean, don’t get me wrong, some of them can be pretty wild, but not all of them. True. I mean, I’ve seen some of those biker bars, and they’re just regular bars with a few bikes outside. It’s not like they’re all trying to cause trouble. Exactly. There’s also this whole thing about them being ‘freedom lovers’ or ‘rebel souls.’ I think that’s just another stereotype, though. I mean, I’ve got a friend who rides a bike, and he’s just a normal guy who likes to take the long way to work. Yeah, I guess you could say that. But I still think they’re a bit of a mystery. You know, like they’re always looking at you with those helmets on and all. It’s like they’re trying to hide something. Or maybe they’re just trying to look cool. I mean, if you’re going to ride a bike, you might as well dress the part. That’s probably it. Still, I can’t help but wonder what they’re up to. You know, sometimes I think they’re just looking for a little bit of fun in a world that’s too serious. I agree. It’s like they’re living their lives on their own terms, and that’s something I respect, even if I don’t fully understand it.

Alright, do you want some of these beans on toast? Yeah, thanks. Just a second, I’m trying to find my keys. You’re doing it wrong. You should’ve put them in the bowl by the door. Right, right, I’ll do that. Mum, can I have a word with you? Sure, sweetheart. It’s about tennis. I want to take up coaching. Coaching? You? Yeah, I’ve been thinking about it. I love the game and I’ve been practising a lot. That’s great. You’re really talented. I’m not surprised, he used to play every weekend when he was younger. Really? I didn’t know that. Yeah, he used to play with his dad. They used to have matches in the garden. It was a real thing. We’d have our own mini tournament. What did you play? I played a bit of everything. I tried singles, doubles, even some net play. He was always the one who made the most mistakes, but the most fun. Did you ever play professionally? No, but I did get a scholarship to a local club. That’s amazing. You were really good. It was a good time. I met a lot of people, and it kept me busy. So you think I should do it? I think you should. You’ve got the passion for it. Yeah, and if you’re serious, you could even start training kids. That’s a good idea. Just don’t forget to take it easy. You’re still a kid, and this is a big step. I know. But I’ve been thinking about it a lot. We’re proud of you, son. Yeah, we’re proud. Go for it. Thanks. I’ll start looking into it. You could even take some lessons to get started. Yeah, maybe. And don’t forget to eat your beans. I’m not forgetting that. I’m just thinking about tennis. Alright, let’s get back to cooking. Right, let’s get this meal on the table. On it. I’ll help. What’s for dessert? Just some chocolate cake. Yum, that’ll be perfect. Yeah, and if you finish your beans, you can have some cake. That’s a deal. Deal. Alright, let’s get this over with. Right, let’s get cooking. On it. Alright, let’s get this dinner sorted. Yeah, let’s get this meal on the table.

I don’t know, Mum, I think the turkey’s a bit dry. Well, it’s not my fault it’s been in the oven for three hours. You could have thrown it in earlier, Dad. I mean, it’s been like that since before we even sat down. It was the way you cooked it. You always do it wrong. Oh, come on, you lot, it’s Christmas. It’s supposed to be a bit of a mess. Yeah, but the napkins look like underpants. Yeah, I saw that. I thought someone had left a pair of trousers in the dishwasher. No, they’re just the white ones, aren’t they? Darcy’s got a habit of folding them like that. And don’t even get me started on the music. That’s not Christmas music, that’s a car wash. Oh, spare me, it’s just the usual. It’s been like that since I was a kid. You know, I heard that the Queen’s speech was on YouTube today. Yeah, I saw it. She looked really good. Yeah, I didn’t watch it, but I heard she said something about the NHS. Oh, she always does that. She’s been saying that for years. I’m just glad it’s not the same as last year. That was a disaster. Yeah, and you got stuck in the car because of the snow. I didn’t get stuck, I just had to take the detour. You know what I think? I think it’s all the snow. It’s just been like that all year. I heard that some of your friends in Florida are going to the beach this week. Yeah, I think they’re going to the Keys. That’s a long way to go just to sit in the sun. Well, it’s not like we can go there. We go to the park. Oh, don’t be so dramatic. It’s just a bit of snow. You can’t live in your house forever. I know, but it’s been like that for weeks. I just want to go to the shops and not have to drive through a snowstorm. You could go online. I mean, they’ve got everything now. Yeah, but I don’t trust the internet. It’s full of scams. You know what’s funny? My brother-in-law tried to make his own Christmas cake.

So, do you think we should go to the café tomorrow? I was thinking maybe we could meet up with Helen and talk about the job she’s applied for. Well, I think it’s a good idea, but I’m not sure if she’ll be able to come. She’s been really stressed lately with the interviews, and I don’t want to impose on her. Yeah, I get that. But if we invite her, she might feel obligated to come. You know how she is—she’s always trying to help out. But maybe we could just have a quiet dinner at home instead? That way, we don’t have to worry about anything. That could work, but I was hoping to get some advice from her. She’s got a lot of experience, and I feel like I’m stuck in this job. I don’t know if I want to stay or move on. I understand. I mean, I was in the same boat a few years ago. It’s hard, isn’t it? You’re always wondering if you’re making the right choices. Yeah, and it doesn’t help that the money’s not great. I mean, I’ve seen how much some of the others are earning, and it’s making me feel like I’m not moving forward. But at the same time, I’ve got my own business to manage, and I don’t want to be jumping from one thing to another. That’s true. I just feel like I’m not getting the recognition I deserve. I work really hard, but I don’t think my boss is seeing it. I mean, it’s not even like I’m underperforming—it’s just that I’m not being given the opportunities I need to grow. I hear you. Maybe you should start looking for something else. I mean, if you’re not happy, why stay? That’s what I said to my wife. She’s been thinking about a new business idea, and I’m trying to support her, even though it’s a risk. But you have to take that leap of faith at some point. I guess that’s the thing, isn’t it? You don’t know until you try. I just don’t want to make a mistake. I know my parents always said to be cautious, but I feel like I’m being held back.

I can't believe I've got this far with the transcription. I think I've got three pages done already. It's so weird, I feel like I'm in another world when I'm doing it. Yeah, I can imagine. I mean, you're basically like a detective, figuring out what the person was saying, especially if they're speaking really fast or have a funny accent. A bit, but I think the hardest part is when they're speaking over each other, or someone's got a cold and it's all muffled. It’s really frustrating. I know, it’s like trying to read a book with someone whispering in your ear. But I guess that’s part of the job, right? Yeah, I suppose so. You get used to it. I think I'll be done by the end of the day. That's good. I mean, you're working on this at home, right? So you can take your time. I have to do mine at the office, which is a bit more stressful, especially with the appraisal coming up next week. Oh, you’ve got an appraisal? That sounds intense. Yeah, it feels like it. I’m trying to prepare as much as I can, but I keep second-guessing myself. I mean, I know I’ve done a lot, but I’m worried I’m not doing enough. I get that. I think it’s normal to feel that way. You just have to remember you’re doing your best. I hope so. Anyway, enough about work. Let’s talk about something else. What are you making for supper? I thought I’d make some pizzas. I’ve got all the ingredients, and it’s a bit of a treat. That sounds nice. I’ve been thinking about getting some new Marks and Spencer food lately. I was at the store last week and there was a new range of healthy meals. Oh, really? I always go with the basics, but maybe I should try something different. I think they’ve got some good stuff. I even saw a recipe on the packaging about how to cook them properly. That’s a nice touch. I’ve always thought the M&S food was a bit basic, but maybe I’ve been wrong. Maybe so. I’ll have to check it out next time. Speaking of food, have you seen the new episode of  The Walking Dead ?

So, do you think we should go out tonight? I’ve got this new dress I bought online that I just can’t wait to wear. Oh, you’ve got that black dress with the little gold trim? That’s the one you said looks like it’s from a high-end boutique but only cost £40? Yeah, I saw it too. It’s not bad. But I don’t know if we should go out. I’ve got this big exam tomorrow and I’m just trying to stay focused. Didn’t you say you had a week off? You’re not even in class! Yeah, but I’ve still got a few assignments due next week, and I’m trying to get everything done before the holidays. I don’t want to mess it up. Honestly, I get it. But you’ve got to live a little, right? You can’t just sit at home all the time. Yeah, I’m with her. You can’t just cancel every night. It’s not like we’re not going to have a life after exams. I’ve got this new heels I bought too. They’re these silver ones with the platform. I’m dying to wear them out. Oh no, not again. You’ve had those heels for like a month now. I know, I know. But they’re so comfortable, and the way they look with the dress is just… perfect. Okay, okay, I’m in. But only if we don’t go too late. I’ve got to get up early for that exam. That’s the spirit! So, what’s the plan? Do we meet up somewhere or just go to that new bar near the station? I think the bar’s got a good vibe. They play all the indie bands, and the drinks are decent. Plus, I heard they’ve got a new cocktail menu. Sounds good. But we should probably get something to eat first. I’m not going to be able to enjoy the night if I’m starving. Right, right. I’ll get us some snacks. But I think we should also check out that new boutique that opened on the high street. I’ve heard the drinks there are amazing. Yeah, I’m in. I’ve been meaning to try it out. And if we don’t like it, we can always go to the bar instead.

So, do you ever think about what it would be like if we had lived in a different time? Like, say, the Victorian era or something? I think about it all the time, actually. I mean, can you imagine us in the 1800s? No phones, no internet—just letters, and we’d be writing to each other across the country. I’d probably be writing to you from the countryside, and you’d be in a big city, working in some sort of factory or something. I don’t know, it feels so far away. Yeah, but maybe it would’ve been better. I mean, the people back then were more connected in a way. They had a sense of community. You didn’t have this constant buzz of notifications and the pressure of keeping up with everything. That’s true, in a way. But then again, we have more freedom now. Like, we can travel, we can do anything. We’re not bound by the same rules or expectations. I guess that’s the thing with time, isn’t it? It changes everything. I sometimes wonder what it would’ve been like if I’d met you back then—if we’d been soulmates in a different era, like some kind of historical match. Oh, you’re such a romantic. I mean, imagine us as Victorian-era lovers, making love in candlelight, whispering sweet nothings in the dark. It’s all so dramatic. And you’d be the one with the dramatic flair, I think. You always are. I’d be the one looking at the clock, trying to make it through the night because I have to get up early for work the next day. You’re so much more grounded than me. I’d be the one imagining the lavish parties, the glamorous balls, the secret rendezvous. You’d just be waiting for me to finish my coffee. Exactly. I’d be the one saying, “Alright, love, you’ve had your fun. We need to get up and get ready for the day.” You always do that. But do you ever wonder what it would be like if we had lived in a time where people believed in soulmates? I mean, if you were a Victorian or a medieval person, you’d have no idea what a soulmate was, right? Maybe not. But I think people believed in something like that back then.

So how are you finding the new role, Sophie? I know you've been working as a civil servant for a few months now. It’s okay, I guess. I mean, it’s a stable job, and the hours are pretty flexible, which is a bonus. But honestly, I miss the variety of the previous job. I felt like I was just ticking boxes all the time. I can imagine. I’ve been in admin and HR for over ten years now, and while it’s not the most exciting, it’s predictable. You get used to the routine. But I do miss the days when we had more authority and could make real decisions. Yeah, I’ve been in sales for the past fifteen years, and I still get the same sense of pressure. I mean, the job itself is pretty high-pressure, but the people you work with make all the difference. I’m lucky enough to work with a great team. That’s true. People matter more than anything in any job, right? I mean, I still remember when I was starting out, I had this one manager who used to say, “You don’t need to be perfect to be great, just be consistent.” That’s a good one. I remember when I first started in admin, my boss used to say the same thing. She had this way of making even the most mundane tasks feel meaningful. You know what I found interesting when I was in sales is the way people talk about businesses. It’s always such a mix of enthusiasm and cynicism. Some people are out there trying to build something, and others are just here to make a living. I think it’s about perspective. I mean, I used to work in the education sector, and I always found that people there had a very different view of success. It was more about impact than profit. That’s an interesting point. I think that’s why I’ve always been drawn to the idea of small businesses. There’s something very personal about running your own place. You get to make decisions, you get to shape the culture, and you get to see the direct impact of your work. Exactly. And I think that’s what makes it so rewarding. I mean, every time I close a deal, or meet a client, I feel like I’ve made a difference.

So, do you know what’s happening with the new flat in town? I heard it's going to be like a proper student ghetto, but maybe it’s not so bad. I mean, it’s got a proper kitchen, right? Not like that tiny one we had last year. Yeah, I heard about that too. I think it’s the one near the main campus. But isn't that where all the weirdos from the drama department live? I mean, I’m not saying they’re not cool, but it’s just… different. I don’t know, I’d rather be in the old one, even if it’s a bit run down. Honestly, I think the new one is going to be the best bet. You know, you get used to the smell of takeaway, and the noise from the next door flat. I think it’s just about finding a place that works for you. Yeah, but I’m worried about the rent. I mean, the old one was already a bit of a struggle, and now the prices are going up again. It’s like the university just wants us to pay more and more every year. I know, it’s so frustrating. I still can’t believe they didn’t give us any financial support when we got into uni. I mean, we’re all just students, and none of us have jobs. It’s like we’re supposed to somehow afford everything ourselves. Oh, don’t get me wrong, I’m not someone who complains about money, but seriously, it’s a bit of a struggle. I mean, I had to work part-time in the café just to cover my rent. I had to miss a few lectures because I was too tired. That’s not fair. We’re all trying our best. Maybe they should at least give us some sort of stipend or something. Maybe we’re not just lazy, we’re just trying to get through uni. I agree. I think it’s a bit of a disgrace. I mean, we’re paying all that tuition, and then they just expect us to survive on minimum wage and hope we don’t break down. I think the university should be more supportive, honestly. I mean, I know it’s a tough time for them too, but we’re not asking for much.

So, do you think I should get a tattoo? I’ve been thinking about it for ages, but I don’t know what to get. Oh, you’ve been thinking about it for ages? I thought you were only just considering it. Yeah, it’s been like, what, a year? I mean, you’ve got a whole collection of ideas in your head, but you’ve never actually gone to get one. Oh, don’t be so dramatic. You’re just scared of the pain. No, it’s not just the pain. It’s more about what to choose. I don’t want something dumb, you know? Like, like that one guy who got a basketball logo on his arm. It’s just… generic. I know what you mean. I had a friend who got a giant “I love my dog” tattoo. He’s got a dog named Max, but no one really remembers the name. It’s just, you know, kind of pointless. Yeah, but I do like the idea of something that means something to you. Like, like a quote or something. Do you have something in mind? I was thinking maybe a little quote from one of my favorite books. Or maybe something related to my degree. I’m studying psychology, so maybe something about the brain or something? That could work. You know, if you want something that feels meaningful. But then again, if you’re not sure, maybe just go for something simple. Like a symbol or a small design. You don’t have to be too serious about it. I don’t know. I want it to be something that lasts. I mean, I’m not getting it for the sake of it. I want it to have some significance. Maybe something that represents my journey so far. That sounds like a good approach. I think it’s important to have something that you can look back on and say, “That meant something to me.” Maybe you could get something that’s related to your dog, too? I mean, he’s like your best friend. Yeah, I guess. But I don’t want it to be something too obvious. You could always do a combination. Like a small symbol that represents your studies and something related to your dog. Hmm, that does sound interesting. I never thought about combining them. But I need to think about where I’d put it.

Well, I've just got back from Cornwall, and I must say, it was a right old adventure. We did the YHA volunteering thing, and I’m telling you, it wasn’t all just walking around with a clipboard. No, I bet it was more than that. You’ve been out there all week, haven’t you? Yeah, I heard you had to help clean a lighthouse or something? That’s not exactly a relaxing job. It was, honestly. We had to climb up the lighthouse and clean the windows. It was a bit of a climb, but the view from the top was worth it. I could see the whole coast from there. It was like a painting. I bet it made you feel like you were part of something bigger. Yeah, in a way, it did. We were helping out with the volunteers, and it was good to be out in nature again after all that city life. I missed the sea. I suppose that’s why the YHA does it, to get people out into the countryside and give them a sense of purpose. You don’t get that much with just teaching all day, do you? Not really. But it was nice to meet some new people too – all sorts of ages, from young students to old folks like me. Some of them were really friendly. That’s the beauty of volunteering, isn’t it? It’s a way to meet people and give back. I’ve been thinking about doing something like that myself. Maybe with the cycle race? You should. I’m going to Yorkshire in a day next month, and I was thinking of doing a bit of cycling there. It’s the kind of thing that gets you out of your routine. That sounds like a good idea. You should do that. I found that the more I got out of the house, the better I felt. I even managed to take some photos of the coast and the lighthouse. I’ll show you when I get back. Oh, I’d love to see them. I’ve been meaning to take some photos of the local area too, you know, for the scrapbook. I’ve been collecting photos of the crabs lately – I think they’re a real gem in the estuary. Crabs? That’s interesting. I’ve always liked them, but I’ve never really thought about photographing them.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing I’ve learned since I started working in events? It’s that everyone has a different idea of what “good food” is. Some people want it fancy, others just want it quick. And honestly, sometimes the simplest thing is the best. Yeah, I mean, I’ve been eating the same thing every day for weeks now. Just beans on toast, a bit of cheese, and a can of baked beans. I’m not complaining, honestly. It’s easy, it’s cheap, and it’s got protein. But sometimes when I get home, I just feel like I’ve been living off of soup and toast for a month. That sounds rough. I mean, I know how hard it can be to cook when you’re constantly working, but you know what I do? I used to make a big batch of spaghetti and freeze it. Then I just reheat when I need it. It’s not gourmet, but it’s not a disaster either. Oh, I do that too. But the thing is, I’ve got to get it right, otherwise it’s just a waste of time. You know, it’s like planning an event. If you don’t get the details right, it’s just a mess. So I got into the habit of making a list of what I need, and then making sure I have everything. It’s actually kind of satisfying. That sounds like a good plan. I’m not sure I have the patience for that. I think I’m more of a “just throw it all together and hope for the best” kind of person. Although, honestly, being a labourer means I’m not exactly in the position to have a lot of time or money for cooking. Sometimes I just grab a sandwich from the café. Yeah, I can see that. But even if you’re not in a position to cook, you can still make things taste better. I mean, you can add some herbs, a bit of salt, maybe some olive oil. You don’t need to be a chef. We’re all just trying to survive, right? Exactly. And I think that’s what makes food such an important part of life. It’s not just about eating—it’s about connection. Like, when I was growing up in Doncaster, my mum would always make this big stew on Sunday nights.

So, did you have a good time in Barcelona? I heard you went there for the weekend. Oh, yeah, it was great! I had so much fun. I've always wanted to go there, and finally, I got the chance to. That’s awesome! I remember you talking about it for ages. Did you go with someone? Yeah, I went with my sister. She’s been wanting to go too, so it was a bit of a reunion. We stayed in a nice little apartment in the old town. It was so picturesque. That sounds like a dream. I’ve been thinking about going to Barcelona for the summer, actually. Maybe next year. You should! I mean, the weather is perfect, the food is amazing, and the culture is so rich. If you ever go, take me with you — I can show you all the best spots. Seriously, I’d love that. But first, maybe I should figure out where to go. Have you been to Paris yet? No, not yet. I’ve always wanted to, though. I think I’ll plan to go there next. It's such a different vibe from Barcelona—it's more romantic, I think. Definitely. I’ve seen a lot of pictures, and it looks incredible. I’ve been meaning to plan a trip for a while, but I haven’t quite got the time or the money yet. You don’t need to go alone. I can help plan it. We can start by looking up some places to stay and things to do. That would be great. I’ve been meaning to get out of the house more, but work’s been so insane lately. I’m so tired. I know what you mean. I’m still working a lot, but I try to take time for myself. Sometimes, it’s just about getting away for a few days, even if it’s just for a weekend. Yeah, I totally agree. I think the key is to not let work consume all of our time. We’ve got to take care of ourselves. Exactly. And besides, you deserve some time off. Maybe next month, go for a little get-away? Something close, like a day trip. I’d like that. Maybe a trip to the coast? I’ve been thinking about going to Brighton or somewhere like that. That sounds nice. I’ll ask around and see if we can find a place to stay.

So, do you live in London still? You sound like you're from there. Yeah, I do. I was born and raised in London. I’ve been there all my life, actually. But I travel a lot for work, so I’ve ended up spending time in places like Cyprus, Greece, and even a few times in New Zealand. Oh, really? I’ve always wanted to go to New Zealand. Such a beautiful place, right? It is. I’ve been there a few times for business meetings. It’s a bit of a culture shock at first, but once you get used to the weather, it’s amazing. I’d say it’s one of the best places I’ve ever been. I’d love to go. I’ve never been outside of the UK. Well, except for a few trips to France and Spain for holidays. That’s a start! You should definitely expand your horizons. I mean, I used to be a teacher, so I know how time-consuming it can be to get out, but it’s worth it. Yeah, I know. I’ve tried to do a bit of traveling, but I’ve always ended up working more than enjoying it. I’ve got a classroom full of kids to manage, and I’m barely getting any time off. I get that. I started off as an entrepreneur, so I had more freedom, but the business was always on my mind. It’s not like I had a steady salary, so I had to work really hard to keep things going. I guess that’s the difference between being in education and being in business. I mean, the stress is different. One’s more predictable, and the other is more… chaotic. Exactly. But it’s also more exciting, in a way. I’ve had some incredible experiences. For example, last year, I was in a small village in Denmark. It was during the winter, and there was this little festival that took place every year. Everyone was dressed up in traditional clothes, and there were these amazing lights and music. I’ve never seen anything like it. That sounds incredible! I’d love to go to a festival like that. It’s always nice to have a break from the everyday routine. You should. You know what your problem is? You’re too focused on the job.

So, do you think we should get rid of one of the housemates? Why? They haven’t done anything wrong. I know, but it’s just that we’re always fighting over the last slice of toast and the remote control. It’s getting a bit too much. I get that, but we’ve got to be careful. You know how they get when you start suggesting people should leave. I know, but it’s not just about the small stuff. It’s the way they talk to the others, like they think they’re better than everyone else. I’ve noticed that too. They always seem to have an opinion on everything, even when it’s not their place. Yeah, and then there’s the way they always say things like, “You’re not doing it right,” even when it’s not their fault. Honestly, I’m starting to think we need to have a proper talk with them. Maybe set some boundaries. I was thinking the same thing. Maybe we can all sit down and have a chat about how we want to live together. That sounds good. But I’m worried they might take it the wrong way. I know, but if we don’t do something, I don’t think we’ll be able to keep living like this. You’re right. We’ve got to make a decision soon. I’m not sure how much more of this I can take. Me either. I just hope we can find a way to make it work without hurting anyone’s feelings. Yeah, but if the situation doesn’t change, I’m not sure what else we can do. I know. It’s just that I feel like we’re always on edge. I feel the same. I think we need to take a step back and figure out what we really want from this place. Yeah, and maybe we can talk to the others too. Let them know how we feel. That sounds like a plan. Let’s do it soon, before things get worse. Agreed. I think it’s time we all started being honest with each other. Yeah, and if we do it together, maybe we can make it work. I hope so. I don’t want to be living like this anymore. Me neither. I’m ready for something different. Then let’s make it happen.

Well, I've just been to the supermarket, Elsie. I thought I'd get us some fresh vegetables and a few essentials. Oh, good, I was just about to say we need some more beans. I’ve had those cans for weeks now. I know, I know. I’ve been meaning to buy some new ones. But honestly, I’ve been trying to eat more fresh stuff lately. That’s good, you know. It’s better for you. Though I can’t say I’ve been keeping up with that myself. I suppose not. But I’ve been trying to keep my head down and not think too much about things. Being retired’s a bit strange, you know. Yes, I can imagine. You get used to the routine of work, and then all of a sudden, you’ve got all this time on your hands. It’s like being on holiday, but you’re not actually going anywhere. Exactly. And I think we’ve both got a bit of the wanderlust in us. Though I’m not sure we’d be as quick as we used to be. No, not at our age. Though I think we’re still okay. I’ve been walking with the dog almost every day, and it keeps me moving. That’s a good thing. I’ve been trying to do the same. It’s just that I get tired in the evenings. I know what you mean. I tend to feel like I’ve got a bit of aches and pains in my bones after walking. I do too. But it’s all part of the process, I suppose. You just have to accept it and make the best of it. Yeah, I guess that’s the way to look at it. Although, I can’t help but feel that I’m missing something. Like, I was always busy with work, and now I’m just waiting for something to happen. I think we all feel that way at some point. It’s just the way life is. You work hard for so long, and then it’s over, and you have to find a new routine. Maybe. But I think we’re doing alright, you know. We’ve got each other, and we’ve got the dogs. That’s something. That’s true. And I think we should be thankful for that. Yeah, we should be.

Well, I've just marked a whole pile of maths papers, and I can tell you, it's been a bit of a challenge with some of the kids these days. I mean, I've seen some of the answers, and I can't believe they're even in sixth form. Yeah, I know, Mrs. Wray. I've been helping out with some of the homework, and honestly, I feel like I'm learning more from them than they are from me. It’s like they're all pulling their own weights and not even noticing. Oh, don’t be so hard on the youth, lass. I remember when I was a student, and the teachers were always telling me to “draw a diagram.” I didn’t know what that meant half the time. And I was the one who ended up getting the top marks. Aye, and I remember when I was a lad, I couldn’t even spell “maths” properly. I used to write it as “mats” and get in trouble for it. But look at me now—retired, with a few spare hours on my hands, and still got that short attention span. Oh, you were always the one who would get distracted by the cricket match on the radio. I swear, half the time you were talking to the ball, not the teacher. Aye, and don’t get me started on the days I’d bring my own snacks to school. Pop tarts, crisps, and a Mars bar. I’d tell the teacher it was a “study snack,” and she’d give me a look like I’d just told her I was planning to rob the bank. I mean, I’m not trying to be the best student, but I do find it a bit strange that some of the questions are so complicated. I mean, if we’re talking about probability, how do you even know when to use a tree diagram or a Venn diagram? It’s like it’s a game of chance. Ah, but that’s the beauty of it, lad. It’s not about knowing what to use—it’s about knowing  why  you use it. Some of the best students are the ones who can explain it like it’s a simple thing, even when it’s not. That’s what I always said. It’s not just about getting the right answer—it’s about understanding your own learning process.

So, do you think we should be buying all these health products? I mean, I’ve been reading up on all this stuff about probiotics and stuff, and it’s like, how do you know what’s actually good for you? I mean, it’s a bit confusing, isn’t it? Like, there’s this one guy on the internet who claims he’s got the best supplement for everything. But I don’t know if he’s even a real doctor. Yeah, I think it’s just marketing. Like, the more you spend, the more you think you’re doing something useful. But honestly, I just take my vitamins. That’s it. I’ve been trying to get into fitness more, you know? Like, going to the gym, doing workouts, and all that. But I’ve been thinking about how expensive it all is, you know? Gym memberships, protein shakes, even the clothes you need. Yeah, I get that. I mean, I’ve got this app that tracks my fitness, but honestly, I just walk around the campus a lot. It’s not like I’m training for anything. I mean, walking is good though. It’s free, it’s easy, and it gives you a bit of a break from studying. I’ve been trying to walk more, but I’m not sure if it’s enough to count as real exercise. I heard that the university is getting a new gym. They’re building it in the new building, right? Maybe we should check it out. Yeah, I think they’ve got some premium equipment. I heard people are talking about it in the halls. But I’m not sure if the membership is worth it. Maybe we could all chip in and get a group membership? Like, pooling our money to pay for a shared membership. That way, it’s cheaper. That sounds like a good idea. But I don’t know if I’ll be able to go every day. I’m still getting used to the schedule. Yeah, I can see that. I’ve got a part-time job, so I’m not around all the time. But maybe we can go together on days when we’re free. Speaking of free stuff, I’ve been thinking about the fitness classes they offer on campus. There’s like yoga and pilates, and they’re free if you’re a student.

Alright, so I just thought, we need to make a shopping list for tomorrow, right? I’ve been thinking about what we need, and I’ve got a few ideas. Yeah, that's a good idea. I was just about to say that. We need to make sure we get everything we need for the week, especially with the weather turning. Hey, can we get some bread? I think we’re running low. Actually, I’d rather not get bread. I’ve been trying to cut down on carbs and keep things low GI. But I’d be fine with some whole grain. Okay, well I can put whole grain on the list. Also, I think we need some milk. We’ve been using up the last bottle. Right, milk. And I was thinking about getting some fresh fruits. Maybe some apples or bananas? They’re good for the kids and healthy. Yeah, I like bananas. I eat them every morning. They’re quick and easy. That’s a good point. I do like bananas too. But I’ve also been thinking about getting some nuts. They’re a great snack and good for the brain. Nuts, okay. I can put that on the list too. But wait, what about the insect bite? I got bitten earlier today, and it’s really itchy. Oh no, that’s not good. Did you get it from somewhere? Were you outside? Yeah, I was playing football with some mates in the park and got bitten by a wasp. It really stung. Was it a wasp or a bee? I mean, I’ve had a few bites from different insects, but I always make sure to treat them properly. I think it was a wasp. I don’t know what to do. I’ve got some antiseptic, but I’m worried about the swelling. Any ideas? You could try putting some ice on it. That always helps to reduce the swelling. Also, maybe a bit of hydrocortisone cream? Yeah, I’ve heard that works. I’ve got some of that at home. Should I put it on? If it’s not too bad, yeah. Just make sure it’s clean first, and then apply it. But if it’s really inflamed, I might need to see a doctor. I think you should be okay. I had a similar incident a few years back when I was camping.

So, do you know what’s up with Mrs. Thompson in Science? I swear she’s been acting weird all week. Yeah, I saw her on Instagram last night. She posted this picture of her cat with a physics equation on a whiteboard. It looked like she was trying to make it look smart, but it was just basic Newton’s laws. Oh man, she’s so into that whole ‘educational influencer’ thing. I mean, who even needs that? We’re just supposed to be learning, not making videos for likes. I know, right? I saw one of her videos where she tried to explain photosynthesis, but the audio was all muffled and she kept tripping over the plants. It was so awkward. And then there was the time she tried to do a TikTok dance during P.E. It was like she was trying to be cool, but she was so out of place. She ended up falling over and scraping her knee. Oh man, I laughed so hard. I think she still has a bruise there. But seriously, is it even fair that she gets so much attention for that? I mean, we’re all just kids trying to survive school. Yeah, and don’t even get me started on Mr. Green in P.E. He’s obsessed with fitness influencers. He keeps telling us to do workouts that look like they’re from some YouTube channel, but they’re way too hard. I tried one of his workouts last week. I thought it was going to be easy, but it was like doing a marathon in the middle of a crowded classroom. I ended up collapsing on the floor. I told you he’s not a real P.E. teacher. He’s just a fanboy. I mean, does he even know what the word ‘moderation’ means? He just wants us to be shredded like some Instagram model. Exactly! I think he’s trying to be trendy, but it’s not working. I mean, when he tried to do a yoga flow session, he just ended up falling into the gym equipment. It was like a slapstick comedy. I think we should start a group on Instagram where we post funny videos of our teachers doing stuff they’re not supposed to. Just to show them who’s in charge. That’s a great idea! I can start a hashtag like #TeacherFail or something.

I’m so stuffed up, I can’t even think straight. I think I’ve got a cold. You’ve been out all weekend, haven’t you? You’re probably just catching up with everyone. No, I didn’t even go out. I just sat in my room all day, watching TV and eating chips. That’s not good. You need to get out more. I know, I know. I just feel so awful. My head hurts, and my throat is like on fire. You should probably get some rest. Maybe even go to the doctor. I don’t think it’s that bad. I mean, I’ve had worse. Like that time I got food poisoning after eating at that kebab place in Manchester. Oh, I remember that. You spent three days in bed, practically crying over a bowl of soup. Yeah, and I still have nightmares about that. I keep thinking I’m going to wake up and find out I’m still in the kitchen, vomiting into a bin. I’ve seen you in the kitchen, by the way. You look like a ghost. I know. I feel like I’m been through a war, and I’ve just barely survived. It’s not just your appearance, though. You’re acting like you’ve seen a ghost. Oh, I have. I saw a ghost the other day. I was at the hospital, getting my vaccination. Oh no, did you get the flu shot? Yeah, I finally did. I was so scared, I kept thinking about Lloyd Grossman. Lloyd Grossman? Yeah, the guy from the 70s who used to guest star in all those terrible TV shows. He looked like a man who’d been through a war. I remember him. He used to talk about his time in the army. Always mentioned how he’d seen things no one should ever see. That’s exactly what I thought. I was like, “Okay, I’m getting my shot, but I don’t want to be in the same room as anyone who’s had a traumatic experience.” That’s a bit extreme, but I can see why you’d be nervous. I mean, you’ve never had a vaccination before. No, I’ve been avoiding them since I was a kid. I think I’m one of those people who just believes in natural immunity. That’s not very responsible.

I can't believe we've got a 70-point word in there. That's the highest I've ever seen in a game. It's not even the highest I've seen. I once had a 75-point word when I was playing with my brother. He used to make up words just to mess with me. Oh, I remember when I was your age, we used to play Scrabble with real letters and real boards. Back in the day, people took it seriously. Yes, and I still do. I think it's one of the best ways to keep the mind sharp, even at my age. I've been playing every Sunday for years. It's a good way to pass the time, especially when we're stuck in gridlock at the shopping centre. I was trying to get out of there earlier, but the traffic was a nightmare. I know, I was in the same situation. The butcher’s shop was packed, and we had to wait in line for over an hour. I almost gave up and went to the supermarket instead. Oh, I hear you. I went to the local market yesterday and got stuck in a queue for half an hour just to buy some bread. I was so frustrated. It's one of the downsides of living in a city like Manchester. You can't just walk into a shop and expect to get what you want without waiting. I know, but it's also one of the things that keeps us on our toes. We can’t just sit still and ignore the chaos. It's part of life here. Speaking of chaos, I've been trying to organise a family gathering for Christmas. I was talking to my cousin on Facebook the other day, and she said she'd be coming down from London. That's great. My sister is planning to come too. We’re going to have a big Christmas fair at the school. I think it's going to be the biggest one yet. I hope so. It's been a while since we’ve had a proper family gathering. I miss the old days when we all sat together, played Scrabble, and had a nice quiet meal. I know what you mean. I think it's important to take time out of our busy lives to enjoy the simple things—like a game of Scrabble and some good food.

So, do you know what it's like working in Germany, do you? Oh, it’s a bit of a culture shock, honestly. But I’ve been there a few times for exhibitions and it’s quite an experience. I can imagine. I used to run an antique gallery and had a few shows in Germany, actually. It was fascinating to see how people there appreciate craftsmanship. That must have been a great experience. I mean, I was in the printing business for a while. I designed and marketed printing systems for a few years. It was a different kind of creative work, but I loved the problem-solving aspect. That sounds amazing. I always thought working with machines and design was an interesting mix. It’s not just about the art, but the mechanics too. Exactly. I remember one time, we were setting up an exhibition in Berlin and there was this issue with the printing equipment. It was a bit of a nightmare, but we managed to fix it. It was the kind of thing that kept you on your toes. Oh, I’ve had my share of technical issues too. Once, I had a gallery that was set up in a municipal building, and the heating was so bad that the artwork started to warp. I had to deal with the council and the artists all at once. That must have been stressful. I suppose it’s part of the job, isn’t it? You have to be resourceful and flexible. Definitely. I think the best part of my job was working with people. I met so many interesting people through the gallery – collectors, artists, even some historians. I can relate. I found that working in exhibitions meant I was always meeting new people. Sometimes it was business, but other times it was just interesting conversations. I like that. It’s not just about the work itself, but the connections you make. Exactly. I think that’s what makes these kinds of jobs so rewarding, even if they can be a bit unpredictable. I couldn’t agree more. It’s all about the people, the stories, and the way the work evolves. Yeah, and even though I’m retired now, I still find myself thinking about the exhibitions and the systems I helped create. It’s all part of the legacy. That’s a great way to look at it.

Dad, do you remember when we learned about etymology in school? I still think it's so cool that words have such interesting origins. Oh, I remember! I used to love that. You know, some words come from Latin or Greek, and others from old English. It’s like figuring out a puzzle every time. Yeah, and I think it’s even more interesting when you learn how words change over time. Like, “lightning” used to be spelled “lytning” or something. It’s amazing how the language evolves. Definitely. And some words are just like that—people even make up new ones. I heard someone once say “quinoa” is the new “broccoli,” but I don’t get it. It’s not even that healthy. It’s more of a trendy thing, I think. But I do like the farmer’s market we’re going to in Cornwall. I heard they have a great selection of local produce, even some organic stuff. Yeah, the farmer’s market is a great idea—especially with the summer weather. We can get some fresh tomatoes and maybe even some freshly baked bread. I bet it’ll be a nice break from the car journey. Speaking of which, do you think we’ll see any lightning on the way? I read that there’s a storm system moving into the southwest of England. Maybe. If we’re lucky, we’ll be in Cornwall before the worst of it hits. But if not, we might have to stop at a service station. I remember once we had to pull over because of a lightning storm and got stuck for an hour. That sounds exciting, but also kinda scary. I don’t like storms much. I’m not really squeamish, but the idea of lightning hitting the car is worrying. I know, but we’re safe. The car is made for that. Although, I did read somewhere that organ donations are really important. I think it’s something I should consider. Yeah, I think it’s a good idea. Although, I’m not sure what to do if I ever get into a car accident. I mean, I know it’s not something you think about, but it’s still a possibility. I think you’ll be fine. You’re young, and you don’t have a lot of health issues. But if you ever feel like you want to make a decision, we can talk about it.

Alright, do you reckon we’ve got enough for three? I think we’ve got more than enough, honestly. Maybe even too much. Yeah, I’d say we’re doing well. Not sure if we’ve got enough for a proper meal though. Well, we can always eat more than one thing. I reckon we’ve got all the bases covered. Yeah, I mean, I’m not sure about the veg, though. We’ve got carrots and peas, but that’s it. Oh, I don’t mind that. I like my meals simple. A bit of meat, some veggies, and a bit of bread. That’s enough for me. I’m not sure about the meat, though. I think it’s been sitting in the fridge for a while. Yeah, I know, but it’s still good. It’s just been in there a bit, you know. You know what they say, though? If it’s been in the fridge, it’s still safe. Yeah, well, as long as it’s not off, it should be okay. I mean, I’m not going to eat it if it smells bad or looks weird. Yeah, that makes sense. But I think it’s fine. I’d say we’re better off eating it than throwing it away. That’s true. I mean, it’s not like we’re doing anything fancy with it. Just some basic cooking. Yeah, and we’ve got the potatoes and stuff. I think we’re doing okay. I’m just glad we’re all cooking together. It’s nice to be in the kitchen with people. Yeah, I think it’s better than being alone. Although I can’t wait for the weekend when we can go out and get something proper. Yeah, I know. I’m not sure how we’re going to afford it though. Oh, I don’t mind. I’m happy with what we’ve got. I think it’s good that we’re making an effort. It’s not every day you get to cook with friends, is it? Yeah, I agree. It’s nice to be together like this. Exactly. And it’s a good chance to catch up, too. I feel like I’ve been so busy lately, I haven’t had much time to see everyone. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s been a while since we all got together.

So, do you go to the gym often? Not really. I try to, but I’m too busy with work and studying. I’ve got a lot on my plate. Yeah, I can imagine. I work at the bar, so I’m usually on my feet all day. But I try to take some time to exercise. That’s good. I should take more time for myself. I’ve been feeling a bit run down lately. You should. It’s important. You know, I’ve been thinking about studying for a higher qualification. Maybe something in management? Oh, that’s interesting. I’ve been considering that too. I’m doing a postgraduate course in languages, but I’d like to broaden my skills. I think it’s a good idea. It could help with your career. You’re already a language teacher, so mastering management could open up more opportunities. Yeah, I guess so. I’ve always wanted to work in a more administrative role. I like the idea of being in charge of a team. It’s a bit of a step up, though. You have to be confident in your abilities. I know. But I’m not sure if I’m ready for that yet. I mean, I’m still getting used to my current job. That’s totally understandable. It’s better to take things step by step. What about your driving? You’ve been talking about getting a car, right? Yeah, I’m looking at buying a used car. I’ve been driving for a few years, but I’m not sure if I’m ready for the responsibility. It’s a big decision. I had to get my own car when I started working. It was tricky, but once you get the hang of it, it’s not so bad. I hope it goes as smoothly for me. I’m not a huge fan of driving in the city, though. I’m more of a country girl. I can see that. I love the countryside, but sometimes I miss the buzz of the city. Yeah, it’s a bit of a toss-up. But I think I’ll go for a car with good fuel efficiency. I don’t want to spend too much on petrol. Smart move. I’d go for something reliable too. You don’t want to be stuck in traffic with a broken-down car.

Right, right, we've got to get going, or we'll be late for break time! Oh, I know, I know. I just wanted to finish this cup of coffee. Well, you can't have it all, can you? We've got a lot on our hands today. Yeah, I know. But I've got that banner to put up outside the shop. And the donation box isn't even ready yet. That donation box! You said you'd have it done by midday, and now it's almost two. I’m sorry, I know, I know. I’ve been working on the plants in the greenhouse, and I’ve been helping the kids with the bell ringing. D’you know, I think I’ve seen a sign about Munchausen Syndrome on the internet. Munchausen Syndrome? That’s when someone fakes illness to get attention, isn’t it? Yeah, I think so. I read something about it once, but I can’t remember the full details. I think it's when someone intentionally makes themselves look sick, just to get care or sympathy. Oh no, that’s pretty serious, isn’t it? Yeah, it’s not just making up sickness, it’s actually making themselves ill. I read somewhere that they can even fake symptoms with drugs. That’s a bit of a dark topic, isn’t it? Yeah, but it’s surprising how much people can do in the name of attention. I mean, I’ve heard about people faking illnesses just to get out of work. Or to be the centre of attention. People do crazy things for validation, don’t they? I guess so. Anyway, let’s get back to the task at hand. Yeah, I owe you for waiting so long. We should’ve had that donation box up by now. I know, I know. Let’s just grab our coffee and set off. Oh, wait a second. I think I remember something about Gambia. Gambia? What about it? I think there were reports about some kind of charity drive or something. Yeah, I think it was about people donating to help with education in Gambia. That’s a good cause. We should support that. I was thinking of putting a banner up about it, maybe next to the donation box. That’s a good idea. We could make it a bit more eye-catching. Yeah, and maybe add a few plants as well.

So, do you guys ever just get bored of mobile apps? Like, I mean, I’ve downloaded so many, but honestly, half of them just sit there collecting dust. Yeah, I get that. I’ve got this app that’s supposed to help me track my fitness, but I only use it when I feel like I’m going to fail. And then it just sits there. I know what you mean. I downloaded this social media app for my job, but it’s just full of people posting nothing but pictures of their meals. It’s kind of annoying. Oh, I get that. I’ve been trying to get into this new app that helps you plan your day, but honestly, I’ve only used it twice. It’s just too complicated. I feel you. But then again, I can’t live without my Spotify and my grocery shopping app. Without those, I’d probably starve or drive in circles looking for music. Exactly! It’s like the apps we use now are the only way we function. I mean, I can’t even text without my phone. I tried to tell my brother that, but he said he’s been using a messaging app on his watch. So he doesn’t even need his phone. I’m not sure how that works. Doesn’t that get confusing? Like, you’re on your watch, and then you get a notification on your phone, and then you’re like, “Which one is real?” I think it’s just the future. Eventually, we’ll all be living in a world where we don’t even need phones at all. Oh, I hope not. I mean, I’m scared of what happens if I lose my phone. I barely know how to live without it. I tried cutting back once. I put my phone in a drawer for a week. First day was fine, second day, I was talking to my friend about a movie I saw, and I forgot what it was called. I had to Google it. That’s not even fair. We should all be more like you, though. I’ve been told I’m too dependent on my phone. My mum says I’m wasting my brain. I think she’s just worried. I mean, I’ve been told the same thing by my dad. But honestly, how else would we know where to go, or what to eat, or even how to say “hello” to people?

I don’t know, I just can’t get my head around why we need so many different types of cars. It’s all so confusing. You’ve got these gadgets and switches and buttons, and I just don’t see the point. I know what you mean, Bob. I was in a car shop the other day, and the bloke was showing me all these different models. He said it’s all about personal preference, but I just wanted a reliable old Ford. Oh, you know what I think? I think the problem is that people just want to show off. You see these cars, they’re all shiny and new, but I’d rather have a decent second-hand one that works properly. My son used to drive one of those big SUVs, and it cost him a fortune in petrol. Yeah, I remember that. It used to cost me a fortune to get my old van fixed up. I mean, I didn’t need all that fancy stuff. Just a bit of engine oil and a spare wheel was enough. I suppose it’s the same with everything, isn’t it? I mean, we all want the latest and greatest, even if we don’t need it. I tried getting a new phone last year, and I swear it cost more than my car. And it’s not just phones. I mean, even the way we drive has changed. You know, all these GPS things and sat-navs and whatnot. I still prefer just looking at the road and knowing where I’m going. I had to get a GPS in my van a couple of years ago because I kept getting lost. It was a bit of a pain, to be honest. I mean, the first time I used it, I ended up going the wrong way for three miles. Oh, I’ve heard that story. I think it’s because you’re relying on the machine too much. I prefer to drive it myself. If I don’t know the way, I just ask someone. Yeah, and that’s what I did. I used to drive to my son’s place in the village, and every time I got lost, I just stopped and asked a man in the shop. He always knew the way, and he’d give me directions in a very polite way.

So, do you think we should go through with the move, Sarah? I know it's been a while since we last talked about it, but I've been feeling like I need a change. I think it's a good idea, actually. I mean, the house is getting a bit too big for just the two of us, and with the job market the way it is, maybe it's time to downsize. Plus, Manchester’s got so much going on, right? Yeah, but it’s not just about the space. You know, the commute, the cost of living—it’s a lot to consider. I mean, I’ve been thinking about it myself, but only in terms of moving back to the Midlands, not Manchester. There’s something about the air, the pace, the vibe, you know? Oh, I get that. It’s just that the M6 is so long, and I’ve spent so many years driving it for work. It’s not the same as when we used to drive through it on the weekends, just for fun. That’s true. I remember when we used to take the kids to the seaside in summer and drive all the way through. It felt like an adventure. But now, it’s just another part of the daily grind. And the roads, they’ve changed so much since we were kids. I mean, back then, you could just zip through the countryside and not hit a single traffic jam. Now, even on the motorway, it’s like a maze. I know. And with all the new developments going on, I wonder if it’s even safe to drive through some of those areas anymore. I’ve heard stories about accidents and all that. Yeah, but I think it’s more about the mindset. You learn to adapt. I mean, even as a transcriber, I’ve had to adjust to new software, new systems, new ways of working. It’s the same with driving. It’s just different. I guess that’s the thing. You have to stay flexible. Even though I’m not working anymore, I keep up with what’s happening in the world. I mean, I still follow the news, I still read up on technology, and I even tried to learn a bit of Python for fun. That’s admirable. I mean, with all the changes in the world, it’s easy to feel like you’re falling behind, but I think it’s those kinds of adjustments that keep you moving forward.

Mummy, I’m so upset! My bike was stolen! I was just outside the shop and when I came back, it was gone! I know, sweetheart. I know how upset you are. But don’t worry, I’ve spoken to the police and they’ve found it! Really? Where? I was so worried it was gone for good. They found it in the car park by the library. They said someone must have taken it and then left it there. It’s a bit of a mess, but it’s still there. Oh, thank goodness! But how did they find it? I thought it was gone for good. Well, the police have a system where they check bikes that are left unattended. They must have noticed it was unlocked and left there. I think it’s because of the stickers we put on the frame saying it’s registered. Oh, right! You put those stickers on it for me. I remember you told me to do it so if it got stolen, they’d know it was registered. Exactly. That’s why I’m so glad you listened. It made it easier for them to find. I’ve also spoken to the shop, and they’re going to help us get it back – but we have to take it down ourselves. But I don’t want to take it down! What if someone else takes it again? I know, honey, but someone has to. We’ll go together. It’s a bit of a hassle, but it’s better than losing it completely. Besides, you can still ride it again – just make sure it’s properly locked next time. I will! I won’t let it happen again. I promise. Good. I’m just so glad everything’s okay. You know, I remember when you first got your bike. You were so excited. I think you were about eight or nine. Yeah, I was! I used to ride it all the time. We used to go to the beach together. Yes, and we even took some pictures of you riding it. You were so proud. I think it’s good that you’ve grown up so much and still have that love for cycling. I love it. I just wish I had a new one, though. Well, you could always look into buying a new one, but I think this one is still in good condition.

I can't believe we've got all these train tracks done in such a short time. We're almost there. Yeah, it’s pretty impressive, isn’t it? I mean, we’ve managed to make it all the way to London, and we’ve only just started. I know, and now we’ve got to think about the next move. Should we try to get to Manchester or go back to Cardiff? I think Manchester is easier. The tracks there are a bit more straightforward. Plus, the scenery is nicer. Didn’t you say the trains there go through some hills? Yeah, I remember reading about that. But I'm still not sure about the route. My uncle used to work on the railways and he always said you have to be careful with the train dynamics. He once told me about a time when a train got stuck because of a signal problem. Oh, that sounds dangerous. What did they do then? Well, they had to wait until the signal was cleared. And I think they had to send someone to manually check the tracks. It was a really slow process. That must have been frustrating. I wonder how many people got delayed because of that. I bet it was a real hassle. I remember reading about a similar incident on the south coast. It was the middle of the day, and they had to stop all the trains for hours. It’s all part of the game, though. You can’t have everything perfect. It just goes to show how important it is to follow the rules and check the signals properly. That’s true. I mean, it’s about safety, right? I think we should take it easy today and just enjoy the game. We’ve got the whole weekend to explore. Yeah, let’s not rush. Let’s see if we can get to Manchester. I bet the food there is better too. I’ve heard they have some great fish and chips. Fish and chips? You’re not serious, are you? I mean, I know it’s a classic, but I’ve tried so many versions, and honestly, most of them are just average. That’s because you haven’t had the real deal. The ones in Manchester are different. The batter is thicker, and the chips are golden and crispy. Okay, you’ve convinced me.

So, do you think we should go for a drink after this? I’ve had enough of the board game and I feel like a proper pint is in order. Honestly, I think we both need one. This game’s been going on for ages, and I’m not even sure who won. It’s like we’re stuck in a loop. Yeah, I’m starting to think it’s a conspiracy. Somebody’s got to be rigging the dice, or at least the movement cards. Or maybe it’s just us. We’re both terrible at this game. I mean, I’ve played it a hundred times, and I still get confused about the rules. You’re not the only one. I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve had to look up the rules during the game. It’s like the game is written in a language from another planet. I know, right? I mean, the way the board is laid out, you’d think it was designed by someone who’s never actually played the game. Or maybe that’s just the point. Maybe it’s supposed to be challenging. Like, it’s meant to test your patience and your ability to remember obscure rules. But honestly, I’m not sure if I have the patience for it anymore. I’m with you on that. But I think it’s fun in its own way. It’s a good way to pass the time, especially on a rainy day like this. And besides, we’ve got to keep our minds sharp, right? Yeah, I guess. Although I still think we should be playing something more interesting. Maybe something like Catan or Risk? I mean, those games are more engaging. Oh, you’re just saying that because you always want to be the one who wins. Remember the last time we played Risk? You were so overconfident you ended up losing everything. Hey, that was a strategic mistake. But I think I learned my lesson. I’m not going to let my ego get in the way of a good game. Well, I suppose that’s the spirit. But if we play something like Catan, I’m not sure if we’ll be able to go for a drink afterwards. I think we’ll be too busy trying to build settlements and trade resources. That might be the case.

I can't believe we've actually made it to dinner without anyone burning the place down. I think the only thing that’s not on fire is the fridge. Oh, come on, you two. You’ve cooked before, haven’t you? Yes, but only when there’s no one else around to judge. And that’s a valid reason. Well, I’m here, so you’re going to have to be careful. I’ve had to change the bins twice already. You mean the recycling? No, I mean the kitchen bins. I found a wet towel in one of them. That’s not a wet towel, that’s a napkin I used to wrap the salmon. I thought it was going to be an easy fix. Yeah, well, if you’re going to cook salmon, you might want to cook it properly. I’m not sure I want to know what happened to the salmon. Let’s just say it looked more like a flaky, overcooked crayfish. Exactly. I mean, it’s not like we were aiming for that. Well, I’m not sure I want to eat anything that looks like a crayfish. Maybe we should just go for something simpler next time. Like pasta. That’s a good idea. I’ve got a half-used jar of pesto in the fridge. I thought you were supposed to be an administrator, not a chef. I’m not a chef, but I can make a decent pesto. Yeah, that’s the key. You don’t need to be a Michelin star chef. Just do the basics. And if you do the basics, the bins won’t end up full of wet towels and mystery meat. We’re not even halfway through the meal yet. I think I’ve already overcooked the chicken. Let’s just say this dinner is a work in progress. If you say so. I think we need to rethink our approach. Maybe we should have researched the recipes a bit more. Oh, I think we’ve done enough research. I’ve never seen so many burnt bits in a single kitchen. At least the wine is still good. Yeah, that’s the only thing that’s survived this disaster.
