Well, I suppose that’s the only thing that matters. Maybe we should start by just having a glass of wine and then ordering takeout. That could be an option.

So, do you think we’ll get stuck in traffic again today? I swear this route is always the same—basically the same amount of time as the last time. I think it’s a bit better today. Not sure why, but I felt like the traffic was lighter when I was driving earlier on my way to work. Maybe it’s just the time of day. Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I just wish that this road would ever be improved. I mean, it’s like it’s designed to make us all late for something. I hear you. I used to drive this route every day when I was working at the publishing house. I’d always tell myself that if I could just get through this stretch of road, I’d be home in time for dinner. But now I’ve got a smartphone and a podcast, I’m not even sure if I’d care about being late anymore. I mean, unless it’s something important. But honestly, I’d rather be late than stressed out. That’s a fair point. I think it’s the way we live now. Everything’s about being on time, but I’ve read some studies that suggest that being overly punctual can actually be a sign of anxiety. Maybe that’s just me being dramatic. No, I think you’re right. I mean, I’ve noticed that people in London are just so stressed about time. Like, if you don’t get to your destination exactly when you wanted to, it’s a crisis. It’s amazing how much we put pressure on ourselves, don’t you think? I remember being a student and trying to make it to every lecture on time, even if I was tired or hadn’t slept the night before. It was ridiculous. Yeah, I know what you mean. I mean, it’s not like we’re doing anything that’s that important. But somehow, we still act like we are. I think part of it is the culture. It’s just the way it is here. Exactly. And I think that’s why I’ve started to appreciate the slower pace of life a little more. I’ve been thinking about going back to France for a holiday. Just to get away from all the rush and the stress. France? That sounds great.

So, do you remember that time we tried to get a table at that restaurant in Blackpool during the summer? I think it was the one with the seaside view and the whole thing was just chaos. Oh yeah, that was a nightmare. I mean, we were there like an hour before the place even opened and we still didn’t get a seat. We were just standing around outside like, “Where’s the queue?” I remember! You were so desperate for a table you were basically pulling people’s arms to get in. I swear you looked like a member of the army with a clipboard. Oh come on, I was just trying to be proactive. I mean, we were in a fancy restaurant, right? You don’t just walk in and hope for the best. Yeah, and then when you finally got in, what happened? I think you got the smallest table ever. Like, it was just enough for us to sit and not touch each other. That’s right! And then the waiter came over and said, “I’m sorry, but we don’t serve alcohol.” Oh, the irony. You were all dressed up like you were going to a fancy dinner, and they told you to have a lemonade. You were so mad. You tried to negotiate. I think you actually asked the manager if you could just pay for the table and take it home. Silly. I did! And he looked at me like I was crazy. But I’m not the one who tried to order a steak and then got told it was all out because they were out of meat. That was  your  fault. Oh, I didn’t know steak was the main course. I thought it was just an appetizer. Yeah, that was the highlight of the day. You ordered a side of fries and a ‘steak’ and ended up with a vegetable medley. The waiter was trying to be helpful, but it was all so wrong. I remember you getting so upset. You even tried to sing “I’m a survivor” in the middle of the restaurant. It was the weirdest thing. I think you got a couple of people laughing, but the rest of them were just confused. It was a real moment, wasn’t it? I mean, it was like the worst holiday ever, but at least we had a story to tell.

So, do you know what’s the biggest difference between the way we used to camp in the ‘70s and how people do it now? It’s not just the gear, it’s the mindset. Back then, it was about survival, about pushing the limits. Now it's more about the experience, the meditation, the connection with nature. I suppose that’s true. I’ve been thinking a lot about that lately. My brother’s got this new obsession with solo winter camping. He says it’s not just about the cold; it’s about understanding yourself when you're completely cut off from the world. Yeah, I've heard that. I actually did a solo trip in the Cairngorms last winter. It was terrifying at first, but once you’re in the rhythm of it, you start to feel a kind of clarity you don’t get in the city. It’s like the mind gets quiet, doesn’t it? Absolutely. I remember one night in the Scottish Highlands, I was sitting by the fire, and the wind was howling like it was trying to get in. And for a moment, I just felt… I don’t know, smaller. But in a good way. Like everything else is so small, and you’re just part of this vast, ancient landscape. That must be the real benefit of it, the way it makes you feel so small but also so connected. I’ve always found that when I’m in nature, especially in the winter, there’s a kind of stillness that you can’t get anywhere else. It’s oddly therapeutic. It is. And the physicality of it—sleeping in a tent, cooking over a fire, dealing with the cold—it builds a kind of resilience. You can’t just switch off from the world like you can in a city. You have to be fully present. It’s like a kind of mindfulness, but with the added element of survival. Exactly. And it’s not just about the hardship. There’s beauty in it too. The way the snow falls, the way the light changes as the sun sets. It’s almost like you’re seeing the world through a different lens. Not just the physical world, but the emotional one as well. I can see that. I think it’s why some people get so drawn to it.

So, do you know what’s the best thing about being a consultant engineer? Honestly? I think it’s the freedom. You get to work on all sorts of projects, and you can choose where you want to be based. No one telling you what to do all the time. That sounds amazing. I mean, I get to work with words all day, but I don’t get that kind of flexibility. I know, but it’s not all roses. You have to be constantly on call, and sometimes you’re working through the night. But hey, you get the perks. I guess. I mean, I do get to work from home sometimes, which is a bonus. But I still feel like I’m not really working, you know? It’s more like I’m just managing a bunch of documents. Yeah, I can see that. I mean, I used to work in an office, and even though I had a desktop, I preferred being out in the field. It’s more stimulating. I don’t know, I think I’d struggle with that. Like, I’ve got this grief of not being able to leave the house sometimes. But I suppose if I had a better job, I’d be more motivated. I think it really depends on what you enjoy. If you don’t love what you do, even if you’re in a high-paying job, it’s not going to make you happy. Yeah, I guess that’s true. I mean, I like the work I do, but sometimes I feel like I’m just going through the motions. Maybe I need a change. You could always try something different. I mean, I used to be in a completely different field before I switched to engineering. It’s never too late to change your path. I guess so. I just feel like I’m not making the most of my time. Do you ever feel like that? All the time. Especially when I’m stuck in meetings all day. Sometimes I just want to go home and watch a film instead of going over the same project again. I get that. I love film. It’s one of the few things that makes me feel like I’m actually living. I don’t know, I just feel like I’m always behind. Maybe you’re just not getting enough out of life.

Alright, do you remember the story about the time we went to the seaside and the pier collapsed? Oh, I remember that! You were so scared when the waves came in and the whole thing started to fall apart. I thought we were going to be washed away! I was so nervous! I clung onto your hand the whole time. I didn’t even want to look at the water. I know, but it was a funny story in the end. We ended up getting ice cream and watching the sunset from the beach. Didn’t even get wet. Yeah, but I still don’t like the seaside. I’m more of a homebody. Well, you like stories, don’t you? I think it’s important to talk about things like that, even if they’re scary. It helps us remember and learn. I like stories too, but I also like to play games. I was trying to beat my brother on the PlayStation last night, but he’s always better than me. It’s okay, it’s not about winning. It’s about having fun. You know, I used to play with a typewriter when I was younger. It was so different from now. You had to type out whole stories and then wait for them to print. That sounds really old-fashioned. I mean, I don’t even know how to use a typewriter. I just use my laptop and Excel to make things. Excel? Oh, you’re using a computer then? I thought you were still playing with the old things. Well, I use it for school. My teacher says it’s important to learn how to use Excel for the future. I don’t get it, but I guess it’s part of growing up. I remember when I was your age, I used to read a lot of books. I even started writing my own stories. I used to dream about being a writer. Can I write a story too? I want to write about my robot that can fly. Of course you can! I think it’s amazing that you’re already thinking like that. Just like the Brownie Promise evening we had last month—when you all had to share a promise about being kind and helping others. I remember that. I promised to always help my brother with his homework. It felt like a big deal.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about all this junk mail we get. It’s like a never-ending stream, isn’t it? You’d think with all the technology now, we’d be able to filter it out better. But no, it just keeps piling up. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve got a drawer full of things I never wanted to receive. Though I suppose that’s just part of life, isn’t it? Still, I can’t help but feel a bit frustrated. Especially when it’s something like a catalog for a fruit farm or a garden centre. Oh, I’ve been looking into growing some herbs lately. I found this lovely little box of seeds that Myra gave me. I thought it might be fun to try growing some basil and thyme in the garden. But then I think, “What if it doesn’t work?” And then I think, “Well, at least I won’t be eating junk mail in the garden.” Haha, that’s a good one. I’ve got a bit of a passion for gardening myself, you know. I’ve got this little patch of land next to the house where I’ve tried to grow tomatoes and courgettes. It’s not the most successful, but it’s got a charm of its own. I suppose it’s all about the joy of trying, isn’t it? I remember when I was at university, we had this old professor who used to say, “If you’re not failing, you’re not trying.” He was a bit of a character, but he was right in a way. I’ve got a friend who’s into growing fruit, actually. He’s been trying to set up a small orchard. He said he’s got an old fruit farm in the family, but it’s been abandoned for years. He’s been talking about restoring it. I think it’s quite a lot of work, though. I can imagine. You know, I was thinking the other day about those deserted medieval villages we read about in history books. It’s strange how something so old can feel so abandoned. Do you think people ever really understand the history of their own land? I think it’s a shame, really. There’s so much history in places like Bradford. I wonder how many people even know about the old buildings that were once here.

I just got a new phone, actually. You know, the one with the camera that's supposed to take photos like a pro. Oh, nice. I’ve been meaning to upgrade mine. It’s been a while since I’ve had a decent one. I still have my old one. It’s been so long, I don’t even remember what it looks like anymore. I know what you mean. I got it last week, and I was so excited. I took a photo of the cat, and it looked like it was staring right at me. That’s the magic of modern phones, isn’t it? I still can’t get the autofocus right on my old one. I tried using the camera once to take a picture of my brother, and I think he turned around. I was so scared I dropped the phone. Oh no, really? That’s funny. I once tried taking a photo of my sister, and the flash went off so bright, she actually yelled at me. That’s the problem with flash. I think it’s better to just use natural light. It gives a much more realistic look. Yeah, I agree. I only use flash when it’s really dark, but I’ve had some weird photos. Once, I took a picture of my dog, and it looked like it was wearing sunglasses. That’s the worst. I think the phone just messed up the lighting. I had a similar experience with my kid. I took a photo of him at the park, and it looked like he had a halo. I about cried. That’s such a funny story. I think I need to start taking more photos. I’m tired of just taking selfies. Yeah, you should. I took a bunch of photos last weekend when we went to the countryside. I even took some of the birds. That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to take some travel photos. I think I’ll start with a trip to the countryside next week. That sounds like a great idea. I’ll come with you. I’ve always wanted to see the countryside. Perfect. We can take some photos, and maybe even go to a café. I’ve heard some amazing places there. Yeah, and maybe we could grab a coffee and take some pictures of the view. Sounds like a plan.

So, how’s the part-time job going? I know you said you were trying to get into programming full-time, but I haven’t heard much about it lately. It’s going okay, I guess. It’s not the most glamorous job, but it’s a start. I’m learning a lot, and I’m actually considering doing a full-time apprenticeship next year. But I’m also thinking about going back to university for a master’s degree in tech. I’m not sure yet. That sounds like a lot to juggle. You’ve got a part-time job, studying, and planning for the future. Are you managing it all? It’s a bit much, honestly. But I think I’m getting the hang of it. I’ve got this really good system for managing my time, and I’m not as stressed as I thought I’d be. Plus, the work is pretty flexible. I can do it late at night when I’m not in lectures. That’s great, you’re pretty organized. I mean, I’m still trying to figure out how to manage my own work-life balance. I’ve got this copywriting job, and it’s keeping me busy. Yeah, I can imagine. You work with a lot of clients, so it must be a bit of a rollercoaster. I mean, I’m used to the pressure of deadlines, but I don’t have the same level of responsibility as you. It’s not all that bad. I get a bit stressed when my clients are rushy, but I think I’m getting better at handling it. I mean, I’ve got some great tools now, like project management software and time-blocking, which help me stay on track. That’s exactly what I need. I’ve been thinking about getting a manager or something to help me out. But I guess that’s something for later. Right now, I’m just trying to keep up with the work and my studies. I think it’s important to take it one step at a time. We’re both in a phase of our lives where we’re learning a lot and growing a lot. It’s not easy, but it’s also really rewarding. Yeah, I couldn’t agree more. I think we’re both lucky to be in a position where we can choose our paths.

So, how’s the new gym membership working out for you? I know you’ve been trying to get into a routine. Honestly, it’s more of a struggle than I expected. I thought I’d be hitting the weights every day, but I keep getting distracted by work. And honestly, the gym’s not that far, but I’m just not motivated enough to go. You know, I’ve been thinking about starting something like that too. I’ve been trying to get into a better habit of exercise. I’ve even bought that fancy set of dumbbells, but I still haven’t used them properly. Oh, I saw you at the market last week. You were trying to carry that thing like it was a shopping bag. You’re going to need a bit more strength before you try lifting them, you know. Yeah, I know, but I’m trying. I mean, I’ve been working from home more, and I’m not getting the same level of movement as I used to. It’s been so long since I had a real job where I was on my feet all day. I can relate. I’ve been writing for so long that I’ve basically turned into a couch potato. But I’m trying to make a change. I’ve started walking to the local café every morning, even if it’s just for a coffee. It’s a small start, but it’s something. That’s a good idea. It’s all about building that habit. I think I’m going to try that too. Maybe start with a short walk each day. Also, I’ve been thinking about the housing market recently. I mean, with everything that’s going on, I’m worried about buying a house now. Yeah, I’ve been keeping an eye on the prices. I mean, they’ve gone up so much, it’s hard to figure out when the right time is. I was thinking about looking for something in the outskirts, where the prices are a bit more reasonable. I agree. I’ve been reading a few articles about property and how it’s doing. It’s a bit of a wild market. But I think if you’re patient, there will be a good opportunity. That’s what I was thinking too. But I also worry about the cost of living.

So, do you know what’s going on with the Budget? I’ve been trying to keep up with the news, but it’s all so confusing. Honestly, I’m not sure either. It feels like they’re always talking about the same thing—taxes, public spending, and then they just say “we’ll deal with it later.” It’s like they don’t actually know what they’re doing. Yeah, I guess that’s part of the problem. It’s all so political, and I can’t even tell if it’s good or bad for people like us. I mean, I’m not even sure if it’ll affect my job as a Corpus Administrator. I don’t think it will, honestly. The government tends to focus on big projects, like infrastructure or the NHS, and then forget about the everyday people like us. But I’m not sure how long that’ll last. That’s true. I remember reading something about the cost of living rising, especially with energy bills. It’s gotten so expensive, and I can’t even afford to buy the things I need without worrying about the budget. I know what you mean. My job as a civil engineer is pretty stable, but I’m still paying a lot in rent and bills. I swear, if the government didn’t have so many other priorities, they could actually help people like us. I guess that’s the thing with politics—everyone’s chasing their own goals, and the average person gets left behind. I’m just hoping that when I do get out of university, I can find a job that doesn’t make me feel like I’m just another number in a system that doesn’t care about me. That’s a fair point. I think what we really need is someone who actually listens to the people, not just the ones in power. But, honestly, I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I suppose you’re right. But hey, I’ve got a break coming up, and I was thinking about going to that musical in Cambridge. You want to come? Sure, why not? I could use a night out. It’s not like I’ve got anything better to do. Plus, it might help me forget about all the politics for a while. Perfect. Let’s check the times and see if we can get tickets.

So, do you reckon we've got enough paint to cover the back yard? I think we got just enough, but maybe we should have bought another tin. Yeah, but it was only £10 for the extra, and it's better to be safe than sorry. I know, but I didn’t want to waste money on something we might not need. Fair enough. I mean, it’s not like we’ve done this sort of thing before. Right. But honestly, I think the paint’s going to last a while. It’s a good quality. Yeah, and it’s got that nice, matte finish. I like that. I do too, but I still think the gutter’s the main thing we should be worrying about. It’s leaking again. Hmm, yeah. I noticed that when I was out in the garden the other day. It’s getting worse, isn’t it? I think it’s time we fixed it properly. Maybe I can get a friend round to help. That’d be good. I don’t fancy getting up on a ladder again. Mate, I know the feeling. I’ve had enough of that. It’s not just the ladder, it’s the risk. You don’t know what you might fall into. Exactly. And not to mention the mess. Yeah, and the gutters are getting clogged again with leaves and stuff. Right, so we’ve got to get that sorted. What do you think about the whole house development going on down the road? Honestly, it’s driving me mad. All that noise and the traffic. Yeah, I know. I mean, it’s a bit of a shame. It’s supposed to be a new housing project, right? Yeah, but I don’t think it’s been designed well. It’s all going to be a bit of a mess. I bet it’ll cost a fortune to maintain. I reckon it’ll be a nightmare. I mean, I can already picture the kids running around and the mess. Oh, I can’t wait. It’s just so frustrating. I mean, we’ve got the same problem here. You know what I mean. We’ve got to make sure we take care of our own place before we start worrying about the rest of the neighborhood. Yeah, that’s true. It’s not like we’re in a position to be making complaints or anything.

So, do you think we've got enough food for the whole trip? I know it's only a few days, but I’m not sure how much we’ll be eating. I mean, we’ve got that pasta and some instant ramen, and a few tins of beans. Yeah, I think we’re okay. But I’m starting to get a bit concerned about the cost. I mean, we’ve already spent a lot on the campervan, and now we’re seeing all these little shops along the way. It’s hard not to stop and pick up something, isn’t it? I know, I know. I keep telling myself we’ll just eat the same meals for a few days, but then I see these little bakeries and I just feel like I need to buy something. I mean, the thought of eating the same thing for five days is making me a bit anxious. Totally. I mean, I’ve got a friend who went on a similar trip last year, and she said she managed to eat the same meals for three days—just rice, eggs, and tomatoes. But she admitted it got boring after a while. I can imagine. I might just need to be more disciplined. But then again, I got a text from my brother this morning saying he’s coming to Tarnow tomorrow. He’s stopping by to say hi before he heads to Kraków. Should I make some extra food for him? Oh, that sounds great. He’s been trying to get a job teaching English in Kraków, so it’s good to have a friendly face there. But you know, I was thinking about the whole "clearing the clutter" thing. Do you think we’re doing it right? I mean, I’ve been trying to pack as little as possible, but I still feel like I’m bringing too much. I know exactly what you mean. I had a friend once who packed a suitcase the size of a fridge and then said he was going to Germany for a week. I told him he was just bringing along his own personal museum. Ha! That’s what I was thinking. I almost brought that set of books I got from my course—every single one of them. But I thought, if I end up losing one, it’ll be a disaster. So I left them behind.

So, do you think we’ll get there in time for the Hay Festival? I don’t think so. We’re already half an hour behind schedule because of the train strike. Yeah, and we’re not even halfway there yet. I wouldn’t be surprised if we end up missing the whole thing. But I thought the Hay Festival was on the weekend. It is, but this is just a stop on the way. We’re going to Preston to pick up some groceries, then head back. Oh, right. I thought you were going to go to the festival. I was, but now I’m not sure. I’ve got exams coming up, and I’m not sure I can take the time off. That’s understandable. But if you do, you’ve got to make sure you don’t miss it. I mean, it’s one of the biggest literary festivals in the country. You can’t miss that. Yeah, and you know how much your mum loves books. She’d be devastated if you missed it. I know. I’ve seen her bookshelves and I’ve read some of her favorites. She’s got that list of authors that she’s always wanted to meet. She’s even written her own little book about her childhood and the stories her grandparents told her. It’s not published, but it’s still pretty good. That’s right. She used to tell us stories every night when we were kids. She used to say that being able to tell a good story was one of the most important things about being human. Yeah, and she’s always saying that the Queen is the best person to ever be in the world. She’s got a real soft spot for the royal family. I think that’s because she grew up in Bolton, where the Queen used to come to give speeches. She always said it was the most exciting thing she’d ever seen. She did. And she still talks about how the whole town would turn out, and how the Queen would walk through the streets with her guards and the people would cheer. I can’t imagine that. I mean, I’ve only ever seen the Queen on TV. Yeah, but she’s still a big part of our lives. Even though she’s old, she’s still doing things like helping with the Commonwealth.

Well, I can't believe it's you, Elsie! I thought I was dreaming when I saw that car outside. You've been out of touch for ages, haven't you? Oh, it's been a long time, hasn't it? I've been busy with the school year, and then all the holidays, and then the exams... I just haven't had the chance to come up here. But I'm glad I did. Thirsk is lovely, isn't it? Yeah, it's nice. I like the shops here. The ones in the town centre. You can get everything you need, even if it's not the same as in Newcastle. Though I still miss the fish and chip shop down by the quay. Oh, you can get fish and chips here too, you know. I brought some from the local take-away last night. Though I do admit, they don't taste quite the same as the ones from home in Kendal. I miss the real thing. I know, I know. I miss the ones from Mum's kitchen, too. We used to have them every Sunday. But we’re not as young as we used to be, are we? Yeah, I guess not. I mean, I still feel like I’m in the middle of things, but sometimes it just feels like everything’s moving too fast. It’s hard to keep up with all the new gadgets and apps. I keep trying to learn how to use that new smartwatch my dad got me, but it's just too complicated. Oh, I remember when I used to struggle with that too. Back in the day, we had to make do with just watches and phones. Now it’s all smart, connected, and I can't tell if I’m being watched or not. I think I need to switch it off more often. You're not the only one. I've had to switch my phone to airplane mode every time I'm out with the kids. It's too distracting, you know? I think the kids are more distracted than I am. They’ve got more to worry about than we ever did. Yeah, I mean, you can't even walk down the street without someone trying to sell you something or get your number. It's crazy. But I guess it's just how the world is now.

So, do you think this laptop is going to work? I mean, I just got it, and it's already got a weird noise coming from the fan. Yeah, I saw that. It’s probably just the fan being a bit loud. But you can't really tell unless you’ve had one before. I had one like that once. My dad used to work with computers, and he told me that if the fan sounds like it's grinding, it’s probably going to die soon. Oh no, that’s not good. I was hoping this would last a while. I mean, I’m still trying to get used to the idea of not using my old laptop anymore. My old one was so slow, but it didn’t make that noise. Yeah, I know what you mean. My old laptop had a fan that would just whirr and whirr for hours. I used to hate it. But honestly, the new one’s way better, even if it’s a bit noisy. It’s not just the noise, though. I think it’s the screen. You can’t really see it properly in low light. Yeah, I noticed that. I was trying to watch some YouTube videos last night – like, those MMA clips you love – and it just looked flat. It’s not just the screen. You know what I hate about this? The keyboard. It’s all too sensitive. I accidentally hit the wrong key a few times, and it started typing random letters. I had a keyboard like that once. It was so annoying. I finally had to replace it. I mean, I didn’t even know it was broken, but it just kept typing letters I didn’t mean to. I’m thinking of getting a keyboard cover to protect it, like that thing you put over your keyboard when you’re typing on a laptop. That’s a good idea. Or maybe just use a stylus? I’ve seen people do that. Or you could always just use your phone. I mean, the screen’s not that bad, and you can even run some apps on it. Yeah, but I like using my laptop for work. I mean, I’m an artworker, so I need to be able to design stuff. That makes sense. I mean, you can’t really do those kinds of things on a phone.

So, do you think this place is going to be a success? I mean, it's brand new, and it's in a small town like Tarnow. I don’t know, it feels a bit risky. Honestly, I don’t know. It looks nice, but it’s not exactly the kind of place that draws a lot of people. I mean, it’s not like London or Manchester. You’ve got to think about the local market. Yeah, I suppose. But the owner said they’re going for a modern vibe and all that. I mean, the décor is really different from the old cafés around here. I can see why they wanted to make a statement. It’s true, it’s got that trendy feel. I like the lighting, the music – it’s not too loud, which is good. But I wonder if the locals will even come in. You know, when you’re in a place like this, people are used to the old ways. Change is hard, especially for them. I guess. But maybe that’s the point. Maybe they want to bring something new into the town. You know, it’s not like Tarnow doesn’t have its charm, but sometimes it feels like it’s stuck in the past. Definitely. I mean, I’ve been here a few times, and I’ve seen a lot of the same faces. Some of them are even the same people who’ve been coming here for decades. It feels like a place that’s forgotten about progress. That’s kind of sad, isn’t it? I mean, I think places like this should be evolving. But I guess it’s not just about the place. It’s about us too. I mean, we’re both in our mid-20s, and we are still trying to figure out who we are. Sometimes, I wonder if I’m even on the right path. I know what you mean. I used to think I had it all figured out. I was working as an English teacher, getting by, and then one day I just realized I wasn’t happy. I mean, I was earning enough, but I wasn’t feeling like I was growing. I think a lot of us are like that. We go through phases, right? Yeah, I think so. I mean, I’ve had my own ups and downs. Some days I feel like I’m on track, and then other days I just feel like I’m going in circles.

So, do you think we should go to the Dorset Steam Fair next weekend? I heard it’s a really big event and there are loads of things to do. I've heard about it, but I don’t think I’ve ever been. I think it's one of those things that’s good for families and people who like history. But I’d have to check if there's anything on that’s suitable for someone with a disability. I know that’s important for me to know before we go. Yeah, you're right. They do have some facilities for people with disabilities, but I think it’s always best to call ahead and confirm. I remember when we went to the fair last year, there was a special parking area and some ramps, but it got quite crowded. Still, I think it's worth the trip, especially for the steam engines and the local crafts. That sounds amazing. I've heard the engines are huge and very historic. I wonder if they have any activities for kids. My little brother would love it. Also, I might bring my cat, but I need to check if they allow pets. I don’t want to be the one who brings a cat and it gets sent away. Oh, I think they have a pet-friendly area. I remember reading somewhere that they allow small pets, but you have to keep them on a lead. Though, honestly, I think bringing a cat might be a bit too much for the fair. It's a big place, and someone might accidentally bump into the cat or trip over it. It's better to leave the cat at home. That’s true. But you know, if you really want to bring the cat, I think it's manageable. Just make sure it's in a carrier and keep an eye on it. Maybe even take a little break to let it stretch its legs. I remember when my stepdad brought his dog to the fair once, and it was okay as long as he wasn’t too far from it. I might have to do that. Also, I need to check the ticket prices. I’m not sure if we can get a family ticket or if we’ll have to buy individual ones. And I think there's a chance the property prices in Bournemouth might be going up again.

I just got a text from the estate agent saying we might have an offer on the house in Carlisle. We could be moving in a couple of months, if we don’t lose our heads. Oh, really? That’s great news, but are you sure you want to move? I mean, I know the place is nice, but with the weather being so unpredictable, it's easy to get stuck in a rut. Yeah, I mean, it’s been raining every day this week. I couldn’t even go out to play football. I just sat in the house with my tablet watching YouTube videos about how to build a treehouse. That’s not a bad idea. I’ve been thinking about writing a book about living with technology and nature. It’s a bit of a mix, but I think it could work. That’s an interesting angle. I’ve been thinking about starting a blog about moving house and the emotional journey that comes with it. People usually don’t talk about that, you know? That’s true. I’ve seen so many people move, and it’s always a mix of excitement and nerves. Like, one minute you’re excited about the new possibilities, and the next you’re worrying about everything going wrong. I’m more worried about the new school. I’ve got to start again, and I’ve never really liked change. I mean, I did have a teacher who made me feel like I could do anything, but that was a long time ago. Yeah, I remember that. I had a teacher who made me feel like I could write the next great novel. I still dream about that sometimes. But then again, I did get into university and became a writer. So maybe the dream did come true. Oh, you are such a dreamer, Dave. You should write a book about your life, like that series of books by that writer who passed away last year. I think they were called something like  The Traveler’s Tale . You know, I read that series when I was in school. It was so inspiring. I’ve been thinking about writing a book about my own life, but I’m not sure where to start. Yeah, go for it! Just write about your life, even if it’s not very exciting. I mean, I’m just a kid, but even I can write about my day.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to get really excited about birthdays, especially when they were on the same day as your brother or sister? Yeah, I remember when my birthday was on the same day as my brother’s. We would both get presents, and it was like we were two different people, but we were both excited about the same day. Yeah, I remember that too! My birthday was the same as my sister’s, and we used to get all the chocolate eggs and everything. It was like a mini festival. That’s right. I used to love Easter chocolate. I mean, I still do, but the real joy was when we were little and we could have all that chocolate without worrying about getting fat or anything. Now, I’m the one who has to watch what I eat. Haha, yeah, I can see that. I still love chocolate, but I’m more careful now. I think my mum’s always reminding me to eat healthy, even though I’m still a kid. It’s funny, isn’t it? Yeah, it is. I mean, we’re not even teenagers yet, and we’re already being told we need to eat better. I think we should be allowed to have some chocolate every now and then. It’s not like we’re adults. I know, but it’s not just about chocolate. It’s about the whole idea of growing up and learning to take care of yourself. I remember when my parents used to say that to me. They thought I was too young to understand, but now I see the wisdom in it. I think it’s also about responsibility. I mean, I’m starting to think about things like going to the dentist and getting my hearing tested. My mum says I should be getting my ears checked because I sometimes can’t hear things clearly. Oh, really? Is that true? Do you have trouble hearing? Not always, but sometimes. I think it’s because I wear earbuds all the time. I mean, I like listening to music, but maybe I’m not supposed to do that so much? My mum says that’s part of why I need a hearing test. That’s a good point. It’s not just about birthdays and chocolates anymore. It’s about growing up and taking care of yourself in different ways.

I can't believe it's been a year since we last saw each other. Time flies, doesn’t it? Yeah, it’s crazy how fast it’s gone. I was just thinking about that this morning—how we used to spend every weekend together, like it was normal. I know, it’s like we were practically glued to each other. Remember when we used to make this massive mess in the kitchen, trying to cook that weird fusion dish we both thought was genius? Oh, the time we tried to make Italian pasta with Korean ingredients? I still remember the look on my mum’s face when she walked in and saw the meatballs floating in a pool of soy sauce. And then you tried to explain it was a "modern fusion" and she just said, “You’re not cooking, you’re experimenting.” Exactly! And we both thought we were so clever. I still have that photo of us standing in front of the kitchen, looking like we’d just survived a food fight. Oh, I still have that on my phone. It’s one of my favourite memories. I miss those days, honestly. We had so much fun. I know, it’s just... life got in the way. Work, responsibilities, and then we both got busy with our own stuff. I feel like we’ve both changed so much in the past year. Yeah, and we’ve both moved on, in a way. I got promoted at work, which is great, but it’s also been stressful. I’m working longer hours, and I haven’t had time to myself like I used to. I hear you. I’ve been doing the same. I’m working in the hospital, and it’s really demanding. There’s not much time for anything else. I’m even starting to think about getting a part-time job to help with the bills. That sounds tough. I’m trying to save up for a deposit on my first flat. I’ve been working on it for months, but the market’s so competitive. I feel like I’m always playing catch-up. I know what you mean. My parents are trying to help, but they’re not exactly rolling in money themselves. They’re still paying off their mortgage from when they first moved into the house. It’s so frustrating, isn’t it?

So, do you remember that long cycle ride we used to take as kids? I think it was when we were about twelve or so, and we went all the way from Almondsbury to Exeter. It must’ve been like thirty miles or something. I still remember the hills — oh, the hills! Oh, yes, we did that one time. I think it was the year we got our first proper bikes with gears. It was a real test of endurance, wasn’t it? I was so tired by the end, I just collapsed on the side of the road when we got there. That’s nothing compared to what I used to do. I used to ride all the way from Manchester to Birmingham on a Saturday, just for fun. The only thing that made it bearable was the sense of freedom, and the occasional stop for a pint of beer. I remember one time, I even got a free breakfast at a local pub because I happened to be a dental surgeon — they thought I was some kind of local hero. Oh, that’s funny. I still remember when I was a dentist, the NHS used to give us these perks. You know, like free sailing holidays and lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon. Sounds like a proper job, doesn’t it? Oh, it must’ve been something, but I suppose they were trying to keep us happy and not too bored. Speaking of which, have you heard about the trip to Prague that we’re planning? Our friend said it’s a bargain this year — flights and hotels are really cheap. Oh yes, I saw that. It’s been a while since I’ve been to Europe. I’ve been meaning to go back to Prague for years. I used to love the architecture — those old buildings, the streets, everything just seems so alive there. I think the problem with getting to the theatres and exhibitions is that you always end up missing out because they’re fully booked. I tried booking a few weeks in advance, but by the time I got there, all the tickets were gone. It’s such a shame — I love live theatre. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to get into a couple of exhibitions this year, but the tickets are so expensive. I think the council should do something about it — give some kind of discount for local people, especially those of us who are retired.

So, do you think we could actually make this work? I mean, the idea of creating an educational platform focused on moving image case studies—like, real-life examples of how films, documentaries, and even short films are made—could be really useful for students and teachers alike. I think it’s a great idea. Especially with the way things are moving right now, people are more interested in visual learning. You’ve got all these online resources, but they’re not always structured or tailored to what educators need. If we could create case studies that tie into the curriculum, that would be a real gap in the market. Exactly! And I’ve been thinking about how to make it interactive. Maybe even add some virtual tours of film sets or behind-the-scenes footage. The more immersive the learning, the better the retention, right? Yeah, and we could use social media to promote it too. You know, Instagram and TikTok have a huge audience for educational content these days. It’s not just about the content, it’s about how we reach the people who need it. True, but we need to think about the learning materials as well. What about using open-source tools or free software for editing and creating content? That way, it’s accessible to more people, especially in schools where budgets are tight. That’s a smart point. And we could even offer some free resources to start with, then introduce a premium subscription model for more in-depth content. There’s a lot of potential there. I like that. It keeps the doors open for people who might not be able to afford a full subscription. But we need to make sure the content is high quality. We can’t just throw anything up there. It needs to be relevant and well-structured. Definitely. I know that when you’re teaching, it’s not just about the content, but how it connects to the lesson plan. If we can align our case studies with specific subjects—like media studies, history, or even science—we’ll be way more effective. Right, and we could include interactive quizzes or discussion prompts to encourage deeper thinking. Maybe even have a forum where teachers and students can share their thoughts and ideas. That sounds like a solid go-to-market strategy. But I think we need to start building a prototype.

I just thought of something, do you remember when we were at university and we had that group project on coastal erosion? It was so tedious, wasn’t it? Oh, I remember. We had to go out to the coast and measure the cliffs. It was freezing, and the wind was so strong, I couldn’t even keep my notebook open for more than a minute. Yeah, I remember that. You were so serious about it too. I think you even took a picture of the cliff with your camera and then tried to analyze the angle of the wave action. It was almost like you were a scientist. Well, I was. I mean, I had a passion for the sea back then. I still do, even though I don’t go out much anymore. I think I’d rather read about it than physically be in the cold. That’s true. I think we’re both more of the 'look at pictures and read about it' kind of people. Although, I will admit, I do miss the feeling of the wind on my face when I was out there. Yeah, it’s one of those things. You can’t really capture the real thing through a screen or a book, can you? You have to be there. I mean, I remember the first time I saw the sea, I was so overwhelmed. It was like the world had just opened up to me. That must have been a big moment. I think the first time I saw the sea was when I was on a family holiday in Cornwall. I was about seven, and I’d never seen anything so vast. It was like the sky had fallen into the ground, or something. That’s a nice way to put it. I think I had a similar experience. Maybe that’s why we both ended up in the same field. It’s like we’re drawn to the sea for some reason. Maybe it’s the way it connects us to the past. You know, all those stories about sailors, explorers, and the sea as a symbol of freedom and mystery. It’s like we’re always trying to find our own little piece of that. Exactly. And I think that’s why it’s such a good topic to go back to when we’re talking about our friends.

So, do you think the fashion trends this season are going to be more about comfort or more about statement pieces? I mean, I’ve been seeing a lot of athleisure lately, but I feel like people are also going back to more structured outfits. I think it’s a mix, honestly. Like, there’s this whole trend with oversized blazers and wide-leg trousers that are really making a comeback. But I also see people embracing more casual looks—like, you know, those chunky sneakers and oversized hoodies. It feels like comfort is still king, but with a twist. Yeah, I agree. I mean, I’ve been trying to dress more casually myself, especially since I’m always on my feet teaching. But I still want to look put-together. I think the key is finding a balance between comfort and style. Definitely. I’ve been experimenting with layering, like pairing a jacket with a blouse and jeans. It’s kind of like the 90s, but with a modern twist. But I also saw this article saying that sustainability is becoming a big part of fashion trends now—people are more conscious about what they’re buying and how it’s made. Oh, that’s interesting. I’ve been thinking about that too. I actually bought a few second-hand pieces last week, just to see how they fit into my wardrobe. It’s not just about looking good anymore, is it? It’s also about the impact we have on the environment. Completely. I think a lot of people are starting to realize that fast fashion isn’t sustainable. So, I guess it’s a good thing that more brands are starting to make eco-friendly clothes. But I still think the real change comes from the consumers. You have to be willing to support ethical brands and buy less, but better quality stuff. That’s true. I mean, I’ve been trying to do that too. I’m not sure if I’ve totally broken the habit of buying too many clothes, but I’m more conscious about what I buy. It’s funny, though—I feel like I’m always trying to catch up with the latest trends, even though I know it’s not sustainable. I think the pressure to keep up with trends is part of the problem. If everyone is chasing the same look, it’s hard not to feel like you’re falling behind.

Mummy, I just got back from the library, and I found this book that's like,  so  interesting. It's called  The Midnight Dress . Oh, really? That's a good one. I remember reading that when I was your age. Was it the one with the time travel? Yeah! It was like, the main character gets trapped in a dress that only works at midnight, and then she has to solve all these puzzles to get out. It was so weird but awesome. I loved that. Didn’t you get the sequel? Not yet. I think it’s still coming out. But I’m thinking of getting another book from the library. My friend Lucy said she liked  The Witcher  series. Do you know anything about that? Hmm, not too much, but I know it’s about a guy who can see spirits, right? He’s like a warrior with a sword. It’s a bit dark, but I think it’s good for older readers. Yeah, that sounds cooler than the dress thing. But I’d rather read something I can relate to. What about  Harry Potter ? I’ve seen the movies, but I want to read it now. Oh, that’s a classic. I got the series when I was your age, and I read them all in a month. You’ll love it. You know what I found funny? I used to read them out loud to my sister when I was in bed. She’d pretend she was Harry and I’d be Hermione. That’s so funny. I wish I had a sibling to do that with. Although, I have my friends. We do a thing where we each take turns reading aloud from books. It’s like a secret club. That sounds great. You should tell me more about it sometime. Anyway, I need to go check on the dinner. Did you finish your homework? Not yet, but I’m working on it. I just wanted to talk about books. It’s been so long since I’ve had a proper chat with you. I know, love. I’ve been so busy with work, but I’ve missed you. How was your day? It was okay. I had a photography class today. We were learning about lighting and shadows. I took some pictures of the park, and I think they turned out pretty good. That’s fantastic!

Well, I just popped round to see how you're doing, Fred. I heard you haven’t been sleeping much lately. Oh, I know, I know. I've been up most nights, just tossing and turning. I don’t know why—maybe it’s the new house. It’s got all this strange creaking in the walls, like something’s moving around in there. Aye, I know what you mean. I’ve had the same thing. It’s not like it’s a proper house, though. It’s more like a shabby shed with a roof. I’ve had to fix up the windows and the floorboards, and the walls are still wet in places. I’d say you’re lucky to have a house at all, Mavis. You know, I used to live in a council flat. It was worse than this. At least this place doesn’t leak. Yeah, I suppose so. But I still can’t get used to the fact that I have to do all this work myself. I used to give it all to the builders, and they’d do it properly. Now, it’s like I’ve got to be the boss of everything. You'd think with all the money we’ve got, we’d be able to afford a proper house, but no—now we’ve got this old flat in the middle of nowhere. I still can’t believe we didn’t get our original choice. Oh, don’t get me started. I tried to apply for that new housing scheme, but the forms were a nightmare. I couldn’t even fill in the address properly. It was like they wanted a postcode from nowhere. I know! I had to ask my daughter for help. She said the form was so confusing that even she couldn’t figure it out. Yeah, and the way they asked for things like “expected number of children” and “preferred type of garden” was just ridiculous. I don’t even have a garden. I just stick a shed in the back. Heh, I remember when I was your age, we had the best gardens. Still remember my gran’s house—she had the biggest garden in the street. You could see the whole of the town from her back door. I used to go there all the time when I was a kid. We’d play hide and seek in the garden and eat apples from the tree.

I've been thinking a lot lately, really. Yeah? What's on your mind? Well… I’ve been considering bringing my daughter from abroad to live here with me. Oh, really? That’s a big decision. Why now? I’ve been feeling a bit… lost lately. Retired, you know? The routine has gone. I miss having someone to talk to, someone to look after. I understand. It’s hard to adjust after a lifetime of work. But bringing your daughter here—what’s the reason? She’s been living in Canada for a while now, working, studying. But she’s been feeling unfulfilled. She said she’s not sure where she fits in anymore. I see. And you think bringing her here would help? I do. I know this place better, and I’ve got a routine, a structure. I thought maybe she could find some stability here. It’s a kind thing to want to help her. But have you talked to her about it? I have. She’s been hesitant. She’s worried about leaving her friends, about starting over. That’s understandable. I mean, moving from one country to another is no small thing. It’s not just about the place—it’s about the people, the culture, the sense of belonging. Exactly. And I don’t want to rush her into it. I just want to make sure she feels safe, and that this is something she wants. That’s the right approach. You’re not forcing her, you’re supporting her. I hope so. I also know that she’s been struggling with things—stress, loneliness, maybe some anxiety. I thought maybe being closer to family might help. It could. You know, I’ve seen how much support family can give, even from a distance. I know. And I’ve been thinking about how much I’ve missed her. It’s been years since she left. Then this could be a way to bring some of that closeness back. Maybe. But I also know how hard it is to start again. I’m not sure if I can be the kind of parent she needs. You are. You’ve always been there for her, even from a distance. And if she does come, you’ll be the one who helps her rebuild. I hope so. I just want what’s best for her, even if it means changing everything.

So, do you know what’s been on my mind all week? The Scottish referendum. I just can’t get it off my mind. I mean, I’m a bit conflicted, to be honest. On one hand, I support Scottish independence because I think Scotland has its own unique culture and identity. On the other hand, I can't ignore the economic implications. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about it too. I mean, I’ve got friends who are really passionate about it. Some of them even said they’re going to vote for independence. But then again, I can’t help but think about how it might affect the whole UK. It's such a big decision, isn’t it? Absolutely. I’ve also had a bit of a stressful week with a job interview. I was really nervous, but in the end, I think I did okay. It was for a teaching post, actually. You know, just like yours. Oh, you’re getting a teaching job? That’s great. I mean, I’m still at the same school, but I feel like I haven’t had a proper promotion in years. It’s frustrating to be in a position where you’re still in the same place, even though you’ve been here for ages. I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about my daughter a lot lately. She’s getting ready for her A-levels, and I’m trying to support her as much as I can. It feels like such a big step, doesn’t it? I remember when I was at her age, I was so focused on just getting through each day and being able to sleep at night. You know, I’ve been there. My son’s just finishing his GCSEs, and I can see the pressure he’s under. I’m trying to be as supportive as possible, but I also have to be realistic. Life doesn’t always go the way you expect, and that’s just part of the journey. Exactly. I think that’s what makes it so difficult. We all want the best for our kids, but we also have to accept that not everything is in our control. I guess the key is to be there for them, no matter what. I couldn’t agree more. I’ve been trying to work on my own schedule a bit more too.

So, do you think we've got all the bits for the mousetrap game? I was just checking the box, and I thought, “Where’s the spring?” I think we might be missing something. Let me check. No, I don’t see a spring. Maybe it’s in the box? Or maybe we’ve got the wrong one? I’m pretty sure we got the right one. My mate Alex had one of these when he was a kid. He said it was the most complicated thing he’d ever tried to build. He tried to make it look like a real mousetrap, but it just kept bouncing off the wall. Yeah, and he almost got himself caught in it. He was trying to set it up in the garden, and he tripped over the wire, and it went off. He screamed like he’d seen a ghost. Oh, I can just imagine that. I mean, I’ve seen enough YouTube videos to know that these things can be pretty dangerous if you’re not careful. I’d rather have one of those big, clunky ones with the metal rod that you pull. You know, the ones that actually work. These fancy ones just make a mess. Well, maybe we should just try it out. I mean, it’s not like we’re going to be eating mice or anything. It’s just for fun, right? Yeah, but I’m not sure about the safety. I mean, I heard about this guy in the US who tried to build one and ended up with a broken finger. He said it was because the spring snapped. That’s not funny. I mean, I’ve seen people get injured doing things far less dangerous than this. It’s just a matter of time. Speaking of which, have you heard about the US? I mean, I visited once, and I was amazed by how different it was. I mean, they don’t do things the same way we do here. Yeah, I went to New York for a conference a few years back. The whole thing was just nonstop energy. It was like being in a simulation. You couldn’t even get a quiet moment. And the kids? I mean, I’ve heard stories about American kids being so into technology. I remember reading that they have these apps where they can order food from anywhere and have it delivered in minutes.

I’m back! You’re back! How was the shopping trip? It was okay, honestly. I got a bit carried away, though. Oh no, did you spend too much? Not too much, but I bought a few things that I didn’t really need. Like what? Well, I got this new coat. It’s a bit of a splurge, but it’s really nice. What colour is it? Dark green. I thought it would look really smart with my new jeans. That sounds good. You’ve always had a good eye for clothes. Thanks, I think so. I also got a couple of scarves. Oh, you’re going to be the winter version of you then. Haha, yeah, I guess. I also got a couple of new dresses for the office. Oh, you’re getting more into the fashion game, aren’t you? I don’t know, maybe. I’ve always liked nice clothes, but I think I’ve been a little too practical lately. Well, I think you’ve been right to be practical, but it’s good to have a bit of fun with it. Yeah, I guess so. I also got a few pairs of boots. Boots? Cold weather is coming, isn’t it? Yeah, and I’m not going to be walking around in those old ones anymore. I’m getting a bit too old for that. Fair enough. I’ve been thinking about buying some new shoes too. My old ones are falling apart. Should I show you the new ones when I get them? Yeah, I’d love to see. I might have to take some inspiration from you. You know, I think I’ve been missing out on some of the fun stuff. Yeah, maybe it’s time to start having a bit more fun with your wardrobe. Maybe you’re right. I think I’ll try to be more adventurous next time. That sounds like a plan. I’ll be waiting to see your new look. Don’t hold your breath. I might still end up buying a few more things. That’s the spirit. You’re coming alive again, aren’t you? Maybe I am. I think I’ve been holding back a bit too long. Well, I’m glad to see you’re starting to enjoy it again. Thanks, I think I needed that. Anytime. Now, let’s just hope you don’t end up buying anything too expensive.

Well, did you see the rugby match last night? I think it was the best one we've had in a while. Yeah, I did. It was intense. I've been waiting for a proper rugby match since the summer. Did you enjoy it? Honestly, I didn’t get to watch it because I was putting my toddler to bed. But I heard it was really good. I’ve been meaning to start watching rugby again, but I just haven’t had the time. Oh, I watched it. I got up early just for it. The kids were all over the place, but I managed to catch the highlights. I thought it was a real heart-wrenching game. The way they came back from behind was something else. Yeah, I agree. I was really on the edge of my seat. Especially when they had that last-minute try. It was unreal. I still can’t believe they scored that. It was like a dream come true for the team. I think it was the best moment of the whole match. I was cheering so loud, I woke up my mum. She said I was shouting in my sleep. Haha, that sounds like me too. I’ve been so into it lately. I even started reading up on the players. I’m trying to learn more because I want to understand the game better. That’s great. You know, Oisin and I used to play rugby in school. We were on the same team. I still remember the way the field looked at night, especially when we had the lights out. It was like stargazing through the grass. Stargazing? I hadn’t thought about that. I used to do that with my dad when I was a kid. We’d go out to the fields and just lie back and watch the sky. It was so peaceful. That sounds nice. I’ve been trying to get my friends together to go stargazing. It’s something I’ve always wanted to do. You know, just to get away from the city for a bit. I’d love to do that with you. Maybe we can plan it when the weather’s better. I’ve been thinking about it a lot. It’s one of those things that’s on my list of things to do. You know, I’ve been meaning to plan a little trip with Oisin.

So, do you know what’s going on with your sister? I heard she’s got a baby now. Yeah, she did! It’s a boy, actually. He’s just over a month old. She’s absolutely obsessed with him. Wow, that’s so exciting! When did she tell you? Just last week. She wanted to keep it a surprise for longer, but she couldn’t hold it in. She said she’s been so tired all the time, and now she’s just... exhausted. I can imagine. I mean, I’ve been helping out with my cousin’s baby, and it’s not easy. Still, it’s amazing to see them grow. Yeah, it really is. I think she’s already planning on moving house, though. She said she’s got no room for a baby and she’s been thinking about it for a while. Oh, really? I heard the housing market’s been pretty tough in London. Are they thinking of moving to somewhere more... family-friendly? Yeah, she’s seriously considering moving back to Lincoln. She said she loves the countryside, and she wants to be closer to her parents. Plus, she feels like she needs more space. That makes sense. I mean, having a baby is a big change. It’s not just about the space, though—it’s about the whole lifestyle. Exactly. She also mentioned that she’s been trying to get a part-time job to help with expenses, but she’s not sure what she wants to do. Any ideas? Maybe something in the language sector? I mean, she’s got a degree in linguistics, and she’s really into language learning. Maybe she could teach or work with kids? That’s a good point. She’s also been thinking about learning Spanish. She said she wants to be able to speak it with her baby when he’s older. That’s sweet. I think it’s a great way to bond. And if she’s moving back to Lincoln, maybe she can do some language exchange with the local community. Yeah, I’ll mention that. She’s always been into learning languages. She even used to teach French at the language café in the town. Oh, right! I remember you telling me about that. She was really passionate about it. I think those kinds of skills could help her find work more easily.

So, do you reckon people actually notice the difference in accents in this part of Bedford? I mean, I've heard some people say that the Bedford accent is pretty distinct, but I can't tell if I'm just being too sensitive. I think it's more about how you pronounce certain words. Like, if you say "bath" instead of "bat" or something. But honestly, most people here just speak in a pretty standard English way. I don’t think we're that different from anywhere else in England. Yeah, but you can still tell the difference. I mean, I grew up in Luton, and I still hear that slight “l” sound at the end of some words. It’s not like we’re all speaking the same way. I guess that’s the thing. I think it’s more about where you’re from, even if you’re not from the same area. I mean, I’m from Bedfordshire, and my mate from Bedford is from the same county, but we still have our own little quirks. Exactly, and it’s funny because sometimes when I go to London, I feel like I sound like an accent from somewhere else. It’s like watching a movie and suddenly someone says, “Blimey!” and you think, “Wait, I didn’t think that was how people spoke here.” Oh, I’ve had that before too. Last year, I was in a pub in Cornwall, and I said “cheerio” instead of “goodnight,” and the guy next to me said, “You’re from Bedford, aren’t you?” I was like, “How did you know?” He said, “You said ‘cheerio’ wrong.” Oh man, that’s true! I’ve been to pubs and people have picked up on my accent before. It’s like they can tell I’m from the East Midlands. I think it’s just the way we say words like “bottle” or “butter.” I could see that. I mean, I’m from Bedford too, so I do notice the difference in the way people speak. Some people here use that “th” sound more, and others just drop the “r” in some words. It’s like a mix of different regional influences. I think it’s the same with the rest of the country. If you go to Yorkshire, you’ll hear a totally different accent, and in Cornwall, it’s even more pronounced.

So, do you think I should get a car? I mean, I’m trying to save money, but driving is so expensive these days. I don’t know, it depends on how much you’re planning to use it. If you’re not commuting every day, maybe you can just take the bus or bike. But if you’re going out a lot, a car might be more convenient. Yeah, I’m thinking about it more because I need to get to a few places outside the city. But the cost of fuel, insurance, and maintenance is just so high. I’ve heard people say that even if you don’t drive much, it still adds up. That’s true. I had a car when I was living in Peterborough, and it cost me more than I expected. You end up spending a lot on things like parking and tolls too. I know, I’ve been trying to budget this out. Maybe I can look into a cheaper car, like a used one? Or even a hybrid or electric? I’ve heard they’re more efficient. Yeah, hybrids can save you money in the long run, especially with fuel costs. But even then, it still might not be worth it if you’re not driving a lot. You might want to try a rental car first to see if you actually need it. That’s an idea. I could rent for a few weeks and see how much it costs. But what about the hassle of dealing with breakdowns and repairs? I don’t want to be stuck somewhere with a broken car. Fair point. I had a car that broke down a few times, which was a huge inconvenience. I think if you’re not sure about buying, the best option is to keep using public transport or maybe walk more. I’m thinking of taking the bus more often. I know it takes longer, but I’ve been trying to cut down on expenses. Plus, I could save the money for other things, like saving up for a trip or something else. That’s good. It sounds like you’re being practical. Maybe take some time to think it over, and if you do decide to get a car, start with something reliable and affordable. Yeah, I’ll do that. It’s just so hard to balance saving money and needing to get around.

Right, right, well I've got to get to the post office before they close. I need to send off those exam papers I've been marking. I’m feeling pretty fed up with the amount of time this has taken me. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to get on top of my GCSE revision, but it’s just so heavy. I’m dreading the exams. I’ve got a maths paper tomorrow, and I’m not even sure if I’ll be ready. Oh, lassie, don’t you worry your little head off. You’ll be fine. You’ve got a good brain, and I know you’re smart.
