I mean, it’s one thing if it’s a medical issue, but if it’s just lack of confidence or something, then it’s a different story. Yeah, I guess. But I mean, she was really into him, and now she’s just like, “I don’t even want to talk about it anymore.” That’s sad. I mean, it’s not like it’s a moral issue or anything. My brother had a bit of an issue with that once, and it really messed up his relationships. I know, but I just don’t know how to approach it. If someone says, “I’m not feeling up to it,” is that just a sign they’re not interested, or is there something else going on? It can be tricky. Sometimes people don’t know how to say it, or they’re too nervous to bring it up. But if it’s a recurring issue, then it’s probably worth having a conversation about. Yeah, but it’s so awkward. I mean, it’s not like you can just say, “Hey, did you know you have ED?” It feels like stepping on a landmine. Exactly. But if you’re in a relationship, it’s not something you should ignore. It’s about communication, right? Whether it’s a physical or emotional issue, you need to address it together. I guess. But I’m just worried that if someone is having trouble, it might mean they don’t care about me or the relationship. I get that. But it’s not always about caring. Sometimes it’s about health, stress, or even anxiety. It’s not something you can just assume is a rejection of you. I suppose. I just hope that if someone ever mentioned it to me, I’d be able to handle it. I mean, it’s not something I’ve ever had to deal with, so I don’t know what I’d say. Yeah, it’s a sensitive topic. But it’s better to talk about it than to let it fester. Relationships are about being open and honest, even when it’s uncomfortable.

So, do you know what’s the deal with these free food boxes from Slimming World? They’ve got like... everything, but half of it is technically 'healthy extras' which I don’t think counts as a syn? I know, I got one last week and there was a whole section of cheese and biscuits. I mean, it’s not like they’re giving you free food—just making you feel guilty for eating it. Exactly! And then there’s that 0 calorie syrup. I tried it once and it was like drinking sugar water with a bit of artificial flavour. Tastes like... like someone tried to make a sugary drink but failed. Ugh, I know. It’s so weird. I’ve even heard people say it’s like drinking a spoonful of regret. Ha! Yeah, I’m not even gonna touch it. I’ve got better things to do with my syns than drink that stuff. Speaking of syns, have you checked the new Quorn range? I saw it at Tesco and it’s got like, organic stuff and everything. I’m thinking about getting some for the roast. I did, and I tried the chicken bites—it was okay, but it’s not like the real thing. Still, it’s better than the real thing in terms of calories, right? Oh, I know, but it’s hard not to feel like you’re cheating yourself. Like, are you even allowed to have one of those? I don’t know, maybe we should just go for the cauliflower cheese. It’s delicious and it’s got way fewer syns than anything else. Yeah, I agree. Although I’m still trying to figure out how to get the cauliflower to taste like cheese. I’ve got this spice mix I bought, but it’s not doing the trick. Maybe you need to use more of it. Or just add some extra Parmesan. I think I’ve got some in the fridge. Perfect. We could make it as part of our treat day Saturday. You know, that day where we can just eat anything we want? Yeah, I was thinking the same! I’ve got some double peas in the freezer, if you want to use them. And I saw some frozen mint in the shop. Maybe we could make a mint chocolate chip sundae? Oh, that sounds amazing. Although I’m not sure how many syns that would be.

I was thinking about our holiday plans again. You know, we’ve been promising ourselves a proper getaway for ages. I feel like we’ve been stuck in this routine, and I just need something different. Yeah, I know. I’ve been meaning to talk about it too. I was actually looking at some places online last night. Maybe somewhere with some good scenery and not too much hustle. You know, somewhere we can actually relax. That sounds good. I was thinking maybe somewhere in the south. We could go to Cornwall or Devon. I’ve always wanted to visit those places. Cornwall sounds nice. I’ve heard it’s beautiful. But I’d also like to go somewhere that’s a bit more off the beaten track. Maybe somewhere in the countryside? I’m getting tired of the same old places. Yeah, I can see that. But do you think we could do both? A bit of the coast and some countryside? Maybe a mix of the two. I suppose so. As long as we don’t end up with a holiday that’s just one long road trip. I mean, we’ve done that before and it’s exhausting. Fair point. I was also thinking about a little writing project I’ve been working on. Maybe I could take some time off work to focus on it. I’ve been meaning to write a short story or something. That’s a good idea. You’ve always had that creative side. But I’m not sure how that’ll work with our holiday. I mean, you’ll need to have a bit of space and time to yourself. I know, but I think it could be part of the trip. Maybe I can write while we’re there. I’ve always found that being in a new place helps me get inspired. That’s true. I’ve found that when I’m somewhere new, I can think more clearly. Although, I’d still prefer to have some time to myself. I’m not sure I’d be able to write with you around all the time. Fair enough. I can understand that. I guess the key is finding a balance. You know, not too much time alone, but enough to get some work done. Yeah, I agree. I was also thinking about my own future plans. I’ve been thinking about getting a tattoo.

Well, do you know, I’ve been thinking about the weekend. I need to get the arrangements sorted for the birthday party. I’ll be honest, I’m feeling a bit overwhelmed with all the details. Yeah, I can see that. You’ve got a lot on your plate. But it’s not that bad, honestly. Just make sure you get the invitations out by Friday, and you’ll be fine. I know, I know, but I keep forgetting. It’s not like it’s a huge event, just a small get-together with friends and family. But still, I like to do things properly. I get you. I always like to make sure everything is set. Speaking of which, did you get the postcard from the holiday? I was just looking at it earlier. Oh yes, I did. It’s from the Highlands. I think it was from Inverness. The view was absolutely stunning. The way the light catches the hills, it’s like something out of a painting. I’d love to see that. I’ve always wanted to go up there. But I’ve heard the weather is a bit unpredictable. You might have been lucky to have such nice weather. It was lovely – no rain at all. I almost felt guilty because I was so comfortable. But I suppose it was a blessing. I can imagine. You know, I’ve been meaning to ask you about your thoughts on the Scottish independence thing. I heard you’ve been pretty vocal about it. Yes, I have. I think it’s a big decision for any country, and it’s about time Scotland had the chance to make its own choice. It’s not just about politics; it’s about identity and culture. I agree, but I can see the arguments on both sides. Some people are worried about the economic impact, and others are worried about losing the union. Definitely. I think it’s a matter of time before the referendum happens. I just hope the process is handled wisely. I hope so too. It’s an important topic, and I think it’s nice that we can talk about it in a friendly way. Absolutely. Just don’t expect me to be on the fence. I’ve made my position clear. No, I won’t expect that. You’ve always been passionate about your beliefs. I think that’s one of the things that makes you such a good friend – you’re honest and upfront.

So, do you think we should draw a chair for the Syrian refugees then? A chair? Like, a real chair? Or is it more symbolic? I mean, it’s a way to show we care, right? Like, if you draw a chair, it’s like saying we’re making space for them. Yeah, but isn’t that a bit… weird? I mean, how do you even draw a chair? It’s not that hard! You just draw the basic shape—like a rectangle with legs and a seat. It’s not like we’re drawing a spaceship or something. I guess, but what if they don’t even know what a chair is? Well, they probably do. You know, they’ve used chairs in school. I mean, most kids, even if they’re not in school, have seen a chair. Yeah, but what’s the point of drawing one? Are we supposed to give it to them? No, not really. It’s more about raising awareness. I mean, we’re not going to be giving them real chairs, but the idea is to show that we’re thinking about them. I get that, but isn’t it a bit naive? Like, how does drawing a chair actually help? It helps in a way. It’s a small act, but it’s also a way to start a conversation. And maybe, if we draw enough chairs, we can donate them to a charity or something. But what if we draw a  bad  chair? Like, a weird-shaped one or something? That’s okay! It doesn’t have to be perfect. It’s more about the intention. Maybe we should do a drawing competition for the kids. Like, let them draw chairs and then we can display them. That’s a good idea! It would make them feel involved. And who knows, maybe one of them will come up with a really creative chair. I’ve got an idea. What if we draw a  big  chair? Like, a giant one. So it’s like a symbol that we’re not just giving them a small space, but a whole seat at the table. That’s brilliant! We could even call it the “Chair of Welcome” or something. Yeah, and we could write a note with it, like, “This chair is for you.” Exactly. It’s not just a chair—it’s a message of hope.

I just got a message from Lucy saying she’s expecting her first baby next month. It’s so exciting, isn’t it? Yeah, I guess it is. I mean, she’s been talking about it for ages. I remember when we first met, she was still in the thick of her PhD and all that. Now she’s about to become a mum. Time flies. It really does. I wonder if we should start thinking about that, you know? Like, maybe in a few years? Or maybe we’ll be too busy with work? Honestly, I don’t know. It’s one of those things that’s on my mind sometimes. I mean, I’ve been thinking about it more since we’ve both been lecturers for a while now. The hours, the deadlines, the pressure—it can be tough to balance. But then again, if we were to do it, it would be worth it, right? I agree. I think we’d be good parents. We’re both pretty responsible. And we have each other. But I can see how it could be overwhelming. Especially with teaching and all the administrative stuff we have to handle. Yeah, and then there’s the whole financial side of it. We’re both in higher professional occupations, so we’re not exactly broke, but it’s still not easy. Rent, utilities, the cost of living in London—there’s a lot to consider. I know. It’s not just about money though. It’s also about time. You know, having to take time off, adjusting your schedules, all that. But then again, maybe it’s not too bad if we plan properly. Maybe we can have a few years of stability before trying to start a family. I like that idea. We could take some time to just enjoy being together, figure out what we want, and be sure we’re both ready. I mean, we’ve been friends for so long, and we’ve always had a strong connection. I think we could make it work. Yeah, I think you’re right. It’s not something to rush into. Especially with the kind of work we do, it’s important to be on the same page. Plus, we have our friends to support us. I mean, if Lucy’s going through it, we could help her out, and maybe she’ll be the one giving us advice when the time comes.

So, do you remember that time we were in Bath and we got stuck in that comedy show with that guy who kept talking about his dog? It was so funny, and I think he even had a sign that said “I am not a dog, I am a man.” Oh, I remember that! That was one of the most ridiculous things I’ve ever seen. I still can’t get over how he kept referencing his dog like it was the best part of the show. It was like he was trying to be edgy, but it was just… awkward. Yeah, and then the host said something like, “He’s just trying to keep it real,” and I was like, “Real? Real? My real is sleeping in my bed right now!” I mean, I was joking, but I couldn’t help it. It just felt so out of place in that setting. I think that’s the thing about comedy – it’s so subjective. One person finds it hilarious, and another finds it completely off-putting. I mean, I actually like some of that kind of thing, you know? Like, the kind of comedy that’s a bit surreal or quirky. It’s the kind that makes you think, “Wait, did I just watch that?” Yeah, I guess that’s what makes it so fun. It’s like a game of “what’s the weirdest thing that could possibly happen?” But I do wonder if we ever get to the point where the joke is just too much. Like, when it’s not funny anymore, just weird. Totally. I think it’s a fine line. But then again, I’ve always liked people who take risks with their humor. I mean, I think about the time we went to that comedy club in Edinburgh and that guy was telling jokes about policemen. He barely even had a script, but he kept going. And then he said, “I once got pulled over by a cop who asked me if I knew the time. I said ‘Yes, it’s 3:30,’ and he said, ‘Well, you’re 30 minutes behind.’” I nearly died. Oh man, that’s a classic. I remember laughing so hard I almost spilled my drink. I can still hear it in my head. It’s weird how something so simple can become so funny, isn’t it? Exactly. And I think part of the beauty of comedy is that it’s so unpredictable.

Dad, do you remember when we were kids and you used to take me fishing by the river near the old mill? It was so much fun. Oh yes, I remember that well. You were probably about seven or eight. You’d sit there for hours just waiting for a bite, and then when you finally caught one, you’d scream like you’d won the lottery. Yeah, I used to think I was the luckiest kid in the world. And you’d always make me put the fish back, even though I was so excited to keep it. I don’t know why you did that. Well, I thought it was important to respect the river and the fish. It’s not like we had a lot of fish to begin with. Plus, you’d never get to keep them anyway, they’d just end up in the stew. That’s true. I suppose it made sense. But now I’m thinking about getting a van to move house. I’ve got this job in Manchester, and I need to get my stuff sorted. Do you think I should hire a van, or maybe just rent one for the day? Well, I’d say if you can afford it, go for a van. It’s easier to move everything all at once. But if money is tight, maybe just rent one and take it to the new place. You can’t really move a house without a van, can you? I know, it’s just that I’m not sure how much I need to carry. I’m already thinking about the Great Dorset Steam Fair. I want to go this year. It’s been a while since I’ve gone, and I’d love to take some pictures with the old trams and the steam engines. That sounds like a good idea. The steam fair is always a great day out. You should definitely go. My sister went last year and she said it was absolutely magical. I’d love that. But I was also thinking about the lottery. I’ve been playing it every week, and I’m starting to think maybe I should increase my stake. What do you think? I don’t know, lass. I’ve never been too hot on the lottery. I think it’s more about the dream than the money. But if you think you’re on a winning streak, by all means go for it.

I just got a call from the council. They’re saying the local library might be up for demolition. What? That can’t be true. The library’s been around for decades. It’s a real community hub. I know, it’s shocking. They’re saying they want to replace it with a new development. A development? What kind of development? A shopping centre? A housing complex? No, it’s more like a mixed-use space. They’ve been talking about it for months. The council says the library is underused. Underused? I’ve been going there every week. I’d say it’s packed every day. I know, but maybe they’re just looking for a way to fund other projects. They’ve been cutting budgets for public services. That’s not fair. The library is more than just a place to borrow books. It’s a meeting point, a place for kids, for adults to learn, for events. Yeah, and it’s a historic building too. They’ve got that old facade, the original design. It’s part of the town’s history. Exactly. I remember when it was built. It was a big deal. The whole town came out to see the opening. And don’t get me started on the upholstery. I was looking online the other day for fabric ideas for the living room. Oh, you’re finally getting around to it? I thought you’d had that done for ages. I had plans, but then things kept coming up. I’ve been putting it off for months. Well, you should get a nice, durable fabric. The library is losing its old look, but at least the furniture in the house should last for years. I know, but I want something that’s a bit more modern. Maybe something with a pattern, but not too flashy. That sounds good. I’ll help you pick out some samples next weekend. I’ve got a few ideas from the local market. That would be great. I owe you one. No problem. And while we’re at it, you should check out that new newspaper stand on the corner. They’ve got a better selection than the old one. You’re right. I’ve been relying on the old stand for ages. Maybe it’s time to upgrade. Yeah, and maybe the council will listen if enough people speak out.

So, do you know what’s on tonight? I was thinking of watching something a bit different, maybe something like  The Crown  or one of those period dramas. But I’m not sure if it’s worth it. I’ve seen  The Crown  — it’s great, but it’s a bit intense. I mean, it’s very dramatic. I think it’s more like a costume drama. Maybe something lighter? Yeah, I’ve seen some of it. It’s interesting, but it’s so long. I don’t know if I can commit to the whole series. I’d rather watch something like  Fleabag  or  Killing Eve . Oh, I loved  Killing Eve ! It’s so addictive. I binged the whole series in a weekend. But I’ve been meaning to watch  Stranger Things  again. It’s better than  Killing Eve . Haha, I don’t think  Stranger Things  is better than  Killing Eve , but I do like it. I mean, it’s got that nostalgic feel, right? Yeah, it’s like stepping back in time. But I think the best thing about it is the soundtrack. The music just gives it that 80s vibe. I agree. The music is part of what makes it so good. It’s like the show was made for the soundtrack. I’ve been listening to the  Stranger Things  theme on repeat. Oh, I know that one. It’s so catchy. I think it’s from the 80s, isn’t it? Yeah, I think it’s a cover of the original 80s song. It’s like they found the perfect track to accompany the show. Maybe we could do something like that for our next group watch. Like pick a show and a soundtrack. It could be a fun way to enjoy the content together. That sounds like a good idea. I mean, we could even make it a tradition. Maybe next time we can do  The Crown  with some classic 60s music. I like that. It would be a nice way to combine our hobbies — music and TV. Speaking of which, I’ve been meaning to get a new playlist. Yeah, I could really use some new tunes. I’ve been stuck on the same playlist for months. Maybe we can start a music group. Like, each of us brings a few tracks, and we make a shared playlist. That’s not a bad idea. It could be a great way to discover new music and bond over it.

Right, right, so you've got your driving test coming up soon, haven't you, laddie? Yeah, I’m doing it next week. I’ve been practising a bit, but I’m still a bit nervous. Aye, that’s natural. I remember when I first got my licence, I was twitchy as a cat on a hot tin roof. But you’ll be fine, I’m sure of it. Thanks, Nan. I hope so. I’ve been trying to remember all the rules, but sometimes it feels like the examiner’s watching me every second. Aye, that’s the way it is. But you’ve got to trust yourself. You know the roads better than anyone. Just keep calm and drive like you normally do. I know, but I keep thinking about the insurance part too. What if something happens? I don’t want to get stuck in a mess. Oh, you’ll be covered, laddie. Your dad’s got the insurance sorted, right? Yeah, he said it’s all set up. But I don’t know much about it. I mean, I’ve heard about no claims bonuses and all that, but I’m not sure how it works exactly. Well, let me explain. It’s basically about how much you pay for your car insurance based on how many years you’ve been driving without making a claim. The longer you go without a claim, the cheaper your premium gets. Oh, so it’s like a reward for being careful? Exactly. And if you do make a claim, it can push your premium up, and you might lose some of your no-claims bonus. So it’s really important to be safe and not take unnecessary risks. Yeah, I guess so. I don’t want to be the one who causes an accident and ends up paying more for the next few years. That’s the ticket. You’ll be fine, though. I’m sure you’ll be a good driver. Just keep your eyes on the road and don’t rush. I’ll try. I think I’m getting the hang of it now. It’s just the pressure of the test that gets me. Aye, that’s the thing. You don’t have to be perfect, just safe and responsible. And don’t forget, I’ll be here to give you a bit of a pep talk before you go.

So, do you think the way we test for stress at work is actually effective? I mean, they just give you a questionnaire and then say you're fine or not. I don’t think it’s really measuring anything real. I don’t know, I think it’s better than nothing. But seriously, I feel like I’ve been stressed for months and I haven’t even noticed it until I started having these weird headaches. It’s like my brain is just overworked. Yeah, I know what you mean. I mean, I don’t have a job right now, but even being responsible for a toddler all day is enough to make me feel like I’m going to explode. I can’t even imagine what it’s like when you have to manage a team and all the stress that comes with it. I know, I think the real stress is when you feel like you’ve got to be perfect all the time. You know, like if you make one mistake, it’s like you’ve failed. That’s what I think is the worst part. And I don’t even like that kind of pressure, but it’s just how it is. Yeah, it’s like when you’re at work and you’ve got a meeting coming up, and you’re like, “I hope no one else is thinking of leaving.” I mean, I know that’s not fair, but it’s just how I feel. I think it’s also about the way we talk about stress in this country. We always say “I’m stressed,” but nobody really wants to discuss it. You just keep it all inside. It’s like we’re all carrying this giant weight, but we don’t even realize it. And I think that’s the problem. When you don’t talk about it, you don’t know how to deal with it. I think that’s why I found this podcast about mindfulness. It’s not like it’s going to fix everything, but it’s helping me feel a little better. I’ve been trying to do some breathing exercises, and it actually helps when I’m at home. That’s great, I think I need to do that too. I mean, I’m not even allowed to go out much, so I can go for a walk in the park sometimes.

So, do you know what’s the biggest difference between a bird and a plane? Hmm... Well, a bird flies with wings, and a plane flies with engines, obviously. But they both have wings, though. Yeah, but planes also have wings, and they can go faster. Exactly! But I think the real difference is that birds are free, and planes are... well, they’re stuck in the sky, right? You’re making me think of when I was a student and I used to dream of flying like a bird. I know, we all did, didn’t we? Especially when we were kids. I think I still do. I want to fly like a dragon. A dragon? You’re gonna get in trouble if you say that out loud. Well, unless you’re in a fantasy novel, you’re not gonna get anywhere with that. I think it’s more about the desire to escape, though. You know, like the hilltop villages we used to pass on the way to the countryside. Yeah, those places always looked so peaceful, like they were untouched by time. I think they actually are untouched by time. I mean, some of them haven’t changed in centuries. That’s the beauty of them, isn’t it? But they’re also tricky to get to. I remember once trying to visit one, and it took us three hours to get through the countryside because of the weather. I bet the weather was a nightmare. Oh it was. It rained so hard that the roads were like rivers. That sounds scary. I remember something like that. My cousin once tried to drive up to the Lake District and got stuck in a landslide. Oh no, that sounds dangerous. Yeah, but he was fine. He just had to wait until the mud cleared. I think I’d rather take the bus. Yeah, but the bus wasn’t running. You’re just not used to the weather up there. I think we’re all just trying to get used to it. Speaking of weather, I heard that the EU referendum was a big deal for people like us, right? Yeah, it changed a lot of things, especially for people who were used to moving freely around Europe. And for people like me, it changed the way I think about immigration and borders. I don’t know, I think it’s still a bit confusing, honestly.

So, do you think we should go vegetarian? I mean, I’ve been thinking about it more since I started reading about the environmental impact of meat production. Honestly, I've been vegetarian for years. I don’t eat any meat or dairy. It’s just easier for me now, especially with how much I’m writing and illustrating. I think it’s more about what you believe in than what you eat. But I do wonder if people would ever go fully plant-based. It’s a tough one. I’ve been thinking about moving towards a plant-based diet too, but I still love the taste of meat. I guess it’s not just about ethics, it’s also about habit and culture. Plus, there’s the whole synthetic meat thing now—shmeat or whatever you want to call it. Yeah, I’ve heard about that. I think it’s a bit of a gimmick, but it could be a good step towards reducing animal cruelty and environmental damage. People can still enjoy the taste without the ethical issues. I think it’s a good alternative for people who are worried about animal welfare or the environment but still want to eat meat. It’s still early days, though, and I’m not sure how sustainable it will be. I mean, it’s not like we can just stop eating meat overnight. True, but if we’re going to make changes, maybe start with small things. Like taking vitamin tablets or supplements for things like B12, which is harder to get from a plant-based diet. I’ve been taking some for a while now, and it’s actually helped me feel better. I’ve considered that too. I’ve been reading a lot about how important certain vitamins are for energy and mental health. It’s funny, I didn’t realize how much of an impact that could have. I mean, if you’re not getting enough, you could feel really sluggish or even depressed. Yeah, that’s true. I think it’s a common thing with people who switch to plant-based diets. You have to be careful about what you’re eating. Also, I’ve noticed that some people who go vegetarian end up over-consuming processed foods, which is not ideal for your health. That’s a good point. It’s not just about cutting out meat or dairy—it’s about making sure your diet is balanced and nutritious.

So, do you think we should get a new TV? This one’s getting a bit old, and it’s not even Christmas yet. Honestly, I think it’s fine. I mean, it works, doesn’t it? It’s not like we’ve got a lot of problems with it. Unless you want to watch something more high definition? Yeah, I mean, it’s not a bad TV, but I think we could do with a newer one. And with all the streaming services now, it’s just not the same with the old one. I agree. I watched a movie the other day and it looked like it was from the 90s on this thing. It’s like the movie was in black and white. I think it’s time to upgrade. I suppose, but I’ve been thinking about doing a bit of internet shopping. Maybe wait till Christmas for a better deal? You know, the usual sales. That’s a good idea. I mean, even if we don’t get the TV, we can still buy some new games or something. Christmas is just around the corner, right? Yeah, and I’ve been thinking about getting some new games anyway. I’ve got a few on my list. You know, the new FIFA game is out, and I still haven’t played it. Oh, don’t tell me you’re playing FIFA again. I thought you were done with that after the last time you got into a massive argument with your brother over who was the best player. Oh, come on, it’s just a game. Besides, I still think Messi is the best, even if he’s about to retire. Yeah, I still think he’s the GOAT. But you know, I was thinking about doing some travel this summer. Maybe up north, to the Lake District. It’s been a while since I’ve gone there. That’s a good idea. But I think I might have to wait a bit. You know, with me being unemployed and all. I’m not sure I can afford a holiday just yet. That’s true, but maybe you could do a short trip with us. I mean, we can go together. I think it would be fun. Plus, it’s not like we’re going anywhere fancy. Just a bit of a walk in the countryside. Yeah, that’s a good point.

So, do you know what’s happening with the Alumni Day? I think they’re doing some sort of tour of the campus and showing off all the new buildings. Yeah, I saw a flyer about it. It’s like a mini reunion, kind of. They’ve got a coffee corner and they’re letting people catch up with old friends. That sounds nice. I’ve been meaning to get in touch with some people from my year. I feel like we’ve all gone our separate ways, but it’s good to see everyone again. Definitely. I think some of the people I’ve lost touch with are still in the area, so it’s a chance to reconnect. Speaking of which, did you hear about Anna’s trip to Spain? She was talking about how amazing it was and how she’s definitely going back next year with her family. Oh yeah, she’s been raving about it for weeks. She said the food was incredible and that she ate more paella than she ever thought possible. I can imagine. I’ve always wanted to visit Spain, but I keep putting it off. I think I need to start planning a holiday soon. You should. Have you got any ideas about where you’d like to go? I was thinking of Greece next year, maybe. The weather is supposed to be perfect, and the food’s amazing too. Greece sounds good. I’ve always wanted to go to Santorini. I think the views are supposed to be absolutely stunning. It’s on my list too. I’ve been reading up on it, actually. There are so many places to visit, but I’m trying to focus on one or two. That’s smart. I think I need to do the same. Maybe I’ll start with a short trip first, like a weekend getaway somewhere. Yeah, that’s a good idea. It’s easy to get overwhelmed with all the options. I think the key is to just pick somewhere that makes you happy. Exactly. I’ve been thinking about booking a trip to the Lake District for a couple of weeks. It’s quiet, peaceful, and perfect for relaxing. That sounds lovely. I might have to go there too. I’ve heard the scenery is beautiful, and it’s a great place to unwind. You should definitely consider it.

I can't believe I've got a lecture tomorrow at 9 a.m. Seriously? That’s brutal. You're going to be so tired after that massage you had yesterday. Yeah, I know. I feel like I’ve been through a rollercoaster. But it’s worth it, right? I’m just trying to get through this year. I get that. But you have to take care of yourself, you know. If you’re not sleeping or eating properly, you’ll just crash harder. I know, I know. It’s just the pressure of being a student. I feel like I’m the only one who’s working so hard. Everyone else is like, “Oh, you’re not even in a degree yet, just doing A-levels.” But I’m doing sixth form, and it’s still intense. Wait, you’re still in sixth form? I thought you were in university. No, no, no. I’m still in the last year of sixth form. I’m applying for uni next year, but it’s so stressful. I don’t know if I can handle lectures and all that work. You’ll be fine. I mean, I left sixth form and went straight into postgrad studies, and I survived. You’ll get used to the routine. Just don’t burn out. I’m trying. I’ve been trying to balance everything. I have to work part-time, do assignments, and then have time for my friends. It’s not easy. I get it. I still feel like I’m in a never-ending cycle sometimes. But you’re not alone in this. You’ve got me, and your friends. You just need to take it one day at a time. Yeah, I guess. But I’m worried about the lectures. I heard they’re so different from what we do in school. I know. I tried to explain to my sister, but she just said, “Oh, lectures are just like school, but with more boring people.” That’s not fair. I’m sure there are some good lecturers. Yeah, probably. But you’ll find your own way through it. And if you ever need a break, just remind yourself that you’ve got your massage and your friends to help you through it. Thanks. I needed that. Anytime. You’re not alone in this. We’ll get through it together. I hope so.

So, do you think we should bring some of those lentils from the market? I mean, they’re on sale, and I thought we could make a proper stew or something. Yeah, I was thinking the same. We’ve had the same old things for a while now. A little bit of variety wouldn’t hurt, especially with the weather being so gloomy lately. Yeah, I agree. A good soup or stew can really lift your spirits. And besides, I’ve been reading about these new recipes online—some with different spices and stuff. Maybe we can try one of those. That sounds nice. I’ll go grab a few more things from the shop tomorrow. But before that, what’s the news? I heard something about the migrant crisis in Calais, but I’m not sure if it’s true. Yeah, it’s been in the papers a lot. I think there are more people trying to cross over, and the situation’s getting worse. The government says they’re trying to do something, but I don’t know how much that helps. It’s sad, really. I mean, people are just looking for a better life, aren’t they? I can’t imagine what it would be like to be in that situation. So many people are stuck in limbo, not knowing where they’re going to end up. Yeah, it’s heartbreaking. I think it’s something we should all be more aware of, even if it feels far away. It’s also making me think about what the future holds for us. I mean, with everything that’s going on, how do you plan for the next few years? Honestly, I’m just trying to stay positive. I’m thinking about getting my teaching qualification upgraded so I can move into a more senior role. Maybe that’ll open up some more opportunities. That’s good. I was actually thinking about taking some courses too, maybe in something more practical. You know, just to keep my skills up to date. It’s never too late, right? Definitely not. I’ve been thinking about trying to find some part-time work, just to have a bit more stability. Though I know it’s not easy these days, with the economy the way it is. I get that. But even small steps can make a difference. And with the support of family, I think we can make it.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about redecorating the house. It’s been a while since I’ve done anything with the bathroom. I’m feeling like I need a bit of a refresh. Oh, I can see that. You know, I’ve been in the same house for years, and I’ve been meaning to do the kitchen. But honestly, I’m too busy with work. I’ve got a backlog of things to do. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve got a few projects I want to tackle. The plumber came round the other week to check the pipes, and he said there’s nothing wrong, but he mentioned the bathroom tiles are starting to look a bit tired. Tired? I’d say they’re more like ancient. I had to replace them about three years ago. It turned out the tiling was a bit of a nightmare. Took me weeks to get it right. I’m not looking forward to that. I remember when I first moved into this house, the bathroom was actually quite nice. I mean, it had that retro look, like the 70s. Oh, I remember that era too. I think there was something about the tiles, the green ones, and the way the light used to bounce off them. It was almost like a museum. Yeah, I think I might go for something a bit more modern. Maybe a clean white with some grey accents. I want it to feel airy and open. That sounds good. I’ve been thinking about going for something similar. I’ve been sketching out some ideas in my head. Maybe a new kitchen layout would help. That’s a good idea. I always found the kitchen to be the heart of the house. It’s where we all gather. I think it’s important to make that space welcoming. Absolutely. I was talking to my wife the other day about maybe replacing the old cabinets. She was all for it, but I’m not sure yet. I don’t want to rush into anything. That’s wise. It’s a big investment, so you have to be careful. I think I’ll start by getting some quotes from the local tradespeople. I’ve had some good experiences with a few of them. I’ll do that too. I’ve got a few contacts I can reach out to.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing I’ve ever eaten? I was in Dublin, and there was this place that served a whole chicken with a side of potatoes. It was huge, like, I think it was the size of a small dog. Whoa, that sounds crazy. I mean, I’ve had big chicken before, but not that big. Did you finish it? I didn’t even get to the potatoes. I got halfway through the chicken and thought, “I think I’ve had enough for the day.” But it was good. It was like a big meal for a big person. Oh, I know what you mean. When I was younger, I used to eat a whole pizza by myself. My mum used to say I was a pizza monster. That sounds like a lot. I’m more of a small plate person. I prefer to eat a little bit of a lot of things. Like, I’ll have a few different things on my plate instead of one huge dish. That’s how I was when I was younger too, but now I think bigger meals are more satisfying. Especially when you’re with family. I think that’s what makes eating special—sharing it with people. Yeah, I agree. My son just turned three, and I’ve been trying to cook for him. I thought I’d be able to make big meals, but he only eats a little bit. I keep thinking, “It’s just a snack,” and then he finishes it. It’s a bit of a struggle. I’d say it’s a badge of honour. If you can finish a meal, you’re doing well. I’ve been trying to eat more healthily lately, though. I mean, I’m a student, so I don’t have a lot of money, but I try to eat balanced meals. That’s smart. I used to drink a lot when I was younger, but I’ve cut back a lot. I think it’s better for your health. You know, your brain and everything. I had a friend who drank too much, and it affected his work. I’ve heard that. I think I’ll try to drink less too. Maybe with the kid, it’s even more important to stay healthy. Yeah, I can see that. I don’t drink much anyway, but I’ve been told that you should be careful with alcohol when you’re looking after a toddler.

I've been thinking a lot about Halloween, you know, since we've been catching up. It's been years since we had a proper one with the kids around. Oh, yes, I remember when we used to dress up and go door to door. It was such a joy, especially when the kids would come home with their faces covered in chocolate and pumpkin guts. And don’t forget the nights when we’d have a small party at home. The whole house would be lit up, and the kids would be bouncing off the walls. It was the best time of the year. Yeah, I guess it's been a while since I've had the real thing. I’ve been in school and all, so I haven’t really had the chance to do much of it. But I heard the school is doing a Halloween event this year. They’re even making costumes for the kids. That sounds good. I hope they’re not making them too complicated. When I was a kid, we used to make our own costumes out of old clothes and paper. It was messy, but it was fun. Oh I remember that. We had one year where my sister dressed up as a ghost, but she didn’t have enough paper. She ended up looking like a floating sheet. My dad thought it was hilarious. That’s a classic. I remember my mum trying to make a witch costume for me. It ended up being a big pile of fabric and fake hair. She said she was trying to be creative, but it looked more like a costume for a Halloween party at a nursing home. Hey, what about horse-riding? I heard you used to ride horses, Mr. Smith. Was that part of the Halloween tradition? No, not exactly. I used to ride horses as a child, but it wasn’t really connected to Halloween. It was more of a hobby. I used to go to a stable near the village, and the horses were always excited to see me. I bet they were! My brother used to ride as well. He always said he’d never make it as a jockey because he was too short, but he was the fastest on the field. I think the key thing about riding is that it’s more about the connection with the horse than the competition.

So, do you think we’ll get there on time? I mean, the traffic around this time of year is... Well, it’s not exactly a walk in the park. Honestly, I don’t know. I’ve heard about the roads near Basingstoke being a nightmare. I think there’s some sort of event going on today, or maybe just the usual Christmas rush. Yeah, and I bet the parking situation will be a nightmare too. I remember last year, there was a sign saying “No parking for disabled vehicles” and then the next thing you know, some grumpy old man was trying to park in a spot that was clearly marked for people with disabilities. My uncle had a bit of a row about that. He said he’s got a mobility scooter and he doesn’t see why he should be turned away. And you know what? I think he was right. I mean, the council should be thinking about the people who actually need these spaces, not just making it a bit of a hassle for everyone else. I’ve had some experience with that too. I work with quite a few elderly people, and I’ve seen how difficult it is for them to get around, especially if they can’t park anywhere. I remember one lady who had to walk three miles just to get to the shop because there was no disabled parking near her house. That’s terrible. I mean, isn’t that what council housing is supposed to be for? Providing safe, accessible living conditions for people who need it? Exactly. But I think the problem comes down to underfunding and poor planning. I used to work in local government, and I can tell you, it’s all about budget cuts and making things as easy as possible for the people in power. Yeah, and that’s just not fair. I mean, if you’re an elderly person, you’ve got more needs than the average person. You need proper housing, accessible transport, and you need to be able to get out and about safely. I suppose it’s a bit of a catch-22. If the housing isn’t set up for people with disabilities, then they can’t live independently. And if the council can’t afford to provide that, then they’re stuck in a loop. That’s exactly it. And then there’s the parking at events like The Great Dorset Steam Fair.

So, do you think we should go for the allotment in Mitcham? I’ve been checking the website and there’s one that’s available with a nice mix of vegetables and herbs. I think it’d be a great idea. Mitcham? I’ve heard of it. It’s a bit of a drive from here, but I think it’s worth it. I’ve actually been thinking about getting an allotment myself. It’s such a good way to get back to nature and eat healthier. Plus, there’s something satisfying about growing your own food. Yeah, I agree. I’ve always loved the idea of growing things, even if I’m not the most experienced gardener. I’ve got a bit of a green thumb, I think. My mum used to have this amazing garden, and I used to help her plant tomatoes and peppers every summer. That’s great! It sounds like you’re already off to a good start. I’m a bit of a beginner myself, but I’ve been reading up on companion planting and soil preparation. I think I need to get some books and do a bit of research before I even start digging. Oh, definitely. I remember when I first tried to grow something in a pot, I ended up overwatering it and it died. It was such a shame, but I learned a lot from that. I think we should start small—maybe just a few herbs and some easy vegetables like carrots or beans. That makes sense. Starting with something simple will help us build confidence. I was thinking of getting some raised beds too—easier to manage and less backbreaking. Do you think that’s a good idea? I think so. I’ve seen a few people using them and they seem to work well. It might be harder on the knees, but easier on the overall garden work. Plus, it makes it easier to keep the soil warm and avoid weeds. Exactly. I also heard that raised beds can help with drainage, which is important if the soil is too heavy or wet. I think the key is to figure out what kind of soil we’ll have and how to prepare it properly. Yeah, I’ve read that you can add compost and some organic matter to improve the soil. I think we should check what the allotment has already in terms of soil quality, but I imagine it could use a bit of help.

So, do you know what’s up with Lucy? I haven’t seen her in ages. She’s been like... vanishing. Yeah, I know. I asked her last week, and she just said she’s “busy with stuff.” I mean, it’s been like three months. Hasn’t she even tried to get in touch? I tried messaging her a few times, but she just ignores it. I mean, we were like, inseparable last year. It’s weird, isn’t it? Yeah, it’s strange. I think she’s just been too caught up with her new job or something. I heard she got a part-time gig at that café near the uni. Maybe she’s been working too much? Maybe. But I’m not sure. I mean, she used to text me every day. Now it’s like she’s just... gone. I don’t even know if she’s still in Doncaster. You know, I was thinking, maybe she’s moved back to Cambridge? I mean, her family’s still there, and she always said she’d like to live closer to her parents. That could be. I mean, I haven’t heard from her parents either. Maybe they’re the ones who’ve been keeping her busy. But I feel like I’m missing out on something. Like, I don’t even know if she’s still friends with everyone. I know, right? I mean, we’re still in touch with most of the group, but Lucy just... disappeared. I wonder what’s going on with her. Maybe she’s going through something? Maybe. But I don’t know about her. I mean, sometimes people just... change. You know? Like, they get into different things, or they meet new people, or they just lose touch. Yeah, I guess. But it still feels like a big deal. I mean, we were all so close before. I was really hoping we’d still be in touch. You know, maybe we should try to catch up with her. Maybe she’s just been busy and we’ve just not tried hard enough. Yeah, that’s true. Maybe we should message her together. Or go and see her in person if she’s still around. I mean, I really miss her. She was always the one who kept us all together. I know. I miss her too. Maybe we should plan something.

So, do you play any games? I’ve been trying to get into the new FIFA, but it’s like... I don’t know, it’s just so complicated. I can’t even figure out how to get past the first level. Oh, you’re not trying the right one. You should stick to something like Stardew Valley or something. It’s chill, you know? You don’t have to worry about real life or anything. Just farming and talking to villagers. Yeah, I do that. It’s like my version of therapy. But I’ve also been playing some of these like,  Fortnite  or  Valorant  with my mates. It’s wild. Sometimes we get so caught up, we forget to eat. That’s how I got my first D on a test. I was playing  Call of Duty  all night, and the next morning I was like, “Oh, I just need to do this one thing.” And then I realized it was like,  three  things. I can relate. I was doing that with  Among Us  last week. I thought I was being super clever, but then I got caught, and my friend just laughed and said, “You’re literally a red flag.” Mate, you’re just not paying attention. It’s not like you’re the first person to get caught. It’s all part of the game. Yeah, but I also just got into this new game called  Elden Ring  and it’s like, I don’t even know where to start. It’s got all these fancy words and sword fighting and giant monsters. It’s like a dream. I tried to play that too, but I got stuck in a cave and had to ask my mate for hints. He was like, “Just go to the left, you idiot.” Oh, I did that once. I was trying to go right, and then all of a sudden I was in this huge castle with a dragon. I was like, “Oh, this is a boss fight,” and then I died. That sounds like a  Final Fantasy  moment. You know, the kind where you’re goin’ on a quest, and then you get so far, and then you die, and then you go back to the beginning. Exactly! I think that’s the point. It’s like, you’re forced to level up and learn your lessons. But I also think I’ve got a chance to do something cool with this.

I just watched this film called  The Favourite  and I thought it was absolutely brilliant. I mean, it’s got such a strong story and the performances are just... I don’t know, it really grabbed me. Oh, I’ve heard about that one. I think it’s one of those films that’s been getting a lot of hype, isn’t it? I’ve been meaning to see it. Did you like it? I did. The way they portrayed the characters was so interesting. I mean, you feel for them, even when they’re doing really bad things. It’s not just like, “Oh, they’re villains,” it’s more about the complexity of their relationships. That’s a good point. I guess it’s not one of those films where the characters are just good or bad. It’s more nuanced. I think I’ll have to watch it soon. Do you know if it’s on any streaming services? I think it’s on Amazon Prime. I saw it there. I rented it, actually. It was a bit of a splurge, but I thought it was worth it. I mean, with the way the world is right now, sometimes you need to get lost in something like that. Yeah, I can see that. I’ve been meaning to watch more films like that. I’ve been really busy with work, though. I’m a production controller, so I’m always juggling deadlines and meetings. It’s hard to find time for anything else. I know the feeling. I’ve had a lot on my plate too, but I still try to make time for things that make me feel good. You know, it’s about balance. I think I’ve been trying to get back into watching films more. Maybe I’ll take you to see one of them. That would be great. I’d love that. I’ve been talking to my sister about going to a film festival, but I haven’t found the time. Maybe we can plan something. You know what? We could. I’ve been thinking about going to a local cinema in Cambridge. There’s a few places that show indie films and stuff. You might like that. That sounds perfect. I go to the cinema sometimes, but I always end up seeing the same old blockbusters. It’s nice to try something different.

So, do you know what’s up with the board games? I’ve been trying to get us together for like weeks, and no one’s even brought up playing anything. I’ve got this new one,  Clue , that I think we’d all like. Yeah, I’ve been meaning to ask you about that. I heard it was a bit of a classic. But actually, I’ve been so busy with this interview I had yesterday. It was a nightmare. Oh, you had an interview? What was it for? It was for a magazine article I’m writing. It’s about people who’ve been on  The Undateables . I’ve been trying to get some real stories, but honestly, most of the people I spoke to were just… not interesting. I mean, the show’s pretty chaotic, but some of those stories are honestly gold. Like that guy who said he’d been a vegan for three years and then admitted he just didn’t like meat. It’s the kind of thing people actually remember. Yeah, I know, but it’s hard to get people to open up. They’re either too shy or too embarrassed. I’ve got this one guy who said he was a vegetarian but got really defensive when I asked about it. He said, “I’m not just avoiding meat, I’m avoiding guilt.” It was so weird. Ooh, you’re writing about  The Undateables ? That’s cool. I’ve been trying to get my friends to watch it. I think it’s the only dating show that doesn’t make me want to throw something at the screen. I know, right? Everyone else is just the same old: “I’m looking for a partner, not a roommate.” But  The Undateables  is like, “I’m looking for a partner, and I’ve got a PhD in how to be awkward.” I think that was the one comment that actually stuck with me. It was from a girl who said she didn’t like talking about her job, but when I asked what she did, she told me she was an editor. I said, “That’s amazing. What kind of stuff do you edit?” And she said, “Oh, just boring stuff like articles and stuff.” You know what’s even more boring than that? Trying to get people to talk about their  real  jobs. Exactly!

So, do you know what’s going on with the washing machine? I’ve been trying to get it to work all day and it’s just not cooperating. It’s like it’s possessed or something. Oh no, really? I thought you were just being dramatic. You know how those things can be. My friend’s washing machine once decided it didn’t want to spin anymore and just sat there like a broken robot. I had to call a plumber just to get it to work again. Yeah, it’s not that dramatic, but it’s really frustrating. I was trying to do a load of laundry for the weekend and it just  clicked  and then nothing. No water, no spinning, no lights. It’s like it’s holding its breath. That sounds more like a ghost than a machine. But hey, I’ve seen stranger things. Like that time I was staying with my aunt and her washing machine started humming at 3 a.m. and then she said it was the ghost of her ex-husband. I didn’t believe her, but I definitely didn’t want to stay the night. Oh, I’ve heard about that. You know, the one that only works on Fridays? My mum used to say that if you leave it on for too long, it’ll start singing opera. I don’t know, maybe there’s some truth to that. I’m starting to think my washing machine might be trying to tell me something. Maybe it’s trying to tell you it’s time for a break. You know, like a little vacation from doing laundry. I’ve had it with folding clothes. I think I’ve got a new hobby now—collecting socks. You know, about 300 of them. Some are even still in pairs. That’s not a hobby, that’s a disorder. But I get it. I’ve started doing the same. I’ve got socks in every color and size, and I’m just waiting for the day I’ll find the matching one for the grey one with the hole in the toe. You know what I just remembered? There was this film I watched last year called  The Washing Machine . It’s about a haunted appliance that takes over a house and starts washing the owners’ clothes in the middle of the night. It’s not scary, but it made me rethink my entire relationship with laundry.

I just can’t believe how much the house prices have gone up since I retired. I mean, I thought I’d be able to sell my old place in Dublin and find something reasonable in the North, but it's like trying to hit a moving target. I know, it’s crazy. I mean, I’ve been working from home for the last few years and I still can’t afford to buy a house in the South. I keep telling myself I’ll just rent forever, but even that’s costing a fortune now. Yeah, I agree. I was in the oil industry for years, and I thought I’d be set for life. Now, I’m out of work, and I can’t even think about buying a house. I’m just trying to scrape by on benefits and see if I can find a way to get back into something. It’s not just the housing market, it’s the whole system. I remember when I was in teaching, the pressure to buy a house was always there, even for people like me. And now, with the VW scandal and the way the economy’s going, it feels like everything’s in chaos. I think the VW scandal has done a lot to erode people’s trust in big companies. I mean, it’s one thing for a car company to make a mistake, but the way they covered it up and the impact on the environment and the people who bought the cars—it’s just so scandalous. And don’t get me started on the way the government handled it. I mean, they tried to paint it as a technical issue, but the truth is, it was a massive cover-up. People started questioning everything about the company, and even the way the media reported on it. Exactly. It’s like the whole thing was a big conspiracy. And now, people are more cynical than ever. I’ve got a friend who’s been trying to buy a house in the South for years. He told me he’s just waiting for the market to crash so he can get a good deal, but I don’t know if that’s going to happen. I hear you. I’ve been reading a lot about housing in the North versus the South. It’s like the South is on another planet when it comes to prices.

I don’t know, I just feel like I’ve been grumbling about the same things for years. The pension system, the housing, the computers—how do you even use them anymore? It’s all so complicated. You’re not the only one, you know. I tried to get my benefits sorted last week, and I swear the woman on the phone thought I was trying to scam them. She asked me to confirm my National Insurance number three times. I said, “Yes, yes, I know it,” and she still didn’t believe me. It’s like we’re all suspects. I had to go to the library just to fill out a form. The librarian said I needed to bring in my photo ID, which I don’t have. I left it in the house somewhere, and I haven’t found it yet. I’ve been sitting in the car for an hour, just waiting for someone to call me back. That’s not fair. I used to be a civil engineer, for God’s sake. I used to design buildings, not fill out forms. I mean, do you think I know how to use a tablet? I can open the camera, that’s about it. Everything else is like learning a new language. I tried to teach my wife how to use the computer. She got so frustrated, she just walked out. I’ve been trying to explain it to her for weeks, and now she won’t even look at the screen. She just says, “I’d rather stay in bed and watch telly.” That’s not a bad idea, honestly. I’ve been in bed all morning. The heat’s been so bad, and I don’t want to get up. I think I’ll just stay here all week. I’ve had enough of this weather. I’m with you. I’ve been in bed for three days. My daughter texted me and said, “Dad, are you still alive?” I told her, “Yes, I’m alive, just very disappointed in life.” She laughed, but honestly, I think she was just trying to make me feel better. I think we’re all just waiting for the next government to fix things. I mean, it’s not like we’re asking for much. Just a bit of dignity, a bit of respect, and maybe a bit of help with the technology.

So, do you guys remember that video we saw last week about that guy who claimed he could lift a car with just his bare hands? I mean, it looked fake, but it went viral anyway. Yeah, I remember. I thought it was a trick at first, like maybe he was using some kind of hidden support or something. But then I saw the comments—some people were actually convinced he did it. That’s the thing with the internet, right? If something gets a lot of views, people just go along with it. It doesn’t matter if it’s true or not. I guess it’s just because people like to believe in the extraordinary, you know? Like, they want to think there are people out there who can do impossible things. It’s kind of like the whole “American Dream” thing, but more dramatic. That’s true. I think it’s also about the thrill of the unknown. People are always looking for something to believe in, especially when they’re bored or looking for a laugh. Yeah, but sometimes it’s just about ego. Those people who post things like that—they don’t just want to be seen as funny or interesting. They want to be seen as special, or even genius. I mean, who wouldn’t want to be considered a genius? It’s a pretty cool label. Especially if you don’t actually have to do anything to get it. Exactly. It’s kind of like someone who starts a TikTok account and gets a million followers just because they’re doing weird things with their face. It’s not about the skill, it’s about the spectacle. Haha, I guess you’re right. But sometimes I wonder if those people even know what they’re doing. Like, they just start doing stuff and then it blows up. It’s kind of scary to think that someone’s whole identity could be built on something that might not even be real. I think that’s the danger of the internet, though. Everyone has a platform now, so the line between reality and fiction is getting thinner. People don’t even notice when something isn’t real anymore. That’s why I think it’s so important to think critically about what we see online. I mean, if you don’t question it, you could end up believing in things that aren’t even true.

So, how’s the new house coming along? I know you’ve been working on it for ages. It’s coming along, yeah. I’ve been doing a few bits and pieces, but honestly, it’s not easy with the budget I’ve got. I remember when I was your age, I used to paint the whole house myself. No help at all. Aye, but you were in a lot better shape then, Pat. You could carry a can of paint and a ladder without breaking a sweat. That’s true. I can barely lift a bag of groceries these days. I know, I’ve been trying to get the MOT done for my car, but the garage’s been so slow. I’m terrified I’ll get a fine if I don’t get it done soon. You’re not the only one. I’ve been trying to get mine done for weeks, and they just keep putting it off. Aye, and I had to get new tyres for mine last week, and it cost more than I expected. I thought the MOT would be cheaper, but no. I was thinking about getting my car checked over too, just to be safe. I’ve been meaning to, but I keep putting it off. You should do it soon, honestly. I don’t want to be stuck in a situation where I can’t drive because of someone else’s mistake. That’s the thing, isn’t it? We all know the rules, but sometimes we don’t follow through. Yeah, especially when it’s about money. I know I’ve had a few problems with my old job, and I just don’t want to be caught short again. I remember when I was your age, I used to work like a dog. Now I just want to enjoy the weekends without stressing about bills or deadlines. I hear you. I’ve been getting a bit too caught up in work lately. I’ve been thinking about taking some time off, but I’m not sure if I can afford it. You know, I think the best thing you can do is make sure you’ve got a few extra savings tucked away. You never know when life will throw you a curveball. Exactly. I’ve been planning to take up acupuncture, you know, to help with the back pain.

Alright, do you know what slavery was? I think it was when people were forced to work for others, right? Yes, exactly. People were taken from their homes and made to work in terrible conditions, often without pay. It happened a long time ago, but it’s still a big part of history. Was it only in Africa? No, it wasn’t just in Africa. People from all over the world were enslaved, including from Europe, the Middle East, and even parts of Asia. But the most well-known form of slavery was the transatlantic slave trade, where millions of Africans were taken to the Americas to work on plantations. That must have been really sad. I mean, not having a choice to do what you wanted? Exactly. It was a system of extreme oppression. People were treated as property, not as humans. They were beaten, forced to work for long hours in dangerous conditions, and sometimes even killed. How did they get from Africa to the Americas? They were taken on ships, often in extremely overcrowded conditions. The journey was very dangerous, and many people died on the way. These ships were called slave ships, and it was a brutal part of history. I can’t imagine how scary that must have been. It was. But there were also people who fought against slavery. Some countries, like Britain, eventually abolished the slave trade. It was one of the biggest social changes in history. So slavery isn’t just something from the past? No, it still exists in some parts of the world today. Although it’s illegal, there are still people who are forced into slavery, often through things like debt bondage or forced labor. It’s something we still need to work on. That’s really sad. I wish we could do more to stop it. We can. By learning about it, talking about it, and supporting organisations that help people who are still enslaved. It’s important to remember the past so we can make sure it never happens again. I think it’s really important for us to know these things, especially if we’re learning in school. I agree. Understanding history helps us understand the world today and the struggles that people have faced. That’s why it’s so important to talk about it, even with kids. Yeah, I think it’s something we should all be aware of.

I just watched the new series of  Sherlock , and I have to say, it's absolutely brilliant. Benedict Cumberbatch is just so charismatic. I’m so glad they brought back the show after all these years. Yeah, I agree. I think it's one of the best adaptations of the stories. I mean, the way they've modernized it is really clever. But tell me, have you seen the new  Doctor Who  season? I’ve been dying to watch it, but I keep putting it off. I did watch it! It was okay, but I think the pacing was a bit off. The new actor as the Doctor is good, but I found the first few episodes a bit confusing. I still prefer the older versions. Though I have to admit, the new storyline was interesting. I’ve been meaning to catch up with  Doctor Who  as well. I’ve got the whole series on DVD, but I’m just not in the mood to sit through five episodes in one go. I think I’ll start with the more recent ones. I don’t get into TV that much anymore. I mean, I used to love it when I was working in catering. I’d go on breaks and watch the latest shows. But now, I just stick to the classics. I still watch  Monty Python  every now and then. It’s like therapy for me. That’s a great idea. Maybe we should all set up a movie night this weekend. We could get some snacks and watch a few of our favourite shows. I think it would be a nice way to catch up and relax. That sounds like a plan. I could bring some popcorn and maybe a couple of my old DVDs. I still have that  Friends  box set from when I was in college. It’s like a time capsule. I have a few  Friends  episodes on my phone. I can stream them. Though I have to be careful not to watch too much; I might end up staying up too late. I’m good with that. I’ve got a lot of time on my hands these days. If I do anything, it’s usually reading or trying to get back into some sort of hobby. I’ve been thinking of taking up photography again. Photography? You’re not going to start that now.

Alright, right, we've got to unload the dishwasher, haven't we? Yeah, I was just about to say that. I’m so tired of putting dishes in and then just leaving them there. I don’t even know how to use the dishwasher. I just put the plates in and hope for the best. Well, it’s not that hard. You’ve got to separate the plates, cutlery, and glasses. And don’t forget to put the little trays in the bottom. Oh, right! The little trays – I always forget those. They’re like the ones that go under the plates to catch any water or stuff. Yeah, I’ve seen those. They’re like the ones that go in the bottom of the dishwasher, and then you put the plates on top. It’s like a whole system. Exactly. It’s a bit like a kitchen in a way. You’ve got to keep everything organized, or it’s a mess. It’s like the Hogwarts kitchen, maybe? I mean, not really, but if you think about it, the dishes are all in one place, and there’s a magical way to clean them. Yeah, maybe – but I still don’t think the dishwasher actually does the work. It’s just a big machine. Silly. It’s got magic in it. Like, you put in the dishes, push a button, and they come out clean. It’s like the magic of the modern world. I think the real magic is George Stephenson. You know, the guy who invented the first steam engine. That’s real magic. Oh yeah, George Stephenson was a legend. He was the father of the railways. You know, he built the first locomotive that actually worked. I think he was called the “Rocket,” wasn’t he? No, that was a later one. The first one was called the  Locomotion No. 1 . And it was a complete disaster at first. It took the whole team three hours just to get it to travel a mile. That sounds like a real struggle. I wonder how they even made it work in the first place. Well, it was a lot of trial and error. But Stephenson was really determined. He believed in the power of steam and the potential of rail travel. Sounds like he’s like a wizard with engines. Yeah, maybe. He was a true pioneer.

Alright, so I was just talking to my brother-in-law about different metals and fabrics for a project I’m working on. You know, like how they’re used in different ways. Oh, really? So, do you know what’s happening with the heating? It’s like we’re living in a freezer in here. I don’t know how we’re supposed to study with this. Yeah, I know, it’s so cold. So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to get really excited about Christmas, even though we didn’t have much? I swear, every year it felt like the biggest event of the year. So, do you know much about Northern Cyprus? I mean, I’ve heard a lot about it through the news, but I’m not really sure about the details. Not sure? It’s a nice place to live, even if it’s a bit of a political mess. I can imagine. I mean, if you like the sea and the beach, I can see why someone would want to live there.

It’s frustrating. I mean, we talk about it in the office, and we both know we should do more, but it’s hard to make a difference when the system is so messed up. I was thinking about our friends who came to visit last month. They said they missed the air, the clean sky, the way you could actually see the stars at night. And now, I can barely even see the moon. Yeah, that’s what worries me. We’ve always loved being out at night, walking, chatting, just being in the open. It’s like we’re losing that. I was also thinking about the way people here treat the environment. I mean, I know it’s a big city, but I feel like there’s a lack of awareness. People don’t even seem to care about what they throw away, or how much they use. I think it’s a mix of things. There’s the pollution from the factories, the traffic, and then the mindset—people just don’t think about it as much because it’s so ingrained in the way the city runs. It’s hard not to feel helpless. I know that we can make a difference, but sometimes it feels like we’re just a drop in the ocean. I know. But I think we can start small. Maybe if we encourage our friends to do more, or even just start with our own habits. Like, not using single-use plastics, or recycling properly. Yeah, that makes sense. I mean, if we start with ourselves, it could ripple out. I’ve been trying to do that already, like carrying a reusable bottle and avoiding plastic bags. That’s a good start. And I’ve been thinking of starting a small sustainability group in the department.

I think I've got the ingredients all ready for tonight, so we can start cooking. Do you think we should make something simple or go for something a bit more special? I think simple might be better, especially since we all had a long day. But if you're up for it, we could make a nice stir-fry with some veggies and noodles. I reckon it's quick and easy. A stir-fry sounds great! I’ve got some frozen veggies in the freezer and some leftover rice from yesterday. Maybe we could add some chicken or tofu for protein? That sounds like a good plan. I’ve been wanting to start a food blog, and I think these kinds of meals would be perfect for it. It’s not like we have to be perfect, just real and colorful. That's a great idea.
