Still, I think it’s a nice way to document the day. I’m up for it. Just don’t expect me to be the one holding the camera.

So, do you know about the new bus route they're planning to start from here? I heard they’re talking about running it through the university area. Yeah, I remember hearing something about that. I think they’re trying to make it easier for students to get around. But I’ve also heard some people are worried about the route—like, it might cut through some quieter streets. Oh, right, I think that’s what’s causing the controversy. Some people are concerned about noise and traffic. But then again, if it makes commuting easier for students, maybe it’s a good thing. I guess it depends on how it’s managed. I mean, Cambridge is such a hub for students, so having better transport links is definitely something the city needs. But I wonder how they’ll handle the pushback from local residents. I heard there was a protest last week about it. Some students were trying to get the university to support the route, but others were against it, saying it’s just another way for the city to expand and ignore the needs of the local community. Yeah, I can see both sides. On one hand, the bus route could help reduce the number of cars on the road. On the other, it might just be adding to the congestion in a different way. True. I mean, I’m not sure if it’s the solution they’re looking for. Maybe they should be focusing on better cycling infrastructure instead? I think the university has been talking about expanding bike lanes. That’s a good point. I’ve seen more people using bikes here recently. I mean, it’s not perfect, but it’s better than nothing. I think the key is finding a balance between transport, sustainability, and community needs. Speaking of which, have you been to the Cambridge University Press bookshop? I went there the other day, and it was absolutely packed. I bought a few books on linguistics, but there was a student protester outside with a sign that said something like “Knowledge for All, Not Just the Elite.” Oh, I’ve seen that sign before. I think it’s part of a wider movement around campus. Some students are pushing for more affordable access to academic resources, especially since the university has been raising tuition fees. Yeah, I can see why they’d be upset.

So, do you think we should go to the new café in Cheshire? I hear the food’s quite good. I’ve heard about it, actually. It’s a bit of a walk from here, but the reviews are pretty positive. I think it’s worth a try. I’m up for it, honestly. It’s been a while since we had a proper lunch out. I’ve been working from home too much lately. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s nice to get out and do something for a change. Although, I still can’t believe I’ve been retired for a month already. Time flies. I know, it’s surreal. Being at home all day, not having to get up early or deal with the stress of the office. You’d think it’d be easier, but the silence is quite hard to adjust to. I can imagine. You used to be so busy, and now you have all this time on your hands. I’m still working full-time, so I don’t have that luxury. I know, and I’m not complaining. I’m enjoying the freedom. But I do miss the routine, to be honest. It’s strange not having a morning rhythm anymore. I can see that. I often think about how I used to structure my day, but now I just kind of drift from one thing to the next. It’s a bit confusing at times. I think it’s just a transition. I mean, I’m sure you’ll get used to it. And besides, you have your family and friends to keep you busy. I’ve had a few calls from my parents today about how I’m doing. Oh, my kids are great. They call every Sunday. I always get that ‘how are you?’ message, and then they tell me all about their lives. It’s nice, honestly. They’re growing up so fast. I can relate. My brother just had a baby, so I’ve been helping out with the baby-sitting and everything. It’s surprising how quickly life changes. That’s true. I remember when I was that age, I thought I had all the time in the world. Now it’s like time is flying by. I suppose that’s the way it is. But I think it’s important to make the most of it.

I can't believe we've walked all this way from Woolwich. I thought it’d be a bit easier once we got to the river, but it’s like walking through a dream—so peaceful, yet so long. Yeah, I know, it’s a bit of a trek, but the view is worth it. You can see the whole of London from here if you look up. Though I don’t know how many people actually do that anymore. Most just take photos of the O2 Arena and call it a day. I mean, the O2 is impressive, but it’s not exactly a landmark. It’s more of a modern tourist trap. Besides, the real landmarks are the ones that have been here for centuries, like the Tower of London or the Houses of Parliament. They’ve got history, you know? That’s true, but then again, the O2 doesn’t have car parking, and I’ve got this thing about not owning a car. It makes me feel like I’m always being left behind. I mean, how do people actually get around without one? You know, I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately. I’ve got a few friends who’ve managed to live without cars, but it’s not easy. I’d love to go on holiday with my family without one, but I can’t imagine it. We’d end up stranded somewhere, or worse—having to take the train for hours just to get to a beach. I’ve actually been thinking about that too. Maybe next year, we could go somewhere that’s a bit more accessible. Like the Lake District or the Scottish Highlands. There’s no need for a car in those places, right? You just walk or take a bus. That sounds nice. But I can’t help but think about the philosophical side of it. If we don’t own a car, do we become more connected to the world? Or do we just become more dependent on others? Like, do we lose a sense of independence? Hmm, that’s a good point. I think it’s a bit of both. You’re always relying on public transport or friends to get you around, but at the same time, you’re not as caught up in the rush of the city. You really get to see things more slowly.

I can't believe it's already raining again. I was just going to go out for a run, but now I might as well stay in and watch a film. I know, it's been like that all week. I was hoping the weather would break by now, but no luck. I guess it’s just one of those dry spells that won’t end. Yeah, I don’t mind the rain, honestly. I think it helps keep the kids inside, which gives me a break. Although, if it’s going to keep raining like this, I might need to start planning for the children’s sports day. Oh, don’t forget about the sports day. I was thinking about that yesterday. It’s only a few weeks away, and I still haven’t got the list of activities sorted. I feel like I’ve been putting it off for too long. I know, I’ve been trying to get the details from the school, but they’re being really vague. I’m not even sure if they’ve confirmed the date yet. I hope it’s not too late to change the plans. I’m not sure either. But as long as the kids are having fun, I think it’ll be fine. I just hope it doesn’t rain on the day. I remember last year when it rained, and we had to move everything inside. It turned into a kitchen party, and the kids were still having a great time. That’s true. They always enjoy the activities, even if they’re not outdoors. It just makes it harder on us, trying to set up everything in the kitchen. I know, but it’s not all bad. I did get a few nice photos of the kids playing in the kitchen. I think I’ll frame one of them. It was such a silly moment, but it’s a reminder of how much fun they have. Definitely. I think I’ll take some photos too. Maybe even a few of the cuddly toys. I’ve been thinking about getting a new one for the kids. I saw a build-a-bear online, and it’s just adorable. Oh, I’ve seen those. The kids love them. I think it’s a great idea. They go through so many toys, and it’s nice to have something they can personalise.

So, do you think we should actually talk about what we want to do next? I mean, we’re here in Australia, and it’s been a while since we’ve properly discussed where we’re headed. I feel like we’ve both been going through a lot lately, and it’s time we sat down and planned properly. I agree. It’s been a bit of a blur, honestly. Between work, the house-sitting, and just trying to make ends meet, I haven’t really thought about what’s next. But now that we’re here, and this place feels like a real break, maybe it’s time we actually start setting some goals. Yeah, and I’ve been thinking about it a lot. My business is doing well, but I feel like I’m not quite there yet. I want to expand a bit more, maybe take on some new projects. But I also know that if I don’t get my priorities right, I’ll just be running on autopilot. That makes sense. I’ve been thinking about my career too. If we combine our strengths, we could make something really special. That’s a nice thought. But I also want to think about family planning. I’ve been feeling like it’s time to start thinking about having a child, or at least seriously discussing it. It’s something I’ve put off for a while because of work and the uncertainty of where we’re going. I completely understand. I’ve been thinking about that too. With the way things are going, it feels like the right time to settle down a bit more. I’ve been getting a lot of offers for business ventures that could take us out of Australia, but I think we both need to be in a place where we feel stable before making those kinds of moves. Yeah, I think that’s exactly it.

So, do you reckon we should be able to tell where people are from just by their accent? I mean, I got this weird feeling when I was in Leeds the other week, like I was in a different country. Yeah, I know what you mean. I can tell when someone’s from Wigan just by the way they say “chips” instead of “crisps.” It’s like a whole different dialect. I don’t even know if I can tell anymore. I’ve been hanging out with Leeds girls so much, I’m starting to think I’ve picked up some of their ways. Oh no, you’re not. You still say “sporran” the right way. You’ve got that Warrington drawl. You’re just trying to be mean. I’ve been trying to get into the Leeds accent for weeks. I even watched a YouTube video on how to sound like a local. That’s not how it works. You can’t just shout words louder and call it an accent. It’s more about the rhythm, the way you stress words. And the way you say “football.” Like, “Foot…ball,” with that extra pause. It’s got to be the most pretentious thing I’ve ever heard. Oh come on, that’s just how we say it. You don’t even know what a “sporran” is, for goodness’ sake. I do. I read about it in a book. It’s that wee pouch that men wear. You know, like the one with the tartan? I did know that. I just don’t think the English need to take it too seriously. I mean, I’ve seen some people trying to be more “authentic” by wearing tartan and using Gaelic words. It’s kind of funny. I think it’s a bit of a badge of honour. Like, if you can speak like a local, you’re part of the community. But it’s not about being a local. It’s about being genuine. I mean, you don’t have to be from Leeds to be a real Leeds person. Exactly. And I think that’s what’s so cool about this place. We all come from different backgrounds, but we can all still talk like we’re from the same town. Yeah, but I think some people overdo it. I saw this guy in the bar last week trying to tell us about the local legends.

Well, I've just had a look at the post, and I think we've got a bit of a problem with the next-door bloke. He’s been making all sorts of noise again, especially in the evenings. I don’t know how he can stand it, being so close to the road. Oh dear, I’ve heard him too. It’s quite alarming, actually. I thought maybe it was just the wind or something, but no, it’s definitely him. And it’s not just the noise—there’s also the smell. I don’t know what he’s been cooking, but it’s not exactly pleasant. Honestly, I don’t know how the council can still let people live like that. My lectures are all online these days, so I’m not really disturbed by it, but I do feel for the people who are trying to relax at home. It must be so frustrating. I can only imagine. I mean, I’ve been in lectures all day, so I haven’t had much of a chance to hear the noise. But I would hate to live in a place like that. It’s not a good environment for anyone. It’s not just the noise, though. I’ve also noticed there are quite a few spiders in the garden. I’ve seen them in the bushes and even near the gate. I don’t know if it’s the weather or something else, but they’re everywhere now. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve had a few in my garden too. I even had one in the kitchen the other day. I was about to call the pest control, but then I thought, maybe it’s just a sign of good luck or something. I don’t know. I think it’s more likely to be a sign of a damp problem or something. I mean, the weather has been so wet this year. My house is fine, but I’ve heard that some people are having issues with damp and mold. Maybe it’s a combination of all that. I suppose that makes sense. We had quite a few rain showers over the last few weeks. It’s been a bit of a damp year. I do wonder how the council deals with these things. I mean, if the noise is a problem, then it should be addressed.

So, do you think I should drop out of uni? Why would you even think about that? You’ve got a good degree, you’re not doing bad, and you’ve got a good support system here. I know, but I just feel like I’m not really enjoying it. Every time I think about the lectures, I just get this panic. It’s like, I don’t even know why I’m here. Oh, I get that. I still remember the first day of lectures—my shoes were covered in mud, and I was trying to figure out where the toilets were. I didn’t even think about it, and by the time I got to uni, my feet were like a combination of puddle and mud. That’s brutal. I feel like I’ve got the same problem with my shoes. I just can’t be bothered to clean them, and now they’re so dirty, I don’t even want to wear them. You’re not alone. It’s just one of those things. If you’re already in a situation where you’re stressed out, the last thing you want to do is clean your shoes. I guess. But I still don’t know if uni is for me. I mean, I love the idea of it, but the reality is just so overwhelming. I don’t even know what I’m studying for. Wait, you know what you’re studying for? I think so. But I’m not sure if I’m actually interested in it anymore. I just feel like I’m going through the motions. That’s what I thought at first. I remember my first year, I was like, “I don’t want to do this.” But then I started to find the stuff I was learning interesting, even if it wasn’t everything. Yeah, but it’s like I’m not even getting the chance to really explore what I’m into. I feel like I’m just getting the basics, and then it all just gets thrown at me.

I can't believe it's been so long since we last saw each other. It feels like ages. How have you been? Oh, honestly, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. Work has been hectic, and I've been trying to figure out what I want to do next. I'm kind of stuck between wanting to move forward and just wanting to stay put. I totally get that. I've been in the same boat. I've been thinking a lot about my future as well. I've been considering moving to another city for a new job opportunity. That sounds exciting. Have you found anything yet? Not officially, but I’ve been in touch with a few people from my network. I’m hoping to hear back soon. I’m really looking forward to it, but it’s been a bit stressful trying to make the decision. I can imagine. I’ve been trying to work on my own projects too. It’s been hard not having a clear path, but I think it’s making me more determined. That’s good to hear. I think sometimes the uncertainty can be a good thing. It pushes you to think about what you really want. Yeah, I guess it does. I mean, I’ve always been a bit of a planner, but now I’m realizing that some things just can’t be planned. You have to be flexible. Definitely. I’ve been trying to be more open to change. It’s also made me think a lot about my habits. I’ve definitely been working a lot, and I haven’t been taking care of myself as much as I should. Same here. I’ve been trying to get back into the habit of regular exercise and eating better. I’ve been going to the gym a couple of times a week, but I haven’t been consistent. That’s great. I’ve started going to yoga classes on the weekends. It’s helping me unwind and focus on my mental health. That sounds amazing. I should really try that. I’ve always been a bit intimidated by yoga, but I think it would be good for me. It’s not as hard as you think. It’s more about the breath and being present. It’s a great way to disconnect from work and just be in the moment.

Right, so I just got an email from Amazon saying they’re going to be delivering this new set of cookware I ordered next Wednesday. Cool, I got a few things on Amazon too, but I’m not sure if I should trust them. Why not? I mean, they’re pretty reliable, aren’t they? I guess, but sometimes the delivery takes ages. I ordered this game console last week and it’s still not here. Oh, that’s frustrating. I got my new tablet in two days, though. Yeah, but I’m worried about the price. I mean, I found the same thing on eBay for a bit cheaper. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve bought a few things on eBay before. Some of the sellers are really good, but others are dodgy. Yeah, I read some reviews before I bought, but sometimes people don’t tell you everything. That’s the thing with online shopping, isn’t it? You don’t know what you’re getting until it arrives. Exactly. I think I’ll stick with Amazon for now, just to be safe. Fair enough. I’ve had a few problems with eBay, like fake items and poor customer service. I’ve seen some crazy stuff on there too. Last week, I saw someone selling a fake PlayStation 5 for almost half the price. Oh no, that’s a bit of a rip-off. I’d have been really upset if I’d bought that. Yeah, I wouldn’t have known it was fake until I tried it. It’s just so easy to fall into that trap. I think I’ll just keep using Amazon for now. Maybe. I guess it’s better to be safe than sorry. And if you ever want to try something on eBay, just make sure you check the reviews and the seller’s reputation. I’ll do that. I mean, I do like the cheaper prices, but I don’t want to end up with a dummy. You got it. It’s all about being careful online. Hopefully, I won’t have to pay for anything else. Well, I hope your game console arrives soon. I’m dying to play it. Yeah, I’m excited too. I’ve been waiting ages for it. I think we’re both in the same boat. Let’s just hope the delivery doesn’t take forever.

So, do you know what’s going on with the council? I’ve been trying to get some information about the housing scheme, but it’s all a bit of a mess. Yeah, I know, it’s been a nightmare. I tried to call them last week, but the line was down for hours. I finally got through, but they just said they were “undergoing system upgrades” and couldn’t give me any real details. Honestly, it’s all a bit of a farce. I know, I’ve been trying to apply for that new council flat for ages. You know, the one near the station. I mean, I’ve been waiting since the beginning of the year. It’s like they’re just dragging their feet. I can’t even get a proper response. You know, they kept saying I’d be contacted by email, but I’ve checked every day. No sign of anything. I’m starting to think they just don’t want to give out the flats to people like me. Yeah, I feel you. I mean, I’ve been out of work for years, and it’s really hard to find anything. You know, I’ve tried everything – job centres, agencies, even local shops. It’s like there’s no real help out there. It’s just… frustrating. I know, it’s really tough. I’ve been trying to manage as best as I can. I’ve got a job at the factory, but it's just part-time, and I’m always working extra hours just to make ends meet. I mean, what’s the point of working when the hours are so unpredictable? I can only imagine. You know, I did try to get a job at the local supermarket last month, but they said they didn’t need anyone else. They said they were “full.” I mean, how do they expect people to get by if they just keep saying that? It’s just so unfair. You know, I was thinking the other day – maybe I should try to get back into training? I’ve got a bit of a head start with the skills I’ve picked up over the years. I’ve been thinking about going back to college, maybe something in IT or something like that. I’ve heard that’s a good field. That’s a good idea. I mean, I’ve always said that education is the key to getting your foot in the door.

So, do you think we're actually going to get any snow for Christmas? I mean, it’s been like... barely any rain this year. I was just thinking about how we used to have proper snow when I was a kid. Not like this soggy mess. Yeah, I was just talking to my mum about that the other day. She said she remembers coming home from school in knee-deep snow every year. But I think this year’s too warm. Still, I’d love to have some snow for Christmas. We can have the traditional snowball fights and all that. Honestly, I’d rather have a bit of snow than roadkill deer, though. I had to deal with one last week on the way to work. It was like a giant, frozen, dead thing in the middle of the road. I almost hit it. Scared the pants off me. Oh no, really? That’s not nice. I remember when I was in Australia, we’d have kangaroos everywhere, but they didn’t cross the road like that. They’d just stand there and look at you like, “What are you doing?” Yeah, it’s weird how different it is. I mean, in London, we’ve got foxes running around the park. I saw one the other day with a baby. It was actually kinda cute, but I was like, “What if it comes into the flat?” Oh, don’t worry. They’re just curious. My gran used to say that if you leave out some bread, they’ll come sniffing. But you don’t want to feed them too much. They’re not pets, after all. I know, I’ve had to chase one off my café once. It had a mind of its own. Maybe that’s why it’s called a fox. It’s got a cunning mind. You know, I’ve always thought that if you feed a fox, it’s like saying, “Hey, I’m easy to catch.” I tried once, just out of curiosity. We had a good laugh. But then again, I’m not from here. I don’t know what the local rules are. I think the rules are, if you see a fox, go back to your room and close the door. That’s what my nan always said. She said that if you ever saw a fox in the house, your mum was going to be really upset.

So, do you think we’re gonna get a bad reception in Cambridge? I mean, it’s a bit of a drive from Birmingham, and I’m not sure how good my signal is on this old phone. Honestly, I wouldn’t worry about it. It’s only like an hour and a half drive, and we’ve got plenty of time to get there. Plus, I’m pretty sure the roads are all clear. Although, if we hit any traffic, I might have to start singing along to some cheesy 80s hits to keep me sane. That’s the spirit. You know, I’ve been thinking—do you ever notice how much people change the way they speak when they’re in different parts of the country? Like, I swear my accent’s shifted since I moved from London to Cambridge. Yeah, I get that. I was born in Birmingham, and even though I’ve lived in Manchester for a few years now, sometimes I catch myself slipping back into that Birmingham lilt. It’s weird how your accent follows you around, isn’t it? Absolutely. I’ve always loved that. I think accents are like a fingerprint—unique to each person and place. But then again, I also think it’s kind of funny how people from the same region can sound so different. Like, I’ve heard people from Birmingham and Manchester both claim to be the real “English” voice, but they all sound different to me. That’s true. I mean, someone from Cambridge probably sounds more posh than someone from, say, Bury St Edmunds. But I’d rather have a strong accent than a flat, unremarkable one. It’s part of who you are, right? Definitely. But I still can’t get over how much of a difference the car makes. I mean, I’ve driven this old car for years, and I just feel like it’s got this kind of “character.” It’s not fancy, but it’s reliable. Plus, it’s got that classic look that makes me feel like I’m in a movie. Yeah, I get that. I always liked old cars. They have that sort of charm that modern ones just don’t. But honestly, I’m a bit nervous about the drive. I’m not exactly a confident driver. Don’t worry, I’ll take the wheel. I’ve got a GPS, a playlist, and a backup plan if something goes wrong.

So, did you guys see the new Harry Potter movie? Yeah, I did. It was pretty good, but I thought the music was a bit off. Yeah, I agree. The soundtrack seemed like it was trying too hard to be dramatic. I mean, it’s Harry Potter, so you’d expect some epic music. But honestly, it felt a bit too modern for the vibe of the story. Totally. It was like they were trying to make it sound like a superhero movie instead of a magical one. I think they were trying to make it more accessible to a younger audience. You know, like how they changed the actors and everything. Yeah, but it lost some of the old magic for me. I mean, the original soundtrack was just perfect. I know, right? I still have that soundtrack on my phone. It’s like a throwback to the old days. I still have the original CD. I like to listen to it when I’m trying to focus on physics homework. Hey, did you guys hear about the new band that’s been playing at the school concerts? No, what’s their name? I think it’s called The Echoes. They’re really into indie rock and stuff. Yeah, they’re pretty good. I saw them last week at the talent show. They played this song that was like a mix of classic rock and something modern. Cool, I’d love to check them out. Alright, do you remember how we were talking about balanceability earlier? I think you said it’s like when you try to do something and you’re not sure if you’ll fall over. So, do you ever find it hard to balance work and relationships? I mean, I know it’s a common problem, but I’m just curious how you manage it. If the weather’s nice, we could go for a run in the park. That sounds perfect. I’ll let you know if I’m free. I’ll also try to make sure I actually go.

Alright, skipper, you've got your pizza, and I've got mine. You know, it's like a proper meal after that long drive. Yeah, it was a right proper drive, wasn’t it? I couldn’t believe how far we went. You know, I was thinking, you’ve got a lot of energy for a kid your age. Most of them would’ve been napping by now. Well, I like driving. It’s like my little adventure every week. Didn’t you get lost again, lad? I saw the map on your phone, and you were going in circles for half an hour. It wasn’t me, it was the sat nav. I swear, it thought we were going to the moon. Speaking of instincts, you still haven’t told me what you’re going to do after school. You know, future plans? I’m not sure yet. I’m just trying to figure it out. Maybe something with cars? Cars? You mean like mechanics or driving? Maybe both. I like the idea of fixing things and driving them. That’s good. You’ve always had a knack for that. I remember when you were little, you used to fix my old tractor. Yeah, that was fun. I didn’t know it was broken, I just thought it was part of the game. Aye, that’s how we all start. You stick your hand in and then…  blammo ! Something goes wrong. Well, I suppose the next step is you get a proper job. Not like that man in the village who tried to get a job as a mechanic and ended up working at the fish and chip shop. That bloke’s a legend. He used to tell us stories about the fish he used to catch. Aye, and he still talks like he’s in the middle of a storm. “Fish and chips, that’s the life!” he’d say. I’d like to be like him, in a way. Not the fish and chips, but the sense of adventure.

So, do you know what’s the best thing about Cambridge? The pubs. You can’t even walk five minutes without finding one. Yeah, I know, it’s like every other building is a pub or a café. I’ve been here a few months and I still haven’t seen them all. Honestly, I think I’ve been to more pubs in Cambridge than I have in my whole life before this. That’s not possible. You’ve been in Sunderland your whole life. Well, I mean, I’ve been to some good ones, but nothing like the variety here. I’ve even been to a pub that serves only vegetarian food. Oh, really? That’s interesting. I’ve tried a few vegetarian places around here, but I’ve never been to one that’s  only  vegetarian. Yeah, I mean, it’s not like they’re serving meat. I mean, I like vegetarian food, but I think there should be a little bit of meat on the menu. I guess. But I can see why they do it. It’s a way to promote healthier eating. Maybe, but I still think it’s a bit much. I mean, what if you want to have a beer with a burger? I get that. But I’d rather have a good vegetarian meal and a beer than a burger and no beer. I guess. I’m not trying to argue, just saying it’s a bit extreme. Yeah, I can see that. But it’s a reminder that there are some really cool places here. Like, I was in this tiny little pub the other day, and they had a vegan cheese board. A vegan cheese board? That’s something I would’ve never thought of. Yeah, it was amazing. It was all these different kinds of plant-based cheeses, with some fruit and nuts. It was like the most unusual thing I’ve ever had. That sounds fancy. I guess some of the food here is a bit different from what I’m used to. Definitely. I think it’s because there’s so many students and people from all over the world here. It kind of brings a mix of cultures into the food scene.

Alright, do you know how to play this game? I’ve only played it once before, and it was like... trying to guess a word with a group of people who all think they’re clever. It’s not that bad. Look, it’s basically like a game of charades but with words. You get a category, then you have to guess the word before your team runs out of time. Yeah, but the twist is you can only use the letters from the category. Like if the category is “foods,” you can only use letters from the word “foods” to guess the actual word. Oh, I get it now. So it’s like a word game that’s also a bit of a puzzle. Fun, but a bit confusing at first. Exactly. It’s not just about guessing. It’s about using logic and creativity. You almost have to think like a detective to crack it. That’s true. I remember one time, the category was “kinds of sports.” We had to guess “rugby” using only the letters in “sports.” I think we ended up spelling “sprots” by accident, and someone laughed so hard they almost fell off their chair. Oh, I remember that. You got the letters S, P, O, R, T, S. And somehow you ended up saying “sprots.” I still don’t know how you got that. It was a group effort. We all tried to think of different words. “Sport” was the obvious one, but we couldn’t use “sport” because it had to come from the category. So we had to think of a different word. I think we ended up guessing “rugs” because that was the closest we could get. And then we all laughed because we realized we’d made up a word that didn’t even exist. That’s the beauty of it. It’s not about being right, it’s about being creative. We all had such a good time. Yeah, and it’s not just about the game itself. It’s about the conversations you have while playing. Like, we started talking about how we used to play this game growing up. You know, I think I remember my cousin playing it with my dad. He always said it was the only way he could get me to speak without being forced. That makes sense. It’s like a way to engage without pressure.

Alright, let’s see… I’ve got a King of Hearts. That’s a good start, isn’t it? Yeah, but I’ve got a Queen of Spades. That’s a strong card too. I’ve got a seven of Clubs. Not much, but I’m hoping to pick up some higher cards. I’ve got… a two of Diamonds. Aww, not great. But I’m not here to win, I’m here to have fun. Yeah, and I bet you’re right about that. You’re always the one saying that. Still, I’ll take the two of Diamonds and hope for the best. Hey, I’m not saying I don’t want to win.
