Just me and my mates, maybe some pizza and a few drinks. Oh, do tell, what’s the prize? Well, not much. Just bragging rights for a week. Okay, that’s fair enough. But I’ve got a feeling I’m going to end up with the least amount of cards. You’re not the only one. I think we’re all in the same boat. Speaking of boats, have any of you seen the new boat that’s been moored at the local marina? No, I haven’t. What’s so special about it? I heard it’s a speedboat. And the owner said it’s faster than most. I don’t know if I believe that, but it’s definitely got a bit of a reputation. Oh, I heard that too. I think it was called  The Windy Lady . Sounds like something out of a movie. You know, I once knew someone who tried to race a speedboat. He ended up with a broken leg and a very expensive ticket to the hospital. Wow, that sounds like a disaster. I wouldn’t want to get into a race with that kind of boat. Yeah, I’d rather stick to the game. You know what they say – you can’t win if you’re not playing safe. Exactly. So let’s just focus on the cards and not the speedboats. Unless we start a new game… Oh, I like that idea. Let’s play again. Maybe we can all take it a bit more seriously this time.

So, do you think I should go to university or do an apprenticeship? Honestly, I think it depends on what you're interested in. If you like something practical, apprenticeships are a great option. But if you're into theory and want to study a subject you love, uni might be better. Yeah, I mean, I think it depends on your career goals too. Like, if you want to be an accountant, like me, you can do an apprenticeship, but you can also go to uni and get a degree. It’s just about what you want to do in the long run. I think I’d go to university, actually. I mean, I’m already working on my degree, and I feel like it’s helping me get closer to my goals. Plus, I get to study what I love – engineering. It’s not always easy, but it’s worth it. I’m a bit confused. I don’t know what I want to do, so I’m thinking about doing an apprenticeship first. It’s safer, I guess, and I can earn money while I learn. But I’m not sure if I’ll like it. Yeah, I can see that. I’m kind of leaning towards university too, but I’m scared about the debt. I mean, I heard it’s a big deal. I know, it’s a big decision. But I think if you’re passionate about what you’re studying, it’s worth it. Plus, a degree opens up so many doors. I think the key is to be clear about what you want. If you’re not sure, maybe do an apprenticeship first to get some experience. That way, you can figure out what you like before committing to a degree. Yeah, I think that makes sense. My sister did that. She worked for a few years before going to uni, and it helped her figure out what she wanted to study. I guess that’s a good idea. I mean, I’m not sure what I want to do with my life right now. I just know I don’t want to be stuck in a job I don’t like. That’s the main thing, isn’t it? You don’t want to end up in a job you don’t enjoy. I mean, I’ve seen people do that. It’s not fun.

I don’t know, I just feel like I can’t walk that far anymore. It’s been a while since I got out and about, you know? It’s not like I can just hop on a bus or anything. I know, I’ve been trying to get out more too. But it’s just the weather, isn’t it? It’s so cold and damp. I don’t think I can even bring myself to cycle to the shops without a coat. Yeah, I tried to cycle to the corner shop last week, but it was so icy I nearly slipped. I think I’ve got frozen toes now. Still haven’t warmed up. Oh, don’t do that! You’ll end up with a bad infection or something. I heard a story about someone who had a foot infection from walking too much and couldn’t walk for months. It was in the paper, actually. That’s terrifying. I mean, I suppose I could walk to the shop, but it’s just not worth the hassle. Plus, I don’t like being out in the cold for too long, and I don’t trust myself to make it back without getting lost. I know, it’s so annoying. I used to love walking. I used to walk miles every day. Back when I had a job, I’d go for runs and stuff. But now, I just stay in. Maybe you should try to get back into it. It’s good for you, you know. It keeps you fit and helps with your mental health. Plus, it’s better than sitting around all day. I suppose you’re right. I’ve been feeling a bit down lately, and I think it’s because I’m not doing anything. But I just don’t know where to start. I mean, I don’t even own a decent pair of shoes anymore. You could always borrow some from me. I’ve got a few pairs that I use for the garden. They’re not too fancy, but they’ll keep you warm. That’s a good idea. You could start with short walks, just around the block. It doesn’t have to be too far. Even just getting outside for a bit can make a difference. Yeah, maybe. I’ll think about it. I mean, I do miss being out and about.

So, do you know much about the Basque language? I’ve been reading a bit about it for a project I’m working on, and it’s fascinating how it’s related to other languages like Spanish and French, but it’s quite distinct. Actually, I did a bit of research on it when I was in Spain a few years back. I remember that the Basque language is actually one of the oldest languages in Europe, right? Not related to any other language family. It’s like a linguistic island. Yes, and that’s one of the things that makes it so interesting. I studied it briefly during my time at university. It’s a unique language with its own grammar and structure. It’s also still spoken in parts of the Basque Country today. That’s really cool. I’ve heard it’s used in some areas of Spain and France, but it’s not as widely spoken as other languages. Do you think it’s at risk of disappearing? It’s definitely in danger, unfortunately. There’s been a lot of decline over the years, especially among younger generations. But there are some efforts to preserve it, like language classes and media in Basque. I think it’s important to keep it alive. I’ve been to the Basque Country a couple of times. I remember the locals spoke a mix of Basque and Spanish. It was interesting to hear the language in conversation. Do you know if it’s used in education there? I think it is. I remember reading that in some schools, they teach Basque as a subject, and it’s also used in official contexts. It’s part of their cultural identity. Exactly. Language is such a big part of cultural identity. I remember when I was in Wales, they had similar things with the Welsh language. It’s surprising how much language can shape a community. Yeah, I think that’s why it’s important to celebrate and preserve them. I was also in China a few years ago, and I noticed how much the language there influences the way people think and interact. It’s a huge part of their culture. That’s true. I was in London recently, and you can hear so many different accents and languages there. It’s such a multicultural city. I think that’s one of the reasons it’s so vibrant.

So, how’s the new house? I heard you moved in with your sister last year. It’s alright, it’s a bit small for us both, but it’s cosy. We’ve got a little garden, and we’ve even planted some herbs—rosemary, thyme, and lavender. I think we’re going to make our own pesto soon. That sounds nice. I’ve been meaning to start a garden too, but I’m not sure if I have the patience. I think I’d just end up watering the plants and then forgetting them. You could start with something low-maintenance. Maybe just a few houseplants? I’ve been trying to get my succulents to grow, but they seem to hate me. I tried growing succulents once, and they died in about a week. I think I watered them too much. I still don’t know how to tell when they need water. Maybe that’s the problem. I’ve heard you can’t just water them whenever they look dry. You have to wait until the soil is completely dry, or something like that. Yeah, that’s what I’ve read, but I’m not sure if it’s true. I mean, when I got my first succulent, it looked really healthy, and then I watered it once a week, and within a week it was shrivelled and brown. You don’t have to be perfect. I mean, at least you tried. I’ve been trying to get my own garden going, but my sister keeps telling me to just let the plants do their thing. I think she’s more of a “no effort” kind of person. I can relate. I’m not really into gardening. I prefer things that don’t require me to know when to water or how much sunlight they need. I’m more of a “set it and forget it” type. I think I’m getting there. My mom always said that if I wanted to grow plants, I’d have to learn to be patient. I’m starting to think she was right. That’s probably the key—patience. You just have to wait for things to happen. I mean, even in our family, we’ve had to wait for a lot of things lately. Like my brother’s wedding, and then the kids’ births. Speaking of kids, have you heard from Ethan?

I just can’t believe how much this coffee machine costs. I mean, it’s just a coffee machine! We’ve got one at home that’s been working fine for years. Yeah, I know, but this one’s got all the bells and whistles. It can make lattes, cappuccinos, even espresso. It’s like a little café in our kitchen. I don’t know, mate. If it’s got all those features, maybe it’s worth it. But do we really need to spend that kind of money? I don’t know. It’s just one of those things that’s supposed to make life easier, right? But I’ve already got the removal costs for the old one. I think I’m going to have to take it to the bin. Oh no, you can’t just throw it away. What about storage? I heard that if you store it properly, you can sell it later. Yeah, but even if you do, how much would you get for it? I mean, it’s a couple of years old. Maybe not much. I know, but it’s just easier to get rid of it now. I don’t want to be stuck with it when I move. I get that, but what about the cost of a new one? I mean, if you’re going to buy a new coffee machine, might as well get one that’s actually worth the money. That’s true. But I still think there’s a lot of idealism in buying something like this. You know, like, “I want a better life,” and then you end up buying a coffee machine instead of doing something real. Haha, maybe you’re right. But I think the coffee machine does bring some joy to the mornings, don’t you think? I suppose. Though I’m still not sure it’s worth the cost. I mean, I’ve got a cup of tea that costs nothing. Well, maybe we can compromise. If you really want the coffee machine, do you think you could maybe look for a cheaper model? That’s a good idea. I’ll see if I can find something a bit more affordable. And maybe we can look into storage costs too. I know some places offer free storage if you’re moving. Yeah, and maybe we could even use the old machine for a bit longer.

So, do you think we’ll be able to get away with just a small Christmas this year, Mum? I mean, with everything that’s going on with work and the kids. I don’t know, love. I feel like we should do something special, but I can’t imagine how we’ll manage all the holidays with the kids. It’s like we’re running on fumes all the time. Yeah, I know. But this year, maybe we can just have a quiet one. You know, just the four of us. No extended family, no friends coming over. Just a small get-together. That sounds like a plan. I mean, it’s not like we haven’t done it before. You remember last year, when the snow was so bad, and we had to cancel the whole thing. I think the kids were so upset, they cried for hours. Oh, yeah. I remember that. They were all in their pyjamas, and we had to make do with a pizza and a few cans of pop. But it was nice, honestly. Just us. Yeah, I suppose. But I feel like I should do something for the kids. Maybe buy them something nice. They’re growing up so fast, you know. It’s like one minute they’re still little, and the next they’re trying to argue with us about everything. I know. I feel the same way. I keep thinking, “When did this happen?” But then I remember the last time they were like this – playing with blocks or pretending they were pirates, and now they’re talking about exams and college. It’s crazy how fast time flies. I remember when you were the same age as them, and you were just trying to survive university. Now you’re teaching English to people in Spain and Italy. You’re so far away from home. I know, it’s wild. But I love it. I mean, it’s a different life, but it’s also a good life. You know, I’ve got my own little family of students, and they’re always trying to teach me new things. That’s good. You always said you wanted to be a teacher, and here you are, living it. But I worry sometimes about what’s next. I mean, you’re in your thirties now, and I can see the pressure of getting a better job or something more stable.

So, do you remember that time we were all at Waterfields and someone started snoring so loud that the whole bar got quiet? Oh yeah, I remember! It was like a giant steam train in the middle of the floor. No one said anything, just stared at them like, "Is that normal?" I think it was actually   Jamie  . He had that weird habit of snoring when he got too drunk or too tired. I swear, sometimes he’d fall asleep in the middle of a conversation and just start making that noise. Yeah, and then someone from the   Bakers   next door came over and asked if we wanted to buy some sausages. We were like, "No, we’re just here to talk!" But he said, "Well, if you’re not buying, I’m just going to leave them here." So he just left a whole tray on the table. I mean, that’s the thing with Richmond sausages. You can’t even eat them without getting a handkerchief. I had one once and I was like, "This is like eating a wet sock dipped in molasses!" Oh come on, you’re exaggerating. I mean, they’re decent. But yeah, the smell does get to you – especially if you’re sitting next to someone who’s just  finished  a whole plate. And then there’s the   Waterfields   themselves. I swear, the bouncers just walk around with a clipboard and a smile. They don’t even care if we’re drunk or not. They’d rather just let us all crash and be loud than stop us. I remember once we had this guy who was eating a   Richmond sausage   and then started shouting at the barmaid because he thought she was charging too much. He was like, "You think I’m paying for this? I’m just here for the atmosphere!" And she was like, "Well, you’re paying for it, mate." That’s what I love about Warrington. It’s like a microcosm of everything – the sausages, the pubs, the people. It’s chaotic, but in a good way. Yeah, and the   snoring  . It’s like a running joke. You never know when it’s going to happen. I once had a friend who said he’s going to start snoring in public just to see how people react. He’s been planning it for weeks. I’d pay to see that.

So, did you have a good weekend, Dad? I couldn’t wait to hear all about it. Oh, it was a bit of a mixed bag, to be honest. I had a lovely time with the boys, but then the weather turned and it started raining like a flood. Oh no, that’s a shame. I know you were looking forward to the garden. Yeah, I was. I had a plan to clean out the greenhouse and get the tomatoes ready for the summer. But the rain made it impossible. I had to keep bringing in the plants just in case. That sounds like a lot of work, especially with the weather being so unpredictable. It was. I’m getting a bit tired, to be honest. I suppose it’s just the age, you know? I used to be able to work the garden all day, no problem. I know, Dad. You’ve always had that knack for gardening, even when you were a kid. I remember you used to help Mum with the roses, and she used to say you were the best in the whole street. Haha, I did have a good eye for plants. But I suppose age has got the better of me – I can’t bend as easily, and my back doesn’t hold up like it used to. I know, but I’m sure you’ll get back into it. Maybe you could just start with something smaller, like a few pots on the windowsill. Yeah, maybe. I was thinking about starting a small herb garden – basil, mint, maybe some parsley. Not too much work, just something to keep me occupied. That sounds perfect. And you could even start some seeds for the tomatoes next week. The weather’s supposed to be nice for a bit. You know what? That actually sounds like a plan. I’ll start looking into some seed packets. Perfect. And I could help you with that, if you want. I’ve got some experience with plants, too. That’d be great. I’d rather have someone with a bit of knowledge helping me out. I’d be happy to. But I’m also going to be busy with work this week – I’ve got a big project due. I understand. You’ve always been quite busy, you know. I think you’re doing a great job. Thanks, Dad. It means a lot that you’re supportive.

So how’s the new job going? I heard you moved schools last year. Yeah, it’s been alright. I’m teaching German now, which is a bit of a shift from English, but I like it. It’s nice to have a change of pace. How about you? Still teaching Spanish? Yeah, still with the same school. I’ve actually been thinking about taking on a part-time language course myself. I know it sounds a bit odd, but I’m really interested in learning Mandarin. My sister’s moving to Beijing next year, and I want to be able to speak some of the language. Oh, that’s great! Mandarin is such a useful language. I’ve always wanted to learn it too, but I just never got around to it. Maybe I should start something soon. It’s funny how you think about learning languages when you’re in a different place or working with people from other countries. Definitely. I think it’s a bit of a responsibility too. You know, being a language teacher, you kind of feel like you should be setting an example. Plus, it’s always easier to learn when you’re surrounded by the culture. I’ve been watching a few YouTube channels about Mandarin, and it’s pretty fascinating. The way they use tones and the characters—they’re so different from English. I can imagine. I’ve dabbled in a bit of French and Spanish, but I never really got the hang of it. I mean, I could get by in basic conversations, but I never felt like I could really speak it fluently. I think it’s more about immersion, though. If you’re in a country where the language is spoken every day, it just comes naturally. Exactly. I think that’s why I’m motivated now. My sister’s moving there, and I want to be able to connect with her more. Plus, I’ve always thought it would be cool to visit China one day. The culture is so rich, and the food is amazing. I mean, I’ve only tried a little bit of it so far, but I’m really looking forward to learning more. That sounds incredible. I’ve always wanted to travel more, but I get stuck in this cycle of work and family obligations. I have a little one now, so it’s hard to imagine planning a trip to China, let alone figuring out how to learn a new language.

Well, I've just been out in the garden, and I found a bird's nest in the old birch tree. It's got a few eggs in it, and I thought maybe I should put some feeders up for the birds. You know, the ones with the little bits of seed in them. Oh, I’ve got a few of those up already. I think I’ve got a couple of them in the shed. I’ve been meaning to put more up, but I’m not sure if the birds are coming back yet. It’s been a bit of a quiet spring, hasn’t it? Yes, it has. I’ve been watching the birds every morning, and I’ve noticed that they’re not as active as they were last year. Maybe it’s the weather? I mean, the cold spells have been a bit harsh. I’ve been putting out some cake for them too, just a bit of sugar and whatever I can find in the house. Oh, you do that? I never thought of giving birds cake. But I suppose they like the sugar as much as we do, maybe even more. Although, I’m not sure if it’s healthy for them. I’ve heard that too much sugar can be bad for birds, especially ones with diabetes, like the robins I used to see near the park. Yeah, I’ve heard that too. I think they might be more like the ones who get the sugar from the fruit they eat. But maybe the cake is just a treat. Although, I’ve been told that a bit of cake is better than nothing, especially if the birds are struggling. I suppose so. I’ve got a bit of a sweet tooth, and I thought maybe the birds could use a little something too. I’ve even made a little cake for them yesterday. I used some leftover cake mix and just added a bit of honey. I think they like it. I’ve seen them pecking around the edges. Oh, that's sweet. I think it’s a way to make the garden a bit more welcoming. I’ve also been putting up some old puppets in the garden, just to see what happens. I thought the birds might be curious, but I haven’t seen any of them near the puppets yet.

I think I’ll go for the moussaka. It’s one of the few things I can eat without feeling too guilty. That’s a good choice. I’ll have the grilled lamb with rice, thank you. You know, I’ve been meaning to learn a bit of Turkish. It’s been on my list for ages. That’s a good idea. I’ve always found languages fascinating, even if I never actually studied them formally. Yeah, I’ve been trying to pick it up through apps and watching some Turkish TV shows. It’s not easy, though. I can imagine. I’ve only ever had a passing interest in it, but I’d love to be able to speak a bit. You know, I once met a guy in the market who was teaching himself Turkish by watching old films. He said it helped him connect with the culture. That sounds like a cool way to learn. I’d love to be able to talk to people more directly, rather than just pointing and hoping. Yeah, I think that’s the key to language learning—immersing yourself in the culture. I remember when I first moved to Cyprus. I used to be so nervous about speaking, but now I can hold a conversation without too much trouble. That’s impressive. I’m still at the very beginning. Don’t worry, it takes time. I still struggle with the accents, though. I’d love to be able to understand the locals better. It would make things so much easier. I agree. I think it’s the best way to feel at home in a place. Speaking of which, I heard there was a new restaurant opening in the area. Should we check it out sometime? That sounds like a great idea. I’d love to try something new. I’ve been meaning to ask—do you know anyone who’s into shamanism or dowsing? I heard someone talking about it at the market. You mean the guy who said he could find water with a stick? Yeah, that one. I thought it was a bit strange, but I guess it’s part of the local culture. I can see how it might be interesting. I’ve always been curious about people who believe in destiny and spiritual matters. I think it’s fascinating how people find meaning in different ways. Totally.

So, mum, how's the house coming along? I know you've been thinking about renovations for a while now. Oh, it’s coming along nicely, actually. I've been getting a few ideas from the estate agent. I think the kitchen needs a bit of a face-lift, and maybe the living room too. I’ve even started sketching out some ideas on my phone. Sounds ambitious. I remember when I bought this place, I thought I'd be living here forever, and now it’s just me and the cat. But I must say, it's a solid place. Yeah, it's a good spot. I've been thinking about getting a new sofa for the living room too. I’ve got these new ones in the shop that look really modern, but I’m not sure if they’d fit with the style of the house. Oh, you should look into it. I actually saw this company that does bespoke furniture in the town. They might be able to customise something to fit the space better. That sounds like a good idea. I’ve always loved the idea of having something that’s a bit more unique. But I don’t want to go overboard, you know? Absolutely, it’s good to be practical. My father used to say that a house is only as good as the people in it. So as long as you’re comfortable and happy, the rest is just decoration. True. Speaking of comfort, have you heard about the new café that just opened near the village? Yeah, I went there last week with some friends. The food is decent, but the coffee is amazing. I nearly bought a whole bag just to take home. Oh, you should try it. It’s not too far from here. I think the owner is a former teacher, if I remember correctly. Funny thing, he used to teach at the same school as me. Oh really? That’s interesting. I’ve always liked that café, but I never thought of the connection. So, what do you think about moving the Christmas tree this year? I’ve been thinking about putting it in the living room instead of the hallway. That’s a good idea. The hallway is a bit small, and the living room has more space. I think it would look fantastic with the new decor.

So, do you know what’s up with the catfish thing? I saw this video the other day that was just ridiculous. Oh yeah, I saw that! It was like a fake dating profile, right? And then the guy ended up meeting the girl in person and things went wrong? Yeah, exactly. I think it was some sort of prank or something. But it was so creepy. I mean, I can’t even imagine what that person went through. It’s like, you just go online, you create this perfect profile, and then suddenly you’re being chased by a guy you’ve never even met. I can’t believe that happened. Honestly, it’s like one of those Jeremy Kyle show stories. You know, the ones where people go on these wild emotional rollercoasters because of the internet. Oh yeah, definitely. I remember one episode where someone was convinced they were in love with someone they’d only ever spoken to online. And then when they met, it turned out they had nothing in common. It was so sad. Yeah, I think that’s the worst part. You get all these emotions and expectations built up, and then it’s just… nothing. Like, it’s not even a real relationship. Exactly. And with the Jeremy Kyle show, it’s always like, “You knew this was going to happen.” But you don’t know until it’s too late. I mean, someone should have just said, “This is a fake profile.” But no, they went along with it. It’s like a nightmare. I guess it’s just one of those things that makes people question how much they trust the internet these days. You can’t even tell if someone is real or not. I know. I mean, it’s not like we’re all just going to stop using the internet, but it’s scary how much it can mess with your head. Yeah, I think we’re all just getting more and more paranoid. We know there are scammers, catfish, and all sorts of people out there. It’s just hard to tell who’s who. I mean, it’s not the end of the world, but it’s definitely something you have to be careful with. You don’t want to end up in a situation like that. True. I mean, I’m not even that into online dating, but it’s still something to be aware of.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to talk about going to Paris? I think it was one of the first places we ever dreamt about visiting. Oh yes, I remember that well. I think we were about ten or so, and you used to draw little maps in your notebook, and we'd talk about the Eiffel Tower and the Seine. It was like a fantasy. Yeah, and I still think about it sometimes. I mean, I’ve been to Paris a few times now, but it never quite feels the same as when we imagined it. That’s because you’ve grown up. I think we both have, though. You know, you’ve always been a bit of a dreamer, like I was. Still are, to be honest. Maybe I just like the idea of it more than the reality. But you know, when I was in university, I used to study French for a while. It’s not like I speak it fluently, but I can get by. And I still remember that time I went to Italy, and I accidentally said "bonjour" instead of "buongiorno" in Florence. The locals thought I was a total tourist. Oh, that sounds like you. Always mixing up the languages. But I think it’s part of the charm, doesn’t it? You know, learning to speak another language gives you a different way of seeing the world. Yeah, that’s what I always thought. And you know, I’ve always thought that Germany is one of the places I'd like to visit more. I’ve got some friends who live there, and they talk about it a lot. I mean, I’ve never been, but the stories they tell are so vivid. You know, I used to live in Vienna, so I’ve got a lot of German in my blood. My mother was Austrian, and I grew up speaking German at home. It’s funny how something like that can shape your entire life. I could never get my head around German. I tried learning it once, but it felt like a mountain. I mean, the grammar is so complicated. Still, I think it’s worth it if you want to understand the culture better. It does take work. But I think you’ll get there. You always have that kind of perseverance, even if your head’s in the clouds half the time.

I just want to say, Dad, you were so wrong about that thing with the sat nav. I know it’s got a big screen and everything, but it just doesn’t work properly on the motorways. I mean, we were going to Dorset, and it kept telling us to take the A28 instead of the M27. I had to turn it off and use my phone instead. Oh yeah, I remember that. I used to think sat navs were a miracle, but now I know it’s just another piece of tech that can cause more problems than it solves. I agree. I had one of those big ones once, and it once told me to go through a red light and then a sign said “no through road.” I nearly got pulled over. I had to switch to my old phone, and I think it turned out to be the right way. Yeah, and I remember when I was in London, I tried to use a sat nav for the first time, and it didn’t even know where I was. I had to ask a shopkeeper for directions, and he just laughed and said, “You’re not even near the city centre, lass.” That sounds like a classic example of how GPS can be misleading. I’ve heard stories about people getting lost in the middle of nowhere, because the sat nav thought they were somewhere else. It’s not just tech—it’s also about knowing the geography. I think the worst was someone who tried to drive from Essex to Cornwall using a sat nav, and it told them to go through the Channel Tunnel. It took them all the way through France and ended up in a village in Belgium. They had to call the police to get them back. Oh wow, that’s a nightmare. I think part of the problem is that people rely too much on the sat nav and don’t pay attention to the route. I mean, if you’re going somewhere, you should know where you are at least roughly. I think that’s true. I always check the map before I start driving. I also like to know where the next motorway entrance is because I don’t like being stuck in traffic. Still, I’ve had my share of bad sat nav experiences. Speaking of bad experiences, I think the other day I saw a sign in a town that said “Welcome to Bury St Edmunds.”

I've been thinking a lot lately, you know. About things. About the way things used to be. Yeah, I’ve been feeling that too. It’s funny, isn’t it? Sometimes I look back and can’t believe how things were. It’s strange, isn’t it? I remember when we used to walk down to the village every Sunday. It was a different world back then. Everything was slower, more quiet. Oh, I remember that. We used to go to the post office and get the weekly newspaper, and the butcher would know your name before you even said it. It’s like the whole community knew each other, you know? It was a bit of a shame when the post office closed. I used to go there every week. I’d buy the local paper and have a chat with the old man who ran it. He used to tell me about the war and all that. Yes, and then there was the old library. I used to go there every few weeks. It was a place of stories, of imagination. Now it’s just sitting empty most of the time. I know. I think there’s something to be said for the rhythm of life back then. You didn’t rush about. You planned your day, and you made time for things. It’s not that we don’t have time now, it’s just that it feels like everything’s in a rush. We’re always looking for the next thing, the next big thing. I’d like to think that maybe we’re being too hard on ourselves. Maybe we should take a step back and just enjoy the little things. Exactly. We used to take pride in what we had. A warm meal, a chat with the neighbours, a quiet evening in. Now, it’s like we’re always chasing something. I think it’s a bit of a lost art, don’t you? To just sit and listen to the silence. We’re so used to noise, to being constant. I suppose that’s what I’ve been thinking too. Maybe there’s something to be learned from the past. Maybe slowing down is the key to living better. Maybe. I’d like to try, you know. To be more patient, more present. I’d like that too. It might not be easy, but I think it’s worth trying.

So, do you know what’s on the playlist tonight? I’ve been trying to mix some new tracks in with the old ones. I think it’s a good balance. Yeah, I heard you added that new indie band from Newcastle. That one with the moody guitars. It’s a bit different, but I like it. Yeah, I think it adds a nice contrast to the more upbeat stuff. I’ve been trying to keep the vibe a bit eclectic. You know, like how we used to do in university. Oh, I remember those nights. Always some weird mix of everything. I think it’s part of what made it fun. But I’ve been thinking about getting back into gardening. It’s been a while since I last got my hands in the soil. That sounds nice. I’ve been meaning to start a small vegetable patch in the back. It’s been a bit of a struggle with the weather, though. Yeah, the weather’s been so fickle lately. One minute it’s warm and sunny, the next it’s raining cats and dogs. I think it’s been the worst spring we’ve had in years. For sure. I tried to plant some tomatoes last week, but it rained all night. I’m worried they’re going to get all washed away. I guess I should have waited a bit longer. Maybe next week. You know, I’ve been thinking about our old friends from the village. It’s been ages since we all got together. I feel like we’ve been so busy with work and studies, we’ve lost touch. I know, it’s sad. But maybe we can plan a get-together soon. I’ve been meaning to catch up with Sarah and Tom. They’ve been going through some stuff, but I think they’re okay. Yeah, I’d like that. Maybe we can do something simple—like a BBQ in the garden. It’s been a long time since we had a proper catch-up. I miss the old days when we could just sit around and talk for hours. Absolutely. I’d love that. I’ve been thinking about how much I miss the simplicity of those times. Sometimes it’s good to step back and remember what’s really important. Definitely. I think we should make it happen. It’d be good for the soul, and maybe even the garden.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about what I’m going to do after my PhD. I mean, I’m not exactly sure yet. I’m feeling a bit stuck, honestly. I can see why. I’ve been in the same boat for a while now. I mean, I’ve got my PhD, but I’m still struggling to find a proper job. It’s not like I’m just looking for any job— Yeah, I know. It’s frustrating, isn’t it? You work so hard for your degree, and then when you finish, you’re just another number in the system. Exactly. I’ve been thinking about applying for some research positions, but I’m not sure if I’m qualified enough. And honestly, I’m worried about the cost of living too. I mean, I’ve got student debt, and now I’ve got to think about post-grad loans as well. I know. It’s such a financial burden. I mean, I’ve managed so far, but I’m still worried about the future. My parents are always asking me, “When are you going to land a real job?” and I just don’t know. I feel that. I remember when I got my offer for the PhD, I thought, “This is it, I’ve got a future.” But now, it feels like I’m just going in circles. I get that. There’s also this pressure to have a stable job. I mean, I’m already in a management role, but it’s still not what I dreamed of. I want to do research, but I’m not sure if that’s even a viable option anymore. I think the system is just broken. I mean, you spend years studying, and then you’re left with no real job prospects. I’ve heard so many people talk about the same thing. It’s like the university fees were just a scam. I think it is. I mean, how can you justify spending tens of thousands of pounds on education if there’s no guarantee of a job? I’m not saying it’s not worth it, but it’s just hard to see the point. Yeah, I know. I mean, I’ve always loved musicals. I used to go to the theatre every week. But now, I can’t afford to. It’s like the only thing that made me feel optimistic was the idea of seeing a show, but now even that feels out of reach.

So, do you think we should go with the idea of a book about the family tree? I mean, it’s got to be something the kids can relate to, right? I think it's a great idea. We can make it fun and educational at the same time. Maybe add some pictures of all the family members, like the uncles and aunts and even the step-uncles? Oh, I love that! I could even draw some pictures of the old days, like when we were all living in Glasgow. You know, before the family moved around so much. Yeah, that'd be nice. I could write the story parts and you could draw the pictures, Mum. Just like when we did those little storybooks when I was little. I’d be happy to. It’s been a while since I’ve done any drawing, but I can still do it. I mean, I still draw for the toddler’s books, you know. That’s right, isn’t it? You’ve got a real talent for drawing, even if you don’t admit it. I remember when your brother was a kid, and you made all those cards for his birthday… they were amazing. Yeah, she was amazing. But I think we need to include more than just the pictures and the story. Maybe some of the family traditions? Like the way we used to celebrate birthdays back in London. That’s a good point. Maybe we can add a section about the different family styles. Like how some families still do things the old way, and others have changed. Oh, there’s so much about that. My cousin in Edinburgh still bakes those traditional Scottish scones every Sunday, and my sister-in-law in Belfast uses the same recipe as her mum. It’s all about tradition, isn’t it? Exactly. And we can talk about how even though the family is spread out, we all share the same roots. I mean, even the step-uncles and step-aunts are part of the family now. That’s true. It’s not just about blood relations anymore. It’s about who you choose to be part of your family. I think that’s something the kids should understand. I agree. You know, when I was your age, I never thought I’d be someone who would have a family of my own, let alone a stepson and stepdaughters.

So, do you ever just get fed up with shaving? I mean, it's like, every week, you're like, “Oh god, I need to do this again.” Yeah, I totally get that. I mean, it's not like you can just leave it, right? You end up with that  babe  look, like you haven't shaved in days, but you haven’t. It's just a constant battle. Exactly. And then you get all that stubble, and you're like, "I’m not a guy, I don’t need to look like one!" But then you go to the barbers and they’re like, “Oh, you’re just like everyone else.” Oh, I know. I mean, I’m not even into the whole  manly  thing. I just want to feel clean, you know? Like, fresh. But then again, I guess it’s not just about looking clean. It’s about confidence too. Yeah, I mean, I think it’s more about how you feel. If you’ve just shaved, you feel more put together, like you’ve done something for yourself. It's like a little ritual. True. But then again, I’ve started thinking – what if I just let it grow? Like, natural hair? I mean, I’ve seen some people with facial hair and they look cool. Oh, I mean, if you’re into it. But I’m not. I just like the smoothness. I mean, what if I start to grow a bit and then I feel like I’ve failed? You won’t fail. I mean, not unless you’re the type of person who thinks you need to be absolutely smooth all the time. But I think it's more about how you  choose  to present yourself. Yeah, I guess. Although, honestly, I’m not sure I would ever go full beard. I mean, I tried once, and it was like,  Oh my god, what am I doing?  Ha! I can relate. My cousin had a go at it for a week, and then he was like, "This is not me." I think it's more about confidence than anything. If you’re comfortable in your own skin, you don’t need to shave. Right. I just feel like it's part of my routine. I mean, I know people who don’t shave at all, and they’re fine. But I guess it's just a personal thing.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing about the alphabet? What? It’s not just letters, it’s the whole structure of how we communicate. I mean, think about it—without the alphabet, we wouldn’t even be able to talk about racism in football or boxing. Haha, that’s a bit of a stretch. But I guess you’re right in a way. Yeah, seriously. The alphabet was a game-changer. Especially when it comes to understanding things like alcohol and drugs, or even how we talk about racism. It gives us the language to debate and discuss. That’s true. I mean, think of how much we’ve been able to talk about these issues since the alphabet was developed. You can’t really argue about boxing without words. Exactly. And even something like drinking. Without the alphabet, we wouldn’t have words like “alcohol,” “doping,” or “addiction.” That’s a good point. It’s interesting how the alphabet has shaped the way we think about the world. It definitely has. And I think that’s why we’re here tonight, right? Because without the alphabet, we wouldn’t even be able to order a drink. True. But I’ve seen people try to talk about alcohol without using the whole alphabet. It’s like trying to describe a punch without using the word “punch.” That’s funny. It’s like when I was in boxing class, the instructor said, “You can’t throw a punch without using your alphabet.” Oh, I’ve heard that before. I think the point is that without the alphabet, boxing would be chaos. No clear rules, no understanding of the sport. Exactly. And that’s why we need to keep pushing for better language around issues like racism in football. Without the right words, we can’t even begin to address it. Yeah, and that’s why we’re here tonight. Even if it’s just a bit of drinking and talking, the alphabet helps us make sense of it all. I think that’s the real secret of the alphabet—without it, we’d still be trying to communicate like cavemen. That’s one way to put it. But you know, even with the alphabet, we still have a long way to go with racism in football. It’s a tricky issue. It’s not just about the alphabet—it’s about how we use it to challenge and change things.

I just got a call from the council about the request for funding for that old farmhouse in Radcot. They’re considering it, but they want more specifics on how the renovation would preserve its historical value without over-modernizing it. That’s always the tricky part, isn’t it? You’ve got to balance preservation with practicality. I remember one project I worked on in Oxford where they wanted to install a wheelchair ramp, but the original entrance was so narrow and steep, it almost felt like a sacrilege to alter it. We ended up removing the steps and building a bridge over the garden. Oh, that sounds like a clever solution. I was thinking about the same thing with the Radcot house. The front entrance is a bit of a problem. I think I’ll suggest a more subtle approach—maybe reinforcing the existing structure instead of replacing it. They might be more receptive to that. That makes sense. And if you’re going to apply for funding, you’ll need to be clear about the long-term maintenance plan. Councils don’t want to fund something that’ll fall apart in a few years. You need to show they’ve got a sustainable strategy. Right, I’ll make sure to include a detailed maintenance schedule. I was also thinking about the materials. Using local stone or wood could help with authenticity. I know a quarry near Banbury that sells reclaimed stone, and it’s quite affordable. That’s a good point. Authentic materials not only help preserve the building’s character but also support the local economy. I’d love to see more of that in heritage projects. It’s not just about the building—it’s about the community too. Exactly. I think I’ll mention that in the proposal. Also, the client has been very keen on using sustainable practices. Maybe I could suggest energy-efficient windows that still look traditional. The council might be more inclined to fund that. Definitely. And if you’re going to bid, make sure to highlight the historical significance. That old farmhouse is a rare example of 18th-century architecture in the area. It’s got a story to tell, and people want to hear it. I agree. I’ll make sure to weave in the history and the community impact. Oh, and I was thinking of including a small exhibition or guided tour once the project is done.

So, do you know what’s really weird? I was reading this paper the other day about regional dialects and how they’re starting to shift because of the internet and social media. It’s like people from different parts of the country are mixing their accents more now, especially among younger people. Yeah, I saw that too. I mean, I was in Manchester last week, and I heard this guy talking with a real East London accent, and I was like, “Wait, is that even possible?” It’s like the dialects are becoming more fluid. You can’t really tell where someone’s from anymore just by their speech. Exactly. And it’s not just the accents, it’s the vocabulary too. I think a lot of it has to do with the way we communicate online. You see the same phrases, same slang, used across the country. It’s like the internet is breaking down those traditional boundaries. Totally. I mean, I’ve noticed in my own research, even within academia, there’s this kind of shared jargon that people use, regardless of where they’re from. Like, we all use terms like “syllabic structure” or “phonological patterns” in the same way, even if we’re from different regions. Yeah, but I think it’s also about how people want to feel connected. If you’re in a university like Cambridge, you’re surrounded by people from all over the country. It’s almost like you’re forced to speak in a more neutral way to be understood. Although, I have to say, I still find it weird when people from the North start using a lot of Southern English words. It’s like they’re trying to sound more "posh." That’s the thing, isn’t it? There’s this pressure to fit in, especially in places like Cambridge or Oxford. I mean, if you’re not from here, you kind of have to adjust your speech to be more like the locals. It’s not just about the accent, it's about the whole way of speaking—the way you phrase things, the rhythm, the intonation. I guess that’s part of what makes linguistics so interesting. It’s not just about the words you say, it's about how you say them, and how that reflects your identity. But I do wonder, are we losing something by becoming more linguistically homogenized?

So, do you remember when we were talking about the school dinners last week? Yeah, I remember, and I was telling you about how my lunch at Granny’s is always better. Oh, of course, you said that every time. But I think it’s true—Granny’s lunches are always more interesting than the school ones. Yeah, I like the school dinners though, they’re got that weird meat pie thing. Oh, you mean the one with the weird texture? That’s the one that always tastes like it’s been sitting in the fridge for a week. Yeah, and then there’s that weird green stuff they call “vegetable” that’s just like… not really a vegetable. You’re right, it’s sad. I think the school meals are actually getting worse every year. I think they just want us to eat more so they don’t have to buy as much food. That could be. But I still think it’s better than the school tennis tournament. What about the tennis tournament? Did you hear about that? Yeah, I did. You have to pay for it, and it costs a fortune. I remember when I was your age, I’d rather have been in the circus. Yeah, the clowns are way more fun. I mean, they make you laugh, they do tricks, and they’re not trying to hit you with a ball. Exactly! And the circus is way more exciting. I mean, do you know how much it costs to go to the circus? It’s not that expensive, is it? I think it’s just a few pounds. Yeah, but if you’re going with the whole family, it adds up. And then you have to pay for the tickets, the snacks, and the ride on the carousel. Oh, that sounds like a lot. But I think it’s worth it. You get to see the big elephants and the fire-breathing lions. Oh, I’d love to see that. But I think I’ll stick to the school trips. Yeah, but I think the school is planning a trip to the circus next month. Oh, really? That would be awesome!

So, did you enjoy the film we went to see last night? I thought it was quite thought-provoking, especially the way it tackled the history of the Industrial Revolution. I did, actually. I found it very interesting, though I had a bit of a hard time keeping up with some of the historical references. I mean, it’s been decades since I studied history at school, and I don’t remember everything. That’s a common problem, isn’t it? Especially with the way history is taught now. I was at a debate in Cambridge last week about how the national curriculum is being reformed, and it really got me thinking. They talked about making the curriculum more relevant to modern issues and less focused on rote memorization. I agree. I think the current system is a bit outdated, especially for students who are going to go into higher education or the workforce. I mean, when I was at school, we were taught to memorize dates and events, but I don’t remember how any of that helped me when I got to university. Yeah, and I think that’s one of the main reasons I struggled with my A-levels. I didn’t see the point in learning so much about the past if it didn’t connect to anything I’d actually use later in life. I remember my history teacher, though, he was really passionate about it. He used to make the class feel like it was alive, not just a list of facts. That’s the key, isn’t it? Making history relevant to the students. I was lucky enough to have a few good teachers at university too, but even then, I had to teach myself a lot of the material. I did a postgraduate degree in history, and the thing that helped me the most was connecting it to my own work in advertising. Understanding how historical events shaped culture helped me better understand consumer behavior. That’s interesting. I was thinking about that last night. I’m actually planning on doing a degree in education, and I’ve been wondering how I can make history more engaging for students. Maybe if we can link it to real-world issues or current events, students might actually care more about it. That sounds like a great idea. I think the younger generation is more connected to the world than ever before.

I've been thinking a lot lately about the war, you know. Not the one in the papers, but the one that happened a long time ago. When I was a boy, in the forties. It's strange how time flies, isn't it? Yes, it does. I remember when I was a girl, the war was everywhere. My father was in the navy, and we used to get letters from him all the time. Sometimes they were full of details, and sometimes they were just a few lines saying he was safe. That must have been tough. I was too young to remember the war properly, but I've heard so many stories from my parents. They always spoke of the bombs and the rationing, how everything was scarce. I can't imagine what it was like to live through that. I think it's important to remember those times, even if they’re painful. It shapes who we are and how we view the world today. But at the same time, it's amazing how much has changed. I was born in Harrow, and I remember when the weather was so unpredictable. There were times when the sky would be clear one day, and the next it would be raining for hours. Yeah, it's funny how the weather can be so dramatic. My gran used to say that if you could predict the weather, you could predict the rest of the day. I remember when I was a kid, we had that old wooden shed in the back garden. It was full of things—old chairs, furniture, even a few trinkets. I used to play in there all the time. That sounds like a lot of fun. I used to have a similar shed, but it was more of a tool shed. Although, I had a few odd things in there too. One of my cousins used to leave things there when they moved out—old toys, books, even a few photos. It was like a time capsule. You know, I was thinking the other day about my grandfather. He was a very strong man, and he had a lot of land. He used to say that the best way to preserve history was to have things around you. That's why he always kept furniture from the old days, even when it didn't really serve a purpose anymore.

So, do you think we're gonna make it to Dad's before the traffic gets too bad? I don’t want to miss the last one. I hope so. I've been trying to keep up with the traffic updates on my phone, but it’s all just a mess out there. You know how it is when you’re driving between Bedford and Northamptonshire—there’s always something happening. Yeah, I remember last time we drove this way, there was a massive pile-up near the A5. We ended up stuck for an hour. Didn’t even get to see the view. I still remember that. You were so frustrated, shouting at the car behind you like it was your fault. I still laugh about that. Oh, come on, I was just trying to get us moving! I think the guy behind me had an attitude too. Anyway, forget about that. What are we going to do once we get there? The house is being sold, and we need to figure out the next steps. Yeah, I know. Mum said the estate agent is coming tomorrow to talk about the mortgage again. She’s really stressed about it. I think she’s worried we might not be able to afford it. She’s been sick a lot lately too. I don’t think she’s been sleeping properly. It’s been hard on her. It’s not just the house, it’s everything else. I know. She's been through a lot. But I think she’s trying to stay positive. She said she’s glad we’re getting closer to moving. She wants to make it work. Me too. It’s just a lot to take in. I mean, moving from Mum’s to Dad’s—everything changes. I don’t even know how we’re going to cook anymore. The kitchen up there is tiny. Oh, you’ll get used to it. And you’ll learn how to cook the English way. You know, proper meals with proper ingredients. Not just takeaway every night. I  am  learning. I’ve been trying to cook more. I even tried making steak and kidney pie. It was a disaster, honestly. The kidney was too tough, and the pie crust fell apart. Well, you’re trying. That’s what matters. I think you’ve got a good eye for it. Maybe after a few more attempts, you’ll be a proper chef.

So, do you think we've got everything for the birthday meal? I've been going through the list again. I think so, but I'm still a bit nervous about the seating. We’ve got seven people coming, and I don’t want anyone to feel left out. Yeah, I know. I’ve been thinking about the table plan. Maybe we can split them into two smaller groups so that everyone can chat. The ones who are close are on one side, and the others on the other. That sounds like a good idea. But, I’m still not sure about the menu. Should we stick with the classic ones like meat and two veg, or go for something a bit more modern? I think a bit of both is okay. Maybe start with the classics, but include some lighter options too. My mum always says if you don’t like the food, you can’t complain—so it’s better to have variety. True, but the thing is, my gran doesn’t like anything too adventurous. She prefers her meat well done and her vegetables not too spicy. Got it. So maybe go with a roast chicken and a few side dishes like roast potatoes, Yorkshire puddings, and green beans. And then maybe have some gluten-free options for those with dietary restrictions. That sounds doable. Also, I was thinking about the candles. We’ve got a big cake, and we need to make sure the candles are in good condition. Oh, and also, I need to check the candles aren’t too long or they might tip over. Right, and don’t forget the cake topper. I’ve got it in the kitchen. I think it’s the same one from last year, but I’ll check. Speaking of which, I’ve also been worrying about the fish. I mentioned to the fishmonger that we need a whole fish for the meal, but he said they only have a few left. I was told to come back tomorrow to see if it’s still available. Hmm, that could be a problem. Maybe we can take a backup plan and order from the fish shop if it’s not there. Or maybe even source it from a local market? Yeah, that’s a good idea. I’ll give them a call tomorrow and see. Also, I’ve been thinking about the rearranging the cupboards.

I can't believe I've got to go through with this. I’ve been putting it off for months, but I think I’m finally going to get my wisdom teeth out. Oh no! That sounds terrifying. Are they really necessary? I mean, I’ve heard some people just live with them and don’t have any problems. I know, I know – but they’re causing me so much pain, especially when I eat anything crunchy. It’s like there are holes in my mouth everywhere. I can’t even eat a sandwich without feeling like I’m going to lose a tooth. That sounds awful. I can’t imagine going through that. When are you getting it done? Next week, actually. The dentist said it’s better to do it before the end of term, and I don’t want to be stuck with this for the whole year. Plus, I’m moving house next month, and I don’t want to be in pain during the whole process. Moving house? That’s a big deal. How’s that going? It’s a bit of a nightmare, honestly. I’ve got to sort out the entire place, and my parents are helping, but it’s not exactly making things easier. I’m worried about all the stuff I’m leaving, and I’ve got to find a new place that’s within budget. That sounds stressful. Are you going back to uni next year? Yeah, I’m going back to uni in September. I’ve got a place sorted in Cambridge, but it’s a bit of a commute. I’m trying to make it work, but it’s not easy. I can imagine. Cambridge is a lovely place, but it’s also pretty expensive. Have you got a flat mate? Yeah, I’m sharing with someone from my course. We’re trying to split the costs, but it’s still a lot. I was thinking about getting a student rental, but I’m not sure if I can afford it. That’s a lot to take on. I think it’s going to be tough, but I hope you manage. You’re so proactive – I think you’ll get through it. Thanks. I hope so too. I just need to make sure I don’t go through this whole process with a mouth full of holes. I’m planning to get some soft food and take it easy for a few days after the surgery.

Okay, so I was thinking, maybe we could do something nice for someone else this Chinese New Year. You know, like a random act of kindness? That sounds great! What kind of things could we do? Maybe help someone in need? Like, if we saw someone struggling, we could offer to help them with something? Yeah, that's a good idea. But I was also thinking about the lactose-free cakes and cookies. I've been making them for a while now, and I've been wondering if I could donate some to a local charity. That’s a fantastic idea! I mean, we could even make some for the community centre or something. They always need snacks for their kids’ activities. Yeah, and maybe we could make some for the elderly too. I’ve heard some of them are having trouble with their health, and they might not have the budget for treats. Exactly. I think it would be a nice way to celebrate Chinese New Year, giving back to the community. Plus, it’s a good way to spread some joy. I love that! But what about the Chess and Draughts pieces? I still have those from when I was a kid. I was thinking of using them as a way to raise money for something. Maybe sell them online? That could work! You could put them up on eBay or something. I mean, they’re pretty old, but they’re in decent condition. And people might actually want them for collectors or for fun. Yeah, and if we sell some, we could donate the money to a local charity too. It’s a way of giving back, just like making the cakes and cookies. I like that. It’s like doing two good things at once. Speaking of which, have you thought about dying your hair different colours for the New Year? Oh, I was actually considering it! I saw a video about how to dye hair with natural dyes, and I thought it might be a fun way to celebrate. What do you think? I think it’s a great idea! It’s a way to show off your creativity and also bring some colour to the celebration. I mean, it’s not every day you get to change your look for the New Year. I’m in! Let’s make it happen. Maybe we could even do it together.

Mm, so, um, how’s your day going, Mum? It’s been a bit of a day, honestly. I had to run down to the post office this morning, and then I got stuck in traffic for ages. But I’m glad I got everything done. How about you? I’ve been okay. I was just sitting on the sofa reading  Alice in Wonderland  again. I love that book. It’s so magical, isn’t it? I’ve read it so many times, and each time it feels different. That’s the beauty of it, isn’t it? It’s like you never really finish it, you just keep finding new things. I remember when I was a kid, I used to get so excited about the chapters. I’d read them out loud to my brother, and he’d laugh at the nonsense. Yeah, it’s so funny, isn’t it? I mean, like the Cheshire Cat just disappearing, or the Queen of Hearts being so dramatic. I think the part where Alice falls down the rabbit hole is my favorite. That’s a classic. I think that’s where it all starts, and it’s such a clever way to show how confusing and strange life can be. Speaking of strange, have you heard about that car accident on the promenade? No, what happened? A car hit a lamppost and then went into a parked car. It was pretty bad. someone got hurt, but I think they’re okay now. It was all over the news. Some people were saying it was a red light, and others said it was a pedestrian crossing. Wow, I hope no one was seriously injured. That must have been scary. Yeah, it was. I know that the area near the promenade is a bit tricky to drive in, especially with all the pedestrians. I was actually thinking about it earlier when I was walking with my neighbour. She told me she saw it happen. That’s really sad. I hope they’re all okay. Anyway, I was also thinking about the party we’re having next weekend. I was going to ask you if you wanted to come. Oh, I’d love to. I’ll see if I can get some time off work. I just need to make sure I don’t mess up my schedule. You know your dad’s coming too, right?

I just had a call from one of the local protest groups, you know the one that's been fighting against the wind turbines on the hill near Winchcombe. They said they were going to call a meeting this evening and they wanted my help to do some research on the environmental impact of the turbines. I saw that on the local news last week. It’s quite a big issue, isn't it? I mean, I can see the benefits of wind energy, but if they're building them in the wrong place, it could cause more problems than it solves. Exactly. And it's not just about the visual impact. There's also the noise, the effect on the wildlife, and the potential disruption to the local community. I remember when we fought against the solar panels on the edge of the village – the main argument was about the lack of consultation and the heavy-handed approach by the council. And I still think the council has a lot of work to do in terms of being transparent. Last time, we had to go through a planning appeal, and it took months to get any real answers. They should have had proper research done before even considering these proposals. I agree. It’s not just the local people who are affected. The energy companies are getting all the subsidies, yet the research – the kind of innovation that could make these projects sustainable – is being underfunded. I mean, how do you store the energy if the wind isn't blowing? There’s also this question of political influence. The local planners often seem to be more aligned with the energy companies than with the residents. And with the Scottish referendum coming up in two weeks, I wonder if that’s going to make things even more complicated. You know, the energy policy in Scotland is different, and it might affect how these proposals are handled nationally. I’m not sure. It might galvanize the local protest movement, or it might just add more confusion. Either way, I think we need a more informed public. People need to understand not just the opposition, but the alternatives – the real long-term solutions that could work for everyone. And that’s where the research comes in. If we can’t convince the council or the planners with emotion or arguments, we need facts.

I just got a call from the garage, love. Your dad’s car’s had an inspection, and it’s all good to go. He’s been meaning to get his license back for ages, hasn’t he? Yeah, he’s been talking about it since last summer. But he was always so nervous. I remember when he first tried to learn, he kept asking me if I wanted to come with him to practice. I said no, but he insisted. I ended up going anyway, just to keep him company. Oh, I remember that! He was so awkward. He’d park the car like it was a tank, and when he tried to reverse, the wheels kept spinning. You know, like a child’s toy. I swear he made me laugh more than I’ve ever laughed in my life. It’s funny, isn’t it? But I think he’s really serious about it now. He even signed up for a driving course last week. He’s been doing the theory part, and he’s planning to take the test in the next few months. That’s great. I think it’s about time. I mean, he’s been driving for years, but he always said he wasn’t ready. I reckon he’s just been scared of getting caught out. But now that he’s got his head around it, I think he’s going to be fine. Yeah, he’s always been a bit of a nervous wreck when it comes to anything new. But that’s what makes him so endearing. He’s a good man, just a bit of a fluster. I know. But seriously, I think it’s a good opportunity for him to get out more. He’s been staying home a lot lately, especially since the kids have moved out. Maybe this could be a way to meet new people and get out of the house more. That’s true. And it’s not like he doesn’t have the money. He’s got his pension, and he’s always talking about how he wants to travel more. Maybe once he gets his license, he’ll be able to go somewhere by himself. You know, like a road trip. That would be nice. I’d love to see him go somewhere. He’s always had that adventurous spirit, even if he hides it behind his cautious nature.

So, Dad, I just got a message from my mate about that new app they’re trying out on Facebook. It’s like a mobile notification thing, but it’s supposed to help you manage your alerts better. I was thinking about whether I should start using it, but I’m not sure. I don’t know, luv. I’ve got these little things on my phone all the time, and I’ve got to keep swiping and swiping and swiping. It’s like a never-ending scroll. I think I’ve got more notifications than my cat has lives. Yeah, I know. It’s so overwhelming. I’ve been trying to cut down on my screen time, but it’s hard. Especially when you get these messages about new food trends or health stuff. I’m trying to eat better, but I keep getting these ads for kale smoothies and superfoods. I remember when we used to just have tea and biscuits and no one cared about health. Back in the fifties, people didn’t think about that. I mean, we had to survive with what we had. Now it’s all about special diets and organic produce. It’s funny, isn’t it? I mean, I’m studying nutrition, and it’s so different from what my gran used to do. She’d just throw together a sandwich and some chips. Now, people want to know if the chips are non-GMO or if the bread is made with ancient grains. That’s the thing with the modern world, luv. You can’t buy what you like, you have to buy what’s good for you. I used to make my own bread, and it was about as healthy as any shop-bought loaf. I guess. But I’m trying to cook more for the kids. I mean, it’s not like we’re living in a time of famine or anything, but I do worry about food banks. I heard on the news the other day that more people are relying on them than ever before. I know. It’s sad, isn’t it? People are struggling. I remember back in the day, if you didn’t work, you didn’t eat. Now, if you don’t work, you still have to pay for everything. It’s not fair. I’m trying to be proactive. I’m working part-time at a café, and I’ve been planning to start a small side business, maybe selling healthy snacks.

So, do you remember that time we tried to act out a Shakespeare play in front of our mates? Oh yeah, I still remember that. You were Hamlet, and I was Ophelia. No, no, no! You were Hamlet, I was Ophelia. You kept pretending to drown in a puddle and crying. Oh come on, I had a tragic backstory! My “father” had died, and I was going mad. Yeah, and you kept saying “To be, or not to be” in a really posh accent. That’s what you get for choosing me as Hamlet. You’re the one who said I had the “theatrical flair”! I know, I know. But you turned out to be the most dramatic one. Anyway, it was a disaster. We got laughed at by everyone. And then you tried to tell us that you were “acting” so seriously that you actually started crying. I didn’t cry! I just… I don’t know, got really emotional. It was the real thing. You were the one who kept saying, “If I had a dagger, I would kill myself.” That’s what the script said! Speaking of scripts, do you remember that one time you tried to learn golf and said you were “winning” every round? Oh yeah, I had a  flash  of brilliance. I thought I was playing like Tiger Woods. Yeah, and you kept hitting the ball into the bushes and then pretending it was a “strategic move.” It was! I was trying to make the ball go around the trees, not through them. You ended up in the water hazard, and you just said, “I win, I win, I win!” I did! I won the game by default. And then you tried to tell us that the fact that your surname is “Smith” makes you a  winner . I said it’s not just a surname—it’s a  legacy . Yeah, and you said that “Smiths have always ruled the world.” I  did  say that. You laughed so hard you almost spilled your coffee. And you were so serious about it, too. You looked at the ceiling like it was the throne of England. Anyway, I think I’ve made my point. I don’t need to be a “Smith” to be a winner. I just need to be me. Yeah, but you  are  a winner. You just have a weird way of doing it. That’s what I like about you.

So, do you know what’s up with the whole work thing? I’ve been trying to get a new job for ages, and it’s just not happening. I mean, I’ve got this great resume, and I’m really good at what I do, but no one seems to be interested. I know the feeling, honestly. I’ve been applying for jobs like crazy. I’ve even been looking into doing some freelance work, but it’s so competitive out there. I mean, how do people even get hired these days? I hear you. I’ve been trying to switch roles too. I like my current job, but I’m not excited about it anymore. I’ve been thinking about moving to a different industry, maybe something more creative? But I’m not sure where to start. Yeah, I feel you. It’s so frustrating. I’ve even been thinking about doing something part-time while I search for a better job. But with rent and everything, it’s not easy. I’m just not sure how people manage. I know, it’s tough. I’ve got a roommate, so it’s cheaper, but even then, it’s not easy. I’ve started cooking more at home instead of eating out. I mean, it’s not healthy, but it’s cheaper. You know what I mean? Totally. I’ve been trying to cut down on takeout as well. I’ve even started making my own smoothies and healthy snacks. Honestly, I feel like people are always talking about diets and fitness, but it’s hard to stick to them when you’re working long hours and stressed. I know, I’ve been trying to do that too. I mean, I walk a lot, so I’m not totally sedentary. But I’ve been eating out a lot because I just don’t have the time or energy to cook. I guess that’s why I’m not in the best shape. I feel you. I’ve been told I need to eat better, but honestly, I just don’t have the time. I mean, I’m working full-time, and then trying to catch up on work during the week. It’s non-stop. I get it. But I think it’s important to take care of yourself, even if it’s just a little bit. I’ve started going to the gym a couple of times a week, and it helps.

I just got a call from my cousin in London, and he said he wants to set up a Skype call. I said, “Well, I’ve got a bit of a problem with that, you know, because I don’t have a proper internet connection.” Oh, you haven’t got it? That’s strange, I thought you got it sorted. It’s not that I haven’t got it, but I’ve got this old laptop, and it keeps crashing. It’s like it’s got a mind of its own. Maybe it’s because you’re not using the right browser. I’ve had trouble with that before. I think it’s better to use Firefox or Chrome. My son told me that. Oh, right. I didn’t know that. I’ve been using Internet Explorer because that’s what I’ve always used. Yeah, but that’s an old browser. It’s not safe, and it’s not modern. You should switch, or maybe use a laptop that’s not so old. I know, but I can’t afford a new one. My wife said we’ve got enough problems with the TV licence. Oh, that’s always been a problem. You know, I remember when we first got the TV, and we had to pay the licence. It was quite an expense back then. It still is, you know. And now they’re even going after people who don’t pay. I heard they sent a notice to one of our neighbours. I heard about that too. It’s a bit of a scandal, really. They make it sound like you’re doing something wrong when you’re just trying to save money. Maybe they should be giving people better advice instead of sending threats. Yeah, I don’t know. I’ve got a bit of a soft spot for the cosmos, though. I used to love watching the stars. Me too. I remember when I was younger, I used to try to find constellations with my dad. It was one of the things we did together. I’ve been reading a lot about black holes lately. They’re fascinating, if you ask me. Yeah, I read that they’re like the universe’s vacuum cleaners. They suck everything in, even light. Oh, that’s right. And they’re at the centres of galaxies. I find it amazing that something so small can have such a big effect.

So, do you know where the best fish and chips in Sunderland is? I was just thinking, like, if we ever go back, I’d love to try somewhere good. I mean, sure, there’s the oldies, but I feel like there’s got to be something better than the ones near the market. Honestly, I don’t think there’s anything better than the ones near the market. I mean, I’ve tried a few places in the town, and they all just taste like they’ve been sitting in a fridge for days. The one near the market? It’s always fresh, even if it’s not the fanciest. Yeah, but I feel like there are places that are kind of hidden. Like, you know, somewhere you don’t really hear about until you go there. I mean, I heard this place called The Anchor. I think it’s in the old part of town. Wait, is that even still open? I’m not sure. I think it closed a few years back. But I’ve heard people talk about it, like, it was one of the oldest places around. I mean, if I remember correctly, it was one of those places where the fish was so good, people would travel from other parts of the city just to get it. Mate, I’d do that. I mean, if it’s that good, I’d go out of my way. But I guess I’d have to ask someone who actually lives around there. Like, someone who knows the area better than me. You know, like, a local. Yeah, and I think the buses can get you there. If you take the number 2 or the number 6, I think they run all the way to the old part of town. I mean, I’ve been on them before. Not the best experience, but it does get you there. Yeah, I’ve always found the buses here are a bit of a nightmare. I mean, they’re always late, and the drivers don’t seem to know what they’re doing half the time. I prefer driving myself. Although, if it’s a weekend, I can’t really drive because I’m supposed to be at work. Yeah, I can’t argue with that. Work comes first, I guess. But seriously, I think driving is just not the way to go.

Oh, do you know, I’ve been trying to identify the birdsong outside this morning, and it’s driving me nuts. I thought it was a blackbird, but I’m not sure. Oh, I know that one! That’s the song of a greenfinch. It’s got that little, chirpy, high-pitched trill, isn’t it? Yeah, I think that’s it. But I’ve also heard this other sound, like a low, continuous hum. What’s that? That’s probably the nightingale. Or maybe a sparrow? Although I’ve heard it more at dusk. I used to live near a wood and could tell them apart like a second language. That’s impressive. I tried to listen carefully this morning, but I couldn’t pick it out. I even got my phone out to record it, but it just sounds like a mess of noises. Haha, I know what you mean. I remember once, my neighbor’s cat got out and chased a bird, and that’s when I heard the most chaotic mix of bird calls I’ve ever heard in my life. Oh, that sounds like a nightmare. I’d rather not know that. Speaking of which, have you ever had trouble with birds coming into your garden? I’ve been feeding them, and they’ve started to hang around quite a lot. Oh, I’ve had that problem too. I put out some sunflower seeds, and now the birds are like my own little family. But I had a funny incident last week—there was a redpoll that got too close to my tea, and I had to chase it off with a broom! That’s hilarious. I had a similar experience. I was having my morning coffee, and a crow landed beside me. It didn’t run away; it just stared at me like I was the guest. I thought I was going to have to open a window to get it out. I tried that once too. I opened the window and said, “Come on, you’ve had enough,” and it just flew off like it was being chased by a ghost. I still think it’s haunted. Maybe it is. I’ve had my fair share of strange happenings. Just yesterday, I had a nosebleed that lasted for like fifteen minutes. I was reading the paper, and suddenly—I was just splattering the page.

So, how’s everything going? It’s been a while since we last caught up. How’s the teaching going? Oh, it’s going okay, thank you. I’ve been trying to get back into the swing of things after the holidays. It’s been a bit of a rollercoaster, to be honest. I’ve been thinking about changing things up a bit. Oh? What do you mean? I’ve been seriously considering taking a break from teaching for a while now. I was thinking about going back to working with children in a different capacity—maybe something like a parenting support group or something like that. I feel like I’ve been giving a lot of advice but not always getting the support I need. That sounds like a good move. You’ve always had a knack for connecting with people. But then again, you’re a teacher—so it doesn’t surprise me that you’d want to keep working with kids. Yeah, I suppose you’re right. But I’ve also been thinking about writing a book. I’ve had some ideas for a while, but I’ve been too busy. A book? That’s amazing. What would it be about? It’s about single parenthood and the challenges of raising a child alone.
