I’ve seen so many people go through it, and I wanted to write something that could help others feel less alone. That’s such a great idea. I think it could really resonate with people. It’s such a tricky path, especially when you’re trying to balance everything else in life. I know. And honestly, it’s been on my mind a lot lately. I’ve also been thinking about IVF. I’ve been in touch with a few friends who’ve gone through it, and it’s opened my eyes to how much it can affect someone’s life. Yeah, I can imagine. It’s such a difficult decision, isn’t it? I mean, it’s not just about the medical side—it’s emotional, too. Absolutely. I’ve been thinking about it more recently, but I haven’t decided yet. I’m not sure if I’m ready to go down that path. I get it. It’s a big choice, and I think it’s important to take your time with it. Speaking of big choices, have you been using social media more lately?

Oh, hello there, Mr. Thompson. You're looking well today. Ah, thank you, dear. I’m just about as well as can be, considering I've been feeling a bit off for the past few weeks. I’m sorry to hear that. Are you sure it’s nothing serious? I’m not sure, to be honest. The doctor said it might just be stress or something, but I’ve had a few headaches and a bit of fatigue. That sounds like it could be burnout, especially with all the political talk these days. I’ve been reading the papers and it’s been quite intense. You’re not the only one. I’ve been watching the news too, and honestly, I’m getting more tired from all the arguing than I am from the actual work. I know what you mean. It feels like the world’s been turned upside down in the last few years. But I’m glad I’m still teaching—it gives me a sense of purpose. That’s admirable. I used to teach, too. I retired a few years back, but I still miss the classroom. It’s a bit strange not having that routine. I can imagine. My days are pretty structured too, with lesson planning and all. But I’ve got a lot of students who are really passionate about language. It’s rewarding. That’s great. I always said teaching was a calling. I still read books on education, just for fun. That’s a good habit. I’ve been trying to get back into reading more, but my time is so limited. I’m always juggling work, family, and hobbies. You know, I used to have a garden. I planted everything—roses, tomatoes, herbs. It was a big part of my life after retiring. That sounds lovely. I’ve always wanted to try gardening, but I’m too busy. I do have a few pots on the windowsill, though. You should try it. It’s a great way to unwind. You can grow your own herbs, and it’s so satisfying when things go well. I still do a bit of it, even though it’s not as big as it used to be. I might just give it a go. I’ve heard it’s good for mental health too. Exactly. It gives you a sense of accomplishment, and you get to connect with nature again.

So, do you know what’s on tonight? I was thinking of watching that new sci-fi film they’re talking about. I heard it’s got some pretty cool visuals. Yeah, I remember hearing about it. I think it’s called  Celestial Vortex  or something like that. It’s supposed to be a mind-bending story with some really good special effects. Sounds interesting. I’ve been meaning to check out more sci-fi lately. I’ve been watching a lot of old classics, like  2001: A Space Odyssey  and  Blade Runner . But I think I’m ready for something new. That’s a great idea. I actually saw a trailer for that film last week. The director is someone I really respect—had a few hits with environmental themes. I think it’s got a message about the future of Earth and space exploration. That sounds like something we’d all appreciate. I’m a bit of a sci-fi geek, so I’d love to see it. But have you guys seen any good music lately that goes with the vibe? I’ve been really into some experimental electronic stuff lately. There’s this artist from Berlin, I think, named  Lumen . They blend ambient music with light shows. It’s pretty trippy. I’ve heard of that. I think I’ve seen a few of their performances online. It’s like a visual and auditory experience all at once. But I’ve also been listening to some indie rock. There’s this band from Manchester called  The Echoes —they’re really getting some attention. Oh, I know them. I think they’ve been playing some festival shows. I actually met one of the members a few months ago at a networking event. He said they’re working on a new album that’s going to be more introspective. That’s cool. I’ve been into some indie stuff too, but I’m not sure I’d call it introspective. I think I prefer something with a bit more energy. Like, maybe some punk or alternative? Yeah, I can see that. I’ve been listening to some alt-rock lately too. There’s this band called  The Reckoning —they’ve got a really passionate live show. I think they’re playing a gig in Newcastle next week. Maybe we could go? That sounds like a good idea. I could use a night out.

So, do you think we should go to the gym tomorrow? I’ve been trying to get back into shape. Honestly, I’m more of a ‘do it when I feel like it’ kind of person. But if you’re serious, I’d say go for it. Just make sure you don’t overdo it. I tried going to the gym last month. It was a mess. I got so sore I couldn’t even walk for a day. That sounds brutal. You didn’t even go for long, did you? No, I went for like an hour. And I was doing heavy weights. I thought I was being smart, but my body just rebelled. I’ve been thinking about taking a trip soon. Maybe somewhere warm? I’ve been feeling the cold weather all week. Yeah, I could do with a break from the rain. I was in South Spain last summer, and it was amazing. The sun, the beach, the food. I went to Greece last year. I stayed in this little town near Santorini. It was beautiful, but the weather was crazy. One day it was sunny, the next it was pouring with rain. Mate, that’s the Mediterranean, isn’t it? You can’t really plan anything because the weather throws a curveball every day. True. I was thinking maybe I should just take a road trip. Go somewhere with good music, a good view, and maybe a bit of adventure. What’s the point of music if you don’t have it when you’re driving? I mean, I’ve been trying to build a playlist for my upcoming road trip. It’s going to be all classic rock and some indie stuff. That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been compiling my own list too. I think I’m going to include some 80s synth pop. I mean, it’s not too cheesy, right? No, that’s fine. I mean, if it’s not too cheesy, it’s just nostalgia. Anyway, I’ve been trying to get into some new music too. I’ve been listening to a lot of lo-fi beats. It’s so calming, especially when you’re working on a project. You know what would make a road trip even better? A kids’ camp. A kids’ camp? You mean like a summer camp? Yeah, like a place where kids can go and have fun, learn new things, and maybe even make friends.

So, do you think the Euros are going to be as big as the Euros last time? I think they might be, but I don’t think the same excitement will be there. It’s a bit of a different vibe now with everything going on in the world. Yeah, I guess. I mean, football has always been a big deal here, but I feel like people are more distracted these days. Still, I can’t wait to see some top matches. The England vs. Germany game is gonna be a classic, right? Definitely. It’s always a big one. I just hope they don’t make the same mistakes as last time. You know, getting too defensive early on. Yeah, they did that last time. It’s like they always start too cautious. I mean, they’ve got some good players now. I think they could definitely do better than the last Euros. I agree. They’ve got a lot of potential, especially with the younger squad. They didn’t have that much experience back then, but now they’ve got players who’ve been through the Championship and other tournaments. Right, and they’ve got a few real stars now. I’ve been watching a few matches, and it’s been pretty good. I think the excitement is back, even if it’s not as loud as before. Yeah, maybe people are just more selective now. If the teams aren’t playing at their best, they don’t get the same reaction. But when they do, it’s still electric. True. I mean, the way they play now is more entertaining, I think. It’s not all about physicality and long balls anymore. It’s more about quick passing and clever moves. Exactly. I think that’s part of the reason why younger fans are more engaged. They grew up watching the more technical style of play. It’s not like the old days when it was all about power and brute strength. Speaking of which, have you been keeping up with the films? I know you mentioned you’re into some of the newer ones. Yeah, I’ve been catching up a bit. There’s been a few good ones lately. I just watched this one about the 1970s footballers, and it was really interesting. It’s got that nostalgic feel but with a modern twist. That’s cool.

I can't believe how much he's grown. Look at this photo—just a little boy, running around like a puppy, and now he's almost a teenager. Time flies, doesn't it? Yeah, it really does. I remember the day he first started walking. He was so clumsy, and you couldn't trust him to stay upright for more than a few seconds. Now he's got a whole personality and a lot of opinions. I know, it's amazing. I still remember the first time he ran into the living room and knocked over the lamp. I was so worried, but he just laughed and said, "Mum, I'm learning!" It was such a funny moment. Oh, I remember that too. You were so strict about things back then, weren't you? But I think it was good. He learned quickly. It's funny how the little things become memories when you look back. Yeah, I suppose I did. I wanted him to be safe, you know. But now he's growing up, and I can't stop him from doing everything. It's both exciting and scary. It's definitely a mix of emotions. You want to protect them, but you also want them to be independent. I think that's what growing up is about—learning to take care of yourself. I know. I’m trying to be more supportive and less strict. I understand that he needs to make his own choices now. But it's still hard to let go. It's a natural part of life, isn't it? Watching your children grow up and being part of their journey. I remember when he first started going to school. I used to take him every day, and now he's off to college. Time really does fly. Speaking of which, have you heard about the London Marathon? My brother-in-law is training for it. He said he wants to run it with his son. It's going to be a nice way to celebrate their bond. That sounds like a great idea. I can’t wait to see him run. He’s been talking about it for weeks. I think it’s a way for him to stay active and make some good memories with his son. Yeah, it's a great event. I’ve always thought it was inspiring, especially for people who want to challenge themselves.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play that game with the wooden blocks? The one where you had to build a house and then knock it down? I swear, we spent hours on that. Oh yes, I remember that! We used to use the biggest blocks we could find, and we’d try to make the tallest tower. But of course, it always collapsed in the end. I think it was because we were too excited and kept knocking it over. Oh, it was always you and your brother trying to be the best at everything. I used to just sit and watch, because I was scared of knocking it down. But you and your brother would always argue about who made the best tower. Yeah, and I remember you used to get so upset when you lost. But I think you were the one who made the most stable ones, even if you didn’t get the prize. You always had a way of making things last longer. I remember one time, we even used the blocks to build a little house for the dog. It was just a box with some paper on it, but it looked like a real house. The dog loved it. Oh, I remember that! You used to put little bits of clothes on it too – bits of old socks and things, like it was really important. And you even tried to make a door with one of the blocks. It didn’t work, but it was funny to watch. Oh yes, and we used to read books about building and gardening, because we thought it made us smart. I think we even tried to grow vegetables in the garden, but we only got weeds. I think we even tried to make a little garden shed with the blocks. It was just a square box, but we thought it was the best thing ever. We even painted it with the wrong colours, like red and green, because we thought it was more creative. Oh, I remember that too! You used to call it ‘The Castle of Glass’ or something like that. It was just a wooden box with some ribbons tied to it, but you thought it was the most amazing thing in the world. And you started to get into knitting and crocheting later on, didn’t you?

Well, I've just had a cup of tea and a sandwich. It's nice and warm, isn't it? Yes, it’s a good old cup of tea. I always say that tea’s the best thing about being at home, isn’t it? You can have it whenever you like. Mmm, true enough. It’s not like when you’re out and about. I remember when I used to work, I used to have a cup of tea in the morning and then again during the lunch break. But now, I just like to have it in the evenings when I’m relaxed. That’s the way to do it, really. You’ve got to make time for yourself. I suppose so. But I used to think I had to be doing something all the time. Now I just like to sit and listen to the radio and have a cup of tea. That’s what I do too. I’ve always been the type to like a bit of quiet time. I remember when I was young, we used to have to work hard and never stop. Now, I just like to be at home, have a cup of tea, and enjoy the peace and quiet. I think it’s important to take time out. Especially after all those years of work. Oh, I know. And I think the kids used to think we were lazy, but they didn’t understand. It’s not that we don’t want to do anything, it’s just that we want to do what we like. Exactly. I think people today don’t know how to slow down. They’re always rushing about. Yeah, it’s all about speed these days. Everything has to be done quickly. I miss the days when things were slower. You had time to think, to reflect, to enjoy life. I agree. You can’t just rush through everything. Life’s too short to be in a hurry. That’s the thing, isn’t it? You’ve got to live for yourself and not for the clock. Exactly. I think that’s why I like being at home. It’s all about being comfortable and being with the people I love. It’s a good way to live, really. Just being content with what you’ve got. I couldn’t agree more. I think we’ve both had a good life.

So how’s life treating you, Jess? You’ve been quiet since we last caught up. It’s been a whirlwind, honestly. Work’s been hectic, and then there’s this new project that’s thrown me for a loop. I’m kind of over it now, though. I think I need a holiday. A holiday? You haven’t even taken a break since you started this job. You should go somewhere nice, like the coast. I heard there’s this amazing place in Cornwall that’s really laid-back. Oh, I’ve been meaning to go there too. I’ve got this friend from school who’s been raving about it. I’ve only got a few days off next month, though. I’m not sure if I’ll make it. That’s what I’m talking about! If you take a break, you’ll be fresh when you come back. I’m thinking of taking a gap year. Maybe a bit of travel and some time to myself. I feel like I’ve been working non-stop since university. That sounds like a good plan. I’ve been thinking about it too. I’ve been meaning to do some writing and maybe even start my own blog. It’s been on my to-do list for ages. I just never get around to it. That’s inspiring, really. I’ve been meaning to write more too. I’ve got this idea for a short story, but I’m not sure where to start. Maybe someone should help me get it off the ground. That’s a great idea. Maybe we could work on it together? I’d be happy to help. I’m not the best at writing, but I can at least give you a few ideas to get started. Yeah, I’d love to help too. I think it’d be fun. And besides, we’re all just trying to find our way. It’s part of the journey, right? Exactly. It’s not about being perfect. It’s about trying, and having the support of friends like you two. I feel like I’ve been getting a bit lost lately, and I really need to refocus. That’s what friends are for, isn’t it? To keep each other on track. I know I’ve had some ups and downs lately, but I think I’m starting to find my feet again.

So, do you live in the same area as your family, Sarah? No, actually, I live in a different part of the city. My mum and dad are in the old part of town, near the docks. It’s a bit of a commute, but I like the place I’m in now. It’s quieter, more family-friendly. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve only been here a few months, but I’m starting to feel like this is home. I live in a flat with a couple of other people. We share the bills and the kitchen. It’s not the most luxurious, but it’s cosy. Cool, I live in a house with my mum and dad. It’s not too big, but it’s got a garden, which is nice. I don’t know if I’ll ever move out. Living with them is easier than dealing with rent and all that. Fair enough. I grew up in a small flat in the city, but I moved to the suburbs a few years ago. It’s more space, more privacy, but you get less of that local community vibe. I miss the convenience of being in the city, though. I can imagine. My mum always used to say that living in the city is like being on a bus – you’re always moving, always running, but you’re never really still. It’s exhausting, but it’s also exciting. I think the city is great for some things, but it’s also so expensive. I don’t know how people afford to live there. I mean, I have a job, but I still feel like I’m barely making ends meet. Rent alone is a big chunk of my salary. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been saving up to buy my own place, but I don’t think I’ll be able to do that for a while. My dad says I should just wait until I’m older and have a better job. But I don’t know if I’ll even be in the same place then. It’s a tough market. Even people with high-paying jobs struggle. I’ve heard stories about people renting out their homes and then trying to buy one themselves, only to find their mortgage payments go up because of property prices. It’s a bit of a cycle.

I've been thinking a lot about our trip to Nepal, you know. I was just reading about the places we could visit and how it's such a beautiful country. I remember when I was younger, I used to travel all over the world, even to the Far East. It was a different time, wasn't it? Oh yes, it was. I still remember when I was in my twenties, I went to India and stayed with a family in Delhi. I had so many stories to tell. But I think it’s nice that we’re planning to go now, even if it's just for a few weeks. I’ve always wanted to go to the Himalayas, you know. You know, I think the best time to go is late spring or early autumn. The weather is usually the most pleasant then, and the views of the mountains are absolutely stunning. I remember when I was a teacher, I had a student who wrote an essay about the Himalayas and how they looked like they were made of glass. That's how beautiful they are. That would be amazing to see. But tell me, have you gone anywhere else recently? I know you used to go to the countryside a lot. Oh, I went to the Lake District last month. It was so peaceful. I remember when I was a child, my family used to go there every summer. We'd stay in a cottage and just enjoy the quiet. I've been meaning to take my grandkids there again. Oh, that sounds lovely. I read somewhere that the Lake District is still a very popular place for people who want to get away from the hustle and bustle of the city. I’ve also been thinking about about how much food has changed over the years, especially with all the gluten-free diets and food allergies. Absolutely. I remember when I was teaching, we had to make sure that all the food we served in the school was safe for everyone. It was a lot of work, but it was important. Do you think there’s a way to make gluten-free meals just as tasty as regular ones? I think it’s doable, especially with the variety of alternatives these days. I actually tried a gluten-free sandwich last week and it was quite good. Of course, it didn’t taste exactly like the regular one, but it was still satisfying.

So, do you ever find it weird that we’re all in our late twenties and still haven’t really figured out what we want to do with our lives? I mean, I know it's not that simple, but sometimes I look at my friends and they’ve got their jobs sorted, or they’re moving abroad or starting up their own businesses, and I’m just… well, I’m still doing events coordination, which is a bit of a boring job if I’m honest. Oh, don’t get me started. I’ve been in the same role for almost three years now, and I still feel like I’m just waiting for the right opportunity to come along. I mean, I’m not complaining, but sometimes I wonder if I’m just stuck in a rut. I keep telling myself I’ll start my own production company eventually, but I’m not even sure what that would even look like. Honestly, I think we all feel that way at some point. I’ve been in admin for over two years now, and I keep thinking, “I should be doing something more meaningful.” But I don’t know what that is. I mean, I enjoy my job, but it’s not as fulfilling as I thought it would be. I guess we’re all just… waiting for something to happen, right? Yeah, it’s like we’re all in limbo. I mean, I’ve got a postgrad degree, and I thought that would open up more doors, but it hasn’t really. I mean, someone at work just said I’m “constantly overqualified” for my current role. That’s not something I ever expected to hear. I’ve heard that too. My boss keeps saying I have “a lot of potential,” but I’m not even sure what that means. I mean, what does potential even mean in a job like this? It’s not like we’re in a position where we can just quit and start something new. I can’t afford to take a risk right now. I know, it’s frustrating. I tried to get into a different field last year, but I couldn’t find anything that paid enough. I’ve got a postgrad in business too, and I still feel like I’m not getting anywhere. Sometimes I think the system is set up so that it’s really hard to move up unless you have the right connections.

So, do you think we should go ahead and start the petition for the library? I mean, it's really important to us, isn't it? I think it's a great idea, honestly. I mean, the library has been a cornerstone of our community for years. It's not just about books, it's about the space people use for study, meetings, even just hanging out. If it gets demolished, we lose so much more than just a building. Yeah, exactly. And think about the kids—where would they go for homework? The council can't just say "we don’t have the money" and make that decision so lightly. We need to make them aware of how many people are affected. I agree. I think we should also rally more people to sign the petition. Maybe even get some local councillors to back us up. It might be a bit of a battle, but if we present it properly, we could make a real difference. That’s what I was thinking. I’ve been thinking about the shifts I have at work—maybe I could take some time off to help organize this. I mean, it’s not as if I’m overworked or anything. I’d rather spend my time supporting the community than just sitting in an office. Mate, you’re a legend. I mean, you’re already working part-time, and you’re willing to put in more for something you believe in. I don’t even know where I’d start. I’m stuck in this admin job, trying to keep afloat, and I can’t even think about getting involved in something like this. It’s not about the money, it’s about the people. The library’s been a part of our lives for so long. I remember when I was a kid, going there every Saturday to study. I mean, it’s not just about the books—it’s about the memories and the sense of belonging. That’s true. I think it’s a shame how so many of these places are being closed down or redeveloped without input from the people who use them. It’s like they don’t even care anymore. I’ve heard about the borough council trying to get rid of the library in the proposal. It’s so frustrating. They say it’s about “streamlining services,” but I don’t think they’ve actually done any real research into what the community needs.

So, do you know what’s up with the Jehovah’s Witnesses around here? They’ve been knocking on doors like it’s the end of the world again. I swear, I’ve seen more of them in the past week than I have in the past ten years. Oh, they’re just doing their thing, I suppose. I don’t mind them, but I reckon some of the villagers are getting a bit fed up with all the door-to-door stuff. I heard someone was even giving them a bit of a tongue-lashing last week. Oh, I heard about that. I think it was the guy from the bakery. He’s always been a bit of a tough nut, and he’s not the type to let people walk in and start preaching. I think he said something about them being a bit too pushy. Yeah, I bet he did. I mean, look at the way they’re all dressed up, and they just go around saying stuff like "the world’s going to end soon." It’s not exactly subtle. I mean, why not just put up a sign and save people the trouble of knocking on doors? Well, it’s their job, I suppose. But I still think they’re a bit over the top. I remember when my wife was still alive, she used to get quite annoyed with them. She said they were trying to convert the whole village. Oh, I can imagine. I’ve heard some of the stories, and some of them are pretty wild. But I’m not sure they’re all that bad. I mean, they do help out with the food bank, and they’re always asking if people need anything. Yeah, I suppose they do. But I still think they’re trying to push their own beliefs on everyone. I mean, not everyone wants to hear about the end of the world. Some people just want to enjoy a nice cup of tea and a nice piece of cake. I hear you. I think a lot of people are just tired of hearing about them. You know, the whole village has got its own way of doing things, and they’re just not respecting that. I agree. And it’s not just them. I’ve heard some people talk about the dentists lately. I mean, if you don’t get your teeth done, you just end up with a lot of pain, but I think some of the dentists here are charging way too much for simple things.

So, do you think we should get a log burner? I mean, the one in the living room is starting to look a bit tired, and it’s getting colder now. Yeah, I think it’s about time. We’ve had the same one since we moved in. But I was also thinking about the fudge shop down the road. You know, the one that just opened up last month? I heard they make some amazing dark chocolate fudge. Oh, I’ve heard about that. My husband and I went there last weekend and it was absolutely delicious. The owner even made a batch for us to take home. I’m still eating it, actually. That sounds wonderful. I always think of fudge when I’m in the mood for something sweet. But I’m more of a mashed potato person, myself. The kind you make with butter and cream, not the instant stuff. I agree. I mean, there’s nothing like a good bowl of mashed potato with a bit of gravy. But I have to say, I’m still trying to figure out how to get the perfect texture. I’ve tried everything from using a masher to a food processor, and I still can’t quite get it right. Maybe it’s the ingredients. You know, the kind of potato you use makes a big difference. I’ve heard that Russet potatoes are the best for mashed potatoes. Oh, I’ve heard that too. And I think the butter is just as important. I remember when I was a headmistress, one of the teachers once told me that the key to a good mashed potato is being able to make it fluffy and smooth, not just a lump of mashed up potatoes. Exactly. And the real trick is to let it rest for a bit after you cook it. That way, the starches have time to settle and the texture becomes lighter. I’ll try that. But I’m also worried about the budget. I mean, with all the things we have to pay for, like the log burner and the new restaurant down the street, I’m not sure if we can afford to keep up with all these little luxuries. I know, it’s a bit of a strain. But I think it’s worth it if it makes us happy. And besides, the new restaurant is supposed to be fantastic.

I don’t know, I just don’t think we can afford to buy a house. Not with the way things are going and the taxes they’re trying to hike up. I mean, what’s the point of having a pension if you can’t even afford the mortgage? Yeah, I was thinking the same thing. I mean, we’ve got the pension, but if we had to pay more in council tax and then also buy a house, it’s just going to eat into what we have. Plus, who’s gonna look after the garden and the house? I don’t even want to think about it. I know, I know. I used to manage a few kids, and I had to make sure the house was always in order, even if it was just a small flat. But now, I’m not even sure I’d want to be responsible for a whole house again, let alone try to buy one. I’d rather just rent somewhere simple and keep my money in savings. Yeah, but even savings are not safe. I mean, with the way the banks are acting these days, you don’t know what’s going to happen. I keep telling myself that if I had a bit more, I could maybe buy something, but it’s just not happening. I remember when we were younger, we could afford almost anything. Now, even a new TV is a big decision. I mean, I still have that old one from the 90s, and it works just fine. I don’t think I need a new one. I had a new one last year, but it broke after three months. I got a refund, but I still feel like I got ripped off. I mean, what’s the point of having the latest tech if it doesn’t last? I think they just make things break easier now. I think it’s all the Sat Nav stuff. You know, the ones that can’t even find your way home if you’re in the middle of nowhere. I was trying to get to a friend’s place in a remote part of Norfolk the other day, and the Sat Nav said to take a road that didn’t exist. I had to turn around and go the long way, even though I knew the way.

Alright, did you get the computer fixed, love? Not really, dad. The guy from the shop said it's still under warranty, so he's gonna take it in tomorrow. Oh, good. I was worried it would cost us a fortune. Yeah, I know, but it’s better to get it sorted properly. You know how these things can go. Yeah, I know. The thing is, I’ve had it for like three years now, and it's starting to get a bit slow. I can’t even imagine. I’ve been trying to keep up with my toddler’s tantrums, and now I’m trying to figure out how to log on to my email. It’s ridiculous. I know, I know. But you know, I had an old PC at home and it was like that, too. You just have to be patient. Mummy, my ears are sticky out! Oh no, not again. Come here, sweetheart. Let me get you a towel. You’re not the only one with sticky ears, mate. I had the same thing when I was little. Mate, you’re just like your mother, you know. She used to have a reputation for sticky ears and making a mess at the table. Shush, you. I was a perfect child. Yeah, right. You were the one who once tried to paint the walls with your fingers and left a big blob in the middle of the living room. I remember that. You were so proud of your masterpiece. I was. It was a very... creative expression. Right, well, the computer thing is on hold for tomorrow. What about the rugby match? Did you get the tickets sorted? Not yet. I was going to ask you when you got back. Yeah, I’ve got them here. I’ll bring them over later. I’ve got the schedule, too. Perfect. I can’t wait to see you all play. It’s been a while since we had a game. I know. I’ve been practicing my kicks in the garden all week. You’ve been practicing? Yeah, I had to, since I’ve been playing with the backup team this week. I’m so proud of you. You’ve done really well. Thanks, Mum. I think I’ve got a real chance to make the first team now. That’s great, lad. You’ve worked really hard for it.

Alright, do you want some pizza? Yeah, I’m really hungry. Me too! I could eat a whole pizza by myself! Well, we’re getting some for the party tonight, and I think it’s going to be a really good one. What kind of pizza? I wanted to do a vegetarian one. A lot of veggies, like peppers, mushrooms, olives, and maybe some pineapple. Pineapple on pizza? Is that even allowed? Oh, it’s totally allowed! Some people love it, some people hate it. I think it’s a bit of a controversial choice. I think it’s weird. I mean, pineapple is sweet and pizza is salty. It doesn’t go together. Yeah, and it looks like a fruit salad on a pizza! I think it’s just about personal taste. Some people say it’s a guilty pleasure, but I actually like it. Okay, but what about the communication part? I’m still not sure how to tell my mom I don’t like pineapple on pizza. You just say, “Mom, I’m not a fan of pineapple on pizza.” That’s it! Yeah, but she might not take it well. Maybe you should try to explain why you don’t like it. Oh no, I’m scared she’ll get mad. Don’t worry, she’ll understand. Or maybe she’ll be like, “You don’t like pineapple? That’s not a big deal!” I think she’ll be cool with it. I mean, she’s not that strict. Speaking of things we like, did you know there’s a story about the Loch Ness monster? Yeah, I heard about it before. But I don’t believe it. I think it’s just a big fish or something. But people say it’s a monster that lives in the lake. What does it look like? I think it’s supposed to be really big, like a dinosaur or something. Is it like a dragon? Maybe. Some people say it’s like a serpent. Oh, I think I saw a picture of it once. It looked like a giant crocodile! That’s funny! I mean, if it’s a crocodile, then it’s not a monster. It’s just a big lizard. Yeah, maybe it’s just a big fish. I mean, no one has ever seen it, so maybe it’s just a myth. Exactly! And if it is real, maybe it’s just hiding.

So, do you think we should go for the fish or the steak? I’m really hungry, but I don’t know what’s better here. I think the fish is probably fresher, especially since we’re in Istria. Plus, I heard the seafood here is amazing. But I also want to try the steak, just to see what they do with it. Yeah, I’m with Speaker_2. I love steak. But I’m also curious about the seafood. I’ve never been to a place where they serve fresh fish like this before. Maybe we should split the bill and try both? That’s a good idea. But we need to be careful with the portions. I don’t want to overeat because I still have to drive back later. And I’m not sure what the weather is like today. Yeah, the weather was a bit chilly this morning, but it’s supposed to warm up a bit later. I don’t know if we should go for a swim or just stay in the restaurant. I’d love to go for a swim, but I don’t know if the pool is open yet. I think it might be early in the season. Have you seen any signs? I saw a sign outside saying the pool is open from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. today. Maybe we can go after we eat? But I don’t know if it’s too crowded. Honestly, I’d rather stay in and talk. I’ve read about a lot of bad experiences with swimming pools in Croatia. Also, I heard about some people getting sick from the water because of the chemicals. Not sure if it’s safe. That’s true. I’ve heard about some water issues in other parts of the country. Maybe we can just enjoy the food and the view instead? Yeah, that sounds better. I mean, the food here is probably the main attraction anyway. Plus, we can always go for a walk after. You know, I’ve been thinking about going to the cities in Istria. Have you ever been to Pula or Rovinj? I’ve heard Rovinj is amazing with its old town and the sea. I’ve been to Pula, actually. It’s a beautiful place, but I think it’s a bit touristy. I prefer smaller towns. What about Buzet? I’ve heard it’s quite peaceful and has a nice vibe.

I've been thinking, you know, about all those people who get chased by debt collectors. They're always shouting and all that. I don't know how they can be so rude. I've never had that problem, though. No, I suppose not. But you know, it's not just the debt collectors. I had this one time when I was working as a childminder, and a man came to the door asking for money. He said he was from a financial services company. I thought, "Oh no, not again." I just told him I had no debts and sent him away. That sounds like a good idea. I used to work in a bank, so I know how they can be. Just keep your doors locked and don't let them in. They're just trying to scare you into paying more than you should. Yeah, and they often try to make it look like you've signed up to something. I had this thing with a PPI claim. It took me ages to get through all the red tape. I had to fight for every penny. Oh, I remember that. I think I had a PPI claim once too. It was a nightmare. I just gave up and didn't bother. I thought, "If I can't get my money back, then I won't bother with it." Yeah, I think that's the way to go. You know what I found interesting though? I read this article in the magazine about how people are using TV to escape from their problems. It's amazing how much we watch. I suppose it's better than being bored. I used to make a point of watching the most popular shows. I always thought it was a waste of time, but I can't deny it helps me relax. I know what you mean. I watch a lot of crime dramas. It’s like I'm living someone else’s life. Although, I did get into trouble once for watching a show too late. I missed my train and had to walk all the way home. Oh, I've been there. I used to catch the 7:45 train to London every morning. One day, I got so caught up in a programme that I stayed up watching it on the computer. I missed the train and had to walk for an hour in the rain.

So, how’s the court work going? You mentioned you’re a part-time court usher, right? Oh, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster lately. The court’s been really busy, especially with all the changes in the justice system. It’s been quite a shock for some people, I think. I mean, the procedures are changing so much, and it's all so different from how it used to be. Yeah, I’ve heard about that. It’s quite interesting, actually. I teach languages, so I like learning new things. But I can’t imagine how you’d handle all that legal jargon day in and day out. It’s not all that bad, honestly. You get used to it. And the people in the court – they’re from all walks of life, so it keeps things interesting. But I must say, the climate’s been a bit of a challenge lately. The weather’s been so unpredictable, and it’s affecting the schedules. One day it’s freezing, the next it's pouring with rain. It’s hard to keep things running smoothly. I can imagine. I mean, even in the city, the weather is so variable now. Have you noticed any changes in how people are dealing with it? Like, more people taking holidays or trying to adapt? Yeah, quite a few. Some people are trying to make more money by taking on extra shifts or side jobs, especially with the cost of living going up. I know a few people who’ve started doing deliveries or even a bit of gardening on the side. It’s a bit of a struggle, though. That must be tough. I’ve been reading a bit about how the economy is affecting different parts of the country. It’s quite worrying, really. I guess that’s part of the reason why people are trying to find extra ways to earn. Exactly. And it’s not just about money. There's also the transport issue. With the roads getting worse and public transport being so unreliable, it’s hard to get around. I know some people are planning to travel more, but it’s not as easy as it used to be. Yeah, I think that’s something a lot of people are dealing with. It’s frustrating when you want to go somewhere or meet up, but the transport just doesn’t work.

Alright, do you know what makes you really happy? I think it’s when I get to play with my toys and have a nice big bowl of cereal! Yeah, and when we all play together and laugh, that makes me happy too. That’s right. Laughter is the best medicine, isn’t it? Yeah, and when I get a new toy or a storybook, I’m so excited! I like when we go to the park and run around. It’s like flying! That’s a great feeling. And when you feel happy, you can sing and rhyme too. Oh, I know! Like “In the morning, when the sun shines bright, I’m happy, I’m happy, I’m so happy today!” Mm, that’s a good one. I like “I’m a little teapot, short and stout, here is my handle, here is my spout.” Very nice! You both have such a good memory for rhymes. I wish I was as good as you. You’re a teacher, so you should know all the rhymes! Ha! Maybe I should start teaching you more. Can we learn a new one together? Of course! What’s something you like? I like cookies! Okay, here’s one: “I like cookies, they’re so sweet, I like cookies, they’re so sweet.” That’s good! What about about money? Do you think having lots of money makes you happy? Hmm, that’s a good question. I think having money is important, but it doesn’t make you happy all the time. I don’t think I care about money. I just want to play and have fun. Yeah, I think having money is good for things like food and toys, but if you don’t have friends or family, it’s not as important. That’s a very wise thought. I think happiness comes from love, laughter, and being with the people you care about. Yeah, and when we’re together, we’re always happy! And when we sing and rhyme, we’re even happier! You two are making me feel really happy too. Let’s keep singing and rhyming all day! Okay! Let’s do it! I can’t wait! Alright, let’s start with “I’m happy, I’m happy, I’m so happy today!” I’m happy, I’m happy, I’m so happy today! I’m happy, I’m happy, I’m so happy today!

So, do you think you're gonna go into a proper career or just be like me, working in a shop when I’m older? I don’t know, man. I think I might want to do something with tech or maybe invent something. You know, like a patent or something? Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. I reckon if you invent something, you could be rich. Like, if you invent a new kind of robot or something, you could make millions. Yeah, but it's not that easy. You’ve got to get it right, and then you’ve got to get it to the right people. Plus, the government might not even let you sell it if it’s too dangerous. Yeah, but what about China? I heard they’re building all these cool things. Like, the biggest bridges and fastest trains and everything. They’re investing so much in tech. That’s true. I think they’re going to be the biggest economy in the world soon. Like, maybe even bigger than the US. You know, with all the money they’re putting into infrastructure and stuff. I’ve read that they’re investing in AI as well. Like, they have these supercomputers that can do things way faster than ours. Maybe they’ll even take over the world one day. Haha, maybe. But I don’t think that’s going to happen. You need a lot of people to agree on something like that. Plus, the world’s too big for one country to control. Yeah, but what about patents? I mean, if you invent something, you can copyright it, right? Like, if you make a new app or something, the company can sell it forever. Yeah, but you have to register it. I think it costs a lot of money to do that, though. And if you’re not careful, someone else could copy your idea and sell it as their own. Oh man, that would be so unfair. I’d be like, “That’s my idea!” and they’d just ignore me. I guess that’s why people have to do it properly. Yeah, and then you have to get a lawyer. I heard my uncle had to get a lawyer for his invention, and it cost him a fortune. That’s not cool. I mean, what if you could just invent something and make a million quid in a day?

So, do you think we should go skiing tomorrow? I mean, we’ve had a few days of snow already, and the slopes are still pretty good. Honestly, I was thinking the same thing. I don’t know, I feel like we’ve already done a lot of the main runs. But maybe we could try something a bit more challenging? Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve heard the Black Forest run is quite a decent one. It’s not too technical, but it’s a bit longer. Maybe we can do that in the morning and then take it easy in the afternoon? Sounds like a plan. Although, I’m a bit worried about the weather. It’s been a bit unpredictable these past few days. I don’t want us to get caught in a storm. Yeah, the forecast does say there might be some snow showers later today. I think we should check the forecast again before we decide. But honestly, I’d rather be out on the slopes than stuck in the hotel eating cake and watching TV. I know, I get that. I’ve been dying to get back on a chairlift. It’s been so long since I last skied properly. I feel like I’ve been surviving rather than actually enjoying it. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to keep up with my routines, but honestly, it’s not the same without the proper gear and the right mindset. I mean, I still have that old pair of skis from when I was a kid, but they’re definitely not up to scratch. You should really think about getting a new pair. It’s not just about the sport, it’s about the experience. You can’t really enjoy it if you’re struggling with your equipment. I know, I know. I just haven’t had the time. My business has been quite hectic lately, and I’m trying to balance everything. But maybe this trip will be the push I need to actually take some action. I hope so. And you know, if you do, I’d be happy to help you find a good pair. I’ve been doing some research on the best skis for beginners. Plus, I’ve been looking into some rental options too. Maybe we could check those out together. That would be great.

Alright, so I’ve been thinking about this racket repair thing. I’ve got a few ideas, but I’m not sure what’s the best way to go about it. I mean, I know the strings break because of the tension, but how do you actually fix them? Well, I’ve seen a few different methods, but the most common one is using cable ties. You know, those little plastic ones you use to bundle stuff up. They’re strong and don’t stretch, so they hold the strings in place better. But you have to be careful not to over-tighten them. Yeah, but I’ve heard that cable ties can cause problems with the grip of the racket. If they’re too tight, you might not be able to get a good hold on the strings. I’m thinking about using something more flexible, like a type of wire or maybe even a special string holder. But I’m not sure what’s available or how much it costs. That makes sense. I’ve also thought about the materials. You have to make sure the cable ties or whatever you use are the right size and strong enough to hold the tension. I remember seeing a video where they used a plastic clip that goes around the frame and then tightens. It’s a bit more expensive, but it seems more durable. I agree, but cost is always a concern. If the customer is paying out of their pocket, they might not want to spend too much. Still, if the repair lasts longer, it could save them money in the long run. I’m just not sure how to explain the value without making it sound like a scam. Right, but that’s part of the marketing. You have to make people understand why it’s worth the investment. Maybe you could show them how much cheaper it is to fix a racket than buying a new one. Or, if they’re in a school, you could talk to the PE department about bulk orders. That might cut costs and make it more appealing. Speaking of schools, I wonder if you could pitch this idea to a primary school first. They tend to have more young players, and the rackets are more likely to get damaged. Plus, you could even set up a trial run with a few kids.

I've been thinking a lot about art lately. Oh, really? What's got you thinking about art? It's just that I saw a documentary on TV about the old masters—Turner, Constable, those sort of people. That’s interesting. I always liked Constable. His landscapes are so vivid. Yeah, I remember seeing one of his paintings in the National Gallery. It was a stormy sky, and it looked like it could actually rain. Didn’t it? I mean, he was a real observer of nature, wasn’t he? I think he was. He must have had a keen eye for detail. I remember reading somewhere that he painted the sky differently every day, depending on the weather. That’s amazing. It must have taken a lot of skill. I mean, even now, I can’t imagine painting something like that. I suppose it’s not just about the skill, though. It’s also about the emotion and the story you want to tell through the painting. Exactly. And I think that’s why art can still move people today, even after all these years. I agree. My gran used to say that art was like a window into the soul. That’s poetic. I think that’s why I love teaching art. It’s not just about the technique—it’s about the connection between the artist and the viewer. I can see that. Though I never got much into art myself. I’m more of a practical person. That’s okay. Not everyone has to be an artist. But I think even the most practical people can appreciate the beauty in art. Yeah, I think so. I mean, even the way we arrange our homes, the furniture we choose, it all reflects some kind of artistic choice, doesn’t it? Absolutely. It’s everywhere. So, maybe I should start learning a bit more about it. I mean, with all the time I’ve got now that I’m retired. That’s a good idea. Maybe you could try visiting some local galleries or even taking a course. Or maybe we could all go together on a trip to some art museum. It’d be a nice way to spend a day. I’d like that. I’ve been meaning to visit the Norfolk Art Gallery anyway. They’ve got some really interesting exhibits. That sounds like a plan.

I swear, I don’t know how anyone can be a woman anymore. I mean, it’s like,  what  do they do? Just sit around and be judged for everything? I mean, I’m not saying it’s easy, but I feel like I’ve been judged for  everything  I’ve ever done. Yeah, I get that. But come on, not all girls are like that. I mean, I work in mental health, and I’ve seen so many people who are just  so  hard on themselves. It’s like, why do we even have to act like we’re perfect? I know, I know. But sometimes it feels like the whole world is watching you and waiting for you to mess up. Like, if you take a wrong step, everyone’s like, “Oh, there she goes again.” I’m sorry, but you’re not  that  perfect. I mean, everyone has a bad day. Yeah, but I feel like I have to be perfect in every way, or else I’m not worth anything. And it’s not even just the people I know — it’s like, the whole culture. It’s like, we’ve got this idea that women are always supposed to be the best, the most capable, but then when we’re not, we’re just…  hated  or something. That’s not fair. I mean, I don’t even know what’s going on with you sometimes. You work so hard, and you’re a project co-ordinator, and you’re so good at your job. Why do you feel like you’re under so much pressure? I don’t know. Maybe because I used to be such a perfectionist. I mean, I used to  panic  if I got a B in an exam. Like, I thought I was going to fail for life. But now, I’m like, “Yeah, I got a B. I’m still okay.” But it’s hard to shake that mindset. I think part of it is just being in a world where people take so long to act. Like, do you remember the last time you actually  cleaned  this kitchen? Because I swear, it looks like a war zone. Ugh, I know. I’ve been so busy with work and everything, and I just… haven’t had time. I’m planning to clean this weekend, though. Yeah, yeah, but you’ve been saying that for  months .

I just don’t get how people can be so against smoking, you know? It’s not like it’s a secret or anything. You can’t just walk into a café and not have a cigarette if you want one. I mean, I don’t even understand the anti-smoking campaigns. They’re like, “Don’t smoke,” but they don’t say, “Don’t smoke if you’re not in a place where people can smell it.” Yeah, I mean, I don’t smoke, but I know plenty of people who do. And I also know that the whole point of the campaigns is to make it harder for people to smoke. If you can’t even go into a café and have one, then it’s like forcing people to quit. But I still think it’s a bit much. People need to make their own decisions. That’s the thing. It’s not like they’re forcing you to quit. They’re just making it inconvenient. And honestly, I don’t think it’s about the health aspect as much as it is about the culture of it. I mean, I’ve seen people who are super intelligent and healthy, and they still smoke. So, what’s the point of banning it? It’s like, “We’re smarter than you, so we don’t do that.” That’s a good point. I mean, sometimes it feels like people who are into feminism or anti-smoking campaigns have this idea that if you're not doing something, you’re not smart enough to do it. Like, "If you’re not a vegan, you must not care about the planet." Or, "If you smoke, you must not be smart." It’s like they’re equating intelligence with morality or health, which is just not true. Exactly! And I think part of it is cultural. In some countries, smoking is just a part of life. You can’t go anywhere without seeing people with cigarettes. But in places like the UK, it's become this huge taboo. You can’t even light up in your own garden anymore in some places. You have to go to a designated area, and that’s just not practical. I keep telling my sister that. She’s the one who always says, “Oh, I’m going to quit soon.” Then she goes out on the weekend, and there she is, smoking like it’s nothing.

So, did you both have a good time at the farm today? I heard you went there with the grandparents. Yeah, it was really fun! We saw all sorts of animals – cows, sheep, even a horse. I tried to feed the sheep, but they just stared at me like I was a weirdo. I was the one who got really close to the horse. It was so big, but it was really gentle. I even got to ride it for a bit. That sounds amazing. Did you take any photos? Yeah, I did. I even got one of me holding a baby lamb. It was so cute, and the lamb didn’t even blink. Oh, you’re such a good photographer. I wish I had half your talent. Anyway, how was the rest of the day? We had a picnic in the field, and we played some games. There was a little obstacle course, and I won the race! I was so proud. That’s great to hear. I was worried about how you’d behave at school today, especially after that farm visit. You both seem to be getting more restless lately. I know, Mum. I’ve been acting out a lot at school. My teacher said I got distracted during class and didn’t pay attention to the lesson. I didn’t mean to, though. I understand, sweetheart. It’s been a big week for you. The farm was fun, but maybe it made you a bit overstimulated. I’ll talk to your teacher and see what we can do to help you focus better. I’ve been trying to do better at school. I even brought a sticker chart for myself to keep track of my good behaviour. That’s brilliant! I’m really proud of you both. You’re growing up so fast. Maybe you can tell me about the DVDs you watched last night? I heard you got a new one. Oh, we watched a movie about a girl who lived on a farm and had a magical horse. It was so exciting! I wanted to ride a horse like her. I thought it was amazing too. I even started drawing my own farm with a horse and a sheep. I’m going to put it on the fridge. That sounds lovely. I can’t wait to see it. Just don’t forget to eat your vegetables before you watch another DVD, okay?

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing I’ve learned since I started knitting again? It’s not just the actual making of the stuff, it’s like, it’s calming. I feel like I’m in this little bubble, you know? Yeah, I get that. I’ve been knitting on and off since uni, but it’s been a while. I think I’m actually going to try a scarf this week. I’ve got the yarn and everything. Maybe I’ll even make it as a gift for someone. You know, the kind of thing that’s super useful but also shows you care. That sounds nice! I made a pair of socks for my mum last week. She loved them. It’s weird, isn’t it? The way you can make something so simple, but it still feels like a special gift. I think it’s because of the effort you put in, you know? Totally. I mean, I still feel like I’m not that good at it, but I keep going. It’s like the Olympics, isn’t it? It’s not about winning, it’s about participating and improving. I guess that’s the same with everything else, really. Yeah, I think that’s true. I remember watching the Olympics last year and thinking about how much dedication it takes to be at that level. It’s not just about talent—it’s about years of training and sacrifice. But then again, I’m not sure I’d ever be able to do any of that. I’m more of a ‘I can do a bit of this, a bit of that’ type of person. Hey, that’s okay. I think that’s what makes life interesting. I mean, I’ve always been into art, right? I mean, I’m not a professional, but I like to paint and draw. I even did a bit of sculpture in uni. My best work was probably the Easter egg I made out of clay. It was just a little bunny, but it turned out really nice. Oh, I remember that! You said you were going to sell them at the Easter market. Did you? I think I saw one of them in the local shop. I think it was a bit pricey, but it looked really good. Yeah, it was a bit of a hit.

I just got back from the National Museum of Natural History, it was absolutely packed, you know, like a rush hour in the middle of the day. Oh, I was thinking about going there this morning, but I got up late, and then I decided to take the tube to the Imperial War Museum instead. Oh, the Imperial War Museum? I’ve wanted to go there for ages. I heard they have some amazing exhibits from World War II. Yeah, it’s pretty good. But the thing is, when you're in London, the public transport system is a bit of a nightmare. I mean, I had to wait 20 minutes for the bus to get to the station, and then the train was delayed by like 15 minutes. I know, I was on the tube this morning and it was so crowded, I couldn’t even get a seat. I had to stand the entire time, and I was worried my knees would give out. I told you, the public transport is a mess. I mean, it's not like in the States, where I can drive anywhere I want. But here, you’re at the mercy of the system. Yeah, I was thinking about going to the IMAX cinema tonight. I saw a trailer for that new dinosaur documentary, and it looked amazing. Have you seen that? No, I haven’t. I mean, when I was younger, I used to love them, but now, with all the glasses and the processing, it’s a bit much. I know what you mean. I think it’s just the way things are now. You can’t really get away from the technology. Except when you're on a bus or the tube, and the screen is flickering like it’s on a broken television. Ha! That’s true. I think I’ll just go with the IMAX and leave the 3D for another time. Okay, sounds like a plan. I’ll meet you there, then. Great. Just make sure you get to the cinema on time. So, do you think we should go through with the Christmas dinner thing then? Honestly, I was just waiting for you to bring it up. I’ve been thinking about it all week. Good. I’ve been meaning to ask you — what’s the plan? Are we going to do it at my place or yours? My place actually. I’ve got a few things sorted. I’ve got the roast chicken in the fridge, and I’ve even got the side dishes. We can just pop the wine and some snacks in the fridge before we come. That sounds great. I’ll bring the dessert, then. I’ve been thinking about making that chocolate yule log again. You remember that one, right? Oh, I remember. It was a disaster the last time. You burnt the top layer, and the chocolate sauce didn’t set properly. Hey, I was in a rush! It was the first time I’d ever attempted it. But I’ve got a few more tricks up my sleeve this time. Well, I’ll take that as a challenge. If you’re going to be the dessert expert, I’ll be the main course expert. Sounds good. I just hope we can get the timing right. I’ve got a few colleagues stopping by later, and I want to make sure the whole thing goes smoothly. What’s the plan for the evening? Are we going to stay in or do we have any plans to go out? I was thinking we could have a couple of beers, maybe watch a movie or two. I’ve got a few old classics I want to show you. That sounds perfect. I’ve been wanting to watch that old John Cleese Christmas film. You remember the one with the snow globe? Oh, you mean  A Christmas Carol ? That’s the one. I was actually thinking of watching that myself. I thought you were going to say  The Life of Brian . That always comes up at this time of year. Yeah, that’s a good one too. But I think the classic is still the best. I mean, if you’re going to go for a Christmas movie, it’s hard to beat Dickens. Fair enough. But I’ll still be watching  Life of Brian  when we’re done. Just don’t let it get too late. I’ve got a meeting tomorrow morning, and I need to be up early.

So, do you ever just rage-quit on Twitter when someone says something really passive-aggressive? Like, I saw this review for a restaurant in Margate the other day, and it was like, “The service was slow, but the food was okay.” I mean, okay? What does that even mean? I’ve been there. I posted a photo of my cake and someone replied, “That looks like a cake, but not the best.” I was like,  what even is this?!  You just want to go and delete your account. I know, right? It’s like, why even bother? I mean, I get that people are harsh, but sometimes it feels like they’re just venting. I’ve had some terrible customers at the café, but I try not to take it personally. Yeah, but sometimes you just want to tell them, “Hey, I’m not your personal chef.” Like, I’ve had people come in, order the wrong thing, then say it’s not what they wanted. And I’m like,  I know it’s not what you wanted, but maybe you should’ve read the menu?  Haha, that’s so true. I reckon the worst part is when they write a one-star review and then say something like, “It was okay, but the coffee was bad.” And like,  okay?  You spent all that time making the coffee, and you’re just gonna say it’s “okay”? I’ve had a customer once who left a review that said, “The staff was rude and the coffee was cold.” But then I walked in and  they  were the ones waving around their phone like they were a critic. I just stared at them and said, “You’re the one who said the coffee was cold.” And they just looked away. That’s  so  good. I’d love to see that. But honestly, it’s so hard. I mean, I run a café, and I know how hard it is to get good reviews. Especially when people don’t even take the time to write a proper review. I’ve seen some of the worst reviews ever. One person wrote, “I had a terrible experience. The manager didn’t know anything.” And then they wrote, “I just wanted to say that I’m a customer, not an employee.” That’s just passive-aggressive to the max. I think I’m going to start taking reviews more seriously now.

Alright, Oisin, you've got to eat your vegetables. It’s dinner time. I don’t want to eat them. They’re so boring. Well, you’re not eating them then. You’ve got to try them. I don’t want to eat vegetables anyway. I want chocolate ice cream. You can have chocolate ice cream after you’ve eaten your veggies. No, I don’t want to eat vegetables. I just want to eat ice cream. Yeah, I don’t care about veggies. I like ice cream. Well, I think vegetables are good for you. You should eat them. Yeah, they’re good for you. And I’m not going to let you have ice cream unless you eat your greens. But I don’t like them. I just want ice cream. I know, I don’t like veggies either. I only like berries. You mean raspberries? Yeah, I like raspberries. They’re sweet. I like raspberries too. I think they’re nice. So why don’t you eat some of those with your dinner? But I don’t want to eat them with my dinner. I want to eat them with ice cream. Well, maybe you could try having some raspberry ice cream. That might be nice. Yeah, that could work. Or you could have a raspberry smoothie. Yeah, that sounds good. I like smoothies. I like smoothies too. I like strawberry and banana ones. You could try a raspberry one. It’s healthy, and it tastes good. I think it’s important to eat a variety of fruits and vegetables. Yeah, I know. I just don’t like to eat them with dinner. I don’t like them either. I just like chocolate ice cream. You can have chocolate ice cream after dinner, but you have to eat your veggies first. Okay, I guess I’ll try that. That’s the spirit. Now, let’s all have dinner. Yeah, let’s start with some veggies and then have some ice cream. Yeah, I’ll try them. Okay, I’ll try them too. Great, I can’t wait to see you all enjoying your meal. Yeah, let’s eat and then we can have some ice cream later. Sounds good. Yeah, I’m really looking forward to chocolate ice cream. Alright, let’s get started. Alright, let’s eat. Yeah, let’s eat. Yeah, let’s eat. Alright, let’s start with some green beans and carrots.

So, do you think we should go out for dinner tomorrow, Mavis? I was thinking maybe that new Italian place in the centre. Oh, I’d love that, but I’m not sure I’m up for it. I’ve been feeling a bit off lately. Hasn’t it been hot in the house lately? I feel like I’ve been sweating more than usual. Maybe that’s why I’ve been so tired. Yeah, it’s been a bit stifling. I might have to get the fan out again. But don’t worry, I’ll get the air moving. I think it’s the heat, honestly. I’ve been sleeping so badly since the summer started.
