I’ve been so busy with work. But I do feel guilty about it. I should be helping out more, don’t you think? Oh, you’re doing enough, love. You’ve been more than helpful. I just… I’m not as young as I used to be. True, but you still have that sharp eye for cleaning. You could help me out with that new place I’m trying to tackle. What’s that? That dusty bookcase in the living room. It’s been gathering cobwebs since the last time we moved in. Oh, you know I’d be happy to do that. I do enjoy a bit of a challenge. But I’m still not sure I’m up for a night out. Well, I’m thinking of doing a food shopping trip next weekend, so maybe we can go out then. I can pick up some nice groceries for you. That sounds great. I could do with some fresh vegetables and a bit of meat to cook. And maybe some cake? I’ve been craving chocolate cake lately. You’ll have to wait for me then. I’ve been trying to go lighter on the sugar, but I won’t refuse you. Oh, that’s the spirit. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting my eyebrows done. I’ve been growing them out a bit, and they’ve gotten a bit messy. Oh, that sounds like a good idea. Or maybe even a haircut?

So, do you think we're ready for the weaning process? I mean, it's been a week now and she's been refusing the bottle more and more. I know, it's a bit scary, isn't it? But I think we're making progress. She’s been taking the spoon now, and she actually likes the taste of the porridge. It’s just a matter of time before she starts eating more solid stuff. Yeah, I guess so. I just wish it wasn’t so hard on her. She gets so upset when I try to take the bottle away. I feel terrible, but I know it's the right thing to do. I can totally understand. It’s tough on both of you. I remember when my brother was weaning, he had the same kind of tantrums. It’s not just the baby crying—it's the whole family going through it. But I think we're doing well. She’s starting to get used to the routine, even if it's a little chaotic. I hope so. I’ve been trying to get her into the routine of morning and evening feeds, and I think she’s starting to understand. It’s just the middle of the night that’s the hardest. I can’t even get her to sleep through without nursing anymore. I know, and I know how exhausted you must be. I’ve been telling my mum to come over and help out for a few days. She’s been saying she’s free this week, so maybe we can get some support. That way, you can get some rest too. That would be great. I’ve been trying to manage everything on my own, but it’s really wearing me down. I’m not used to the 24/7 thing. I miss being able to have a proper meal without having to stop and feed the baby every time. I know, and you’re not alone in that. I’ve been thinking about signing up for one of those sign language classes that the community center is running. It might help me communicate better with her when she’s upset. I’ve heard it’s really helpful for parents who are struggling with the weaning process. That sounds like a good idea. I’ve been thinking about it too. I remember reading about how sign language can help with communication, especially when the baby is too young to understand verbal cues.

I can't believe how peaceful it is out here. You know, I've been meaning to take a proper walk like this for ages. The city just feels so overwhelming sometimes. Yeah, I know what you mean. It's like the moment you step outside of the hustle and bustle, everything slows down. You can really appreciate the quiet. Exactly. I was actually thinking about how the hills here are so different from the ones in London. In the city, you don’t even get a chance to see a hill that’s not covered in buildings or roads. True. I remember the first time I came here with my parents. We were hiking up this hill and I was so out of breath, I thought I was going to die. But it was one of those moments where you feel like you’re really alive. That’s the thing, isn’t it? There’s something about being in the countryside that makes you feel like you’re in tune with nature. You can hear the birds, you can smell the earth after the rain, and you can just… breathe. I loved that. When I was a kid, my family would go on weekend trips to the countryside. We’d go to this little village just a mile away from our house. It had that sleepy, old-timey feel to it, like time had stood still. That sounds lovely. I’ve never lived in a place where the village was part of the daily life. I mean, here in Norwich, everything’s so close. You can walk to the shops, the university, the train station—there’s no escaping the city. I know what you mean. But there’s a charm to being in a place where everything’s a little slower. You can actually see the changing seasons, the way the fields look different in spring or autumn. It’s like the land itself has a rhythm. It’s almost like the hills here are like old friends. You know, you walk up them, you walk down them, and you always feel like you’re being guided by something bigger. Yeah, there’s a kind of magic to it. I’ve been thinking about going back to that village I mentioned. Maybe we could go there sometime. It’s not too far, and I think it’d be nice to have a quiet weekend in the countryside, just us.

So, do you know what’s really annoying me about the way people talk about cyclists? Like, they’re just... everywhere, and they don’t seem to care about the rules at all. I get that, but I think some of the rules are just outdated. I mean, cyclists are just as much road users as cars, right? They should be treated with the same respect. Yeah, but I still think they’re the biggest headache on the roads. I mean, you're just pulling out of a parking space and suddenly there's a cyclist zipping past, no signal, no nothing. It’s like they think they’re invincible. I know, it can be frustrating. But I think part of it is also the way cyclists are perceived. Like, they’re seen as reckless or arrogant. But I don’t think that’s fair. I mean, I’ve got a cousin who’s a cyclist, and he’s very responsible. He always signals, he’s aware of his surroundings, and he’s pretty good at navigating the traffic. That’s true. I guess it’s not all cyclists. But I still have that one incident where a cyclist was riding through a red light, and I had to brake hard to avoid hitting them. It was terrifying. Yeah, that’s definitely a problem. But I think it’s more about the culture around cycling. You don’t see as many cyclists in cities like London or Manchester as you do in places like Brighton or Bristol. Maybe that’s why there’s more awareness there. That’s a good point. I mean, I have a friend who worked in a film production company and she told me about this project they were doing about urban cyclists. They filmed all these stories from different people’s perspectives—cyclists, drivers, pedestrians. It was really eye-opening. That does sound interesting. I guess it’s like any kind of film, it’s about showing different viewpoints. I wonder if they managed to capture the frustration of drivers as well as the freedom of cyclists. I think they did. They had this one scene where a driver is trying to merge into a lane and gets cut off by a cyclist. It was so realistic, it felt like it was happening right there. I could see that being pretty tense. But at the same time, it’s also a reminder of how different roles on the road can lead to misunderstandings.

So, do you think we've seen all the best spots in this part of Norfolk yet? I mean, it’s got to be one of the flattest places in the country, but somehow the flowers just keep popping up everywhere. I think we’ve seen a lot, but there’s always something new. That field we walked through earlier had some of the most vibrant daffodils I’ve ever seen. I’ve only seen them in gardens before, not like that. Yeah, it’s like nature’s putting on a show. I wonder what the economics of all this biodiversity is. You know, like, is it even profitable to grow these flowers? Or is it just for aesthetics? It could be a cash crop, especially if you’re into things like lavender or roses. I know some places in the south of England make a good living off those. But in this part of Norfolk, it must be more about preservation than profit. Exactly. And it’s not just about the flowers, though. It’s the whole ecosystem. The bees, the birds—everything seems to be thriving here. I guess it’s the rural lifestyle that puts it all together. I suppose so. Although, I can’t help but think about how different it all would be if we were back in London. No flowers, no trees, just concrete and traffic noise. Sometimes I miss the peace of the countryside. I know, it’s a bit of a shock when you come back from the city. But I’ve been thinking about a paper I’m working on. It’s about the impact of language on perception of nature. Like, how people in urban areas describe the countryside versus those who live here. That’s interesting. I can see how someone from the city might describe the countryside as “boring” or “quiet,” while someone who lives here would say it’s “vibrant” or “full of life.” Exactly. And I think it’s a lot to do with the way we use language. Words like “lush” or “bustling” can shift the entire perception of a place. So what are you planning to do with the research? Are you going to present it at a conference? Yeah, I’m hoping to submit it to a regional linguistics symposium in Edinburgh. Hopefully, it’ll open up some interesting discussions. Sounds good. I’ve been meaning to get back into research too.

So, do you think we should go to the Angel of the North tomorrow? I mean, it’s been a while since we’ve done anything like that. Honestly, I've been meaning to go for ages. I think we should. But I need to check if my car can handle the journey. I'm not sure if the engine's up for it. You know, I heard a funny story about the Angel of the North the other day. Someone said it’s so big, it’s like it’s got its own gravitational pull. You can’t help but feel small next to it. That’s not funny. That’s just a bit dramatic. But I guess it does make sense. It’s a massive sculpture, after all. I think it’s one of the largest in the world. Yeah, but I think the real magic is in the way it looks at night. I mean, the lights up there—when they’re on, it’s like the whole thing is glowing. You can see it from miles away. That’s true. I remember when I first saw it, I was really struck by how it stands out against the landscape. It’s like it’s meant to be seen from a distance, almost like it’s a beacon. I know. Plus, I heard there’s a café nearby. I’ve been dying to try the food there. It’s supposed to be really good. And the views from the café, they say, are just as breathtaking. That sounds like a good plan. But I do need to make sure the car is okay. I think I should check the oil and the brakes before we go. Yeah, I know. I’ve been thinking about that too. I mean, it’s not like we're going anywhere that requires a new car. Just a bit of maintenance. Exactly. And if we’re going to do something like that, we might as well make the most of it. What about bringing some sandwiches? I’m not sure if the café is going to be too busy. Yeah, that’s a good idea. I can pack some sandwiches and maybe a bottle of water. It’s not like we're going on a long hike or anything. Just a quick trip to see the Angel of the North. Right. And I’ll text the others to let them know what we’re up to.

So, do you know what’s going on with those geese that keep flying over our house every morning? They’re like a whole army of them, all honking and flapping around, and I swear they think they’re in some kind of military parade. Oh, I know those geese! I’ve seen them every single day. They’ve got this little routine, like they all fly over at the same time, and then they just land in this one spot in the field. I’ve even tried to feed them a few times, but they’re like, “Not today, thanks.” Oh, I remember when I was younger, I used to love watching the birds, especially the ones that migrated. It was so fascinating to see them flying south every autumn. I used to think they had some kind of secret map, like they knew exactly where to go. Yeah, I suppose they do. I mean, if they’ve been doing it for generations, they must have some instinct about it. But I can’t help but wonder if they ever get tired of flying all that way. I think they do, but I don’t think they’ve got a choice. I mean, it’s not like they can just say, “Oh, I’m too tired today—I’ll stay here.” They’re birds, not humans, and they follow the seasons like clockwork. That’s true. I always found it beautiful how nature works. You don’t have to be a scientist to see the patterns. Even when I was working, I’d take a break every now and then just to watch the birds. It reminded me of being a kid again. You know, I’ve been thinking about celebrity trials lately. I mean, those reality shows where people get accused of stuff and you’re just watching it unfold like it’s a drama series. It’s so strange to see how people handle themselves in the spotlight. I know, right? I remember when that one actress was on trial, and it was like everyone was talking about it. I don’t know if it was real or just a big show, but it was weird to see how the media turned it into such a spectacle. I think people are just drawn to drama, even if it’s not real. I mean, I used to watch those shows when I had the time, but now I just prefer to stay in my garden and watch the geese instead.

So how did the job interview go? I heard you were supposed to be meeting with that company in Manchester last week. Oh, it was okay, I suppose. Not terrible, but not great either. I mean, the process was pretty standard, but I think I got a bit nervous. I had a lot on my mind. That’s understandable. I still get nervous even when I know I’ve done all the prep. How did they react to your experience? They seemed interested in my teaching background, especially the part about working with young children. I think they saw that as a good fit for the position they’re looking for. But honestly, the real test was when they asked me about my long-term goals. I didn’t really know what to say. Oh, that’s a tough one. I think it’s important to be honest but also show that you’re adaptable. Did you have a plan? I tried to say that I was looking for a role that would allow me to grow and make a real impact, especially in early years education. I think they liked that, but I’m still not sure if I got the job. Well, even if you didn’t get it, it’s a good opportunity to refine your thoughts. Maybe next time? Yeah, I guess so. It’s just been a bit of a rollercoaster lately. Between the interviews and the baby stuff, I’m not exactly in the best headspace. I can only imagine. Having a baby is a huge shift. How’s the little one doing? She’s fine, mostly. She’s got her own personality, and I’m still getting used to the routine. Some days are easier than others. It’s like a whole new job. That’s true. I remember when I first started teaching, I thought I had it all figured out. But then along came a baby, and suddenly, everything felt different. Exactly. I feel like I’m juggling so many things these days. Between work and home, it’s hard to keep up with everything. I know the feeling. But you’re doing a great job. You’re managing everything, even if it doesn’t always feel that way. Thank you. I guess I just need to remember to take things one day at a time. That’s all you can do.

So, do you ever think about what we're going to do with our lives? Like, what's next? I mean, I know we’re both in our early twenties, and it's like we're just starting to figure things out. Yeah, I think about it all the time. Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I’ve got this job, I’ve got my flat, I’ve got this little social circle, but I don’t really know if it’s the right path. I get that. I mean, I love my job, but sometimes I wonder if I made the right choice with the company. I mean, working in production control is stable, but it’s not exactly the most exciting. I hear you. I think maybe I want to do something more creative. Like, I’ve always loved writing, but I never really thought I could make a living doing it. I know what you mean. I used to write for fun, but then I got into this job and it kind of took over. But I still write sometimes. I mean, it’s not like I don’t have time for it. That’s what I’m thinking too. Maybe I should start taking some courses or something. I mean, I’m not sure if I’m ready to quit my job, but I don’t want to be stuck in the same place for ten years. I think that’s a good idea. I mean, it’s not like we’re not capable of doing anything else. We both have postgraduate degrees and we’re not stuck in some dead-end job. Yeah, I know. But I’m just scared of making the wrong move. What if I try something else and it doesn’t work out? What if I’m not good enough? I get that fear. But you know what? I think the only way to know is to just try. Like, if you don’t take a chance, you’ll never know. You’re right. I guess I just need to stop thinking so much and do something. Even if it’s just a small step. That’s the spirit. Maybe we could even help each other. Like, if you go into writing, I could help you with your ideas, and if I ever want to go back to something creative, maybe I could help you with your job.

So, do you know what’s up with Sophie? She’s been acting so weird lately. I think she’s got a boyfriend or something. Yeah, I heard she saw someone at the café the other day. She was all giggly and kept looking over her shoulder. Wait, isn’t that the guy from the library? The one who always borrows the same books and never returns them? Yeah, that’s the one! She was with him, and he was pulling her arm. She didn’t even look at me when I called her. Like she didn’t even hear me. I mean, I get it, but she’s been with Rob for months. Why is she suddenly interested in someone else? It’s not just her. I think everyone in our group is having some kind of love drama. Jamie’s been acting so weird since he started seeing that girl from the dorm. Yeah, and he’s been avoiding me ever since. I told him to ask me out properly, and he just said, “Yeah, maybe next week.” What does that even mean? Sometimes I think he’s just trying to avoid the whole thing. You know, like he’s not ready. Or maybe he’s got someone else in mind. I don’t know, it just feels like everyone’s got a new crush or something. It’s so annoying. I’m still single, and I’m not even sure what I want. I mean, who even wants to be in a relationship right now? I know, it’s just so much pressure. I feel like I’m constantly comparing myself to other people. Like, why did Sophie get a boyfriend and not me? Why does Jamie even have time for anyone? I think it’s easier to be in a relationship if you’re not in school. Like, once you’re out, you’ve got more freedom. But I’m not sure I want that. It just feels like all the time you spend on a relationship is time you could be spending on yourself. Yeah, but I don’t want to be alone either. I mean, I do miss having someone to talk to, even if it’s just someone to complain about the goings-on in the dorm. That’s true. I just wish I could figure out what I want. I mean, I’ve had some weird crushes before, but I never followed through.

Alright, right, so I've got this weekend trip planned for us. I was just thinking, maybe we could all go to the Lake District? It’s been a while since we’ve had a proper family holiday. That’s very kind of you, mate. I really appreciate it. We’ll have to work out the exact dates and who’s driving. Maybe Friday afternoon, so we can get there in the evening? So, do you remember that time we tried to fit all our friends into the van for the trip to the Redwoods? I swear, we were like a giant, confused version of a human Tetris puzzle. Oh, I remember that! I think we ended up with three people squeezed into the back seat, and the two of us in the front, just trying to drive without crashing. It was a miracle we didn’t end up in a ditch somewhere. Oh, don’t get me started. I think one of the guys fell asleep and started snoring so loud that the whole van was vibrating. I swear, it was like a foghorn in a car. We all had to endure that for an hour. I remember you saying something like, “This is the sound of capitalism,” and then we all started laughing so hard we almost screamed. It was one of those moments where you’re so stressed, but somehow it’s also the best kind of chaos. And then there was that one friend who showed up with a costume. I think it was a pirate outfit? She looked like a Christmas tree in a tent. I mean, we were dressed as ourselves, and she showed up as Captain Hook. Oh, that was hilarious. She even got a little dramatic when the van’s air conditioning broke. “Arrr, the sea of heat has come to claim me!” or something like that. I still laugh about it. And let’s not forget the time we got stuck in a roadside diner because the van broke down. We were all so hungry, and the place was like a scene from  The Hangover , but with more sunscreen and fewer hangovers. So, do you think you've got a chance to get that fine reduced? Honestly, I don’t think so. The bank is already giving me the eye. So, do you think we've got everything sorted for the Mongolia rally? Not really. We still need to apply for visas. I was thinking about it last night. So, did you guys hear about what happened last night? What? Oh, yeah, someone went to the hospital. Yeah, it was Anon. Dad, do you think we’ll get there on time? I’m really excited to see the coast and the sea. I hope so, love. I just got a new client, actually. It's a bit of a challenge, but it's good work. I got to transcribe some old radio interviews from the 70s. It's interesting, you know, hearing the language they used back then. Some of it's pretty archaic. That sounds like a job with a lot of nostalgia. I reckon it's not easy, though. I mean, transcription takes a lot of concentration. I've got to be careful with the accents and the way people spoke. Especially with older recordings, the audio quality is often terrible, and you've got to piece it together. I remember when I was headmistress, we’d have to transcribe things too. It was part of the administrative work. Back then, you couldn't just type it all in, you had to write it out by hand. But I suppose in those days, it was better for preserving the details. You couldn’t just copy and paste. I can imagine. I used to do a lot of manual work like that. I was a carpenter, and we had to measure everything, write down measurements, sketch out plans. It was all about accuracy. I tell you, it's a different world now. You can just have a drawing on a tablet and send it off – no need for handwriting. Sometimes, I think it's easier to make mistakes that way. It’s true. Nowadays, everything's digital, but I think there's something to be said for the old ways. There's a certain level of care and thought that goes into handwritten notes. Though, I don’t mind the technology as much as some people. I mean, it's efficient, and it helps with speed. But there's a certain satisfaction to transcribing something by hand, especially when it's historical. I agree. I mean, it does take time, but the process itself is rewarding. I like the idea of being able to preserve something that might otherwise be lost. Plus, hearing the voices of the past, it's like you're having a conversation with people who are gone. It's a bit of a privilege, really. That's beautiful. I think the act of transcription is almost like a kind of time machine. You get to step into the world of another era, even if only for a moment. I find it deeply moving, honestly.

Alright, do you two want to go to Forest School tomorrow? I think it's going to be a nice day, and it's Mother’s Day, so it’ll be a good way to spend the morning. Yeah, we can go! Or maybe, “Going to Forest School is like having a walk in the woods, but with more adventure!”

She’s been so caught up in everything, she might not even realize how much support she has around her. Yeah, and it’s not just about her.

So, did you get the timetabling sorted for next semester? I was trying to get my head around it last night and it was a bit of a mess. Yeah, I think I got it sorted. There’s something about how language and culture are intertwined in celebrations – like the way you say “Happy New Year” or how you greet people during different holidays. I think it’s a way of expressing identity.

So, do you think we should’ve stopped at that petrol station earlier? I was really hungry, but I couldn’t be bothered to pull over. Honestly, I think we should’ve. I was getting pretty antsy waiting for you to decide. You know how I get when I’m hungry. Yeah, I know. It’s just that I was distracted by the radio. That new podcast about linguistics was so interesting. I mean, I’m not even sure if I’ve ever heard of someone talking about dialects like that before. Oh, come on, you’re a Corpus Administrator. You should be all over that. I mean, isn’t that what you do? Analyse language data? Well, yeah, but it’s more about how language is used in different contexts, not just the podcast. Though I did find it fascinating how they talked about regional accents and how they evolve. Yeah, I guess that’s what’s happening with the dialects around here. I mean, I’ve noticed people from Sunderland and Harpenden talking differently, even though we’re both in England. I mean, we’re not that far apart, but the way we speak is like night and day. Oh, I know. It’s amazing how even within the same country, people can have such different ways of speaking. I mean, I don’t even know if I can fully understand what some people from the South say sometimes, even if I grew up in the North. That’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s not just about where you’re from—it’s also about how you’re raised, your education, your social circles. I mean, I grew up in Harpenden, but my dad’s from South London, and he always had this very formal way of speaking. It’s like a whole different world to the way I speak now. I can relate. My mum’s from Sunderland, and she always told me to “keep the lingo,” but I’ve been trying to blend in a bit more as I’ve moved around. It’s like trying to find your own voice in the middle of so many different influences. I think that’s the best part of it. It’s not just about where you come from—it’s about who you become as a result of that. And I think that’s what makes language so interesting.

Well, I've been feeling rather under the weather these past few days. I've got this terrible cough that won't seem to go away, and I've been feeling pretty weak. I don't know what's wrong with me. That’s not good, love. You should have seen a doctor. I had a bad cold last week, and it took me a week to get over it. You don’t want to neglect your health, especially your age. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve been feeling pretty tired lately too. I’ve had a bit of a cold, and I’ve been struggling to get much done. I’ve been trying to keep up with my lectures, but it's like my brain’s been foggy all week. Yeah, I know the feeling. I’ve been trying to catch up on some work, and I’ve been tired all the time. I think I need to take more care of myself. Maybe a bit of exercise would help, you know? Exercise? I don’t think I’ve had the strength for that. I haven’t even been able to climb the stairs without getting out of breath. What’s the weather like today? I’ve been feeling so down, and I thought maybe it'd be a bit brighter. Oh, it's been fairly gloomy all week. There’s been some rain, and the sun hasn’t really shown itself. I think the weather’s been doing a number on me, and I’m not the only one. I remember when I was younger, a bit of bad weather wouldn’t bother me, but now, it really does. I know, it’s been one of those weeks where it feels like the sky is always grey. I’ve been trying to take the dogs out for a walk, but even that is an effort now. I feel like I’m running on fumes. I can relate. I’ve been trying to keep my head above water with work and personal stuff, and I think I’ve been burning the candle at both ends. I need to get my head straight and maybe take a few days off to rest. Well, I’ve been thinking about going to see the football match this weekend. It’s a local team, and I’ve been looking forward to it.

So, do you know what’s happening with Sophie? I haven’t seen her in ages. She’s been like... vanishing. I’m so confused. I asked her last week if she was getting married, and she said, “No, not yet.” But then she started talking about “plans” and “future steps.” I’m like, what’s going on? Maybe she’s just being vague? I mean, she’s always been a bit of a mystery. But I heard she’s been seeing this guy from Leeds. They’ve been going out for, like, three months now. Oh yeah, I heard that too. He’s the one who always sits next to her at work. I think he’s a graphic designer or something. She said he’s really into art, which, I dunno, I guess it’s matching. Wait, doesn’t he work at the same place as you? Like, isn’t he in the marketing team? No, no, no. He’s in the creative department. He’s like, super into branding, and he’s got this whole vibe about him. You know, like he’s got this whole “edgy” look but he’s actually really nice. Yeah, I saw him at the café last week with her. He was wearing these really cool glasses and a jacket that looked like it was made out of something other than fabric. She was laughing and talking to him like they were in a movie. I don’t know, it’s just weird. I mean, she’s had a few relationships, but I think this one is different. Like, she’s acting like she’s actually serious about it. She even mentioned kids the other day. Kids? Really? She never said anything about that before. She barely even had a conversation about boys when we were in uni. I mean, she’s 27 now. I think she’s just getting to a point where she wants to settle down. I remember her telling me once, “I’m not looking for a guy to take me to dinner every night. I want someone who gets me.” That sounds like a good attitude. But then again, sometimes people say that and then do the opposite. I mean, I think she’s just been waiting for the right person, you know? Yeah, and if she’s found it, then maybe we should all be happy for her.

Well, I've been trying to get my computer to work properly for days now, and it's like it's got a mind of its own. You know, I thought I'd finally got the hang of it, but then it just starts up and does the same thing as before. Oh, I know what you mean, old chap. I tried to get my tablet to work the other day, and I thought I'd finally figured out how to use it, but then it just decided to go all wobbly on me. It's like it's got a grudge against me or something. That’s nothing, really. I still can’t get my smart TV to switch on properly. It just sits there, blinking like it’s trying to tell me something. I tried everything – turning it off, plugging it in, even using the remote with my hands. It just stares at me and says, "Not today, old man." Haha, yeah, I can imagine that. I thought I'd finally got the hang of using the internet, but then I tried to stream a film, and it just froze. I thought I’d gone mad, but then it turned out I’d forgotten to log in. It was like watching a DVD that refuses to play unless you give it the right password – which it doesn't even know, really. I remember the days when you had to actually know what you were doing. Now it's like everything’s got a secret password and you just have to guess it. I mean, I can't even remember what my Wi-Fi name is, let alone the password. It’s not just the gadgets, though. I’ve got a feeling we’re all getting a bit baffled by the modern world. I mean, I still can’t get my phone to take photos that aren’t blurry. I think it’s trying to make me feel old, like it’s judging me for not being able to keep up with technology. Oh, I was just saying to my wife the other day – I can’t even get my phone to tell me what time it is. It just shows me the weather and a couple of ads. I asked it, “What time is it?” and it said, “I can’t tell time. You need to ask someone else.”

So, how’s the weather been down in Essex? I heard it’s been quite damp this week. Oh, it’s been the usual, you know. A bit of rain, a bit of sun—nothing really to write home about. But I suppose it’s better than the frost we had last winter. Yeah, I remember that. It was so cold, I couldn’t even get my car started. I had to borrow a couple of batteries just to get it going! It was ridiculous. I can only imagine. You know, I’ve been thinking about how language changes over time. I teach English as a foreign language, so I see how people from different regions speak it differently. That’s fascinating, really. I’ve always found it interesting how people in Essex tend to use different words than, say, someone from London. I mean, even if you’re just talking about the same thing, the way you say it is completely different. Exactly! It’s like, for example, in Essex, people often say “chips” for fries, but in London, it’s more like “fries.” Or even the way they pronounce “biscuit” – it’s almost like “biskit” – very distinctive. Oh, I know that one. My wife used to make fun of me for saying “biscuit” like that. She’d say, “You sound like someone from the north!” That’s typical of how language can be a bit of a point of pride. I think it’s also part of what makes people from different areas feel connected or different. Absolutely. I remember when I was managing director, I used to travel a lot. I’d go to places like Manchester or Glasgow, and the way people spoke there was just so different from the way we spoke back home in Essex. That’s a great point. I’ve always thought that regional dialects are like a little cultural fingerprint. They tell you so much about where someone’s from. I couldn’t agree more. Speaking of which, I’ve been meaning to get back to my old hobby—woodworking. I’ve had a few projects in mind, like building a side table or maybe even a small bookshelf. That sounds wonderful. I’ve always loved the idea of making things with my own hands. Although, I’d never be able to build a table, I’m more of a language enthusiast!

So, did you go out on Friday? I heard it was supposed to be a big Valentine’s Day bash. Ugh, I’m so glad I didn’t. I think I might have been doing my laundry or something. No, I just stayed in and watched  Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason  again. It’s the only thing I could handle. Oh come on, you’re not serious? That’s like the third time you’ve watched it this year! I know, I know! But it’s comforting, you know? Like, I just needed a good cry and a cup of tea and a bit of romance, even if it was fictional. I get you. I left my flat and went to this new restaurant near campus, but it was so sad. The waiter kept dropping things, and the food was like,  meh . I was just thinking about how much better it would be if we had a real date. You mean like a proper date? Not just going out to eat and pretending we’re adults? Exactly! I mean, it’s Valentine’s Day, right? You’d think we’d have something better than a lukewarm pizza from the takeaway. I know, I know. I tried to go out with this guy from my history class. We did this thing where we both brought a book and we read it aloud. It was  Pride and Prejudice . He got all dramatic about Mr. Darcy and I just wanted to throw a pillow at him. Oh no, that sounds like  my  night! I had a guy who kept asking me about the "meaning of life" and then tried to recite a poem by the window. I couldn’t even tell if he was serious or just being weird. You know what’s even worse? Trying to figure out if someone’s into you or not. I was at the cinema last night, and there was this guy who kept looking at me from the row in front. I thought he was just trying to catch a glimpse of the screen, but then he kept leaning back and smiling at me. Oh no, that guy sounds like my ex. He used to do that. He’d pretend he was in the movie, but really he was just trying to get a reaction from me. I think I’ve had enough of this kind of stuff.

So, do you think the housing crisis is just a symptom of capitalism or is it something deeper? Honestly, I think it’s both. Capitalism drives up prices, sure, but there's also this layer of systemic racism and inequality that makes it so that people of colour and lower-income groups are the ones getting pushed out of their homes. Yeah, I’ve heard that a lot. It’s not just about money—it’s about who gets to live where. I mean, I know someone who’s been trying to buy a flat for three years, and they’re still stuck in a rented house because the market’s just impossible. Exactly. And it's not just about buying. Even renting is a race now. I saw a report that said Black people are more likely to be denied housing in London, even if they have the same credit score as white applicants. It’s frustrating. That’s so unfair. I mean, I grew up in Watford, and I know how expensive it’s getting there too. I think the divide between the haves and the have-nots is just getting worse. It’s not just London, though. I’ve seen the same pattern in other cities. It’s like capitalism is designed to create this cycle of poverty and exclusion. But I don’t think it’s just the system—it’s also the way people are taught to see property as something that’s only for the wealthy. True. And I think that’s where politics comes in. People are starting to react, right? There are more protests, more discussions about land reform, and even more politicians talking about housing as a right, not a privilege. I hope that changes. I mean, the fact that we’re even having this conversation shows that people are starting to care. But I’m not sure if it’s enough to actually make a difference. I guess we’ll have to see. But I do think it’s important to keep talking about it. I mean, how else are we going to bring about real change? Yeah, and maybe with more people speaking up, we can push for policies that actually work. Still, I’m not holding my breath. The system is so entrenched. I know. But at least we’re aware of it now. And that’s a start, right?

So, do you know what’s happening with the nursery yet? I’ve been trying to get some information but it’s all so confusing. Yeah, I know, it’s such a hassle. I’ve got a few options, but honestly, I’m not sure which one is the best for us. I mean, we’ve got to think about the hours, the cost, and how easy it is to get in. I know, it’s a lot to take in. I was just wondering if you’ve thought about when you’re going to go back to work. I mean, with the baby starting nursery, it’s going to be a big change, isn’t it? Yeah, I know. I’ve been thinking about it a lot. I’m not sure if I’m ready yet. I mean, I’d love to be back, but I also feel like I’ve got to make sure I’m emotionally ready. It’s just so much responsibility. I can understand that. I mean, even though I’m not working, I still feel the pressure to be the perfect mother, and I don’t think I’ve got that figured out yet. I know, it’s such a big step. I’ve also been thinking about future holidays. I mean, we can’t just go anywhere with the baby, and I know the other parents are already planning trips. It’s not fair, is it? Oh, I know. I’ve been trying to plan something for next summer, but I don’t know if it’s going to work. I mean, if I’m back at work, I won’t be able to take time off, and if I’m not, I don’t know if we’ll have the money to go anywhere. It’s just so hard to balance everything. I know I need to get back to work eventually, but I just feel like I’m not ready. I mean, I’ve been thinking about weaning the baby as well. I was told that it’s easier if you start earlier, but I’m not sure. Yeah, I’ve heard that too. I’ve been reading up on it, but honestly, I don’t know if I’m ready for that yet. I mean, the baby is still so little, and I feel like I’m still getting used to feeding him.

So, did you get the chance to talk to the police about that incident at the shop last week? Yeah, I did. I’m still not sure I was entirely sure what happened, but they took a statement anyway. They said they’d follow up if they needed more details. That’s a bit worrying, isn’t it? I mean, if you don’t know exactly what happened, how can you give a proper statement? I know, it’s not ideal. But I guess it’s better to be safe than sorry. At least they’re being thorough. I suppose so. But I still feel like the whole thing was a bit of a mess. My brother was there, and he said the store manager was really upset. I didn’t know what to do, honestly. Yeah, I can imagine. It’s one thing when you’re in a position where you’re used to dealing with customers, and it’s another when it’s a bit of a surprise. I mean, I’ve had to do a few things like that at work. You know, if a customer gets angry or something. But I always try to stay calm and make sure I have the facts straight before I say anything. That’s smart. I think I might need to do that if something like that ever happens to me. I mean, I’m a director, so I’m used to making decisions, but this is different. Yeah, it’s not like you’re making a decision on the spot. You’re just trying to explain what happened and be honest. That’s all you can do, really. I guess so. I just hope it doesn’t affect my job. I mean, I’m not sure how that would work. I’m a fundraiser, so I guess if the police think I’m being uncooperative, it could make things harder. You know, I was thinking about that the other day. I have a friend who got into a bit of trouble with the police over a theft at work. It turned out to be a misunderstanding, but it still took months to clear up. That’s a long time to be dealing with that kind of stress. I don’t think I’d want to go through that. It’s not like I’m a big fan of getting involved with the police.

So, how’s the new life treating you, mate? Honestly, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. You know, marriage and all. I thought I’d be sipping tea and reading the paper every morning, but I’m now up at dawn shoveling soil and battling weeds. That’s the life of a gardener, I guess. You don’t get to take breaks. Oh, I do. I take breaks. I just don’t get to take days off. Every time I try to take a day off, someone asks me to clear the garden of some kind of invasive plant. Invasive plants? That sounds like a job for a superhero. I know, right? I’m like the gardener version of Captain America: every day, a new villain with a new plant problem. Maybe you should start a YouTube channel. “Garden Hero: Defending the Green.” I’ve thought about it. I could show people how to fight back against weeds, maybe even some tips on how to grow your own herbs. You know, like rosemary or thyme. That would be great. I’ve been wanting to grow some herbs at home. I even got a mortar and pestle because I thought I’d be using it for something. Oh, I’ve got one too. I use it for grinding spices, like cumin or coriander. I even got some chickpeas from the market the other day. Chickpeas? For what? Oh, I make hummus. It’s a bit of a passion project. I thought it would be easy, but I’ve been trying to cook it for weeks and I still can’t get the texture right. That’s the thing with cooking. You can’t just follow a recipe blindly. You’ve got to add your own flair. I know, I know. I just keep thinking,  what’s the secret?  Maybe it’s the bread? I’ve tried making my own bread too. You’re trying to make everything from scratch now? Yeah, I guess I am. I think it’s the whole  slow living  thing. You know, living in the moment, not rushing through life like I used to. That’s a good philosophy, I’ll say. I’ve been trying to slow down too. I even bought a souvenir from China last week. It’s a little tea set. Oh, that’s cool. I like tea. I’ve been trying to switch from coffee to something more calming.

So, do you know what’s happening with the school orchestra? I think they’re doing a concert next week. Yeah, I heard something about it. Are you in it? No, not this time. I’m kind of busy with the English test. I’ve been studying all week. Oh, really? What’s the test about? It’s a reading and writing test. We got a whole passage to read, and then write an essay. I’m pretty nervous. I can’t wait for that. I’m not good at essays. I just write what I think, and hope it’s right. My teacher said it’s going to be tricky. She said the questions are going to be based on the text, so we need to be careful with our answers. Yeah, I know. I was actually thinking about the English lessons last week. The teacher was talking about the wind-band, and she said they have a new piece they’re learning. Oh, you mean the one with the flute and the trumpet? I think it’s called something like  The Magic Flute ? No, I think it’s called  Symphony No. 5 . I’m not sure, though. It’s all a bit confusing. I don’t know about you, but I’m more excited about the art lessons. We’re doing a project on impressionism this week. I got to draw a landscape, and it was so much fun. That sounds cool. I wish I was better at art. I just make random shapes and call them pictures. You can’t be that bad. I think you’re just not trying. Maybe. But I’m not sure if I’m going to get an A. My last project was about animals, and I just drew a cat with a hat. Okay, but that’s not a bad thing. We’re allowed to be creative. Anyway, what about French? I’ve been trying to learn some vocabulary, but I keep mixing up the words for  table  and  chair . I know what you mean. I confused  chine  and  chaise  once in class. The teacher laughed. She did. It was so embarrassing. I think we’re both kind of bad at languages. Maybe we should study together for the English test. That’s a good idea. We can work on the essay together. Yeah, and maybe we can also practice our French.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing I’ve noticed since I’ve been out of teaching? It’s not the lack of money or the lack of proper healthcare—it’s the lack of proper conversation. People just don’t talk anymore. They’re too busy scrolling or being on their phones. I know what you mean. I’ve got this friend who just got his first job as a barista. He’s constantly on his phone, even when he’s at work. And he’s got a whole playlist of music he listens to while making lattes. Didn’t even know the name of the coffee machine until he asked me. Oh, that’s the modern world, lad. We’ve got apps for everything, but not for actually knowing what’s going on around us. I used to know the names of every street in Darlington. Now? I can barely find the café without asking for directions. It’s a shame, really. I used to teach English, and I’d always tell my kids that language is the most powerful tool we have. But now, I feel like we’re all just speaking in emojis and hashtags. Yeah, and I think it’s making people lose their accents too. I’ve noticed that even in our town, more and more kids are starting to sound like they’re from Manchester, or even London, instead of the real North. It’s like they’re trying to fit in with the ‘cool’ accent. I know what you mean. I used to work in Hull, and I remember how proud we were of our dialect—our Yorkshire pride. Now, even my own kids sound like they’ve been raised in Manchester. I think it’s because of the media, you know? Everything’s from London or the South now. The news, the movies, the TV shows—they all come from that part of the country. And if you’re not part of that culture, you feel left out. But I think it’s also because of social media. You can be anywhere in the world and still feel connected to the same group of people. But what do you gain from that? You lose the local culture, the local stories, the local history. Exactly. And I think that’s why I’ve been trying to write a book about the history of our town.

So, do you think it’s better to drive a car or take the bus? Oh, I don’t know, love. I’m more of a car person, but I reckon if you can manage it, the bus is better for the environment. Yeah, but it’s not always convenient, especially if you’re in a hurry. Plus, I’ve had to wait for the bus for ages before, and I’m not too keen on standing out in the cold. I can relate to that. I once got stuck outside in the rain for half an hour waiting for the bus because it was delayed. I’ve been stuck in traffic for hours too, which is even worse. I’ve heard that driving can actually make you more stressed, especially if you’re in a city. I’ve been trying to cut down on my driving lately because of the stress it causes. I can see that. I used to drive everywhere, but ever since I started driving my kids to school, I’ve been more stressed than ever. I mean, it’s not just the traffic—it’s the responsibility. I’ve read somewhere that people who drive more are more likely to be overweight. Doesn’t make sense, does it? You’re moving, but somehow it’s got the opposite effect. Maybe because people sit in cars all day and don’t exercise. I know I’ve been doing a lot more walking lately, even if just for short distances. Yeah, and I’ve heard that some people are allergic to certain types of food. It can be really frustrating when you can’t eat something you love. I know what you mean. My wife’s allergic to nuts, and it’s a nightmare. You have to be careful with everything you eat. I once accidentally gave her a chocolate bar with nuts in it, and she ended up in the hospital. That sounds serious. I had a friend who had an allergic reaction to something and it nearly killed her. You can’t be too careful. That’s why I’ve started keeping an emergency kit in the car just in case. You never know when something like that might happen. Speaking of emergencies, I had a minor surgery last year. It was nothing major, just a routine procedure. But it was scary enough. I had a surgical operation when I was younger, and it was a nightmare.

I just got a message from the department head about the Moodle upgrade. They’re saying it’s going to be a big update and they want us all to be ready for it by next week. Oh no, not Moodle again. I thought we’d moved past that. What’s the problem this time? Well, they’re introducing some new features, like better analytics for student engagement and a more user-friendly interface. But they’re also changing the login system, so we’ll have to update all our course links and make sure everything’s compatible. That sounds like a lot of work. I was just thinking about how much time I’ve spent trying to troubleshoot Moodle issues over the past few months. It’s like a never-ending battle with the system. I know, I feel the same. But I guess it’s part of the job. It’s just frustrating when you’re trying to teach, and then you’re constantly having to deal with technical issues. Yeah, and we’re not even the only ones struggling. I heard from a colleague that even the IT department is having trouble setting up the new version. I mean, we’re supposed to be experts, but when it comes to Moodle, we’re like kids trying to figure out a new game. Ha! Exactly. But maybe this update will finally make it more stable? I’ve had enough of the constant bugs and crashes. I just want to be able to focus on teaching instead of fixing the software. I couldn’t agree more. I was thinking the other day that maybe we should all just take a break from Moodle for a bit and try to find a better platform. But I guess there’s not much choice, is there? No, not really. I mean, it’s what we’ve been using for years, and even though it’s not perfect, it’s still the most accessible option for our students. Unless something changes, we’re stuck with it. I suppose. But I’m still wondering how we’ll manage the transition. I mean, if the login system changes, that means every link we’ve ever created will be broken. It’s going to be a nightmare. I know. I’ve already started planning the update process. I’ll need to go through each course and check all the links, make sure the assignments are all set up properly, and maybe even test the new features before we roll it out to the students.

I can't believe we've just got back from the airport. I still feel like I'm on a plane. I know, I’m still half-asleep. I think the jetlag's really kicking in. Not to mention the fact that we’ve got a baby to look after. Yeah, I feel like I’ve been running on empty all day. I swear, if I didn’t have a baby to take care of, I’d be out dancing in the park right now. Tell me about it. I tried to take a short nap after we got back, but the baby just wouldn’t settle. I think I’ve got the sleep debt equivalent of a week. I’m lucky I got a couple of hours. I think I’m going to try to sleep as soon as I get the baby down. I’m not sure how much longer I can last. I feel the same. I’m just so tired, I can’t even think straight. But we have to make the arrangements for the drama performance this weekend. I know we said we’d go, but I’m not sure if we’re up for it. Yeah, we’ve got to do it. It’s been ages since we saw a good show. Even if it’s just a local one, it’s something to look forward to. You’re right. Maybe it’ll help us get back into the swing of things. Although, I’m not sure how we’ll manage with the baby. We’ll manage. I mean, we have a babysitter. It’s not like we’re going to be in the middle of a performance and then have to deal with a crying baby. Exactly. And it’s only for a few hours. We can make it work. I guess. But I’m still not sure if I’ll have the energy to even walk out the door. I know, I feel the same way. But we’ve got to stick to our plans. It’ll be nice to have something to look forward to, even if it’s just for a few hours. You’re right. Let’s just try to get the baby down and then figure out the rest. Sounds like a plan. Hopefully, we’ll both feel a bit better by the time we get there. Yeah, and if we don’t, at least we’ll have a good story to tell afterwards.

So, do you still keep in touch with people from back in Iraq? I know you’ve been living in the UK for a while now. Yeah, I do. I've got a few friends who still live there, but things are… complicated. Especially since the war. It’s not the same place it used to be. I can imagine. I’ve read a bit about the political situation there. It’s been pretty volatile, hasn’t it? It has. And it’s not just political. The oil politics have messed up a lot of things. You know how oil can influence everything—from government decisions to people’s lives. It’s like the whole country is tied up in it. I suppose that makes sense. Oil’s a huge industry, especially in the Middle East. It shapes a lot of the region’s history. I’ve been reading about the Wahabi influence in some of the areas too. It’s pretty significant. Yeah, it is. There’s a lot of tension between different groups, especially with the religious and political factions. It’s not something you can just ignore. It affects people’s daily lives, especially young people. You know, they’re trying to find their way in a world that’s constantly changing. That must be tough. I can see how it would be overwhelming, especially for someone who’s trying to build a future. Have you ever thought about moving back to Iraq? Or maybe somewhere else? I’ve thought about it, but it’s not that simple. There are a lot of challenges—visa issues, the political instability, the security situation. I’m currently working as an interpreter, so I have to be careful about where I’m stationed and what I’m doing. I see. I’ve been trying to get a visa to visit some of the places I’ve studied in the UK. My family’s over there, and I’d like to see them again. It’s been a while. That’s understandable. I know how much it means to stay connected with family. It’s hard when you’re in a different country, trying to navigate all these systems. Yeah, it really is. I’ve also been thinking about moving house. I’ve got a job that requires me to be more mobile, so maybe I’ll be moving to a different city soon.

I just thought I'd mention that the roast lamb was absolutely delicious. I mean, it's not every day you get a perfectly seasoned, juicy lamb. I’m so glad we got it from that local butcher down the road. Yes, it was really good. I mean, the timing was perfect—just cooked through but not overdone. It was like the kind of meal that makes you forget how hard it is to cook something so simple. I’m so delighted you both enjoyed it. I think it’s one of the things I miss most when I’m not at the school. Cooking for the staff and the students—it’s part of the routine. I used to bring in a few different dishes each week, and the turkey was always a favorite too. Though I must say, I never thought I’d see the day when I’d be eating roast lamb with my own children. That’s funny, I think you’d be proud of us. We’ve taken on a lot of the responsibilities around the house, especially with the landlord’s constant requests and the dogs. I mean, I still remember the time you told me we’d be lucky if we had two decent landladies to take care of us. Exactly. It’s not just the work, it’s the emotional toll. I remember the first time I got a notice from the landlord saying the rent was going up. I didn’t even know how to respond. I just sat there staring at the ceiling for hours. It’s like you’re someone else’s problem, but you’re still paying for it. I know what you mean, dear. It’s the way the system is set up. You think you’re being responsible, but in reality, you’re just fulfilling someone else’s expectations. But you know what? I think it’s all going to be okay. I’ve heard about these new housing schemes, and I think the idea of going on a cruise might be a good way to take a break. I’ve been thinking about it for a while now. A cruise? That sounds like a dream come true. I mean, I’ve always wanted to see the world, but with the way things are, it feels like an impossible luxury. Still, I can imagine us on a ship, watching the sunrise over the ocean, sipping wine and just enjoying the moment.

So, do you think we should get a fridge? I mean, we’ve had this one for like, what, three years now? And it’s starting to fall apart. I mean, the door doesn’t even close properly anymore. I know, it’s been like a disaster. I tried to fix it once, and then it got worse. I think we need to get a new one before the winter. You know, if we’re gonna be living here for a while. Yeah, and I’ve been thinking, maybe we should just start moving things into the new place. I mean, we’ve been living in this flat for like, what, two years now? It’s time we made a move. Yeah, I agree. But I’m not sure if we’re ready. I mean, I’m still doing my teaching assistant job, and I’ve got this new course coming up. I don’t want to be stuck in a flat with no fridge, you know? I get that, but we’re not getting any younger. Eventually, we’re gonna have to make a decision. And I mean, we’re not even sure if we’re gonna be here for much longer. You’re right. I mean, I’ve been thinking about uni again. I’m not sure if I want to go back, but the idea of living in a student flat again is kind of tempting. Yeah, I mean, it’s not like we’re not used to it. We’ve been roommates for ages. I think it’s just the idea of having a bit more space and not having to share a fridge with someone who’s always eating fish and chips. That’s true. Although, I have to say, I miss the fish and chips. Not that I’d ever admit it. Oh, you’re not the only one. I mean, I’ve been eating fish and chips every weekend. It’s the only thing I can cook properly. I tried once. It turned into a disaster. I burnt the chips, and the fish was overcooked. I had to throw it out. You’re not the first. I tried to cook fish and chips once, and I ended up burning down the kitchen. My mum sent me a photo of the smoke alarm going off. Yeah, you could say that. I think we’re all just a bit out of our depth when it comes to cooking.

Alright, do you think we've got everything for the baking lesson? I mean, it's not like it's a complicated recipe or anything, but you never know with kids. I think we’ve got the basics. Flour, sugar, eggs, butter—everything's in the fridge. I even found the mixing bowls in the cupboard. Though I'm not sure if we need that many. Maybe we don’t. I just saw one of the bowls, and it’s got a little crack in it. Maybe we can use the bigger one for the dough? Yeah, that’s probably better. I mean, who needs a little crack in a mixing bowl? As long as it doesn’t fall apart while we're mixing, we’re fine. Speaking of mixing, do you know what the lesson is about? Oh, the teacher said it's about making shortbread. Simple, but I think the kids will enjoy it. And it’s for the half birthday celebration, right? Yes, exactly. It’s a small way to celebrate the kids’ milestones. Though I feel a bit bad that we’re not doing anything grand. Like a big party or something. Well, it’s not like we can have a party in the kitchen. You’d have to clear the table, and I’m not sure if that’s allowed. Plus, the teacher said she wants the kids to learn something practical. True enough. Though I do wonder what's going on with the Tomodachi life thing. I keep hearing about it from the other teachers. Some of them are into it, others aren’t. But I think it’s just another way to spend time with friends. Yeah, but I’m not sure how that relates to baking. Maybe it’s just a way to make the lesson more fun? I mean, if we can make it a little more ‘social,’ the kids might enjoy it more. I guess. Though I would rather just have a nice, quiet lesson. I mean, I don’t want the kids to get distracted by anything. Though I do love the idea of a half birthday celebration. I do too. My sister had a half birthday celebration once, and it was the best thing. We had cake, balloons, and even a little gift. But I guess we can’t do that here. Although, maybe we can make a special cake?

So, do you still drive that old Honda? Ugh, yes, it’s a disaster. I’ve had it for five years now, and I can’t bring myself to part with it. It’s got more miles than most people’s lives, honestly. I know, I know. But I mean, it’s not exactly reliable, is it? You had that breakdown on the A12 last summer, right? Oh, don’t remind me. I was halfway to Cambridge and the engine just died. Didn’t even make a sound. I had to get a tow truck, and I was so embarrassed. I was in the middle of nowhere, with no phone signal and the car just sat there like a tin can. I’m sure the mechanics had a laugh about it. They did. They said it was like a car from the 70s. But you know what? I’ve been thinking about getting a new one. Maybe something a bit more modern. That’s brave of you. I’d be terrified of buying a car. I mean, with all the finance stuff and everything. Yeah, it’s not easy. But I’ve been doing a bit of research. I’ve been looking at some electric cars, actually. They’re pretty good these days. You don’t have to worry about oil changes, and the running costs are lower. Interesting. I’ve been thinking about switching too. My old car’s a bit of a pain. I’m just not sure if I’m ready to commit to something new. It’s a big decision. I’ve been on Facebook groups for car buyers, and it’s been helpful. People share their experiences, and you can ask questions. Yeah, I’ve seen that. I mean, I’m on Facebook, but I don’t really interact much. I just scroll through and laugh at the memes. I tried that too, but eventually, I started joining some groups. It’s a bit of a cliché, but it’s actually pretty useful. I’ve even found some good deals through people who are selling privately. Oh, I bet. I mean, if you’re not using a dealer, you can save a lot. But I’m just worried about scams. Yeah, that’s the thing. You’ve got to be careful. I mean, I’ve seen some dodgy posts, but as long as you check the details and meet the seller in person, it’s okay.

I just want to say, I’ve had a right mess of a day today. You know, work’s been... intense. I’m not even sure I’m going to make it through this shift without snapping at someone. You alright? Look, I know you’ve been working all week, but it’s not like you’re the only one with a job. I reckon you just need to take a breather. Yeah, I know. I just feel like I’m stuck in a cycle. You know, one minute I’m doing one thing, the next I’m doing something completely different. It’s like I’m juggling a thousand things and I’m about to drop them all. Sounds like the kind of day where you need a solid meal and a good film. I mean, I know what you mean about work being crazy, but have you seen the film on? It’s Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs. Haha, yeah, I saw the trailer. It’s supposed to be a kid’s film, but I’m not sure that’s the vibe I’m getting. Well, I think it’s actually quite clever. I mean, the idea of food falling from the sky and causing chaos? That’s not exactly light-hearted. It’s got some – I don’t know – depth, maybe? Like, it’s got a message. A message? You mean about the environment or something? Maybe. I mean, someone said to me that it’s got a hidden meaning about consumerism and how we treat food. Like, the more we crave, the more the world is affected. I don’t know, it’s a bit of a stretch, but it makes you think. I can see that. I guess you could take it that way. But I’m more thinking about the fact that I just ate a piece of toast and it fell off my plate like it had a mind of its own. I don’t think I was being reckless. Ah, but that’s the point, isn’t it? It’s like the world’s reacting to us. Just like a kid’s film can have more depth than you think. Still, I’m not sure it’s the best idea to watch it with a full stomach. Yeah, I think I’ll just stick to watching it with a cup of tea and some chips.

So, do you watch much football, then? Yeah, I do. I grew up in Liverpool, so it's in my blood. Even though I’ve been driving cabs in this part of Finland for a few years now, the Premier League’s still on my mind. That’s interesting. I used to teach English in Germany and then moved to the UK. I’ve always found that football is a great topic to discuss across cultures. Absolutely. It’s like the only thing we all agree on. But I’ve got to say, the politics in the UK these days—it’s a bit of a mess. I couldn’t agree more. From what I’ve seen, the current government seems to be heading in a direction that’s very different from the New Labour era, which was quite progressive. Yeah, definitely. Tony Blair was a good leader—managed to bring the country together, even if he did have his critics. But now, it feels like the political scene is so divided. I think one of the big differences is the way the media portrays politicians these days. It’s much more polarizing. It’s not just about policy anymore—it’s about personality, and that’s been a real shift. I’ve noticed that too, especially with the way the public is reacting. People are more vocal than ever, and social media has just accelerated that. It’s kind of a double-edged sword. On one hand, it gives a voice to people who might not have had it before, but on the other, it can be very divisive. Exactly. I’ve seen how people in my taxi rides talk about politics. Some of them are really passionate, and it’s easy to get caught up in the argument. That’s probably because football and politics are both such big emotional topics. People invest so much in them. Oh, I know. I can’t help but compare it to my time in Liverpool. We had to endure a few years of being out of the top flight, but we always believed in the spirit of the club. That’s a nice way to put it. It’s not just about the results—it’s about the culture, the history, and the community. Definitely. That’s what makes it special. Even though I’m not in the country anymore, I still feel connected to it.

So, do you know what’s the biggest fear of people who do BNC recordings? I don’t know, maybe they’re scared of being judged? No, actually, it’s being scared of flying. That’s the biggest fear among them. Oh, really? I mean, I think that’s pretty common. Everyone’s got something they’re afraid of. Yeah, but when you’re recording BNC, you’ve got to be in that place where you’re not thinking about your fears. It’s kind of like… being in a bubble. Wait, so what is BNC? I’ve heard the term before but I’m not exactly sure. BNC is the British National Corpus. It’s a huge collection of written and spoken English. They use it to study language patterns, like how people actually speak. Oh, I see. So it’s kind of like a database of language? Yeah, and it’s used by linguists, researchers, and even teachers. It helps them understand how people use language in different contexts. That sounds really interesting. I’ve always wanted to get involved in something like that. You should! I mean, if you’re into writing or language, it’s a great way to dive in. I’ve been thinking about doing some research too. Maybe something related to social media? Oh, that’s a good idea. I mean, social media is such a big part of how we communicate these days. Yeah, and there’s so much data out there. You could even look at the impact of different platforms on language use. Exactly. I was reading about how people use hashtags differently depending on where they’re from, like in the UK versus the US. That’s true. I’ve noticed that a lot. Like, some words or phrases just don’t translate well. Like what? For example, 'chuffed' or 'knackered' – you can’t just say those in the US and expect people to get the meaning. Oh yeah, I’ve tried using 'chuffed' in a message and it was like a mystery to the other person. It’s like a linguistic puzzle. You have to think about the context and the audience. I guess that’s why people use so many emojis and slang now. It’s like a way to bridge the gap between different dialects and cultures. Exactly. It’s interesting how social media has changed the way we communicate.

So, do you think I should get a tattoo? I’ve been thinking about it for a while now. Honestly, I think you should. But I’d say pick something meaningful. Not just some random symbols. I know, I’m thinking about getting a small one—maybe a quote or something from my favorite book. That’s a good idea. I’ve got a little one on my wrist that says “I am enough.” It’s pretty meaningful. Yeah, I like the idea. But I’m worried about the pain. I heard it’s not as bad as people say, but still… It depends on where you get it. If it’s on your arm, it’s not too bad. But if it’s on your ribs or something, it’s brutal. I was thinking of something on my forearm. Maybe a little dragon? I mean, I’ve always liked dragons. A dragon? That’s cool. But do you want to go full fantasy or keep it simple? I think I’d go with something sleek. Maybe a stylized one. I don’t want to look like I’ve been in a medieval war. Fair enough. You know, I got mine done last year, and the artist was amazing. You should try to find someone with good reviews. Yeah, I’ll look into that. I just need someone who can handle my slightly suspicious ideas. That’s what I said—look for the right person. Anyway, I’m just rambling. I should probably get back to cooking. I’m making a roast dinner, and the potatoes are starting to smell a bit. Don’t you dare blame me for that. I told you to check on them earlier. I was distracted by the thought of dragons. That’s your problem. Now, I hear someone’s at the door. Oh, that’s probably Jamie. He always comes over at the worst times. Yeah, but he’s bringing a bottle of wine and some Christmas decorations. I hope he’s not bringing that weird hat again. You know he’s got that hat that looks like it belongs in a medieval knight’s closet. Exactly. I’ve been trying to convince him to stop wearing it, but he won’t listen. It’s not even the hat, it’s the way he wears it. Like it’s part of his personality. Listen, I think I need to go get a new one.

So, do you ever find it hard to cook for yourself? I mean, I think it’s easier when you have someone else to cook with, like when you're at home with a partner or something. But I can imagine it being really hard when you're on your own. Honestly, I do. I mean, I try to cook a few times a week, but I’m not really great at it. I think I’m too lazy to plan meals properly. I just end up eating the same things over and over again—like pasta, or takeaways. But I’ve been trying to make more of an effort recently, especially now that I’m doing more exercise and need to eat better. Yeah, that makes sense. I think cooking for yourself is a bit of a challenge, especially if you’re not used to it. I’ve been trying to get better too, actually. I’ve even started taking some cooking classes—well, online ones, because I can’t be bothered to go out. It’s been quite fun, to be honest. I learned how to make a proper omelette, and I even tried making some vegetarian stir fry the other day. Oh, that’s great! I’ve always been terrible at cooking, but I think I should give it another shot. I mean, if I can write about food for a living, I should at least be able to cook it, right? Although, I do have a confession—I burned my first ever lasagna. It looked like a disaster. I think it was more like a charcoal briquette than a meal. Oh no, that is a tragedy. I can’t even imagine that. I once tried to make a soufflé and it collapsed like a pancake. I had to eat it anyway, though. I didn’t want to waste the ingredients. But seriously, I think the key is to not be too hard on yourself. You don’t need to be a chef; you just need to feed yourself. Exactly. I think I’m going to start with something simple, like a basic stir fry. I’ve got some recipe books from the library, and I’ve been meaning to try them out. I’m also thinking about maybe joining a cooking class in the area. I heard there’s a community kitchen that offers beginner classes—maybe that’s a good start.

So, did you get the email from Sarah about the meeting tomorrow? Yeah, I did. She said it’s going to be a bit of a long one—probably like two hours or so. Oh no, not again. I swear, if she keeps dragging it out, I’m going to start doodling on the agenda. You wouldn’t be the first. I’ve seen people do that in meetings. But honestly, I think she just wants to make sure we’re all on the same page. I get that, but I feel like we’ve been over this already. I mean, we’ve got the same syllabus, the same students, and the same university rules. It’s not like we’re starting from scratch. True, but I guess that’s the thing with academia—everyone wants to make sure everything is perfect. I mean, even if it’s just a meeting about teaching methods. Yeah, but I’m not even sure why we’re still doing this. I thought we’d moved past the point of being overly cautious. Maybe we have. But I think it’s more about how we present ourselves. You know, how we appear to the higher-ups. It’s not just about the content of what we teach, it’s about the way we do it. I don’t know, I’ve always thought it was more about the students. If the students are engaged, then it doesn’t matter how perfect the presentation is. That’s a fair point. But I still think Sarah and the others are under the impression that we need to be more interactive in our classes. I mean, the last time we had that discussion, we had to document every little thing. Speaking of which, have you managed to get your toe nails done yet? Ugh, no. I keep putting it off. I’ve got this nail polish I really wanted to try, but I’m just waiting for the right time. You should do it soon. I mean, we’re both lecturers—people are always watching us. You can’t walk into a lecture hall with muddy toe nails. I know, I know. But I’m trying to focus on the work. I don’t want to get distracted by something as trivial as my toes. Well, maybe you should take it as a reminder to take a break.

So, do you remember that thing about the moon landing? I read something the other day that said it was all a conspiracy and they faked it. Like, they made it in a studio or something. Oh, come on, you can’t be serious. That’s the biggest lie ever. I mean, there’s so much evidence—photos, videos, the flags, the footprints. It’s all real. Yeah, I know, but you know how it is. People like to think there’s something hidden behind everything. Like, the government, or the media, or even aliens. It’s like conspiracy theories are the new religion. I suppose. But I mean, what’s the alternative? That we’re just left with the surface-level stuff, right? I mean, if you take everything at face value, how do we know anything for sure? Exactly. And then there’s the whole thing about the moon rocks. People say they’re not from the moon, or that they’re fake. It’s like, how do we even trust our own history? I guess it’s part of the human condition. We want to believe in things, but we also want to question them. But I still think the moon landing is real. Even if it was faked, it still changed the world. Yeah, maybe. But then again, what’s stopping someone from faking everything? I mean, they fake the moon landing, they fake the TV shows, they fake the news. Who’s to say we’re not all just walking around in a simulation? That’s a  different  level of conspiracy. I mean, I’m not even sure I believe the moon landing was real. But I’m not going to go that far. I’m still going to take it as a given for now. Fair enough. But you know, I heard about this new movie coming out. It’s called  The Hidden Truth . It’s about all these conspiracy theories, like the moon landing, 9/11, the Illuminati, everything. Oh no, not that one. I heard that movie was a disaster. People said it was too conspiratorial and didn’t really have a point. Yeah, I read that too, but I still think it’s a good idea to watch it. It’s like a comedy, right? You know, it’s not serious, it’s just a way to make fun of the whole idea.

Dad, do you remember the book  Jamaica Inn ? I read it for English class and it was so spooky. I thought it was about a haunted house and all that. Yeah, I remember that one. It's a bit of a gothic tale, isn't it? I think it's based on a real place in Cornwall, actually. I reckon it's got something to do with a missing woman and a witch. Oh, really? That sounds like a lot of fun. I wish we were there now. I’d love to see the real Jamaica Inn. But I don’t like the idea of being scared. I’m not a big fan of spooky stories. Well, it’s a bit of a classic. You’ll get used to it. I think the real Jamaica Inn is actually a place you can visit. Maybe we can check it out while we’re there. Wait, we are going to Cornwall, right? Yeah, we are. I can’t wait to see the beach and the caravan park. I heard it’s really nice this time of year. It should be. I remember when I was a kid, my family used to go to Cornwall every summer. The scenery is just so beautiful. Have you seen the way the roads are painted? I saw a really bright yellow road sign today. It looked like it was part of a comic book. Why are the roads painted like that? Oh, they do that to make them more visible, especially when it's dark. But some people think the bright colours make the roads look too cartoonish. It’s a bit of a debate. I think it’s cool. I mean, the  Wizard of Oz  had green screens and everything. I guess it’s like that, but for real. You're not wrong. I think the  Wizard of Oz  is one of my favourite books. It’s got such a magical vibe. Do you think there are real wizards anywhere? Probably not. But I do think there are real witches. Auntie Mavis always says she’s seen a couple of them in the woods near the village. You’re not serious. She told me that once. I always thought she was just trying to scare me. She said she saw one with a pointy hat and a broomstick. It was actually really nice. She made me a chocolate cake and everything.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play that game where you had to guess which teacher had a secret hobby? I think it was like, "Who’s into model trains?" or "Who’s got a garden with a greenhouse?" Oh, I remember that well. I always thought it was Mr. Thompson. He was always fiddling with bits of wood in his office. I used to think he was building a model of the castle or something. He probably was.
