Once I got into a car accident on the way home from a pub. I thought I’d made it, but the car came to a stop and I realized it wasn’t going anywhere. Oh no, did you end up staying the night? Yeah, and I had a terrible time trying to get cab rides. Finally, I just walked home. It was about three miles, but I got there. Wow, that sounds exhausting. I prefer to drink responsibly. I was at a protest once, and someone tried to sell me a bottle of whiskey. I didn’t even know what it was. That’s not the first time someone’s tried to sell me something I didn’t know I wanted. I think the worst was when I was in London and someone approached me with a sample of some strange drink. It tasted like cough syrup. That sounds like what I had once at a street fair. I didn’t know it was a drink at first. I just thought it was some type of jam.

So, did you have a good holiday? Yeah, it was really nice. I went to Cornwall with my family, and it was just so peaceful. I haven’t been anywhere like that in a while. That sounds amazing. Did you get to do any sports while you were there? I did a bit of walking, and we went swimming in the sea. It was so refreshing. I haven’t swum in the sea since I was a kid, so it was a bit of a shock at first, but I really enjoyed it. That’s great. I wish I could get out more. I’ve been stuck with work and all, and I’ve barely managed to get outside since the start of the year. I know, I feel the same. I think it’s just the way things are now. You know, with everything going on at work and all, it’s hard to find time. But I think it’s important to take a break and recharge, even if it’s just a short trip. Yeah, I guess it’s about balance. I’ve been trying to make more time for myself lately. Did you meet up with any friends while you were there? Actually, I did. My cousin came down from Manchester for a few days, and we spent a lot of time together. It was good to catch up. We did go out for a few meals and even went to a local pub. It’s funny, I feel like we haven’t spoken in ages. That’s nice. I should really try to get out more and see more people. I feel like I’ve been slipping a bit since I started working full-time. I’m not even sure what I’m talking about anymore. I know, I feel that too. It’s like the time just flies. But I think it’s better to make sure we’re still keeping in touch with the people we care about. Definitely. I was thinking the other day about how much I miss my ex. I don’t know, it’s weird. He’s been out of my life for a while now, but sometimes I just feel like I should reach out. I get that. I think it’s normal to feel that way sometimes. It’s not like you’re in love with him anymore, but there’s just this connection, you know?

I just got a call from Lucy. She’s been going through a really tough time. She’s got cancer, and it’s advanced. I think she’s having more treatments now, but it’s not looking good. Oh no, that’s terrible. I’m so sorry to hear that. Has she been keeping in touch? I haven’t seen her in a while. Yeah, she’s been messaging me a bit. She’s trying to stay positive, but it’s hard. She mentioned that she’s been feeling exhausted and not eating much. I know she’s been struggling with the side effects of the chemo. That’s awful. I hope the treatments are helping her. It’s so hard to watch someone you care about go through something like this. I feel awful for her. I know. I think she’s been trying to stay strong for us, but it’s been really hard. I wonder if she’s thinking about her future. She’s always been such a proactive person, always planning and looking ahead. This must be so disheartening for her. Yeah, I can imagine. It’s not just the physical pain, it’s the emotional toll too. I remember when we were at university, she used to talk about how she wanted to travel the world and live in a place with beautiful views. She had such big dreams. She still does, even now. She’s been mentioning the village we used to talk about, the one in the countryside with those big old houses. She said she’d like to move there when she’s able, just to have some peace and quiet. I think that’s a good thought. Maybe it would help her feel more at ease. Although I guess the planning for that kind of thing is going to be tricky. I mean, there are so many houses for sale in the village, but not all of them are suitable. Some are in poor condition, and others are too expensive. Yeah, I know. I was looking at some of the listings the other day. There’s this one place that’s been on the market for a while. It’s a bit run-down, but the land is gorgeous. I think it could be a good option if she’s able to make the move. I’d say that’s worth considering.

I swear, I don’t know how people do it. Every time I go to the supermarket, it’s like a war zone. People just shove things into their trolleys, knock into you, and act like it’s normal. I can’t even walk down the aisle without someone knocking my arm or spilling something on me. Yeah, I know what you mean. I try to be nice, like I’ve got a shopping list and I’m trying to be efficient, but it’s like everyone else’s just trying to grab the last bag of chips or whatever. It’s so annoying. And the checkout is the worst! I mean, I get it, the people are busy, but some of these cashiers take forever. I’ve timed it before. The average time to check out is like five minutes, but some of them take ten or even fifteen. It’s like they’re not even working. I’ve had this happen to me a few times. I was just trying to get my groceries, and the cashier started asking me questions like, “Do you have a loyalty card?” and, “Do you want a bag?” I just wanted to get out of there and go home. It’s like they’re not even paid to do that. Yeah, and it’s not just the cashier. Sometimes the self-checkout is even worse. I’ve seen people try to scan things and somehow end up with the wrong price or the machine just crashes. And then you have to wait for someone to help you, and it’s like you’re a stranger in a foreign country. Also, I don’t even like the fruit section. I mean, I know it’s there because it’s healthy, but I walk past it every time and it just makes me sad. There’s a whole row of apples that are half-rotten, and it’s like, why are we even buying them? I get that. I mean, I’m not a fruit person, but I still think it’s a shame. I tried once to just buy a banana, but the one I picked had that weird black spot, and I couldn’t even eat it. It was like the grocery store was trying to make me feel bad. I told my mum about that, and she said, “You just need to look at the dates.”

So, do you remember that time we were in Berlin and bumped into that old friend of ours, Graham? He’d got himself a flat in the city and was running a little café. I was shocked to see him, but he was so happy to see us. Oh yes, I remember that. He looked like he’d aged ten years, but he was still the same old Graham. You know, always talking about his travels and how he wanted to be a tourist guide. He was trying to learn German, wasn’t he? I think he even went to a language school for a while. It was a bit funny watching him struggle with the grammar. Yeah, and he kept saying he was going to start a package tour to Antwerp. He said it was the city of love and everything, and he wanted to sell little tours to people who just wanted a quick trip. You know, I remember when he was in his early sixties, he was always talking about retiring and going abroad. He even thought about moving to Spain. But then he decided he’d rather stay in England and start up his café instead. It’s funny how people change. I mean, I sometimes wonder what it’s like to retire. I’ve been thinking about it myself. I mean, I’m still working, but I imagine it’s not like you’re in a rut all the time. I don’t know. I mean, I’ve got a few years to go, but I can already imagine the freedom. I’d love to take a trip to Germany or maybe even France. I’ve been meaning to visit the Christmas markets in Dresden or something. That’s a good idea. I always found the Christmas markets in Germany so charming. The lights, the mulled wine, the treats. You couldn’t help but feel festive. I’ve always wanted to go to one. My niece was talking about a trip to Prague for Christmas, and she said it was magical. I can’t wait to see it with my own eyes. Speaking of trips, I’ve been thinking about Dorset again. We used to caravan there when I was a kid. I remember the seafront in Bournemouth, the way it looked at sunset. It was beautiful. It really was. I remember taking my daughter there when she was younger.

So, do you think the equality vote is going to pass in Ireland? I dunno, it’s all so confusing. I mean, I support equality, but I don’t know how the government is going to handle it. They’ve been so slow on so many things. Yeah, but if it does pass, it’ll be a big step forward, right? Like, making sure people are treated fairly no matter who they are. Definitely. But I’ve heard some people are against it. They say it’s not the government’s job to make decisions like that. You know, like, “why should they decide for us?” I get that, but isn’t it everyone’s job to make sure people are treated fairly? I mean, if you’re a mum, you want your kids to be treated the same as anyone else. It doesn’t matter if you’re a boy or a girl. Exactly! And I think it’s about giving people the chance to live without fear or prejudice. Like, if someone’s gay, or trans, or whatever, they should have the same rights as anyone else. Yeah, it’s not like they’re asking for more than what they deserve. It’s just fairness. I mean, I don’t see why it should be such a big deal, but I guess some people are just scared of change. Change is scary, especially if you’re used to things the way they are. But you know, sometimes change is necessary. Like, when my mum was growing up, women couldn’t even vote. Now, we have a lot more rights. It’s just a matter of time. Yeah, I guess that’s true. Although I can’t imagine living in a time when women couldn’t vote. It must have been so hard. It was. But I think the older generation had to fight for it, and now we can take it for granted. But I think the equality vote is something that will help the next generation even more. I hope so. I mean, I’m not even old enough to vote yet, but I want to make sure the world I grow up in is fair and equal. That’s the spirit! I bet you’ll be a real activist when you’re older. You’ve got the fire for it. Maybe! Although sometimes I feel like all I do is complain about school and homework.

So, do you remember the time we tried to cook that hamster in the microwave? Oh, don’t bring that up. I’m still not sure how it even got in there. I think it was the kids. They were playing around with the microwave and somehow managed to trap the poor thing. It was terrifying. I thought it was just a piece of meat at first. I remember the smell. It was like a cross between burnt toast and something… wrong. Yeah, and then the kids started laughing like it was the funniest thing they’d ever seen. I still can’t get over how they thought it was a prank. I mean, what’s next? A squirrel in the oven? I’ve heard of people doing that with chickens, too. Though I’d say the hamster was the more unfortunate one. It’s amazing how kids think they’re being clever, but they just end up causing chaos. I suppose it’s part of growing up. You start off learning how to use a lathe, and then you’re off to the races with a microwave and a hamster. That’s the thing about being a parent. You never know what you’ll have to clean up after. I did try to teach them about the dangers of microwaves. But they just rolled their eyes and said, “It’s just a hamster, Dad.” I told them it was a serious matter. I even showed them a video about microwave safety. And then they did the exact opposite. I swear, they watched it just to see what would happen. It was like they were testing the limits of how crazy we were. And we fell for it. Well, at least we learned a lesson. Don’t trust kids with microwaves and small animals. And don’t forget to teach them about the dangers of using a lathe without supervision. I’ve got no idea how they even got a hold of a lathe. I thought that was locked away. Maybe they got it from the workshop. I’m still not sure how they managed to get it out. It’s a miracle they didn’t end up with a sliced finger or something. I still can’t believe that happened. I mean, we were all sitting down to lunch and it’s like, “Oh, look at the hamster in the microwave.”

I just got a new recording to transcribe, and it’s got this weird thing about mirror-writing. I couldn’t believe it at first—like, someone wrote the whole thing backwards. It was so strange. Mirror-writing? Like left-handed people sometimes do it unconsciously? Or is it something else? I think it’s more like someone deliberately wrote it that way—maybe for a puzzle or something. It’s not just reversed letters; the whole sentence is mirrored. It was in a letter someone sent to a bank about a debt. You can’t even read it without flipping it around. That sounds rather eccentric. I’ve heard of people writing in mirror script for fun, but I’m not sure how useful it is in a serious context like dealing with a bank. I mean, I had a student once who used mirror-writing in her notes. It took me ages to figure out what she was saying, and I almost failed her. Exactly! It was like a challenge. I thought, “What’s the point of that?” But I guess it’s a sign of creativity, maybe? Or maybe it’s just someone being defiant. It might be a way of keeping things secretive. I’ve heard of people using it in love letters, like to keep the message hidden from prying eyes. Although I can’t imagine that being very effective these days with smartphones and cameras. You know, I once saw a news story about a cat who was the star of a local event. They had a competition where people sent in their own cat stories, and this one cat had the most imaginative tale. It was about being adopted by a witch and living in a tower made of books. I almost believed it. That sounds more like something I’d find in a cryptic crossword clue than a real cat story. I mean, if a cat could read, it would be the only one I’d ever want. Well, I suppose cats do have a way of making stories up. I’ve always thought they were rather mysterious. I could almost believe one had been trained by a witch. And what about the new rules about charging for plastic bags? I heard that in some places, they’ve made it a £0.05 charge again. It’s about reducing plastic waste, but I think it’s just a way to make people think twice before grabbing a bag.

Alright, do you want some more Lego or do you want to do something else? I want to keep building my Ninjago city. It’s almost done. Can I help you? I want to build something too. Of course you can. Just don’t knock over the tower. It took me ages to build. It’s not that tall. I think I can handle it. Well, be careful. You don’t want to lose the spaceship. It’s the most important part. I even painted it gold. That’s cool. I’m building a Minecraft world. I made a mountain and a cave. That sounds awesome. I used to play Minecraft a lot when I was your age. Do you think we can play it together? I’d love to, but I’ve got a lot of work to do today. Maybe tomorrow? Okay, but I want to finish my world first. That’s fine. Just don’t stay up too late. Your dad will be home soon. He’s working late again. He said he’ll be back after 9. I don’t care if he’s late. I’m having fun. I know, but we need to keep the lights low. It’s getting late. I know, but I just want to finish my city. Alright, but let’s take a break for a minute. We can continue later. Okay. I’ll just put my pieces away. I’ll put my spaceship in the safe place. Good. Maybe we can all read a story for a while. I don’t want to read. I want to keep building. I understand, but it’s good to take a break sometimes. I agree. Let’s take a break and then we can go back to building. Yeah, I’m tired of sitting. Let’s go outside for a bit. That sounds like a good idea. Let’s go and get some fresh air. Okay, but I want to finish my Minecraft world first. No worries, just take a quick break. We’ll come back to it. Alright, let’s go. I’m ready for some fresh air. Me too. I need to take a break from building. Perfect. Let’s go outside and enjoy the evening. Yeah, I think I’ll be okay with a little bit of a break. Okay, I’m ready to go. Let’s get some fresh air.

So how did your holiday go, luv? I’ve been meaning to ask you for ages. Oh, it was brilliant, actually! We went to the Lake District, which is where my cousin lives. It was absolutely gorgeous. The weather was perfect, and we had the most amazing time. Yeah, I heard you were there. My friend Lucy said you went hiking with a bunch of family. Was it hard? No, not really. It was a bit of a long walk, but the views were worth it. We saw the mountains, the lakes, and even went to a little village that had the most amazing pub. Oh, really? Did you try the food? Oh, you should have come! It was this traditional English meal—stew, pies, and a really good ale. They even had live music. It was like stepping back in time. That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to visit the Lake District. Have you got any photos? Yeah, I’ve got a few on my phone. I can show you later. But to be honest, I’m not too keen on taking photos on holiday. I prefer just soaking it all in. I know what you mean. I’m more of a “live in the moment” person. It’s nice to just enjoy the experience without worrying about the camera. Honestly, I think I’m more of a “take everything” kind of person. I want to remember every little thing. That’s why I have a camera and a journal. That’s adorable. I have a journal too, but I mostly use it to write down my thoughts and reflections. It helps me process things. That’s really thoughtful. I’ve started doing that too. It’s amazing how just writing things down can make you appreciate them more. I can’t wait to see what you’ve written. Maybe I’ll write something too. We could even start a little journal together. That’d be fun. I’d love that. So, what are your plans for the day? I was thinking of going to the library. I’ve got a few books I need to study for my exams, but I also wanted to check out some new ones. That sounds like a great idea. I’m going to take a walk in the park nearby. I feel like I need some fresh air after that holiday. You should do that.

So, do you think we should get some sandwiches to eat before we start the card game? I’m starving. Yeah, I’m not sure yet. I mean, I like the idea of a proper meal, but I also don’t want to sit there with a full stomach and not be able to concentrate on the game. Yeah, but if we wait too long, we’ll be too hungry. I’ve got this sandwich I made this morning, and I’m not going to waste it. Okay, then I’ll grab a few things from the café. I think they have those little wraps with chicken and salad. They’re pretty good. That sounds good. I like that one. Just make sure you don’t get the one with the chips. I had one once and it was too messy. Oh, I know what you mean. I tried that last week, and I ended up with a chip stuck in my shirt. It was ridiculous. Yeah, I’ve had that happen too. One time, I was trying to eat it quickly, and it just fell out of my hand. My mom nearly had a heart attack. That’s not the only thing that’s messy, though. Have you seen the way Mr. Thompson – our history teacher – talks about the Battle of Britain? It’s like he’s trying to act out the whole thing. Oh yeah, he’s always doing that. He even wore a little cap and a coat last week. I didn’t know what to think. I think it’s a bit weird, but I guess it helps us remember the stuff better. He’s got a way of making even the most boring topics interesting. Yeah, but I still think he should be more strict. I mean, he gave me a warning about sending a message to the school prefects last week. I told them about the exam timetable, and he just laughed. That was funny, though. I don’t think you meant to do anything wrong, did you? No, I didn’t. I just wanted to help out with the study group. We were all stuck on some questions. I think he’s got a soft spot for us. I mean, he’s been giving us extra credit on the topics we’re struggling with. Who knows, maybe he’s thinking of becoming a mentor or something.

So, do you remember Mr. Thompson from physics? He’s such a weirdo. Yeah, he’s the one who keeps talking about quantum physics like it’s something we all understand. He said we’re all made of particles! I don’t even know what that means. I think he meant like atoms and stuff. But he said it like it’s a big secret. Oh, I saw him in the corridor the other day. He was wearing a superhero t-shirt. Was it the one with the green mask? Yeah! He looked like a Marvel hero. I told my friend, and she said he’s a total geek. I think he’s more of a mad scientist type. He’s always got that crazy look in his eyes. He’s also been giving us homework that’s impossible to do. Last week, we had to explain the theory of relativity in one paragraph. I tried to write it, but I kept getting confused. I think I wrote about time travel by accident. Oh, I did that too! I think I got a B for effort. That’s what I thought – it’s not like he checks the work, he just gives it back with the same comments every time. Yeah, and then there’s our form tutor, Miss Hart. She’s always on our case. She’s the one who made us do an essay about ‘the impact of social media on teenage mental health’ last month. I wrote about how people are constantly comparing themselves to others online. But she said it was too vague. I think she wanted us to make a real argument, not just say things that sound smart. I tried to use some proper vocabulary. I used the word ‘metacognition’ and ‘cognitive dissonance’. I told you, you didn’t need that. You just needed to say things like 'people feel anxious because they see others being perfect online'. Yeah, but I thought it would impress her. It didn’t. She said you had to back it up with evidence. That’s the problem with her. She’s like a detective. She’s always asking why and how. I think she’s trying to make us into better thinkers, but honestly, it’s exhausting. I agree. I just want to do the easiest thing possible. Like, I don’t know. Maybe watch ‘17 Again’ again? Yeah, that’s what I was thinking.

So, do you know what’s happening this weekend? I’ve been thinking about going to Transylvania. You know, like the Count Dracula stuff. I’m going to try and find that creepy old castle or something. Oh, Transylvania? That sounds like a great idea. I’ve always wanted to go there. But I don’t think I’d be able to sleep at night. I heard those places are haunted. Yeah, I heard the same. But I think it’s just the stories. You know, people just like to scare themselves. I mean, I’ve been to some pretty creepy places, and it’s mostly just the atmosphere. I’ve only been to Australia, but I think Transylvania is even creepier. I mean, the locals there are like, I don’t know, they seem very mysterious. And the forests? They’re just too thick. You can’t even see the sun sometimes. Yeah, I heard the forests are really dense. But I also heard some people say it’s the perfect place for a solo trip. You know, like, you get to explore and not have to worry about people following you. I think I’d rather stay in the UK and go to the Lake District. That’s pretty much the closest thing to being mysterious without being too spooky. Plus, I’ve heard the water there is amazing. I would go for the Pacific Northwest, actually. The forests there are just as thick, and the mountains are breathtaking. But I’m not sure if I’ll have time. I’ve got a café to run, and I’m still sorting out the new weekend plans. Yeah, I’m stuck in the same boat. I’m trying to figure out what to do this summer. I’ve been thinking of going to the Mediterranean. Maybe Greece or Italy. But I’m not sure if I have the money for that. Maybe I’ll just stay local and go to the countryside. I think I’m going to try and get a few weeks off work. I’ve been working too much lately, and I just need to get out. Maybe take a trip to the countryside or somewhere with nature. I’ve heard that the Lake District is amazing. That’s a good idea. I think I’m going to start looking into some travel plans. Maybe I’ll go to the Scottish Highlands.

Alright, do you two want to go to the party tomorrow? It’s at the community hall, and there’s going to be a live band playing. I think it’s going to be really fun. A live band? You mean like the one that plays at the café? Yeah, the same one, but they’re going to be doing a full set. I’ve heard they’re really good. A lot of people from the village are coming, including some friends from school. Cool. But can we take the aerial hoop? I’ve been practicing so much lately. I think I’m getting pretty good at it. Oh, the aerial hoop? That’s the one you got from the festival, right? I saw it hanging in the backyard last week. Yeah, and I’ve been trying to do little tricks with it. I even did a loop yesterday. I think I might be ready to do something more complicated. That’s amazing! I wish I could do that. I was thinking about doing the muddy obstacle course again. I haven’t done it for ages, and I really enjoyed it. The muddy obstacle course? You mean the one we did at the country fair last summer? I remember you getting covered in mud from head to toe. You looked like a little mud monster. I did! But it was so much fun. I think we should do it again. Maybe at the party, if there's time. I could bring my camera. I’ve been taking a lot of photos lately. That’d be great. I’ve been thinking about doing some family photos too. We’ve been meaning to get a few proper pictures for the holiday album. Maybe the party could be a good time. Can I wear my new dress? I got it for my birthday, and I think it looks really nice. It’s light blue with some sparkles. Of course you can. It’ll look great. I think we should all wear something special. The party is going to be such a good time. Let’s make sure we all look our best. Okay, but I also want to bring some snacks. I’ve been baking some cookies and cupcakes. I think we can have a little snack table at the party. That’s a great idea. We can have some treats to share. Maybe we can even set up a small photo booth with some fun props.

Well, I've just had a look at the results, and I think they're pretty good, especially for her age. She's doing really well in English and Maths. That’s great to hear. I was worried about her with all the pressure from the school. But I suppose it’s only natural for kids to feel that way. Yeah, and it’s not just them. I saw a few of my students this week, and they all seem to be under a lot of pressure. Parents’ evening must be coming up soon, right? Yeah, it's in a couple of weeks. I’m really nervous. I don’t know if I’m ready for it. What if they don’t like me? Oh, come on, you’re a good kid. I mean, you’ve got good grades and you’re smart. Why would they not like you? You’re not a bad person. I know, but I just don’t want to mess up. What if they say something like, “She’s not trying hard enough” or something? You know, I used to be like that too. When I was her age, I thought everything had to be perfect. But it’s not. People don’t expect perfection. They expect effort. True enough. I still remember when I was her age. I used to think I had to be the best at everything. But then I realized that life isn’t like that. You just have to do your best. That’s the key, isn’t it? Just doing your best. I think the pressure comes from being told you have to be the best, but there’s no such thing as being the best at everything. I guess. It’s just so much pressure. I mean, I’m doing driving lessons now, and I’m not even sure I’m going to pass. I keep thinking about how I might fail. Don’t worry. You’ll pass. I’m sure of it. I did my driving test last year, and I had a bit of a struggle with reversing, but I got it in the end. Yeah, I hope so. I just don’t want to be the one who fails. I don’t want to let anyone down. Well, I think it’s important to remember that everyone has their own pace. Some people pass quickly, others take longer.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play Chinese chess with your nan? I think it was the weekend before she passed away. I’m still not sure how she managed to beat me every time. Yeah, I remember that. You were always so proud of yourself when you managed to win a single game. But then she’d just smile and say, “Well, you’ve improved a bit.” I think she was just trying to be nice, but I swear she used to cheat. She didn’t cheat, mate. She just had a better memory. She’d remember every move you made and counter it. I still can’t beat her in the head-to-head version. I think she had the secret weapon of being able to read my face and tell when I was about to make a bad move. Oh, you’re just trying to make it sound like she was better than you, aren’t you? I mean, she was old, she had dementia, and she was playing chess with you in the garden. That was tough. I still don’t know how she managed to remember all the rules. I think she just had a way of keeping it simple. She’d say, “Every move is a chance to learn.” And then she’d go on about how the game was like life. I didn’t really take her seriously back then, but now I think maybe she did have a point. Yeah, and I think the fact that she managed to keep playing with us for so long was a real achievement. It wasn’t just about the game—she loved the way it brought us all together. Even when she was forgetting things, she’d still remember how to play. That’s what I love about the game, though. It’s not just about winning. It’s about the time you spend with people. I remember when I started learning how to play for university. I thought it was just about strategy, but now I see it’s about patience, too. Speaking of patience, I’ve been trying to learn the rules again. I’ve got a player’s manual from the library, but it’s full of Chinese characters. I’m not even sure if I’m pronouncing them right. Yeah, go easy on yourself. I think you’re doing great.

So, do you think you’ll be able to get a teaching job back in the UK? I mean, it’s got to be tough with all the student loans and everything. I know I've been struggling with that since I retired. Not that I was ever really working, but it’s like the system’s just not set up for people like us. Honestly, I don’t know. It’s not like I’ve been working full-time or anything. So, do you know what you're going to do after school? I mean, like, uni or something? Honestly, I’m still trying to figure it out. Right, right, so I was thinking, love, about how the government's handling money these days. It's a bit of a mess, isn't it? Yeah, I think so. I mean, it feels like every time there's a new policy, it's like a different game. I don't know if I can keep up with it all. I know, I know. You’ve got to be on your toes. I mean, there are so many different policies, and it’s not always clear how they affect everyday people.

I just got a new job, actually. You know, I’ve been working on this project co-ordinating a few different events for a charity. It’s been pretty hectic, but I like the challenge. Oh, that’s great! I bet it’s a lot of responsibility, but also rewarding. You know, I’ve been in education for decades, and even now, every day is different. I remember when I first started, I was so nervous, thinking I didn’t know anything. Now I think I’ve got a good grasp of it, but there’s always something new to learn. You need to be patient with the kids, especially at that age. Yeah, I think I’d have to be patient. I mean, I’ve worked with people of all ages, but kids can be such a different experience. Sometimes, they need more than just lessons—they need someone to talk to, someone to listen. That’s true. I think that’s why I’m drawn to work with people. It’s not just about the job, it’s about the impact you can make. Though, honestly, I still can’t imagine being in a classroom all day. You know, I did have a conversation with a student a while ago that really stuck with me. She said she felt like she didn’t belong, like she wasn’t smart enough. I sat down with her and just listened for a while. She told me about her struggles, and I just reassured her that it was okay. She left feeling better, and that made me realize how important those small moments are. That’s beautiful. I always try to be supportive with the people I work with, even if it’s just in a small way. It’s those little things that make a difference. I couldn’t agree more. And it’s not just in work.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about the recycling thing. I was just in the shop the other day, and I saw this new bin for food waste. I thought, “Now that’s a good idea.” But then I looked at the cost and thought, “Oh, well, maybe not.” Yeah, I saw that too. It’s a bit pricey, isn’t it? Honestly, I don’t even know where to start with recycling. I’ve got a bin for paper, one for glass, one for cans, and another for food waste. But I don’t know if I’m actually doing it right. I mean, I’m not sure what goes into which bin anymore. That’s the thing, isn’t it? It’s all so confusing. You think you’re doing the right thing, but then you second-guess yourself. I’ve got this new job, and I’m still getting my head around all the admin stuff. Plus, I have to make sure I’m not missing any important deadlines. I get that. I’ve been out of work for a while now, and it’s a bit of a struggle. But I’ve tried to keep myself busy with things like gardening and cooking. I even started making my own wine last year. It wasn’t the greatest, but it was fun. Oh, wine? That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to try my hand at winemaking. My nan used to make it when she was younger. I’ve got a few bottles of her stuff in the cellar, but I haven’t had the chance to taste them yet.

I can't believe I actually got the conference slot. I mean, I applied like three months ago, and it felt like I was just throwing my name into the void. But then, out of the blue, I got an email saying I was selected. That’s kind of surreal, isn’t it? Yeah, I can imagine. It’s one thing to apply and hope, but actually being chosen? Are you going to be proactive? Are you going to make connections? I mean, I’ve been to a few conferences before, and it’s not just about listening to talks—it’s about networking, meeting other teachers, and maybe even presenting something of your own. Exactly. I feel like there’s a lot of research out there, but not all teachers are aware of it. I’d love to bring that into the conversation. That sounds really good. I’ve been thinking about the same things. I mean, I’ve started using some gamified approaches in my classroom, and the kids are actually more engaged now. Maybe we could collaborate on a presentation or something. If we both go, we could team up. That would be cool. I’ve been meaning to reach out to you about that. But I have to say, going to that conference is going to take a lot of time and energy. I go every year, and it’s like a full-time job.

So, do you think we're on the right road? I’m getting a bit lost in all these Polish signs. I think we are, but I’m not sure. I think we might need to check the map again. I’ve seen some signs pointing toward Rzeszow, but it’s all in Polish, and I don’t read it well. Yeah, I know, I’ve been trying to figure out how to navigate this. I’ve never been to Poland before, and I don’t want to end up in the wrong town. Didn’t we pass a gas station with a map? I think we did. I’ll check the dashboard. Wait, here it is. Okay, the map says we should be heading east, then turn south after about ten miles. I think that’s the route. Okay, let’s take it. I’ve been reading a bit about Polish culture while we’re traveling. I’ve been trying to get into shape for the last few months. I joined a gym and started lifting weights. It feels good to be active again, even if it’s just a bit. That’s admirable. I’ve been meaning to get into a routine too. I used to play netball, but when I moved to Bury, I didn’t have a team. I’m starting to get back into it though, and maybe I’ll meet some people along the way. That’s a great idea. Friendships are important, especially when you’re traveling. It’s not just about the places you see; it’s about the people you meet. Absolutely. I think the best part of this trip is being with you. Even though we’ve been through some rough patches, like the last time we had to find a parking spot in a village and ended up in the wrong one, it’s still a good experience. Yeah, I remember that. It was a bit of a disaster, but we laughed about it later.

So, do you think the Vikings really had anything to do with the pyramids? I mean, they’re like 2,000 years apart, right? No, no, I don’t think they had anything to do with the pyramids at all. They were in Europe and North America, and the pyramids were built by the ancient Egyptians. But I still think the Vikings were pretty amazing. I mean, they sailed across the North Sea and even reached North America, like a few hundred years before Columbus. Yeah, that’s true. But I still think some of the myths about them are exaggerated. Like, I’ve read some stuff about the Viking longships and how they could sail up rivers and all that. It’s impressive, but I’m not sure if they had the technology to do all that. I think they did, actually. They were pretty resourceful. But I guess that’s just one of those areas where history gets a bit fuzzy. Speaking of history, have you ever thought about the idea of immortality? Like, what if we could live forever? Honestly, I don’t think I’d want to. I mean, living forever sounds like it would be really lonely. You’d have to watch everyone you know die around you, and then you’d just be left with all that memory. It’s not exactly the best way to spend eternity. I guess that’s a good point. But what about the science side of it? I heard about telomeres and how they shorten as we age. Is there any way to reverse that? I think some studies suggest that telomeres can be extended in laboratory settings, but I’m not sure if it’s safe or practical for humans yet. It’s definitely an area of research, though. Speaking of which, have you heard about the new energy sources that could help us combat global warming? Yeah, I’ve heard about some innovative ideas, like using hydrogen as a clean fuel or even experimenting with nuclear fusion. But honestly, I think we’re not going to solve climate change overnight. It’s going to take a long time and a lot of effort. I agree. It’s a big problem, and it’s going to require cooperation from governments and individuals alike. But I’m also curious about the future. I mean, with all these advancements in technology, what do you think the world will look like in 100 years?

So, do you think we should go to the new café in town tomorrow? I heard the lasagna is really good. Oh, I’m not sure. I’ve been meaning to try it, but I’m not sure if I can afford it. I’ve been meaning to look into it more. I think some of the older people in the village are really against it, but I don’t want to jump to conclusions.

I just got a text from the estate agent saying they’ve found a new tenant for the flat next door. So that’s one less thing to worry about now. Oh, good! I was a bit worried about the noise.
