Speaking of work, have you been keeping up with your gym schedule? I heard you’ve been really busy lately. It’s been a bit of a struggle, to be honest. Between work and the house extension, I’ve barely had time to get my breath. But I promise I’ll get back on track next week. I know how you feel. Between the house extension and all the shopping I’ve been doing for the new furniture, I’m feeling like I’m running on fumes. I had to stop at the supermarket this morning just to take a breather. Yeah, I can relate. But I think we both need to take it one step at a time. I’m actually planning a weekend getaway with some friends. We’re thinking of heading to the coast. It’ll be a chance to clear my head and get some fresh air. That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been meaning to do something like that too. Maybe we could go together? I’ve been wanting to visit my grandad up in Norfolk, and I think it would be nice to do that together.

So, what are we doing today? I'm bored. Well, it's a bit hot, so maybe we could go swimming? Yeah, that sounds good. But I don’t know how to swim. Oh, you can learn. We could go to the local pool and take a lesson. Okay, maybe. But what about the guitar? I’ve been practising a bit. That’s great, but don’t forget, you still need to help me with the gardening. You know, the garden’s getting a bit overgrown. Yeah, I know. I’ll try to help you out after swimming. Thanks. And by the way, did you see the new episode of Stick with Mick? No, I haven’t. Is it good? It’s really funny. They’re talking about a new adventure this time. Maybe you should watch it with me later. Okay, maybe. But first, I want to finish my guitar lesson. Alright, but don’t forget, we have to make some dinner tonight. We’re having Japanese food. Japanese? Like sushi? Yeah, but we’re making it at home. I found a recipe online, and I think it’s going to be good. Cool. I can help you with that. I’m not too bad in the kitchen. Oh, really? Let me test you. Can you make a stir-fry? I can try. I’ve done it before. Just need to make sure I don’t burn the vegetables. That’s the key. And don’t forget to use the right amount of soy sauce. Got it. But what if I mess it up? I don’t want to make a total disaster. It’s okay. We can always eat it with rice. And if it’s not perfect, we can just have it with some chips. Yeah, that’s a plan. What about Mick? Is he going to be on today? I think so. He’s talking about a new trip to Japan. Maybe he’ll show us some cool places there. That would be cool. I’ve always wanted to go to Japan. I’ve seen some videos of the food and the cities. Yeah, it’s a beautiful country. Just make sure you don’t get lost in the big cities. I won’t. I’ll have my map and my phone. Smart. And if you do get lost, don’t worry. Just ask for help. People there are really friendly.

So, do you remember that one time we went to that little cinema in Prescot and saw that old horror film? It was like, one of those ones where the guy gets stuck in a dentist’s chair, right? Oh yeah, I remember that! I think we were like, pretending it was a comedy. I mean, the whole thing was so over-the-top. I kept laughing even though I was scared. Yeah, and then halfway through, the lights flickered, and someone said, “Is that the film or is that the electricity?” It was the worst. I thought we were all going to get scared out of our minds. That’s the thing about horror movies, you know? You expect something to happen, and then nothing happens. It’s like the whole time you’re waiting for the jump scare, and then it just cuts to credits. Exactly. I think that’s why I like watching them in groups. You can be like, “Okay, this is going to be scary,” and then when it’s not, you laugh it off. Yeah, I mean, we’re not as brave as we think we are. I still get nervous if something happens behind me. Tell me about the last time you saw a horror movie. Did you actually watch it all? No, I got halfway through and started thinking about what I was going to cook for dinner. I mean, what’s the point of being scared if you can’t eat afterwards? That’s the thing, isn’t it? You can’t be scared of something if you’re thinking about pizza. Exactly. I think the real horror is when the film ends and you’re still not sure if anything actually happened. That’s the unspoken question, right? Did that  really  happen? Or was it all in our heads? You know, I think the answer is somewhere in between. It’s not real, but it’s not not real either. It’s like the line between dreams and reality. That’s why I write. I like to explore those lines. You know, the place where the real becomes the imagined. If you’re writing about horror, you’ve got to be careful. You don’t want to scare your readers too much. They might start thinking about the dentist. Or the Citibike. I’m not sure which is worse. I think the Citibike is the worst.

So, how’s the new job going, love? I heard you got the teaching post in Chester? Oh, it’s going well, Mum. I started last Monday, and it’s a bit of a culture shock, honestly. I mean, the children are adorable, but the school’s in a bit of a state. The corridors are full of posters from the previous headteacher's 'vision' — I think they’re all about creativity and innovation, but I don’t know if that’s what the parents are looking for. I hope it doesn’t turn into another of those 'progressive' schools like the one in Walsall. I still remember that place — it was like a revolving door of staff and more than a few controversial policies. Oh, I know, I’ve heard the stories. But I’m trying to be positive. I even got to teach a group of Year 3s, and they’re all so enthusiastic. They actually asked me if I was going to the Easter egg hunt, which was pretty cute. That’s great! You always had a way of connecting with kids. Remember when you used to make those Easter cakes as a kid? I still have the old recipe book from your gran. You used to make these fabulous little sponges with icing and – wait, are you planning on making any this year? Oh, I was thinking about that. We’ve got a Christening coming up in June, and the family’s all in a tizzy about what to serve. I thought maybe we could have a mini Easter cake table with some traditional ones, and some new ones too. Maybe even a few cupcakes with Easter eggs on top, just for fun. That sounds like a good idea. But you’ll have to let me know what you’re using for the icing. I’m still trying to figure out how to make that white fondant without it turning into a glue-like mess. Don’t worry, I’ve got a new recipe from my sister. She’s a bit of a baking madam. We’re even thinking of adding some sprite to the frosting to make it a bit more fun and less sticky. Hmm, that sounds like a risk. But I suppose if the kids like it, it’s worth it. I do hope you’re managing your time well, though. Between work and the Christening planning, I can see it getting a bit overwhelming.

I can’t believe it’s already April. Time flies when you’re busy planning lessons and trying to keep up with all the admin. How are you holding up? Honestly, I feel like I’m barely keeping afloat. Between my teaching job and the children at home, there’s not much time for anything else. But I’ve been trying to make the most of it. That’s a lot to juggle. I know the feeling. I’ve had to juggle my teaching job, my language courses, and my own family. It’s not easy, but I think the key is to not get too overwhelmed. I guess that’s the thing. You have to find little pockets of time to breathe. Speaking of which, how are the kids at school? Are they behaving well? They’re mostly fine. A few little challenges here and there, but nothing too bad. I do worry about the pressure they’re under. They’re starting to think about GCSEs and everything. It’s such a big transition. I remember when I was their age, it felt like the world was ending. I still have nightmares about exams. I know, right? But we’ve got to be there for them. I’ve been trying to encourage them to take some time for themselves, to not put all their pressure on one thing. It’s not all about grades. That’s wise. I’ve been trying to talk to mine about the importance of self-care. But they’re so caught up in their own worlds, it’s hard to get through. It’s tough. I’ve also been thinking about my own future. I’ve started looking into doing some training abroad. I’ve always wanted to teach in different countries, but I’m not sure if I’ll ever get the chance. That sounds amazing. I’ve thought about that too. I’ve been thinking about taking a break from teaching for a while. Maybe go into something different, something more flexible. It’s a big decision, but I think it’s worth considering. You never know what opportunities might come your way. I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately. I’ve got this idea of starting a small business selling homemade beauty products. It’s something I’ve always been interested in, and I think it could work. That sounds like something you could really get into.

So, do you think we’ve got enough matzah for everyone? I know my mum always insists on having a whole box, but she’s probably just being dramatic. Yeah, I mean, she’s a baker, so of course she’s got extra. But honestly, the matzah is just kind of like a sideshow compared to the real star of the show—this chicken soup. It’s so good, it’s like tasting the soul of my grandmother. Oh, I know what you mean. My mother was a literary editor, but she also had a secret passion for cooking. She used to write recipes in the margins of her books. One time she even accidentally wrote a poem about baklava in a manuscript of Jane Austen. It was so weird, but also beautiful. A poem about baklava? That’s the kind of thing that would’ve made her a character in a novel. You know, the kind of woman who could throw a dinner party and turn it into a literary salon. Exactly. And now she’s in her fifties, and all she does is write haikus about shortbread and bake it to perfection. I swear, she could run a bakery in New York. Well, if she wanted to, she could. I mean, I’ve seen her dough rise like a Tolkien novel. One time, she even made a whole batch of challah that looked like a medieval tapestry. Oh, that’s the kind of thing that makes you want to quote Kafka. You know, the one where the bread is always just a little too delicious and you can’t stop eating it. Yeah, and I mean, I’m not even Jewish, but I still found myself saying “baruch atah Adonai” after that first bite. I think it’s the kind of food that just... hits you on the soul. I know what you mean. I remember when I first moved to London, my flatmate brought me to a shuk in Brixton and told me, “If you want to know what real life feels like, just try the falafel here.” And I thought, “What is this, a religion?” But then I ate it, and I was like, “Okay, this is a religion.” I think that’s the thing with Jewish food, though. It’s not just food—it’s like a language. You’ve got kasha, you’ve got matzah, you’ve got everything from the moment you’re born.

So, do you know what’s on tonight? I was thinking of watching that new drama series,  The Halcyon Days —the one about the 1970s. It’s got this really nostalgic feel, and I think it’s going to be really good. I’ve heard about it. I liked the preview. It was all about family and relationships, which is always a good topic. But I’m still trying to decide if I want to watch it or just binge on some old  Doctor Who  episodes instead. They’re comforting, you know? Honestly, I think you should go for  The Halcyon Days . I’ve been meaning to watch it, and I think it’s the kind of show that really makes you think about how things have changed over the decades. But I’ve been too busy with work to get around to it. It’s one of those things I keep putting off. I can relate. I’ve been meaning to start reading that book by Hilary Mantel that’s been on my shelf for ages. I’ve heard it’s brilliant, but I get distracted so easily. Do you think I should read it or just watch something else? I think you should read it. It’s a classic, and it gives you a different kind of satisfaction. Plus, I’ve heard it’s one of the best books of the year. But don’t feel bad if you don’t get through it in one go. I love books, but I can’t help but get distracted by other things. I even started knitting again to help me focus. It’s a bit strange, but it works. Oh, you’re knitting again? I thought that was something you used to do before you got into all that coding stuff. You know me—always switching between hobbies. I’ve been trying to make a scarf for my mum, but I keep making mistakes. I think I’ve managed to knit a couple of squares that are like twisted knots. It’s not bad, though. Maybe if I keep going, I’ll end up with a scarf that looks like a complicated tapestry.

So, do you think you've got it all sorted with the new phone yet? Not really. I've been trying to set it up, but I can't get the Wi-Fi to connect. I keep getting this message that says “No internet access.” Hmm. Did you try turning it off and on again? Sometimes that helps. Yeah, I did. I even tried rebooting the router. Nothing’s working. Maybe it’s the network. We’re in Joensuu, right? Do you know if the Wi-Fi here is any different from back home? I don’t think so, but I’ve heard that some places in Finland use different settings for mobile networks. Maybe it’s something to do with the carrier? Could be. I remember when I first came here, my phone didn’t work properly. I had to go through this whole setup with a local guy. Really? That sounds complicated. It was, but once I got past the language barrier, it wasn’t too bad. I guess it’s just about finding the right settings. Do you know what network you’re on? I think it’s called “Nokia” or something like that. Wait, I think I saw it on the screen earlier. Let me check. Oh, Nokia is the operator here, right? So if you’re on the right network, the phone should connect. Yeah, I think I’m on the right one. But it’s still not working. Maybe the phone is just not compatible with Finns’ networks. Or maybe the settings are wrong. I don’t know. I thought this phone would be plug-and-play. You’re not the first person to say that. I had to set up my phone here too. It took me a day to get it working properly. I can’t wait to get this sorted. I need to be able to send emails and check messages. If you’re still having trouble, maybe you should ask someone at the pub. They might have a better idea. I could do that. Maybe I’ll go check with the barman. He’s always been helpful. Yeah, and if all else fails, just ask. We’re all in the same boat here, right? True. I guess I’ll go try that. Thanks for the help. No problem. Just remember, if you get stuck, you’re not alone. I will. I’m just glad I brought this phone, even though it’s been a bit of a nightmare.

Mummy, can we get a red panda for our birthday? A red panda? That’s a very expensive animal, darling. You know they cost a lot to take care of. But they’re so cute! And they like to climb trees. I saw a video of one climbing a tree and it looked like it was having fun. Mummy, I don’t want a red panda. I want a Malamooche. It’s a dog like the one in the park! Oh, you mean the big black dog with the floppy ears? That’s a Malamute, sweetheart. And we already have a cat, remember? Yeah, but the cat is boring. It’s just sitting there all the time. But we can talk about it when you’re a bit bigger. But I want to have a party for my birthday. Can I have a red panda as a present? That’s not how parties work, sweetheart. You get things like toys, cake, and maybe a new book. A red panda is not something you can just get for a birthday. Can I have a Malamooche? I’ll take care of it! You’re only two! You can’t even walk properly without help. Maybe when you’re older, you can have a dog. Can I have a Malamooche for my birthday then? Well, maybe we can talk to your aunt about it. She has a Malamute, and she might be able to tell us more about them. Yeah! And I can help take care of it. I can walk it and feed it and play with it. I promise I’ll be a good puppy person! That’s sweet, but we’ll have to see. Let’s talk about your birthday party first. What are you hoping to do? I want a cake and some games. Maybe we can go to the park and play with the other kids. And I want to have a big present. Can I have a present too? Of course you can, honey. We’ll make sure everyone gets something special. And maybe we can even have a little party at home with your friends. That would be awesome. Can I have a robot toy?

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to have these huge Christmas parties? I think it was like every weekend in December, no? Yeah, I remember that. It was a mad time. My parents would do these big things, like making all the food and inviting everyone. But I think we were different from the other kids, like we had more people over. Oh yes, I remember too. I think that was the time when we started to notice differences in how people celebrated. Some families had more traditions, others had fewer. It was interesting to see how different families approached Christmas. I remember when I was a kid, the only Christmas we had was with my mum and dad. We didn’t have many friends, and it was much more quiet. We had the tree, some gifts, and that was it. But now, with everyone moving around the world, it’s a different story. Yeah, I think in recent years, people have become more global. You can have Christmas parties with people from all over the world now. I mean, even here, we have people from different countries, and they bring their own traditions. It’s funny, though. I was in Manila for a while, and I was shocked by how different their Christmas was. They have this huge celebration, like, it's a religious thing, but also very festive. They have big meals and family gatherings. It's almost like a week-long event, which is totally different from what we do here. That's fascinating. I always thought Christmas was something that was very British, but now I see how it’s adapted in so many different cultures. I remember when I was teaching, I had students from all over the world, and they had different ways of celebrating. Yeah, that's right. I remember one student who was from South Africa. He told me that they had a very different approach to Christmas — they celebrated it as more of a social event, like any other holiday. There were no big ceremonies, just family and friends getting together. I think it’s a good thing. It shows how adaptable the traditions are. But I also wonder, in some countries, Christmas is more about religion, and in others, it's more about the day off from work or socialising. Yeah, and I think that's why it's so interesting to hear about different people’s experiences.

So, how’s the new detective series you’ve been watching? I heard it’s got a pretty strong plot. Oh, it’s alright, I guess. Not as gripping as the last one, though. I’m starting to feel like I’ve seen the same storyline a hundred times. Yeah, I’ve been on the same boat. I tried watching it last week, but I just couldn’t get into it. Maybe I’ll give it another go sometime. That’s the thing with detective shows, isn’t it? They always seem to follow the same formula. Get a mystery, a few red herrings, and a twist at the end. Exactly. My friend Mark said it was like a modern-day  Sherlock  but with more drama and less logic. He was joking, but I think he’s right. Haha, I can imagine. I’m more of a  Breaking Bad  fan myself. It’s got that slow burn, you know? Oh, I love that show. It’s so intense. I used to watch it every week when I was working late shifts. That’s the thing with work, isn’t it? It always ends up taking over your free time. I’m lucky I got a bit of a break this month. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been working on a new project at the moment, and it’s been keeping me pretty busy. But I’ve been trying to make time to read. That’s good. I’ve been meaning to get back into reading more. I’ve been so caught up in transcription work, I’ve barely had time to read a proper book. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to read more too. I’ve got this Kindle, and I’ve been reading some short stories on it. It’s actually pretty handy. Oh, I’ve got one too. I’ve been using it to read some of the classics. It’s so much better than carrying around a physical book. Yeah, the Kindle’s great. I’ve been trying to get into some non-fiction lately, mostly about psychology. It’s interesting stuff. That’s a good idea. I’ve been thinking about picking up a book on leadership or something like that. Maybe that’ll help me with work. That could work. I’ve been doing some research on how to improve communication in the workplace, so maybe we could share some tips.

Well, I've been meaning to ask you both, what's going on with the garden? It's been a bit of a mess lately, hasn't it? Oh, you know, it's been one of those years. The weather’s been so unpredictable. One day it’s sunny, the next it’s pouring down like a bucket. It’s like the garden’s trying to tell us something. Aye, I know what you mean. I’ve had the same thing with the hens. They’ve been scratching around the garden like they're looking for something, but I can’t figure out what. It’s like they’ve got a sixth sense about the weather. You know, I think it’s the same with the old place. When I was younger, I used to look after the garden, and I used to think I had a knack for it. But now, with all the weeds and the damp, it’s like the garden has a mind of its own. Mmm, you’re not wrong. I remember when we had that big storm a few years back, the garden was completely gone. Everything was flattened. It was like a warzone. But somehow, it all came back, didn’t it? Indeed it did. And now it's more of a wild garden, but I suppose that's the natural way things go. You can’t control everything, can you? I suppose not. You can try, but in the end, it’s the land that decides. I think it's a bit of a lesson, really. Some things you can’t control, and you have to be flexible. That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately. With the way things are going in the world, you can’t always plan for everything. You just have to adapt, like the garden does. Exactly. I’ve been thinking about starting a small vegetable patch. I’ve got a bit of space in the back, and I thought it might be nice to have something growing. We could have fresh produce and maybe even share some with the neighbors. That sounds like a good idea. It’s not like we’re short of space. Plus, it’s good to get the hands in the soil again, you know? Gives you a bit of purpose. I agree. It’s not like we're young anymore, but you still need something to keep you busy.

So, do you think we should go to the party tomorrow? I mean, it's supposed to be a nice evening, and the team really needs a break from all this research. Yeah, I was thinking the same thing. It's been a long week, and we've all been working so hard on the new language project. I think a party would be a great way to unwind. I agree. I've been feeling a bit drained lately, and I think a few drinks and some good company would do us all good. Plus, it's the last night of the month, so it feels like the perfect time to celebrate. So, do you know what’s happening with the new science project? I heard it’s gonna be really tough. Yeah, I heard about it too. I think it’s about renewable energy or something like that. So, did you enjoy the meal, Mum? Oh, it was lovely, thank you. The steak was perfectly cooked, and the dessert was absolutely delicious. I haven’t had something this good in ages. Yeah, it was good. The fish was a bit on the salty side, though. I don’t know if it was the sauce or just the way it was cooked. I thought the fish was fine. Maybe it’s just how it was prepared. So, how’s the new house? I heard you’ve been doing some work on it. Oh, yeah, it’s coming along nicely. I’ve got a few rooms fixed up, and I’m hoping to get the garden done before the season starts. She’s got this thing with her ribs that’s been bothering her for ages, and they’re still not sure what’s wrong. That’s awful. I can’t imagine how hard it must be for you. It is. But I’m trying to stay positive. I know she’s getting the best care possible, and I’d rather be here than out doing something else. That’s admirable. You’ve always been the kind of person who puts others first. Well, I suppose I’ve always thought that way. Not that I’ve ever had much choice, really. That’s not true. You’ve had plenty of choice. You just always chose to do the right thing. I dunno. I guess I just don’t like to leave people hanging. That’s a great quality. It’s one of the things I really admire about you. Thank you. I try not to go out of my way too much, but I think I’ve been doing better lately. I can tell. You’ve been helping your dad with the garden, haven’t you? Yeah, he’s been really down lately, and I thought I could do something to make him feel better. That’s sweet of you. I think it’s great that you’re still so involved in your family.

So, how’s the bar work going? You mentioned you were on shift last week, right? Yeah, I was. It went okay, honestly. I mean, it was a busy night, but I managed. I think I got through it without making too many mistakes. But it was exhausting. I didn’t sleep well after. I can imagine. I’ve never worked in a bar before, but from what I hear, it’s a lot to handle. Especially if you’re new. What kind of shifts do you usually do? Mostly weekends, I think. I don’t like to work during the week because I’m at uni, and I want to have time to study. But sometimes they’ll ask me to do late shifts if they’re short-staffed. I’ve had to do a few of those. I’m just trying to keep up with the courses, and now I’m thinking about work as well. It’s a lot, I know. But maybe it’s good to have some experience. I mean, it gives you a bit of money, and you get to meet people. Plus, you learn how to handle pressure, which is useful for anything you do in the future. That’s true. I guess I should start thinking about getting a part-time job too. I just haven’t had the chance yet. I’m not sure what I’m looking for, though. Any ideas? Well, if you’re interested in working with people, maybe something in customer service? Or even a library job, like what I used to do before I started bartending. It’s not as exciting, but it’s steady. Or, if you like the bar stuff, maybe you could try it. I know it’s not the most glamorous, but it’s a good way to earn some money. I’m not sure if I’m ready for that yet. I mean, I like the idea of working with people, but the hours… and the stress. I think I’d like something more flexible. Maybe something that’s not as physically demanding? Yeah, I get that. It depends on what you’re looking for. If you want to save money and get some experience, maybe something like retail or food service?

So, do you lot ever take holidays? I feel like I’ve been working solid for months, and I’m just about to go on a long weekend to the seaside. Oh, you’re lucky, mate. I’ve been stuck in the office since the start of the year. My manager’s on a permanent holidays, and now it’s like I’m the only one left. Aye, I know the feeling. I’m just going to take a drive up to the Lake District. I haven’t been there in years, and the weather’s been so good lately. Yeah, I hear you. I’ve been meaning to do that too. I’ve got this little cabin in Keswick, but I haven’t managed to get the time off. I remember when I used to go there with my family. It was always so peaceful. I’m glad I had those holidays. Speaking of peace, I heard that the library’s getting a new wing built. I think it’s going to be a proper holiday for the staff. Maybe we can all take a break for a week and have a proper weekend. That would be nice. I’d like that. Maybe I’ll ask my boss. Yeah, I’ll put in a request. I’m tired of the same old routine. I’d like that too. I’d love to have a proper break. You know, I was thinking, maybe we could all meet up for a little holiday together. We could take turns looking after each other’s kids or something. That sounds like a plan. I’d like that. Yeah, I’m in. I’ve been wanting to get out of this office for a while. I’ll let you know what I think, but I’d love to have some time off. It’s been ages since I’ve had a proper holiday. Exactly. It’s important to take time for yourself.

I can't believe the amount of money we're spending on this season’s football tickets. It’s like we’re paying for the seats, not even the match. Yeah, I know. I think it’s just the way the clubs are now. They’ve turned into businesses. You can’t even get a ticket if you’re not a season ticket holder. It’s ridiculous. I mean, I’ve got a season ticket for the local team, but honestly, I only go once a month. The rest of the time, I just watch it on TV. It’s cheaper, and I don’t have to deal with the crowds or the parking. That’s probably the smarter way to go. But I do love the atmosphere when you’re at the stadium. There’s something about the chants, the players on the pitch, the roar of the crowd. It’s like a different world. I can see that. I mean, I did go to a game last week, and it was amazing. The team’s doing really well this season. I think they’ve got a real chance to make it to the Champions League. Oh, really? That’s great news. I’ve been following them a bit, but I didn’t know they were doing so well. I guess the new manager’s been doing a good job. Yeah, he’s a real tactical genius. I mean, the way he’s managed the team’s defense has been incredible. They’re not just winning because of luck anymore. That’s true. But I still think the prices are ridiculous. I mean, the tickets for the games against the top teams cost more than a whole meal at a decent restaurant. I’m not even sure I can afford it. I know, I’ve been trying to budget for it. I’ve even started cooking more at home to save money. It’s not like I’m eating out every day. Although, I did get a takeout the other day. It was really good. Oh, you’re doing the takeaway thing now? I’ve been meaning to try out that new Indian place down the road. They said the chicken curry is amazing. I think it’s a bit of a risk, but I need to try it. I’ll come with you. I think I’ve had enough of fast food.

So, do you remember that old film we watched last summer, Grandma? The one with the mad inventor and the secret lab? Oh yes, I remember that! It was such a strange movie, wasn’t it? I can still picture the guy in the lab with all those crazy contraptions. I think he was trying to build a time machine or something. Yeah, that’s what I thought. It was like one of those old sci-fi classics. But you know what was funny? When the inventor finally got his time machine working, he just wanted to go back and see his wife again. That part really tugged at the heartstrings. I remember that. It made me think of the old tales my dad used to tell us about inventors and their dreams. He always said that the best ideas come from the most unusual places. That’s true. I think it’s the same with cooking, isn’t it? Sometimes the simplest ingredients can make the most extraordinary dishes. Just like that film, it’s about how the heart of the matter is what really matters. Exactly. And I’ve been thinking about that lately. I’ve been trying to get back into cooking more, especially since I’ve been working so much. Maybe I should start with something simple, like a good old bisto gravy or something. It’s comforting, and it gets the job done. Oh, I know what you mean. When I was younger, I used to make all sorts of things. But work got in the way, and then life just sort of took over. Still, I miss it. There’s something about putting a meal on the table that brings people together, doesn’t it? Absolutely. And the thing is, it’s not just about cooking. It’s about the stories that go with it. I remember when I was a kid, my mum used to cook these amazing pies, and every time she made one, she’d tell me a story about how she used to make them for her own family. It felt like passing on something special. That’s beautiful. It’s like passing down a legacy. I’ve been thinking about starting a blog about work and life balance, something that combines my job with the things I really care about. I think it could help other people who feel overwhelmed.

Alright, do you two want some pancakes? It's Pancake Day today! Yes, please! I’m starving. Me too! I’ve been waiting all morning for this. Great. I’ve got the batter ready. Just need to heat up the pan. Wait, does that mean you’re not eating any? I thought you were making them for everyone. Oh, I’m making them for everyone. I’m just not eating any because I’ve already had breakfast. I’m saving them for later when we’ve all had a proper meal. But you  promised  we’d have pancakes today, Mummy. You said you’d have one too. I know, I know. I’m just being responsible. I don’t want to feel sick after the Science Museum trip tomorrow. But what about breakfast, Mummy? I didn’t eat my cereal. I know, I know. You didn’t even finish your toast. Are you sure you’re not still hungry? I am! I want to go to the beach with you both tomorrow. Can we? We’ll see. First, we need to make sure you’ve got your shoes on and your lunch packed. And I need to check if we’ve got enough money for the train tickets. Can we have a picnic at the beach? That’s a great idea. I’ll bring a blanket and some sandwiches. But first, let’s eat our pancakes. You’re still not eating yours, are you? No, I’m waiting for you to start. I don’t want to eat before you do. Oh, you’re so sweet. Alright, here you go. Let’s make a start. Mummy, can we read a story before we eat? I want to hear about Green Knowe again. Sure, but only if you finish your pancake first. You need to eat properly before you start reading. I’m not finished with mine either. I’m waiting for you. Alright, let’s all take a bite. Then we can read the story and plan the beach trip. Can we go to Paris too? I want to see the Eiffel Tower! Paris is a big trip, though. Maybe we can think about that after the beach. For now, let’s focus on today’s plans. Okay, but I want to learn about the Festival Hall too. I heard there are amazing shows there. That’s a great idea. Maybe we can look up some events when we get back from the beach.

So, do you think we should order more food? I’m not sure we’ve got enough for everyone. I’m not sure either. We’ve already got a few left, but I feel like we might need more. Honestly, I think we’re fine. I’m not that hungry anyway, and we’ve got the leftovers from last night. Yeah, I’ve got a full stomach from the last time we ordered. But if you’re not sure, maybe just get a small extra order to be safe. Okay, I’ll do that. I’ll call the restaurant and see what they have left. Wait, do you want to split the order? I mean, if we’re having more, maybe we should share the cost. I think that’s a good idea. I’m not sure how much we’ve already paid, but if we split it, it’ll be easier. Yeah, that sounds fair. I’ll help you check the total. Thanks. I don’t know what I’d do without you guys. Sometimes I think I’ve got this all figured out, but then I realize I’m not even close. You’re not the only one. I’m always messing up with the orders. Last time, I ordered the wrong thing and had to go back and explain it. And I’m the one who forgot to put the order in on time. I was trying to finish a report and thought I had enough time. It’s all part of being in a shared house, I guess. You’re always relying on each other. Exactly. And that’s why I think we should take this opportunity to make plans for the weekend. I’ve been thinking about going to the cricket match. Oh, really? Are you going to be there? I might have to go too. I was thinking about it last night. I don’t know. I’ve got some things to do. But if you two are going, I might join you. That sounds like a good idea. We could all go together. It’ll be fun. Plus, it’s a chance to get out of the house and do something different. That might be a good plan. I’ll check the ticket prices and let you know. Great. And maybe we could all go to a movie on Saturday night as well? That sounds like a fun way to end the week.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to play that game where you had to guess which family member had the most peculiar habit? Oh, I remember that! It was a madhouse. I think we even had a whole list of things — like Auntie Muriel always tried to use the passive voice in every conversation, and Uncle Frank had this obsession with collecting spoons. I think he actually had a full set of every spoon in the village. It was like a weird museum in his kitchen. Yeah, and the worst was when he tried to explain it to us. He said it was a "collective memory of the nation’s cutlery." My father just rolled his eyes and said, "Frank, you’re just a spoon hoarder." That’s the thing about families, isn’t it? You’re always remembering these little quirks. I swear, some of these stories are more interesting than the actual events. Definitely. I think the best one was about Mrs. Carter from next door. She used to say that she was the last person in the village who still used a rotary phone. And she did, for years! I mean, when we got mobile phones, she just scoffed and said, “I like the sound of a dial tone.” I remember her taking it out for a walk every Friday night. She’d walk around the village with this old thing, and people would just smile and say, “Glad to see you’re still with us, Mrs. Carter.” Anyway, I think she had a point. Some of these old habits are actually comforting. I mean, I can’t imagine living without a rotary phone. I’d be lost! I think the real question is, do we still have those habits? I mean, I still use the same method for making tea — pour the water first, then the tea. It’s like an automatic reflex. I’m not sure if that’s a habit or just stubbornness. Either way, it’s a little weird. Yeah, but you know, I think it’s these little oddities that make family so interesting. They’re like little stories that we carry around, even when the people are gone. I couldn’t agree more. It’s like we all have these tiny lives, and when we’re older, we start to really appreciate them. Especially when you’re over 50 and you realize that the only thing that really matters is the little things — the quirks, the habits, the stories.

Alright, do you two want to help me make dumplings for Chinese New Year? I’ve got the dough and the fillings ready, but I could really do with some extra hands. Dumplings? You mean the ones we had last year? With the weird green stuff inside? Yes, the ones with the pork and cabbage. It’s traditional, and it’s actually really good if you do it right. I think I’ve got the recipe from my aunt in Shanghai. Can I have one of those green ones? I like the surprise when you bite into them. You’ll get your surprise soon enough. First, let’s roll out the dough. You know, like folding the paper, but with flour. Oh, like making paper airplanes? But with dough? No, no, no. It’s like folding a dumpling into a little boat. You press the dough down, put the filling in, and then fold the edges over. It’s not as hard as it sounds. Can I help with the filling? I like mixing things. Like, I have this obsession with mixing colors. It’s like art, but with food. That’s a good point. Maybe we can make some dragon-shaped dumplings? Wait, dragon-shaped? I’ve also been thinking about making some Chinese zongzi, the rice cakes with leaves. They’re tricky, but fun. Maybe we can do that after the dumplings. Are we making everything ourselves? What about the soup? I think there’s a soup called hot and sour. Is that one of them? Yes! And I’ve been meaning to try making the chicken and mushroom soup. It’s really good with the dumplings. Can I have a little pond in the kitchen for the fish? I think I saw a video of someone making a fish-shaped dumpling, and it looked like a pond with fish in it. That’s a great idea. We can make a whole scene with dragons, fish, and maybe even a little boat.

So, do you think we should go to that new pizzeria near the Colosseum? I heard it’s supposed to be really good. Honestly, I’m not sure. I’ve had a few meals in Rome already, and I’ve been trying to keep my waistline in check. But if it’s worth the splurge, I guess I could go. I’ve been there! It’s called  La Luna Pizzeria . Oh, and the owner is a bit of a character—she’s from the south, and she insists on using  mozzarella di bufala  every time. That sounds like my kind of place. I’ve been trying to get out of the hotel for days. The room is nice, but I’m starting to miss the café in Sydney, even if I’m just sipping a flat white in a Tuscan café. I know what you mean. I’ve been in Rome for a week, and I’m starting to feel like I’ve seen the same view from the same café every day. I swear, the only thing that changes is the coffee I’m drinking. You’re not wrong. I still haven’t got used to how the locals speak. I keep getting confused between the English accent and the Italian ones. I think I might have accidentally said  “ciao”  instead of  “arrivederci”  the other day. Oh, I’ve heard that. I laughed so hard when I first moved to London and said  “biscuit”  instead of  “biscotti” . But seriously, the Italian language is so beautiful, even if it’s a bit confusing. Yeah, the accents are crazy too. I can tell where someone’s from just by the way they say  “ciao”  or  “grazie” . I’ve been trying to pick up some basic phrases, but I think I’ve got a bit of a British twist on it. I think your accent is adorable. Like, I can’t help but smile when you say  “ciao”  with that Australian twang. You’re too kind. I think it’s because I work in a café, so I’ve had to practice my Italian with the customers. That’s a good point. I’ve been trying to make myself understand the locals better too. I think it’s important to mix in with the people and not just stick to the tourist areas. Exactly. I’ve been hanging out in the Trastevere area, and it’s a completely different vibe.

So, do you think we should go through with the hen do at the farm? I mean, it’s supposed to be a fun day out with all the girls, but I’m a bit nervous about the catering. I’ll do the decorations. I’ve got some glitter and colored paper that I can bring. And I can help with the flower arranging too. Do you think we could set up a little display in the barn? It would look really cute. That would be perfect. I think the whole idea of the hen do is about creating memories and having a good time with our friends. The food is just part of it, right? Exactly. And if we’re all in on making it happen, we can make sure it’s something everyone will remember.

So, do you reckon I should go to London next week? I’ve got this friend who’s staying there and I’ve been meaning to visit them for ages. London? You serious? That’s a long trip. Not to mention the cost. You’ve got to think about the money, mate. I know, but I’ve got some savings tucked away. Plus, I heard the weather’s supposed to be good. And I’ve got a few days off work. I just got a new list of things to buy for the house. I need to remember to get some string and... oh, and some paint. You know, for the art projects we’re planning to do with the kids. Yes, the art and craft things. I remember when I was in primary school, we made those paper snowflakes and painted them with glitter. My teacher said it was a masterpiece. Oh, I bet she said that about every project. I remember one time, we made those cardboard volcanoes and painted them red. Didn’t even need to use real lava. That’s right! And we had to write a short report on what happens when a volcano erupts. My report was full of mistakes, but my teacher thought it was brilliant. I still have the paper in a box somewhere. You know, I used to hate those things. I’d rather have been playing hockey. I still have those old hockey boots tucked away in the bottom of my wardrobe. They’re not even fit to wear anymore. I remember you used to be the best player on the team. You always scored the most goals. I did, didn’t I? Although I did have a bit of a problem with the ball sometimes. Once, I tried to kick it into the net, and it went flying straight into the back of a bus. It took them ages to retrieve it. Oh, I remember that! We all laughed about it for weeks. But I’m glad you didn’t get hurt. Yeah, I was lucky. I think the bus driver thought it was funny too. Anyway, enough about the past. What about the university courses? I hear you’re thinking of studying sound recording again? Yes, I thought about it. I’ve always loved the way sound works, how it can transport you to different places. Maybe it’s time to get back into it. That’s a good idea. I think it would be nice to have you around when we’re doing all the technical stuff at the museum. They’ve been talking about passing some old computer equipment to the museum—like the first ones they had when you were teaching. That’s true. I go there every week to help out. It’s a real passion of mine. I love the history of computing. I remember when we had to use punch cards and everything was so slow.

So, how’s the new place, mate? It’s alright, I suppose. It’s got its charms, but I’m still getting used to it. The gardens are a bit of a mess, though. Not sure if I’ve got the green thumb. You’ll get it. I’ve been telling you, you just have to be patient. I’ve got a friend who moved to Holsworthy last year and now she’s got a whole patch of lavender blooming in her backyard. Yeah, and that’s not even the worst of it. You’ve got the local pub right around the corner, so I reckon you’ll be out there before you’ve even managed to get the shrubs sorted. I know, and I’m not even sure what the pub’s like. I’ve heard the locals are friendly, but I’m still nervous about meeting new people. Well, you can’t be scared of that, can you? You’ve got to step out of your comfort zone. And besides, the walking group meets every Tuesday, so maybe that’s a good start. Yeah, the walking group. I thought you were still in the process of watching the local news. I saw a story about them last week—they’ve been doing some new trails along the river. Oh, that sounds perfect. I did try to go out for a run the other day, but I ended up just sitting in the garden with a cup of tea. It’s all good. I remember when I first moved to the area, I used to be scared of going out. I used to spend all my time in the house, reading. Oh, you’re still reading, aren’t you? I thought you were getting into more of the local stuff. I am, actually. I’ve been reading about the history of the area. There’s a lot to learn here—loads of stories about the old railway lines and the way people used to live. That sounds fascinating. I’ve been meaning to do that. I’ve got a book about the local train lines in my bag, but I’ve been too busy with the job to get into it. How’s the job going, by the way? It’s good, honestly. A bit of a change from what I was doing before, but I like it. The kids are great, and I even got to go to a training course in Exeter last month.

So, do you ever just get fed up with online shopping? Like, I mean, it’s so easy, right? Just click, wait, and then it arrives at your door. But sometimes I think it's like, why do we even need to buy things in the first place? Honestly, I don’t know. I mean, I’ve got this theory that people just shop all the time because they’re bored. Like, if you’re not doing anything, you just log on and buy something. It’s like a way to feel like you’re doing something. Yeah, I get that. I mean, I’m unemployed, so I don’t really have the money, but even when I did have a job, I’d just log on after work and buy a new gadget or some dumb little thing. Easier than going out and actually doing something, right? And you don’t even have to leave the house. I mean, I bought this whole new wardrobe last week using my student discount. I didn’t even have to get up. I just sat on the bed and waved a credit card. I tried that once. Felt like I was still working, but actually, I just ended up with a bunch of stuff I didn’t need. And now I have to deal with all the packaging and the boxes, and I barely have room to move. It’s so much easier to just use the delivery. I mean, I’ve been told that the supermarkets are starting to offer same-day deliveries. I think it’s a bit of a trend. People don’t want to leave the house. Or maybe they don’t want to see the prices in the shop, because it makes them sad. Oh, I know. I mean, I used to work in retail, and I can tell you that the prices in the shop are always better than online. But I think people are just so used to buying things online that they don’t even think about it. Yeah, and it’s not just shopping. I mean, I think people are just used to getting everything delivered. Even food. I mean, I’ve got a friend who gets his groceries delivered every week. He says it’s a lifesaver. That’s probably why I’m so lazy. I mean, I could go to the shop, but I just don’t wanna.

So, do you think we should get a new cooker, Annie? This one’s been in the house since we moved in and it’s starting to look a bit run down. I mean, it’s still working, but it’s not exactly reliable anymore. Yeah, I can see what you mean. I’ve noticed it’s taking longer to heat up the water and the oven seems to be getting a bit sluggish. But I also know how much money that kind of thing can cost. Maybe we should wait until we’ve got a bit more saved up? I think it’s time. You know how these things go — they just keep going until they break, and then you’re left with a mess. I had that with my old fridge. It was still working, but one day it just stopped, and I had to replace it all. I think it’s better to spend a little now and avoid a bigger problem later. That does make sense. I was thinking about it the other day. I remember we talked about ordering a new one from the showroom in Exeter. The man there said they had some really nice models that are energy-efficient. I think we could afford one if we’re careful with the budget. Yeah, and I’ve got this idea about getting some new furniture too. The living room is looking a bit tired, and it would be good to spruce it up a bit before the winter comes. Maybe we could tackle that together? That’s a great idea. I’ve been thinking about the same thing. I reckon we could look at some second-hand shops in Exeter too. There are a few places that sell quality stuff at a fraction of the price. We could save a bit of money while still getting something decent. I like that. I’ve been meaning to start going to that store near the train station. They’ve got some really nice pieces, and the owner’s always been friendly. Maybe we could go this weekend and have a look around? That sounds perfect. I’ll call you both when I’ve got some time to clear my schedule. Also, I was thinking about the coastal walk we were talking about earlier. I’ve checked the tide times, and it looks like it’s going to be a good day for it.

So, do you ever find it weird, like, how time just… slips by? I feel like I was just in the lab yesterday, and now I’m here, having dinner with you, and it’s already been weeks. I know, it’s such a strange thing. I was in meetings all week and now I’m just… here, with you. It feels like I’ve been on a never-ending treadmill of assessments, reports, and deadlines. Oh, I hear you. I think it’s just the grinding pace of life. You know, when you get into a job like mine, everything seems so focused. You’re always thinking about experiments, data, publication timelines. There’s no time to stop and think about anything else. Yeah, I suppose that’s the thing about working in education too. You’re always thinking about how to make assessments better, how to support students better, how to measure progress. It’s a continuous loop. And yet, when we step back, you know, it’s the small moments that matter, right? Like this dinner, just talking, being in the same place, not thinking about anything except the conversation. Exactly. I think we’ve both been so focused on our work lately that we’ve kind of forgotten how much we enjoy just being together. I mean, I know we both have huge responsibilities, but sometimes it’s the little things—like sitting here, eating, and talking—that make life feel real. I think it’s also the contrast. You know, when you’re in the lab or out in the schools, it’s all about structure and being professional. But at home, it’s so different. You’re not expected to be perfect, you’re just being yourself. Yeah, and I think that’s part of what keeps us grounded. It’s not just about work—it’s about family, it’s about being there for each other. I mean, even though we have our own careers, we still have this connection that goes beyond it. I couldn’t agree more. I think we both have to remind ourselves of that. Between lunches, meetings, and deadlines, it’s easy to forget that there’s more to life than just work. Exactly. So, I think it’s important to make time for these little talks, even if it’s just between meals. You know, it’s the kind of conversation that you don’t have in the office or on the phone.

So, do you remember when we were kids and we used to have that old cat, Fido? He was a real troublemaker, always knocking things over. Oh, I remember! He used to chase the dog and get stuck in the garden gate. It took ages to get him out. You were so obsessed with him, weren’t you? Yeah, I used to think he was the best cat in the world. He’d sit on my shoulders and watch me write. It was like he was my personal assistant. Funny you mention that, I still have a cat now. His name is Oliver. He’s a bit of a loner but he’s always got that look like he’s judging you when you’re on your phone. I’ve never had a cat. I’ve had a dog though. A golden retriever. But I was always left-handed, so it was hard to train him. He used to pull the leash in the wrong direction, like he was trying to fight me. Left-handed? That’s interesting. I was left-handed too, but my parents made me use my right hand. It was a real struggle. Did you ever have to deal with that? My parents were okay with it. I think they just thought it was weird but didn’t mind. I actually kind of liked being left-handed. It felt natural. I did have to be careful with the toaster though, because I kept burning the toast. Oh, I remember that. My sister was left-handed too, and we had a similar problem. We’d always have to switch sides when we were cooking. It was a bit of a hassle. I was always told I was left-handed, but I never really noticed. I just used what felt comfortable. I think that’s the key. If it feels natural, why force it? I think it’s more about how you’re raised. My mum always told me to use my right hand, so I did. I tried to change, but I always felt awkward. It’s funny how something so small can affect your whole life. It’s amazing how left-handedness is still considered unusual. I think it’s changing, though. More people are accepting it now. But it’s still a bit of a joke in some circles. I don’t mind the jokes. I think it’s part of being different.

So, do you know what’s the best thing to do when you’re stuck in a car with a granddad who’s on a diet? Oh, I know exactly. You just gotta make sure he doesn’t eat the cheese. That’s the first rule. Yeah, I tried that once, but he still managed to sneak a bit of it. He said it was for his arteries. That’s what they all say. But you know what I think? I think he just likes the taste. Maybe he’s just trying to avoid the guilt. You know, if you eat cheese, you feel worse about the rest of the meal. That’s a bit cynical, isn’t it? No, I think it’s pretty realistic. I mean, I’ve seen it with my own eyes. My cousin once had breakfast with his nan, and he ate half a portion of eggs, then ordered a second portion of toast and marmalade. That’s not even close to guilt. That’s just being greedy. Anyway, what about you, Granddad? You ever go on a diet? Oh, I tried when I was younger. I thought if I lost a few pounds, I could actually walk up the stairs without stopping. But no, I just got more tired and started eating more. That sounds like the classic case of someone who thinks they're on a diet but ends up eating more because they’re so focused on what they’re not eating. Exactly! I mean, I’ve heard people say they’re on a diet, but then they’ll have a big meal and feel guilty afterwards. It’s like a cycle. I know what you mean. And the worst part is that you just end up overeating because you’re constantly thinking about it. It’s like the mind is always on the diet, so it’s harder to enjoy your food properly. Yeah, and then you end up not enjoying the food at all. So what’s the point? I think the point is to just eat the food you enjoy, in moderation. But I think that’s something most people don’t really understand. It’s a bit of an art, isn’t it? Balancing what you eat with how much you eat and how you feel about it. True. I mean, I’ve been trying to eat more food that I like, rather than just cutting back.

So, do you think we should go to the market tomorrow? I mean, it's our first day in China, and I feel like we should try to get some local ingredients for the class. Yeah, that makes sense. I’ve read a bit about the local markets here—there’s a huge one in the city, right? It’s called the   Wangfujing   market. I think it’s a great place to find fresh produce and maybe even some street food. Oh, that sounds interesting. I was worried maybe the food here wouldn’t be as varied as in the UK, but if we can get some local stuff, it’ll make our classes more authentic. Exactly. My colleague mentioned that the market is a bit overwhelming at first, but once you get the hang of it, it's actually quite fun. They have everything from fruits and vegetables to dried goods and spices. I think we should go early in the morning when it's less crowded. Good plan. I can’t wait to see what kinds of things they have. I’ve heard that the tea here is amazing, and I want to try it in the class. I know! They have all sorts of teas—green, black, herbal, even some rare varieties. I think we can find something for everyone. Oh, and maybe we can get some dumplings or something like that too. That’s a great idea. The students will love the hands-on experience. They can make dumplings or learn how to stir-fry. It’ll be a fun way to connect with the culture. I agree. The classes are going to be a mix of theory and practice, and I think this kind of hands-on activity will really help them understand the material better. Yeah, it’s not just about the food—it’s about the experience. I think the students will appreciate the effort we’re putting in to make it feel real. Exactly. And I was thinking, maybe we could also show some local TV or videos that highlight the food culture here. It’ll give them a visual context. That sounds like a good plan. I can look up some clips or even find a documentary about Chinese cooking. It’ll add another layer to the lesson. Perfect. I think we’re off to a great start. It’s amazing how quickly we’re getting into the rhythm of things.

I just thought I'd mention the coffee machine. I mean, do we really need it? I've been thinking... we could save some money by just buying proper coffee instead of wasting all that electricity on this thing. Oh, I know, I've been thinking the same. But it's so convenient, you know. You just pop a pod in and it's ready in minutes. It’s not like we're making coffee from scratch every day. Yeah, but it’s not like we’re using it that much. It’s just sitting there, taking up space, and costing us a fortune in electricity. I mean, even if we only use it a couple of times a week, that’s still a lot of money over a year. Exactly. And what about the removal costs? I was just thinking, if we were to move somewhere else, we’d have to get rid of it somehow. I don’t know if we’d even be able to sell it or give it away. It’s not like it’s in good working order anymore. I know, I’ve been trying to get rid of it too. I’ve put it on eBay a couple of times, but no one seems interested. Maybe it’s just too old, or maybe it’s not the right model. I mean, it’s been in the house since we were married, so it’s got sentimental value, but I’m not sure how much that’s worth. I get that, but I think we all have to be practical about this. We’re not in the best financial position right now. Every penny counts, and if we can cut down on unnecessary expenses, that’s a start. I agree, but I’m also thinking about the bigger picture. I mean, we’re all feeling a bit lost these days, aren’t we? I mean, it’s not just the money; it’s the uncertainty. I keep reading about the Labour leadership and all that. They’re talking about a lot of changes, but I don’t know if it’s going to make things better for people like us. Yeah, I’ve been reading about it too. I think there’s a lot of idealism going on, but I’m not sure if it’s realistic. They’re talking about fairer taxes and more support for working families, but I don’t know if the government is really going to do that.

So, do you know what’s the deal with these pseudonyms? I mean, it’s like they’re trying to be mysterious or something. I think it’s just for fun, you know? Like, they don’t want to give out their real names for some reason. Maybe they’re writing a story or something? Or maybe they’re trying to keep their identities private? I mean, I’ve heard of people doing that online. Yeah, but I still think it’s a bit strange. I mean, when you’re in a group like this, you’d think you’d just go with your real names. Unless you’re hiding something. Or maybe they’re just being quirky. I mean, I got called "Bruno" earlier, and I didn’t even know why. I think it’s just a joke. Oh, I get it—some of them are just nicknames or things they like. Like, I think one person went by "Jelly" because they love jelly. Oh yeah, that’s right! And then there was the one who went by "Parsley" because they’re into cooking. It’s kind of cute, honestly. Yeah, but it’s still weird. I mean, I’m not sure I’d want to be called “Parsley.” It’s not exactly a strong name. Well, it’s not like you’re going to be called that for long. I mean, once the holiday is over, you can just go back to your real name. Exactly. And I think it’s a good way to break the ice. Like, you don’t have to worry about the usual names people use. It’s like you’re all part of this little group. Yeah, but I do wonder, like, do they ever go back to their real names? Or do they just stick with the pseudonyms for life? That would be weird. I mean, I’d be “Bruno” forever. Oh, you’d be “Bruno” forever? What’s the point of calling yourself something else if you’re gonna stick with it? Maybe if you like it. Yeah, but I don’t like it. I’d rather be “Mark.” Well, I think it’s safe to say we’ll all be going back to our real names once we’re done with this trip. But for now, we’re all just enjoying the fun. Yeah, and I think it’s fun.

So, do you think Tinder’s actually useful anymore? I mean, I’ve been swiping for like, what, three months now, and I’ve only had one proper conversation. Honestly, I think it’s mostly just a way to waste time. You end up spending more time on the app than actually talking to people in real life. Plus, half the profiles are just people looking for attention. I know, right? I tried using it a few times, but I just ended up feeling like I was being judged based on how many likes I got. It’s so weird how people think you have to have a perfect profile to be liked. Yeah, and then when you do get a match, you’re like, “Oh, cool, someone’s interested,” but then they never actually message you back. It’s like, why even bother? I’ve been trying to meet people through uni events instead. It’s more awkward, but at least you’re not being judged by a bunch of algorithms. Plus, you can actually talk to people and see if there’s a real connection. That sounds better. I’m just so tired of swiping and never getting anywhere. I mean, I’ve got a few matches, but it’s all just like “Hey, what’s your name?” and then nothing. I think the problem is that everyone’s so busy with uni and work that they don’t have time to actually build relationships. It’s all about quick hook-ups now. That’s what I’ve noticed too. I mean, everyone’s like, “Oh, I’m dating someone,” but they’re still hanging out with their housemates and not really talking to their partner. It’s so sad. I had a guy I met through Tinder once. We talked for like an hour, and it was actually decent. But then he just disappeared. I mean, he was even in my area, so that’s just weird. I’ve been thinking about talking to someone from my uni course. I don’t know, maybe it’s easier to meet people that way. You’re already in a shared space, so you have common ground. That does make sense. But I’m still not sure. I mean, I’ve had a few housemates before, and it’s just so hard to find someone you actually get along with. Yeah, and then there’s the whole issue of cleaning and money.

I don’t know, I just feel like the whole benefits system is a bit of a farce. You get money for nothing, and sometimes you don’t even know why you’re getting it. Yeah, I agree with you. It’s like they don’t even care if you’re actually in need or not. I met a bloke the other day who said he was getting benefits because his cat died. That’s not right, is it? Oh, I heard about that. It’s like the government just wants to make sure people are always looking for a reason to claim. You know what I mean? It’s not about helping, it’s about keeping people on the dole. Exactly. And then you get these new rules and forms that are impossible to fill in. I tried applying for some extra support last year, and I couldn’t even understand half the questions. It’s like they’re trying to trip you up. I remember when I was still working, I used to think the benefits were for people who really needed it. But now, I don’t know. I’ve seen too many people just take it without even trying to work. It’s not fair on the ones who are genuinely struggling. I think it’s all about the government trying to keep the population down. If you’re not working, you’re not contributing, and they don’t want you to be too comfortable. It’s a way to control people, really. I’ve heard that before. But I also think there are people who really do need it. I mean, you can’t just pretend that everyone wants to work. Some people are sick, some are disabled, some have family issues. It’s not always about motivation. That’s true. But they don’t seem to make that distinction. They just give the same amount to everyone, regardless of their situation. It’s like they don’t care about the real reasons people are on benefits. I think the real problem is that the system is broken. Everyone’s waiting for someone else to fix it, but no one’s taking responsibility. The politicians are just playing politics with the numbers, and the public is left with no choice but to suffer. I sometimes think the only way to really get something done is to vote for someone who actually cares about the country.

So, did you get that meeting done today? Ugh, it was a nightmare. I got there early, but the guy I was supposed to meet with had a meeting himself. Then he called me back three times to ask if I was still coming. I thought, "Deer in headlights," you know? Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s like you’re waiting for someone who’s never going to show up. But at least you got to go through the motions, right? Well, I did. But it was all for nothing. I had a whole presentation ready. I mean, I even brought my own coffee because I thought, "Maybe he’s going to be on time." Oh, you brought your own coffee? That’s a risk. You could’ve been sitting there for hours with a cup of coffee that’s gone cold. I know, I know. I’m just so tired of this. I keep thinking, "This is it. This is the one time I’m going to get things done," and then it turns into a farce. I’ve been there. It’s like work has become this never-ending game of chess, and I’m always moving pieces only to find out the board’s been rearranged. Exactly! And I’ve got two kids to take to school tomorrow. I can’t even think about that. I’m just so drained. I get it. I had a meeting earlier today too. I had a ton of emails to reply to, and then I got stuck in traffic. I thought I’d be home by now, but I’m still at the office. That’s the thing, isn’t it? You’re always at work, even when you’re not. You’re sending emails, replying to messages, planning for the next thing. It’s like you never actually get to stop. Yeah, and it’s not even the same as when we were younger. We used to have time to actually do things. Now it’s all about keeping up with the grind. I miss that. I miss the days when I could sit down with a glass of wine and watch some trash TV without feeling guilty about it. Oh, I know. I tried to do that last night. I told myself, "I’m going to watch a few episodes of  Friends  and that’s it." But then I got to the third episode

I just can’t believe how cold it’s been here in Tarnow. It’s like we’ve been living in a freezer all week. I’ve been shivering just getting out of bed this morning. Yeah, honestly, I’ve never felt so cold in my life. I was in Manchester last week and it was barely below freezing, but this is something else. I’m starting to miss the wet and windy weather from England. I know, I miss that too. It’s like it’s not even the same country. I keep looking at the photos of the UK on my phone and thinking, “Oh, I used to live there.” It’s weird, isn’t it? It really is. I feel like I left England a few years ago, but now I’m here, and I’m thinking about how different everything feels. It’s funny, isn’t it? You get used to a place and then you go back, and it’s like a whole different world. I know. I was thinking about that the other day—about going back to Cambridge for the funeral of my aunt. I mean, it’s not that I don’t like Poland, but it feels like there’s something missing. Like, I don’t belong here. I understand. I’m not sure I would ever really feel like I belong in Poland. I don’t know if it’s the culture or the language, but there’s something about being in the UK that just feels like home to me. It’s strange, because I’m working here as a TEFL teacher, and I love being able to help people learn English. But when I see photos of my friends from back home, all of us laughing in the sun, I just feel… lost. I can relate. I’m still teaching English as a foreign language, but I’ve realized I don’t really enjoy it anymore. I used to love it, but now it feels like a job I just do to get by. I’m starting to think about doing something else, even if it means going back to the UK. That’s a big decision. I mean, I’ve been here for a year now, and I’ve met so many people. But I think it’s more about the sense of belonging than anything else. I don’t know if I could go back, but I’d like to try.

So, do you know what’s the deal with the tea in this pub? It’s like it’s been brewed for ages and it’s still not hot enough. I know, right? I’ve been sipping it like it’s the last cup of tea on Earth. But it’s actually pretty good, if you like it weak and with a lot of milk. Yeah, I mean, I love tea but I think this place has a funny way of making it. It’s not like the tea in my flat, which is always piping hot and properly brewed. I know, I’ve been trying to convince my flatmates to try this place, but they’re all like, “No, no, no, you can’t just go to a pub for tea.” I get that, but it’s such a cozy place. And the atmosphere is amazing. You know, it feels like you’re in some kind of old-timey British pub, even though it’s in London. Yeah, I like that. It’s got that kind of character. Plus, the staff are really friendly. I’ve been here a few times and they always remember my order. That’s nice. I’m lucky if the barista remembers my name at the café I go to, let alone my order. I know, right? It’s so different from the usual chain places. You almost feel like you’re in a different world here. Exactly. And the food here is good too. I had this really good fish and chips the last time I came. It was so much better than the takeaway I usually get. Yeah, I had the same. Although, I had to wait a bit for it. The portion was huge, though. I couldn’t finish it. I tried to, but I got distracted by the conversation with my friend and I ended up eating it in two sittings. That’s the thing with London, isn’t it? You’re always rushing. But places like this make you slow down a little. Yeah, I think you’re right. I’ve been feeling a bit stressed lately with work and everything, so it’s nice to come here and just have a quiet cup of tea and enjoy the moment. I agree. It’s good to take a break, even if it’s just for an hour. And with the weather getting colder, I think we’ll be coming here more often.

Alright, do you two want breakfast? I'm not hungry. I'm not hungry either. Well, I thought we could all have some toast and juice. But I had a lie-in, so I'm not really hungry. Yeah, I was up really late watching the moon. It was so bright. Oh, the Neon Moon event, right? Yeah, it was amazing! It lit up the whole garden. I thought it was a spaceship! No, it was just the moon. But it was so bright, it made everything look like it was glowing. It was like a disco ball in the sky! Can we do that again? Well, it only happens once a year, I think. So, do you know, I was just thinking about how politics has changed over the years, especially since I first started working in publishing. It’s almost like the more things change, the more they stay the same, but in a different way. I agree. I remember when I was a student, there was a lot of talk about the future of the Labour Party and how they were going to reshape the country. Now, it feels like we’re stuck in a cycle of political gridlock, with no real progress being made. It’s frustrating, to be honest. Yeah, I mean, I can’t even remember the last time there was a real breakthrough in politics. It’s all about short-term gains and social media influencers rather than actual policy. I feel like the older generations just don’t get it anymore. That’s not entirely true, though. I think there’s still a strong undercurrent of public opinion that wants real change. It’s just that the political system isn’t set up to respond to that, or at least not in a way that people would expect. I mean, do you remember when we used to listen to the radio for news, and it felt like you were part of a community? Now, it’s all divided along political lines, and it feels like we’re just shouting at each other. Exactly. And it’s not just the media—it’s the way people are raised now. My parents were part of the ‘60s generation, and they believed in collective action and working together for the greater good. But now, it feels like people are more individualistic, more focused on their own interests and less on communal goals. Which is a shame because I think about how important community was back in the day. I mean, I’m from Aberystwyth, and even now, there are still some strong local traditions and a sense of togetherness, even if it’s not always shown in politics. I feel like that’s something we’re losing. I can see that. I grew up in London, and while it’s a city that moves fast, there’s a lot of diversity and people from all walks of life. But I do miss the sense of community that used to come with it. I think the key is to find a balance between individual freedom and collective responsibility.

Alright, so I was thinking, what if we make the next story about a little girl who finds a magical book in the woods? It could be something like the Linton Book Festival kind of vibe, where the story comes to life. That sounds fun! But what happens when she opens the book? Does it take her to another world? Maybe she needs to find a special object to save her village or something? Or maybe the book is enchanted, and if she doesn’t finish it, it disappears? That could work. It adds some mystery. What if the girl gets lost in the woods and the cat helps her find her way back? That’s a good twist. It shows the cat being helpful and loyal. Also, maybe the forest is full of other magical creatures and places. Can we have a hidden cave or a hidden village somewhere in the woods? Oh, absolutely! We could even name the girl something like Lily or Elsie to make it sound more magical. I like Elsie. She sounds like someone who could be brave and curious. Perfect. Now, what about the setting? Should it be in a real place or a made-up one? I think it should be based on real places we’ve been to. Like the woods near Comberton or somewhere in Norfolk. That would make it more authentic. And we can even include some details from our own experiences, like the way the trees look or the kind of animals that live there.

So, do you think we should go vegetarian for dinner tonight? I’ve been thinking about it for a while. I mean, I’m not sure if I’m ready to go full-on, but I’d like to try some plant-based meals. It’s not the most pleasant thing to take, but it’s necessary. I think a lot of people are starting to do this more these days. I’ve also started using more synthetic ingredients in my cooking. Like, I’ve been using mushroom-based meat substitutes and plant-based cheeses.

Alright, let’s get this sorted. So, we’ve got the butterfly forks out. I thought they’d be a nice addition to the table. You know, more elegant than the usual ones. Yeah, they’re pretty. It’s not the end of the world, but it’s not ideal either. Yeah, I can imagine. I suppose it’s the same in academia sometimes.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about the way we talk about language in our work. It’s interesting how the nuances can sometimes change depending on where you are in the country, or even where you’ve been educated. Yeah, I mean, I think that’s why it’s so fascinating to work in language research. You get to see how people from different regions use the same words in different ways. It’s like a little treasure hunt every day. Exactly. It’s not just about the words themselves, but the context in which they’re used. I remember once I was in Lincoln and heard someone say “chuffed” in a way I’d never heard before. It was almost like they were using it as a verb, not just an adjective. That’s the beauty of it, really. I mean, in my job, we’re always looking for these kinds of patterns. It doesn’t just happen in one place—it’s everywhere. I’ve noticed that even people from the same city can have different dialects depending on their background. It’s like a language within a language. I can confirm that. I’ve worked with people from Leeds, and even though they’re all from the same area, their speech can vary so much. I was once in a meeting where one person was using a lot of “a’” and “’ere,” while the other was using quite formal English. It was like listening to two different dialects in the same room. That’s definitely true. I think part of it is the influence of education. I mean, being in a graduate program, you start to pick up more standard English, but you never quite lose the way you speak at home. It’s like a mix of both. I think that’s a good point. I mean, I was raised in Aylesbury, so I have that South-Eastern accent, but I also have a guest speaker background. I’ve had people from all over the UK in my classes, and it’s amazing how different the way people speak can be, even if they’re all British. And don’t forget the influence of media and TV. I’ve noticed that people who watch a lot of American shows tend to pick up some of their phrases, even if they’re not American themselves.
