Yeah, I hear you. I’ve been feeling the same way. There’s just so much going on in our lives. I mean, I’m still teaching, but I’ve been thinking about maybe taking some time off or at least a longer weekend trip. Maybe even something like a short break in France or Italy. I’ve been saving up for a while now. That sounds like a good idea. I know that’s not something you can just do on a whim, but if we plan it properly, it could be nice. I’ve been looking at some travel blogs too. There’s this one about a place in the south of France that’s really quiet and has some amazing beaches. I think it could be perfect for us. I’ve heard of that place. It’s supposed to be really peaceful. I think it’s called Saint-Tropez or something like that.

So, did you go out last night? I haven’t seen you since the weekend. Yeah, I did, but it was pretty rough. I ended up going to this bar near campus, and it was full of people who thought they were the best at football. Oh no, that’s  not  a good night out. I always end up in places like that. I mean, I love football, but I don’t like being surrounded by people who think they’re Arsenal’s future. I know, right? It was like the entire place was just one big debate about who’s better: Messi or Ronaldo. I just wanted to order a drink and not have to argue about it. Ha! Yeah, I tried that once. I was at this club with some friends and I just sat in the corner with my coffee, pretending I didn’t hear anything. But one of them started talking about how he’d taken a group of his mates to the Euros and that he’d even met some players. That’s so typical. I tell you, the only thing those people really care about is who’s wearing what kit and how many goals they’ve scored. Exactly! I remember this one guy from my year who used to brag about how he got tickets to a game, but he ended up getting kicked out for shouting “Philippe Coutinho” when the player was on the pitch. Oh man, that’s classic. I think I once saw him trying to sneak into a match with a fake ticket. He had the look of a cat that got the bottle of ketchup. Haha, I love that. But seriously, have you thought about trying to find a group that’s more chill? Maybe some people who are into music or something? Maybe, but I’m not sure. I mean, I do like football, but sometimes it’s just too much. I get it. I think I’m going to try to limit my nights out to places where people are just being themselves instead of acting like they’ve been a professional footballer for the last ten years. Yeah, that sounds like a plan. I mean, it’s not like life’s all about football, right? Right! I mean, we’ve got exams coming up, and I’d rather be studying than arguing about who’s the best striker in the Premier League.

So, do you think we've got everything ready for Grandma to come over next week? I think so, but I’m still waiting on the confirmation from the post office about the ticket. Yeah, and don’t forget the extra blankets for the guest room. She’s not used to the cold up here. Right, right. I’ve got the ones from the attic, but I think they’re a bit dusty. Should I clean them? Oh, just give them a quick wipe and put them in the airing cupboard. She’ll be fine. I’m still not sure about her coming at all, honestly. You know how she is—always complaining about the weather and the food. She’s not like that anymore. She’s been through a lot lately. We all need to be there for her. True. I just worry about the trip. The roads are so bad this time of year, especially near the border. Yeah, and that’s not even mentioning the weather forecast. They’re predicting snow next week. Well, we’ll just have to deal with it. It’s not like she’s going anywhere else. Speaking of which, have you heard about the new FIFA tournament they’re hosting in England? I think it’s gonna be amazing. Yeah, I’ve heard about it, but I’m not really into football. Though I did watch the World Cup a few years back. You’d enjoy it. It’s not just about the players—it’s about the whole atmosphere, the fans, the energy. I guess. I just wish I could get tickets. I’ve tried a few times, but they always sell out. You could always ask your brother. He’s got connections with some people in the sports industry. Oh, he mentioned that the other day. I’ll ask him later. And while we’re talking about being connected, have you ever thought about getting a job again? I know you’re retired, but there are opportunities out there. Honestly, I’ve thought about it. But I’m not sure where to start. I’ve been out of work for so long. You could always try some freelance work. I know a few people who need help with data entry or something like that. Yeah, and you could use the skills you’ve built up over the years. You’re really good at what you did.

So, do you think we've got everything ready for tomorrow? I mean, the flat's still a bit of a mess from the weekend, and I was supposed to tidy up before the family comes over. Honestly, I think we’ve got the essentials sorted. The kitchen’s clean, the living room’s tidy, and the bins were out this morning. But if you're worried about the mess, maybe you should just leave it as is. Some people like a bit of chaos. Honestly, I think you're both being too hard on yourselves. Life’s too short to worry about every little detail. I’ve seen plenty of flats that look like they’ve been hit by a tornado, and people still manage to visit without a care in the world. I agree, but I do love a tidy home. I mean, the last time my cousin came over, she found my old mobile phone in the cereal box and started trying to use it for a camera. It’s not even a camera phone, you know. Oh, that’s so typical of you, Mavis. You’re always surrounded by things you don’t need. But I do like your point. Maybe we can just leave the flat as is. I mean, it’s only a few hours. Yeah, I think that’s the way to go. And while we're on the subject of things you don’t need, I've been trying to figure out how to set up my Blackberry. I keep getting this error message about not being able to sync with my laptop. Ah, Blackberries. I remember those being all the rage back in the day. They were like the Apple of their time. But honestly, I prefer the touch screen now. You can do so much more with your phone than you ever could with a physical keyboard. I know, right? I tried one once, and it was like trying to play a piano with your fingers. I just ended up giving up and going back to my old Nokia. You can’t even get a decent ringtone out of it now. I think I’ve got one of those. I bought it second-hand for a fiver. It still works, but the battery died the other day, and I had to use a charger from my toaster. Oh no, really? That’s not safe at all.

So, do you know what’s going on with the football results? I tried to check on my phone but it’s got no signal here in Tarnow. Yeah, I saw something about a big match last night. I think it was between Manchester United and Leeds. But honestly, I couldn’t tell you who won. I’ve been so stressed about my students this week. You’ve been working so hard, haven’t you? I feel like I haven’t done anything all week. I’ve just been sitting here, drinking coffee and watching the rain. It’s like the weather here is mirroring my mood. Cold, wet and just… not great. I miss the sun. I know what you mean. I’ve been feeling pretty down lately too, especially since the clocks went back. I’m starting to think I might have SAD. I’ve been thinking about that too. I’ve been reading a lot, actually. There’s this book about the effects of the seasons on mental health. It’s quite interesting. That’s a good idea. I should try reading more. But I’ve been so busy worrying about my students. I feel like I’m responsible for their future, you know? I get that. I’ve had some really good students this semester. One of them is actually preparing for the IELTS exam. I’m helping them with their writing. It’s kind of like a full-time job. That sounds intense. I tried doing a bit of teaching over the summer, but it just didn’t stick. I mean, I had a colleague who taught in a school about an hour away. I went to visit the other day. Oh, you did? Did you like it? It was okay, I guess. The kids were polite, but I felt out of place. I mean, I’m not used to the structure. Plus, I was working part-time in a café, so I didn’t have the energy. I can see how that would be exhausting. I’ve been thinking about working on a farm over the winter. I heard it’s a way to keep the body moving and the mind busy. That sounds like a good plan. I’ve been thinking about getting a dog too. Something to keep me company. Yeah, I’ve been meaning to adopt one. I’ve been watching a lot of dog videos on YouTube.

So, do you know what’s up with you and Fran? Like, you’ve been ignoring her texts for like a week now. I know, I know. I just feel like we’re not on the same page anymore. She’s been messaging me about going out, but I’ve been so busy with work. Yeah, but you’re always busy. You need to make a move, though. I mean, if you don’t, she might just find someone else. I know, I know. It’s just… I don’t know how to approach it. I mean, she’s not exactly the type to just jump into something. You could always try asking her out. Like, directly. Maybe she’s been waiting for you to take the initiative. Yeah, but what if she says no? Well, if she says no, you just say thanks and move on. It’s not like you’re desperate or anything. I’m not desperate, I just… I don’t want to ruin things. I mean, we’ve been friends for ages. And that’s what makes it even better. You can still be friends, but then you can also be something more. Exactly. You don’t have to lose your friendship just because you’re dating someone. It’s all about communication. I guess. I just don’t want to come off as too forward. It’s okay to be a bit forward. You’re not a complete stranger. You’ve been through a lot together. Yeah, and besides, you’re not the type to be shy. Remember when we were in uni and you asked that girl from the bar out on the first date? Oh, yeah. That was a disaster. But it was funny. And it taught you a lesson. You can’t be scared to take a chance. Exactly. So, what’s stopping you from being bold with Fran? I don’t know. Maybe I just need to take a deep breath and say something. That’s the spirit! Just do it. You’ll regret it if you don’t. And if she says no, we’ll still be here to support you. You’re both right. I think I’ll just send her a message tonight. Maybe a simple one, like “Hey, wanna grab a drink this weekend?” That’s a start. At least you’re taking the first step. Yeah, and if it doesn’t work out, you’ll still have us to talk to.

So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about going back to China again this year. I’ve been teaching English there for a few years now, and I’ve got a few students who've been asking me about doing their own TEFL courses. It’s a bit of a niche market, but it’s growing. That’s interesting. I was actually just talking to someone last week about teaching in China. They said the demand is up because of the number of Chinese students coming to study in the UK, and they want to learn English to be able to communicate when they're here. It’s a big market. Yeah, I mean, I think it’s more the other way around. A lot of Chinese people are interested in learning English because they see it as a way to access more opportunities, especially in business or travel. But then again, there are so many different ways to teach English now. From online teaching to in-person classes. It’s a very flexible field. Absolutely. And it's not just about the language—it's about culture. I mean, I’ve been reading up on Chinese culture a lot, especially with all the influx of Chinese tourists coming to London. I’ve even met a few Chinese friends who’ve been here on holiday, and they’ve been curious about the way we speak, the way we live, the way we work. It's fascinating. Definitely. It’s not just about the language anymore. It's about understanding the nuances of the culture and the people. I think when you're teaching in China, you have a very different experience compared to teaching in the UK. The students are often more focused on practical applications—like using English in business, in travel, in social situations. It's quite different from the way we teach English here. I can imagine. I mean, I’ve been to China a couple of times, and one of the most impressive things was the number of pandas in the parks. I remember seeing a group of them in a zoo in Beijing. But I think it's not just about wildlife. The cities themselves are amazing—especially Beijing and Shanghai. I mean, the layout of the parks, the way people live, the pace of life, the architecture—it's all so different. I agree.

So, do you know where we're going again? I mean, I thought we were meeting someone at the university, but now I’m not sure. Yeah, I think we were supposed to meet with the team at the engineering firm, but the meeting got rescheduled. I just got a text saying it’s now tomorrow at 10. Oh, right, that’s a bit of a change. I was hoping to go to the café with some friends, but I guess work comes first. It does, especially when you’re in the middle of a project. I mean, it’s not like we can just take a day off, right? I know, but I’m starting to get a bit tired of this back-and-forth. I mean, we’ve been working on this project for months now. It feels like we’ve been running in circles. I hear you. It’s frustrating, but at least we’re getting somewhere, even if it’s slow. I mean, we’ve already built the prototype, and the client is happy with the initial results. Yeah, that’s true. I guess it’s just the way things go sometimes. But I still feel like we’re missing something. Like, there’s this part of the design that just doesn’t quite fit. You’re not the only one who feels that way. I’ve been thinking about it too. Maybe we should take a break and come back to it with fresh eyes. That sounds like a good idea. I mean, we’ve been working so many hours recently, and I’m starting to feel like I’m not thinking clearly. Exactly. And besides, we’ve got the weekend coming up. We could use some time to recharge. Yeah, I’d rather be at the café with my friends than sitting in an office for twelve hours. I mean, I know it’s important, but I need to balance it with my personal life too. I totally agree. You know, I’ve been trying to do the same thing. I’ve been working late a lot, and it’s starting to take a toll. I think it’s time we both really start prioritizing our well-being. I think that’s the key. We can’t keep pushing ourselves to the limit. It’s not sustainable. Definitely not. I think we should start by setting some boundaries.

So, do you know what’s up with Lucy? She’s been really off lately. She’s like,  constipated  and bloated, and she keeps saying her stomach feels like it’s going to explode. Yeah, I know. I saw her at the pub last week. She was curled up in a corner, pretending to read a book, but I could tell she was in agony. She even said she couldn’t eat anything because it made her feel worse. That sounds bad. What did she say was wrong with her? Is it something serious? She didn’t say much, but she mentioned she’s been feeling awful for a few days now. She’s been stressed about work and hasn’t been sleeping well. She thinks it might be a stomach bug or something. She should see a doctor. I mean, if she’s been like this for a few days, it’s not just a random tummy ache. You know how she gets when she’s stressed—she hides it, but it’s really affecting her. Yeah, I agree. She’s always had a sensitive stomach, but I think she’s been pushing herself too hard. She’s working on that new project at the office, and she’s been staying up late all week. Exactly. Plus, she hasn’t been eating properly either. She’s been skipping meals and just grabbing snacks when she can. That’s not good for her. I mean, I’ve been there. When you’re stressed, you don’t think about your health. But it’s not worth it. You have to take care of yourself. I told her that last week. She said, “I’m fine, I’ll just take it easy.” But she didn’t. She just kept going. I worry that she’s not listening to herself anymore. Yeah, and I think she’s hiding it too. She doesn’t want to seem weak or vulnerable. You know how she is—she always wants to be the strong one. That’s one of the things I love about her, but it’s also what gets her into trouble. She pushes herself too hard, and when things go wrong, she doesn’t ask for help. Maybe it’s time she took a step back. Maybe she needs to slow down, rest, and actually take care of herself. Yeah, and maybe she should take a day off.

I just got a message from Lucy. She’s been acting really weird lately. Oh no, what’s going on? She said she’s been having a really hard time at work. She’s been avoiding her team and hasn’t spoken to anyone. Has she said why? Not really. She just said she’s feeling like she’s not cut out for this job. That’s rough. Is she going to talk to anyone about it? She mentioned she might see her therapist next week. I think she’s been struggling with anxiety. That’s understandable, especially with how stressed everyone’s been at work lately. Yeah, and I know she’s been working long hours, especially since the new project started. I can imagine. I’ve been feeling that way too. The pressure is just so high sometimes. I know. I’ve been thinking about taking some time off, but I’m worried about how it will look to my manager. I get it. But your health comes first. You don’t want to burn out. I know. I just feel like I have so much to do and so little time. Sometimes, I think I’m not doing enough. That’s not true. You’re doing a lot already. And you’re not alone in feeling that way. I guess. It just feels like everyone else is so on top of things, and I’m just… falling behind. That’s not fair. You’re not falling behind. You’re just managing all of this on your own, and that’s not healthy. I know. I just don’t know how to ask for help without feeling like a burden. You don’t have to ask for help to feel like a burden. You’re allowed to take care of yourself. I hope Lucy is okay. I really don’t want to see her go through this alone. Me too. We should reach out to her sometime. Maybe set up a coffee or something. Yeah, I’d like that. Just being there for her might help. Exactly. Sometimes, just having someone to talk to can make all the difference. I hope so. I just feel like I’m running on empty right now. You’re not alone in that. I’m here for you, and I’m sure Lucy is too. Thank you. I really appreciate that. Anytime. We’re in this together.

Alright, so I was thinking about the story we read last night about the old witch in the woods. You know, the one who turned people into stones? It’s such a classic tale, isn’t it? Yeah, I remember that one. But what if the witch wasn’t really evil? What if she was just protecting her forest? But why would she do that? She could have just left the forest alone. Maybe she felt like the people were taking too much from the land. You know, chopping down trees and polluting the rivers. The forest was her home, and she was trying to keep it safe. That makes sense. Sometimes people think evil is always black and white, but maybe it’s more complicated than that. Like, maybe the witch was just trying to do what was right for her world. But what about the stones? If she turned people into stones, that’s pretty harsh. Why not just throw them out of the forest? Maybe she didn’t want to hurt them, but she needed to stop them from harming the forest. You know, sometimes the only way to protect something is to make a sacrifice. Like in some of the old legends, where a hero has to give up something precious to save the day. Maybe the witch was like that. She had to make a choice that hurt her, but saved her home. I wonder if the stones ever got better? Like, if they were still in the forest, did they ever turn back into people? That’s a good question. I think in some stories, they do. If the forest is safe again, maybe the witch lets them go. But in others, they stay as stones, serving as a reminder of the balance between good and evil. I think the point is that we should always consider the bigger picture. Just because someone does something that seems evil doesn’t mean they’re truly bad. Sometimes they’re just trying to protect something they love. So, maybe the real lesson is to be careful how we judge others. Even if they seem mean or cruel, there might be a reason behind it. Exactly. And that’s why these stories are so important. They teach us about the world, about ourselves, and about the choices we make every day. I think we should tell this story to the others at dinner.

So, did you get the photos from the school trip? Yeah, I think so. I got them on my phone. You know how it is, they take loads of pictures. Did you go on the trip? Yeah, I was in the group that went to the old castle. It was so cool! Oh, really? What did you do? We got to climb the tower and there was a big old bridge. We had to cross it. Did you get scared? I think I saw a spider on the wall. That’s not scary, that’s just a spider. Yeah, I suppose. I didn’t see anything, but I heard this weird noise. Was it a ghost? No, probably just the wind. Maybe. I didn’t want to stay too long, honestly. I liked it. I got to see the moat. I threw a stone into the water. You didn’t get in trouble? No, the teacher just said to be careful. I think I saw one of the other kids drop a chocolate bar. It rolled into the water and disappeared. That’s not fair! Well, it’s a castle. You can’t expect it to be perfect. Also, it was a bit cold. Yeah, my toes were numb. I had a sock on. You had a sock on? Yeah, you’re supposed to have socks on in the castle. It’s a rule. I didn’t know that. You would have been in trouble if you had gone barefoot. I think the teacher had a funny face when I asked if we could take off our socks. That’s the spirit. You’re trying to be a rebel. Anyway, did you get to see anything else? There was a big room with all the old stuff. They had swords and shields. Did you touch anything? I touched a sword! It was shiny. That’s not safe, you should have asked first. I think it was okay. The teacher said we could handle it. I don’t think I want to touch anything. You’re right. Best to keep your distance. I think the highlight was the tea. They served us real tea with biscuits. Did you get to eat the biscuits? Yeah, but I only had one. I didn’t have any. I was too busy taking pictures. I wanted to take a picture of the castle, but I didn’t have my phone.

So, how’s the new place? I heard you moved into that little shop on the high street. Yeah, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster, but I think we’re getting it sorted. The rent’s a bit high, but at least the location’s good. That’s the thing with Brighton, isn’t it? You pay a lot for a bit of space. I still can’t get over how much the flats here cost. I know, it’s crazy. But I think once the shop starts making some money, it’ll pay for itself. You’ll be the first to know if it’s a success or a disaster. I’m still waiting for my first sale. Don’t worry, you’ll catch on. I’ve been thinking about starting a little recycling corner too – it’s a bit of a Green Party idea, but I think it could work. That’s interesting. I’ve been thinking about the environment more lately. I mean, I still drive that old car, but I’ve started recycling more and cutting down on plastic. That’s great. It’s not like we can just ignore the issues anymore. I remember when I was a kid, the world seemed so much simpler. No climate crisis, no Brexit, just jobs and family. Yeah, times have changed. You know what I found out the other day? My niece’s in a relationship with someone from London. They’re trying to get a place here, but it’s almost impossible. That’s not good. The housing market’s a nightmare. I’ve got a few friends who are stuck in the same boat. Some of them are even considering moving back to the Midlands. I can see why. It’s not just the cost, it’s the lifestyle. Everyone’s so busy, it’s hard to find time for anything. I remember when I was your age, we all used to meet up for drinks and just chat. Now, it’s all about work and keeping up with the bills. Yeah, it’s been tough. But I still think there’s hope. I mean, the Green Party’s pushing for more affordable housing and sustainable living. Maybe one day, things will get better. Hopefully. I mean, I’m not sure I’ve got the energy for all that. I’m just trying to keep my health up and make sure I can afford my pension.

So, do you know what’s up with all these plants in the city? I mean, I’ve seen like, proper greenhouse stuff in the shops, and people just buying them like it’s the next big thing. Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. It’s like everyone’s suddenly into gardening. I mean, I’ve got a bit of a green thumb myself, but I’m not sure if it’s the trend or if it’s just the climate changing and people are getting more into sustainability. I think it’s a bit of both. Plus, people are getting into stuff like hydroponics now. I mean, even my mate’s got a tiny setup in his flat, and he says it’s like the future of food. You can grow your own herbs and stuff in a few weeks. That sounds cool, but I’d probably mess it up. I tried planting a few herbs in pots when I was younger, and I ended up with a bunch of dead basil. I think I overwatered it or something. Yeah, I remember that. I think overwatering is a common mistake. But I’ve also heard that with hydroponics, you don’t need to water as much. It’s like a mini indoor garden. I’m curious, have you ever tried anything like that? Not really, but I’ve been thinking about it. I mean, I did have this obsession with fashion in university. I used to spend hours in the shops trying to find the perfect outfit. But now I’ve kind of settled into a more minimalist style. I think it’s just easier to maintain. Fair enough. I used to be into fashion too, but now I’m more into practicality. Although, I do still keep up with trends. I mean, what’s the point of being trendy if you’re not dressing for the future, right? Exactly! And I’ve got to say, I think politics is starting to have a real impact on people’s lives. Like, the whole debate around tax cuts and public services. I mean, I’m not sure how much of it is real and how much is just a game. Yeah, it’s all so confusing. I mean, I like the idea of having more money in my pocket, but if it means less support for things like healthcare or education, I’m not sure.

I just got a new blue Peter badge for the podcast, you know the one with the whale on it. Oh really? You got one of those? I thought they were pretty rare. Yeah, I asked the guy at the shop and he said it’s only given out if you’ve got a really good story. I told him about that time I got stuck in a lift with a student who thought it was a haunted building. Oh, you did? What happened? Well, it was a bit of a mess. The lift was stuck between floors, and the student started talking about ghosts. I tried to calm him down, but he was really into it. Eventually, the maintenance guy came and freed us. It was ridiculous. That sounds like a classic lecture hall story. I remember when I first started teaching, I had a student who kept drawing on the whiteboard with permanent marker. I thought he was being naughty, but it turned out he was trying to make a point about the importance of visual aids. Haha, that’s funny. I guess it’s part of the job to be ready for anything. Definitely. You never know what kind of chaos you’ll walk into. Speaking of chaos, did you hear about that guy who tried to squat in a university building? No, what happened? He turned up with a tent and some camping gear. The university called the police, and it turned into a big deal. I mean, he was just trying to save money, but the admin side of things went nuts. That’s absurd. I mean, I know people sometimes try to do that, but it’s not really a solution. Maybe they should just get a part-time job instead. I suppose. But then again, I’ve seen some pretty crazy things in my time. Like that time I was on TV discussing violent content and the presenter kept cutting in with his own opinions. Oh, you were on TV? Yeah, it was a panel show. I was talking about the ethics of TV violence, and he kept interrupting with his own take on it. I had to hold my ground. That sounds like a tough spot. I bet you were a bit frustrated. A bit. But it’s part of the job, right? We have to speak up for what we believe in.

Well, I've been thinking about the hostel management again, you know. I was just talking to that bloke from the council, and he said they're having more trouble than ever with the younger ones. They're not taking it seriously, I reckon. They think they're too smart for things like rules and hygiene. I know, love. I've heard the same thing. I've got a couple of granddaughters who are starting to go out on their own, and they're all so sure of themselves. They think they can manage everything, but they're just kids. It's like they don't know what the word 'responsibility' means. That's true, but I think some of that is the education system. When I was at school, we were taught to respect the rules and the authority, even if we didn't like it. These kids nowadays, they just question everything. They’re not wrong, but sometimes it’s just a lack of understanding. I suppose it is. But I can’t help but think about the old days. I remember when I was young, we had to work hard just to get by. I never thought I’d be in this position, sitting here with a cup of tea, thinking about how things have changed. I mean, I never had the chance to go to university, just finished school and went straight to work in the factory. That was the life. I know, love. And we were lucky enough to live through the war, all of us. I remember when the rationing was in place, and we had to queue for everything. It was tough, but we worked through it. I still remember my mum saying, “We never had a spare penny, but we always had enough.” That’s the spirit. I remember my parents always saying that hard work was the key to success. They ran a small shop, and even though it wasn’t the biggest, it was enough to keep us all fed and clothed. I always told them I was going to be different, that I’d get a proper job and make sure we had everything. And I did, in a way. Well, I suppose you did, mate. You’re a teacher now, teaching the next generation the same values that your parents passed on to you. It’s a bit ironic, isn’t it?

So, do you remember when you were in recruitment? I mean, I still can’t get over how much you used to talk about ‘soft skills’ and ‘cultural fit’—like, how did you even measure that? Oh, I know, it’s one of those things that sounds so important until you actually try to apply it. I remember one time we were interviewing for a project manager role, and the candidate had all the technical skills but couldn’t explain why they thought their approach was better than someone else’s. We ended up just guessing whether they’d fit in the team. That’s like trying to guess if someone’s a good teacher based on whether they like coffee. It’s not really about that. I mean, I’ve seen enough universities to know that academic literacy is a real issue for students, even at the postgraduate level. Sometimes they can’t write a coherent paragraph, let alone an essay. I know, it’s frustrating. I used to work with lecturers who were amazing at their subject matter but had absolutely no idea how to assess or communicate complex ideas clearly. It’s like they’re teaching a language they don’t speak themselves. Exactly. And then there’s the other side of it—some lecturers seem to think that just because you’ve studied a subject for years, you can automatically explain it to others. It’s not like the subject is magic. You have to break it down. I’ve heard that from students too. Like, someone who’s been teaching for ten years gets a student who says, “I can’t understand what you mean,” and the lecturer says, “Well, you should be able to.” It’s like they’re not listening. I think part of the problem is that universities are under so much pressure to publish and get grants that they don’t always take the time to develop their teaching skills. It’s like they’re trying to be researchers first and teachers second. Yeah, and the students are just as guilty. I had a student last year who submitted an essay that was all in run-on sentences and didn’t have a single topic sentence. I mean, I didn’t even know where to start. It’s a mess. I mean, the system is set up so that it’s hard to get feedback, and even when you do, it’s often too late.

So, do you know anyone here? I’ve been trying to find a study group for my sociology module, but it’s proving a bit tricky. Not really, I’m just here for a quick break. I work part-time at a bookshop in town, so I can’t really commit to anything too long-term. But I’m open to hanging out if someone’s got the same vibe. Oh, I’m actually here with friends too. I’m studying psychology, and we’re all trying to get ahead with our essays. I’m from Bolton, by the way. Do you know where that is? I’m from Bolton too! Wait, are you serious? That’s actually my hometown. My family moved back to India when I was a kid, but I’ve been living in the UK for the past few years. I’m studying history. It’s wild, isn’t it? Growing up in Bolton and then moving abroad. That’s pretty cool. I’m from Bradford in Yorkshire, which is pretty different. I mean, I’ve never been to Bolton, but I’ve heard it’s a really vibrant place. I’m studying English literature. Oh, that’s interesting. I’ve read a few books by authors from Yorkshire. I think I’ve even studied one in my English class at school. Though I’m more into the practical side of things, I do enjoy learning about literature too. Yeah, I’ve heard that Bradford has a rich literary tradition. I think one of the poets from there even won a big award a few years back. Anyway, I’d love to study with someone from the same area. It’s always nice to have a bit of a connection. I can totally relate to that. It’s funny, I didn’t really think about my roots until I started studying history. I mean, I was born in India, but my parents are both from the UK. I grew up in a mixed culture, which has made me really curious about both sides. I think that’s why I’m into history—because it’s about understanding how different cultures intersect. That’s a great perspective. I’ve always been interested in how people’s backgrounds shape their views, even if they’re not always obvious. I guess that’s why I like studying literature—it’s all about how stories reflect the world we live in.

So, do you know what’s the biggest thing about the military? I mean, it's not like it's secret or anything, but sometimes I feel like people don’t really know how it works. Like, I was talking to my cousin the other day, and he thought you just get a uniform and go shoot things. That’s not even close to the truth, is it? Oh, come on, you’ve got to be joking. I mean, I know it’s not that simple, but it’s not like you just go out and shoot people for fun. It’s all about training, strategy, and... well, keeping the country safe. Though I don’t know how much of that actually happens these days. Yeah, I guess you’re right. But still, I think the image is so skewed. Like, the media shows all the explosions and the guns, but it’s not like they’re out there all the time. I mean, I read this article last week about how the majority of military personnel are involved in logistics, transport, or support roles. It’s not just about being a hero. That’s true. I mean, I’ve got a friend who works in the Ministry of Defence, and he told me that 80% of the budget goes into things like IT, infrastructure, and healthcare for the troops, not actually fighting. It’s pretty much the same as any other big organisation, just with more gear and more rules. That’s kind of scary, actually. Like, how do you even start to understand the scale of it? I mean, what if something happened and we had to rely on the military? I feel like I’d be completely lost. I know what you mean. I remember the time the local library had an event about military history, and even then, people were confused. One guy asked if the military had any kind of app, like for tracking soldiers or something. It was ridiculous. Yeah, I think it’s just something that’s so big and so far removed from everyday life. I mean, I’ve got a few magazines on the table here—look, this one’s about the military, and the other is about tech. You think they’re completely different worlds, but I swear there’s more overlap than you’d think. Oh, definitely. You look at how much of modern warfare depends on computers, satellites, and data.

So, do you think we should go to London for the weekend? I mean, it's been a while since we last went, and I heard there’s some new art show at the Tate that’s really worth seeing. Yeah, I’d like that. But I’m not sure if I can afford it. I mean, I’ve been working on this film project, and it's been really tight on the budget. Plus, I’ve got this thing with my cousin coming over from Manchester, and I don’t want to be short of cash. Didn’t you say your cousin is moving to London? Or is it just visiting? No, he's just visiting for a few days. He’s working on a music gig, and he wanted to check out the city before he makes the move. But I’m glad he’s coming because I might be able to get some help with the gig details. I mean, he’s got this network of contacts in the music scene. That’s great, but I’m kind of worried about the whole London thing. I mean, I know it’s a big city, but sometimes I get that feeling that people are judging you for living there. Like, it's like there's this unspoken thing that if you’re from the North, you’re not really “London.” You know what I mean? Yeah, totally. I’ve had people say that to me before. I mean, I’m from Winchester, and I’ve never even lived in London, but I still get that vibe. Like, they just assume I should know everything about the city, and if I don’t, I’m not “proper.” Oh, come on, I mean, I’m from the North too, and I’m pretty much an expert on London. I’ve been there for years. I barely even know the postcode of my own flat sometimes. But, like, I do know the places. I can tell you where the best kebabs are. Or where to find the best sofa to sit on in Notting Hill. That’s not really the point. I mean, it’s just weird. I think it’s partly the class thing too. Like, you know, the idea that people from the South are more “cultured” or something. I’ve heard that before. Yeah, and I think it's also the politics thing.

So, do you like the flat? I know it’s a bit small, but it's got a nice vibe. Yeah, it’s cozy. I like the kitchen, actually. It’s got that open-plan feel, which I think is really modern. It reminds me of the flats I’ve seen on social media. It’s nice, but I have to say – the kitchen? I’ve seen more in a flat in London than this. I mean, we had a proper kitchen in my old flat. A real oven, not a microwave. Didn’t even have a fridge in some of the flats I stayed in when I was working. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve had flats where the fridge was in the hallway and the oven was in the living room. It was a bit of a mess, I’ll be honest. Well, we’re working on it. We’ve got plans to reorganize the kitchen next month. Maybe even get a new fridge and a proper oven. That sounds great. I’d love to see the new kitchen. You know, I’ve never really lived in a flat with a real kitchen before. I’ve always been in student accommodations or shared houses. That’s a shame. You really need a proper kitchen if you want to cook, and I mean real cooking, not just sandwiches and instant noodles. I did have a bit of a reputation for making a mess in the kitchen, actually. Oh, I can imagine. I used to live with a bunch of people, and the kitchen was always a battleground. Someone would always be burning something, and someone else would be complaining about the smell. Yeah, I remember the time when the oven caught fire. I had to call the fire brigade. It was a bit of a dramatic moment. That sounds like the kind of thing that would happen in a flat. I can’t imagine living somewhere with a real oven. I’d probably burn everything. That’s what I thought too. My wife used to tell me I was a terrible cook, but I always said I was a professional. At least I had the oven. That gave me some kind of legitimacy. That’s classic. You always need some kind of excuse to cook. Maybe that’s why I ended up in care work. It’s safer, I guess.

So, do you think the housing market’s gonna go up or down in the next few years? I’m trying to figure out if it’s worth buying a place or not. Honestly, I don’t know. I mean, I read somewhere that house prices are going to keep rising, but then again, I also heard people say it’s going to crash. It’s like trying to predict the weather. Yeah, I get that. I’ve been watching the news, and it’s like they keep saying one thing and then the next day it’s completely different. I know, it’s so confusing. I’ve been thinking about buying a place too, but with the cost of living the way it is, I’m not sure if it’s the right time. It’s not just the cost of the house. You’ve got all the other expenses—mortgage, insurance, taxes, and then there’s upkeep. I don’t know how people even manage it. I know, it’s a lot. I’ve been thinking about it more, especially after my dad mentioned he’s planning to retire soon and wants to downsize. But even then, it’s not easy. Yeah, I can imagine. I’ve heard stories about people trying to sell their houses, and it takes forever. Sometimes they have to lower the price quite a bit just to get someone interested. That’s been happening a lot in the area I’m looking at. I’ve had a few offers, but nothing that’s really close to what I was hoping for. I guess it all depends on where you are. I’ve heard about some places in the countryside where prices are cheaper, but then again, you’re paying for the lack of amenities. Exactly. I’m not sure if I want to be in the middle of nowhere. I’d rather be near the city, even if it means paying a bit more. I can see that. I’ve been getting into cooking a bit more lately. I mean, I used to always order takeaways, but now I’m trying to save money and cook more. That’s a good idea. I’ve been trying to do that too, especially after I got into a bit of a health rut. It’s funny how eating better actually makes you feel better. I know, I’ve noticed that.

So, do you ever find it hard working with the same people every day? I mean, I work with the same nurses and assistants, and sometimes it’s like a second family, but then again, sometimes it's just exhausting. I can relate. I work with the same copywriters and designers at the agency, and there's a lot of back-and-forth. But I guess it’s not too bad. I mean, I have some great friends at work, even if we're all competitive as hell. Yeah, I can see that. I work with the same people every day too. It’s like a rhythm. You know what everyone’s going to say and what they’re going to do. But sometimes it’s a bit boring, you know? Like, the same routines over and over. I feel the same. I work with the same carers and patients every day, and it's really rewarding, but sometimes I just want to switch things up. Like, I’d love to take a break, even if it's just a short one. I get that. I’ve had some days where I really wanted to take a break, especially when I had a difficult patient. But I know that if I don’t stay consistent, it can be really hard for the patients too. I guess that’s part of the job, isn’t it? You have to be there for them, even if it’s not always easy. I mean, I’ve had some days where I just wanted to go home and not think about work, but then I remember why I’m doing it. Yeah, and being a carer, you really do get close to the people you’re helping. I mean, sometimes you’re the only one they talk to, and they depend on you. It’s a bit of a heavy responsibility, but it’s also really fulfilling. That must be tough. I mean, I know what it’s like to have to take care of someone, but I can’t imagine having to do it every single day. I think I’d get really stressed out. I can see how that would be. But I think it’s the same with any job, really. You have to find a balance. I mean, I do my best to take time for myself, like going for walks or just sitting in the garden with a cup of tea.
